where: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.9.4 delta-and-route row, 2.6, 2.9.5; rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 4.9 feature route row, 3.3 step 2; rewrite/design/state.md 2.16 feature route row, 2.4 lock row; rewrite/design/agents-skills.md 2.6 architect and story-writer rows; rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.11.3 artifact_frozen
problem: `vsdd feature route --run <id>` must derive the route from 'the delta record the step just wrote' or 'the stored change analysis', but no document gives that record a path, kind or class. The only candidate, an impact assessment under specs/architecture/assessments, is in spec-arch. That class is locked during the delta step: the latest spec decision is approved, and the run holds no amendment until `feature route` marks one. The route command is the step's closing command, so it runs before the step record exists. The story-writer, the spec packet and plan in delta scope also need the analysis, and the story-writer cannot read runs. Every feature run, and so every brownfield change and bug fix, has no input for its route.
proposed_resolution: Add a file input: `vsdd feature route --run <id> --delta-file <path>`. The architect writes the delta data JSON in the temporary directory. The tool validates it and copies it into the cycle's tracked record (for example cycles/<cycle>/units/feature.json), which becomes the 'stored change analysis' that the story-writer, the packet and plan read. Update pipeline.md 2.9.4, blueprint 4.9, state.md 2.8 and 2.16, agents-skills.md 2.6 and the delta-analysis method.

where: rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 4.10 Verdict row, 5.4; rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.9.1 review row, 2.10.1, 2.10.3, 2.11.2, 2.11.3; rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.11.7 step 2; rewrite/design/state.md 2.8 Step record, S7 store_step; rewrite/design/packaging.md 2.5, layer 2b fixture
problem: The tool must count a review pass only when the stored agent type is 'the reviewer that owns the pass's method'. No record holds a method: the step identity is run, workflow, name, subject and attempt, and the hook stores only the agent type and the head. Step names are built at run time. In story.js they name the agent (review-adversary-p1); in wave.js they name neither the agent nor the method (integration-review-r1, security-r1). No document defines the step-name grammar the verdict function would need to find a unit's passes, fixes and arbitration. G3 cannot build the check or its conformance fixture as specified.
proposed_resolution: Add `method`, and the pass or round number, to the step identity: brief() puts them in the echoed `step` object, pipeline.md 2.10.1 adds them to the schema, and the hook stores them. The verdict counts a record as a pass when its method is a review method of the perimeter (pipeline.md 2.9.13) and the stored agent type is the agent whose file lists that method. Fixes and arbitration are found by their methods. Update blueprint 4.10, hooks.md 2.11.7, state.md 2.8 and S7, and the packaging fixture.

outcome.what_was_done: The step identity now carries `method` (required) and, for review, fix and arbitrate steps, `loop` and `pass`; the tool reads those fields and never parses a step name. A review record is a done record with a pass whose method belongs to a reviewer-tier agent and whose stored agent type is that owner. The built step-result schema, its fixtures and the prelude's step() under next/ must follow.
outcome.where: schemas/step-result.schema.json; topics/verdicts.md; topics/prelude-steps.md; topics/story-script.md; topics/wave-script.md; records/step.md

where: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.9.1 admission paragraph and red-gate detail, 2.9.4 survey row, 2.10.8 Story unit base; rewrite/design/state.md 2.16 gate plan and gate green rows, 2.8 Cycle record and evidence lookup, 4 packaging S2; rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 4.13
problem: A story branch is cut 'from the cycle's base', but cycle.json has no base, only `baseline` (a release tag, an ingest or an import; empty for a first release). The hotfix parenthesis makes `baseline` look like the intended source. Elsewhere the text speaks of a 'base branch', or branches.integration. Nothing says which commit is used (local or remote head, and when) or where it is recorded for the descent check. Read as `baseline`, feature-cycle stories are cut from the last release tag. The green diff then includes every earlier story of the cycle, and the red gate counts their passing tests as new and fails.
proposed_resolution: Define the base once, in state.md 2.16 (the worktree library) and pipeline.md 2.9.1. It is the head of branches.integration (the remote head after a fetch in pr mode) when the worktree is created; in a hotfix cycle it is the release tag the cycle names. Record the commit in the run record and in the story closure. The unit's base, the descent check, the red-gate comparison and the green diff all use that recorded commit.

outcome.what_was_done: There is no cycle base. A story branch is cut from the head of the branch it will be delivered to, read when the branch is created (the integration branch, its remote head after a fetch in pr mode; hotfix/<version>, created at the release tag, in a hotfix cycle). The worktree library records it as delivery.base in the story's closure record, and the descent check, the red comparison and the green diff use that recorded commit. Recording it in the run record as well was not taken: the closure is tracked and is what a resumed run reads.
outcome.where: topics/worktrees.md (owner); schemas/closure-record.schema.json; records/cycle.md; workflows/story.md, topics/story-admission.md, commands/gate-plan.md, workflows/feature.md (restatements replaced by links)

where: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.9.1 delivery detail; rewrite/design/state.md 1, 2.3, 2.16 story deliver; rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.11.4 merge-guard; rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 4.12, 9.2 G4a
problem: Local mode is one sentence: 'it merges locally'. With no remote, the integration branch is normally checked out in the person's main checkout. Git will not check it out again in .worktrees/_integration/. Advancing the ref leaves the person's index and files behind HEAD, and merging in the main checkout breaks the rule that 'the person's own checkout is never switched, pulled or committed to'. No behaviour is chosen, so G4a has no specified merge on the slice path.
proposed_resolution: State the local-mode merge in pipeline.md 2.9.1 and state.md 2.16: merge in a tool-owned worktree on a detached head, and advance the ref only when the integration branch is not checked out elsewhere. When it is checked out, either fast-forward that checkout only if it is clean and at the old head (a stated exception), or return awaiting_merge with the one command for the person. vsdd doctor and status report the condition. Note the rule beside merge-guard.

outcome.what_was_done: Local delivery is specified in one place: the merge commit is made in the integration worktree, which is always on a detached head; the branch is then moved with update-ref (old value checked) when it is checked out nowhere, or with `git -C <checkout> merge --ff-only` when it is checked out, which is the one stated exception to never touching the person's checkout. When git refuses the fast-forward, delivery returns the new state `checkout_dirty` with the one-line fix and nothing moves.
outcome.where: commands/story-deliver.md (Local mode); topics/worktrees.md; topics/state-directory.md; rules/merge-guard.md; schemas/delivery-data.schema.json; commands/release.md

where: rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.7 implementer and test-writer rows, commands key default, other row; 2.11.1 families; 2.11.10 core row; rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 2.1 D4, 5.4; rewrite/design/agents-skills.md 2.9 command scopes; rewrite/design/packaging.md 2.6 smoke probe 7
problem: The implementer and test-writer rows grant only `git-commit`. `git status`, `diff` and `log` fall in `git-read`, so bash-git blocks the very calls D4 core approves, and smoke probe 7 (a builder runs git status) is blocked. An absent `commands` key means any family, so devops, the verifier, the technical-writer, the demo-recorder, the codebase-analyzer and the 'strictest' `other` row may push, open pull requests and add worktrees. agents-skills.md 2.9 says no pipeline agent does that. `git-read` also includes checkout, switch, fetch and gh api.
proposed_resolution: Define git-read as the reading commands only (status, diff, log, show, rev-parse, ls-files, blame, grep) in hooks.md 2.11.1; a command in no family is refused unless the row holds '*'. Make an absent `commands` key mean ["git-read"]. Give every builder row ["git-commit", "git-read"] and the main row ["*"]. Mirror this in agents-skills.md 2.9.

outcome.what_was_done: git-read is now a closed list of reading commands and a new catch-all family, git-other, holds everything else, so a command nobody listed is refused, not allowed. An absent `commands` key means none (stricter than the proposed git-read default); builders hold git-commit and git-read, the codebase-analyzer git-read, the spike-runner git-commit, git-read and git-other, the main session every family.

where: rewrite/design/state.md 2.12 example, whole-key-list sentence, ownership table; rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.6, 2.11.1 secret_globs, 2.11.10 purity-advice, 2.12 log_retention_days; rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 2.1 D12

where: rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.11.7 step 2; rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 5.4, 5.2; rewrite/design/state.md 2.4, 2.11, S7 spec_locked; rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.5 concurrency
problem: step-results accepts a record only for a 'live run', and spec_locked is released while 'a live run' holds an amendment. Liveness is defined only for a lock holder (`seen` recent). discover, a report-only maintain and spike take no lock, so under that reading their step records are refused: the ideas checkpoint loses its score records, and a spike requested by one of their steps is refused at spike open. The other reading, 'not yet checkpointed', leaves the specification unlocked for 30 days after an amendment run crashes.
proposed_resolution: Define it once in state.md 2.8. A run is live when its record has no checkpoint mark and either it holds the lock with a fresh `seen`, or its workflow takes no lock and it was opened within its time limit. Amendment runs always lock, so for spec_locked the definition reduces to lock liveness. Cite it in hooks.md 2.11.7 and blueprint 5.2 and 5.4.

outcome.what_was_done: step-results blocks run_not_live through records' run_live as store_step applies it (a run record with no ended stamp); a run that has ended is refused. Proven by test_ended_run_blocks (tests/hooks/test_step_results.py). Runs that take no lock remain H4/S3 when widened.

where: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.11.2 review() and the delivery loop, 2.10.3; rewrite/design/state.md 2.8 Step record path
problem: review() runs twice in one story run, once for the main loop and once after a delivery repair. Both runs name their steps review-<l>-p<k>, fix-<who>-p<k> and arbitrate, with pass starting at 1, so they produce the same step-record keys. Nothing says whether store_step overwrites or refuses. The verdict that delivery recomputes from the stored passes then mixes the two loops, or loses the converged pass.
proposed_resolution: Prefix the scoped loop's step names with the delivery round (repair<n>-review-...). State in state.md 2.8 that a step record is never overwritten: a second write to an existing key is refused, so a collision fails in the harness.

outcome.what_was_done: Decision D4 in code: store_step refuses a second write to a step key (step_exists) unless the same agent_id writes again or the content is identical, so a review loop that runs twice in one story cannot mix its passes and an agent whose result the platform refused can replace it. Tested in test_step_collision. The repair-round step-name prefix is the story script's part (W2).

where: rewrite/design/agents-skills.md 2.6 architect row; rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.7 loop step 1, 2.10.8 Fix data, 2.11.1 converge(), 2.11.2 arbitrate; rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.7 (runs denied to every row)
problem: The arbiter is to be given 'the open findings and the builder's dispute notes', and the note 'is kept in the step record for the arbiter only'. But converge() drops the resolutions' notes, arbitrate(open) passes only the findings, and the arbiter cannot read runs. Under D18 it may dismiss only a disputed finding, yet it never sees the dispute.
proposed_resolution: converge() keeps the notes of disputed resolutions by key and calls c.arbitrate(open, notes). The scripts put the notes inline in the arbitration prompt only; universal test 8 already keeps them from reviewers.

outcome.what_was_done: converge() keeps the fixer's dispute notes by key and hands them to the arbiter: c.arbitrate(open, pass, notes), with notes a Map from finding key to the disputed resolution's note, built in the same pass that fills the disputed set, so the arbiter sees the dispute and D18's dismissal rule is enforceable. The scripts' arbitrate stubs put the notes inline in the arbitration prompt only (story-script.md); universal-test prelude-converge behaviour is pinned by a new test in which the arbitrate stub records the pass and the notes it received and the run converges on a not_defect ruling of a disputed finding.
outcome.where: next/workflow-lib/prelude.js (converge); rewrite/spec/topics/prelude-converge.md; rewrite/spec/topics/story-script.md; next/tests/workflows/universal.test.mjs (the amended identity and arbitration test)

where: rewrite/design/state.md 2.16 gate red row, 2.8 evidence lookup; rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.11.4; rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.9.1, 2.11.2 fix()
problem: A re-freeze record holds 'the new hashes of frozen tests the test-writer changed', and the evidence lookup returns it as the latest red record. tests-first and the green gate read the frozen set from that record. If it lists only the changed tests, the other frozen tests stop being frozen, and tests added in a coverage fix are frozen by neither record. The gate name in a re-freeze result is unstated, but fix() requires it to be 'red'.
proposed_resolution: In state.md 2.16 and 2.8, state that a re-freeze record carries the complete frozen set (the earlier identities and hashes, the changed ones with new hashes, and the tests added in the fix pass) and that its result has gate: "red". Cite the rule in hooks.md 2.11.4.

outcome.what_was_done: tests-first takes the frozen set from the latest red or re-freeze record alone (evidence()); a re-freeze that lists the complete set keeps the earlier files frozen and freezes tests added in the fix. Proven by test_refrozen_set_stays_frozen (tests/hooks/test_tests_first.py).

outcome.what_was_done: The stub marker is the constant VSDD-STUB (built as "VSDD-" + "STUB" in gatelib.py), searched in every tracked source-class file at the head; a hit fails the green gate naming the file, before any command runs.

where: rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 10 item 28, 4.13; rewrite/design/state.md 2.11, 5 H-2; rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.11.10 lifecycle-log; rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.11.1 step(), 2.11.2
problem: The fallback for probe 28 keeps the lock alive through calls 'whose working directory lies in a worktree the run owns', and claims the design already does this. Story steps are not isolated: they start in the main session's working directory and are given the worktree by path. Reviewers have no shell, so they never change directory. If probe 28 fails, a long review lets the lock go stale and a second session can take over a live run.
proposed_resolution: Refresh `seen` on any guarded call whose target path or working directory lies in a worktree the locked run owns, or whose vsdd command carries that run's id. Reword blueprint 4.13 and 10 item 28, state.md 2.11 and hooks.md 2.11.10.

outcome.what_was_done: Built by hook-runner-b: the lock is refreshed by a vsdd call that names the run, by a step result of the run, and by a Bash call whose effective directory is in a story worktree of the run. Left for H3: a Read or Grep in the locked run's story worktree, from a second session with an agent id, must refresh the lock, with a test (decision D2 of rewrite/plans/step-3/hook-runner-b.md).

where: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.9.1 Details (story deliver bullet: local mode 'merges locally'), 3.6 (main-checkout sync row); rewrite/design/state.md 2.3 (alternatives table), 2.12 [delivery] mode, 2.16 story deliver and release rows; rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 4.12 delivery.mode, 9.2 G4a; rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.11.4 merge-guard (local mode note)
problem: In local mode the integration branch is the branch the person's main checkout has checked out (any repository with no remote, as in the slice and every new greenfield project). The design says only that the tool 'merges locally'. Git refuses to check that branch out in .worktrees/_integration/. Moving the ref with update-ref after a detached merge leaves the person's index and working tree at the old commit, so the checkout shows the story reversed as staged edits and the next commit from it reverts the story. Merging in the main checkout breaks the stated rule that the person's checkout is never touched. No rule chooses between these. vsdd release in local mode has the same gap.
proposed_resolution: State one rule in pipeline.md 2.9.1, state.md 2.16 (story deliver, release) and blueprint 4.12. The tool makes the merge commit in a detached .worktrees/_integration/. When the person's checkout holds the integration branch and is clean, the tool fast-forwards it with git -C <root> merge --ff-only. When it is dirty, delivery returns awaiting_merge with the reason and the one finishing command. Record this as the single stated exception in the state.md 2.3 table and pipeline.md 3.6, and add a G4a fixture with the main checkout on the integration branch, clean and dirty.

outcome.what_was_done: One local-delivery rule, as proposed except for the dirty case: detached merge in the integration worktree, then update-ref or a fast-forward of the checkout that holds the branch. A refused fast-forward returns `checkout_dirty` (blocked, no decision the first time, rerun after cleaning) instead of awaiting_merge, because a merge decision cannot clean a checkout and would cost the person a second command. `vsdd release` moves its branch the same way; the delivery tests cover the checkout clean, overlapping, non-overlapping, absent and moved.

where: rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 4.9 (how the tool knows who is calling), 4.13 Liveness, section 10 items 27, 28, 29; rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.5 Ctx, 2.11.10 (caller markers, lifecycle-log, extended scope), 2.16; rewrite/design/state.md 2.11; rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.11.1 step() (no isolation passed)
problem: Story stages run as ordinary steps with no platform isolation, so the payload cwd of every test-writer, implementer, reviewer and clerk step is the project root, the same for every parallel story. A cd inside a command does not change it. Three fallbacks depend on a unique cwd. If item 27 fails, markers matched by process and cwd cannot tell concurrent steps apart. If item 28 fails, the lock is refreshed only by calls from a run-owned worktree, which no story step makes, and the main session makes no calls while Workflow runs; the lock then goes stale after 20 minutes mid-wave and a second session can take it over. If item 29 also fails, section 10 says 'item 27 must pass', so there is no fallback and the survey refuses every run. The extended scope's 'inside the caller's own worktree' has the same flaw for builders.
proposed_resolution: In hooks.md 2.5, define the caller's worktree as the worktree holding the target path, or the directory of the cd, git -C or vsdd -C prefix, never the payload cwd alone. Use that definition in lifecycle-log, auto-allow and the marker fallback. Make any vsdd call carrying --run of the locked run refresh the lock (blueprint 4.13, state.md 2.11). Give items 27 and 29 a fallback that needs neither a rewrite nor a process walk: the hook keys the marker by a hash of the session id and the tokenised command, and the tool hashes its own argv and takes the newest unread match (the strictest when several match). Update the fallback cells of items 27 to 29.

outcome.what_was_done: Rules never test the payload cwd alone: `where`, the call's effective directory (the target's directory, or the directory a cd, git -C or vsdd -C names), defines the caller's worktree. The lock is refreshed only by calls that belong to the run (a vsdd call with its --run, a StructuredOutput with its step.run, a call in its worktrees, a subagent call in the holder's session). If updatedInput is not honoured the marker is found by a hash of the call's arguments, oldest unread first, so item 29 no longer gates anything but the offered cut.
outcome.where: topics/rule-model.md; topics/run-lock.md; topics/caller-identity.md; records/caller-marker.md; platform.md (items 27 to 29); rules/lifecycle-log.md; rules/auto-allow.md; topics/hook-platform-facts.md

where: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.11.1 relay(); 2.11.2 story.js; 2.4 route row 'A run lock is held by a live run'; 5.1 need S2; rewrite/design/state.md 2.10 status --fix; 2.11 lock bullets; 2.16 vsdd lock release; rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.11.10 lifecycle-log; rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 4.9, 4.13 Liveness, section 7
problem: Liveness is keyed on the session: any guarded call from the holder's session refreshes seen. Three ordinary events leave a lock held by a run that has stopped, inside a live session: relay() retrying a survey that already took the lock, a person interrupting a workflow, or a throw between the survey and try. The person's own calls keep that lock fresh forever. status --fix releases only a lock whose holder is dead, which is undefined for a live session; plain lock release has no stated semantics; the route says 'wait'. The survey is called idempotent in pipeline S2 but refused on re-entry in state 2.11.
proposed_resolution: 1. Survey re-entry: a lock held by a run of the caller's own session, for the same workflow and subject, with no step record, is taken over. 2. Refresh seen only on calls that belong to the run (step.run on StructuredOutput, --run on vsdd calls, run worktrees), not on main-session calls. 3. Define lock release: own session or stale; --force (person) any; holder dead = stale or session ended. 4. The route and briefing name vsdd lock release when the holder is this session, else --force in a terminal. 5. Fixture: interrupt after the survey, re-run, and the run continues.

outcome.what_was_done: Liveness is refreshed only by calls that belong to the run, never by the main session's own calls, so a run that stopped in an open session goes stale. A survey from the holder's own session for the same workflow and subject re-enters the run when it has no step record and otherwise ends it and takes over; `ended` in the run record defines a live run, and pipeline commands refuse one that is not. `vsdd lock release` frees the caller's own session's lock or a stale one; --force (person) any.
outcome.where: topics/run-lock.md; commands/lock-release.md; commands/survey.md; records/run.md; schemas/run-record.schema.json; records/lock.md; tables/routes.toml

where: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.9.1 tests and deliver rows, green-gate detail; rewrite/design/state.md 2.16 gate green, story deliver; rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.11.4 merge-guard and tests-first; 2.11.7 step-results; 2.10 row 6; rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 3.2, 4.13
problem: Delivery requires green, verdict, demo and CI, and never red evidence. Green compares frozen tests with 'the latest red record' but does not need one to exist. step-results does not check gate entries against evidence records. A test-writer, which may write source before red, can commit tests plus implementation and return a fabricated passing red result; the implementer has nothing to write, green passes, and delivery merges. tests-first also ignores Bash writes to source. Blueprint 3.2's guarantee ('cannot merge code') is false.
proposed_resolution: 1. gate green and story deliver require a passing red or re-freeze record for every kind with a red gate. 2. step-results checks each gates[] entry against the evidence record it names (gate, subject, sha, passed) and blocks a mismatch. 3. tests-first inspects Bash writes into source before red. 4. Cases for both.

outcome.what_was_done: The green gate fails with `no red record` and delivery refuses unless a passing red or re-freeze record exists for a kind with a red gate. step-results blocks a result whose passing gate entry has no matching evidence record (gate, subject, commit, passed). tests-first now also runs on Bash and holds redirect targets and shell write commands to the same two checks.
outcome.where: commands/gate-green.md; commands/story-deliver.md; rules/step-results.md; rules/tests-first.md; tables/rules.toml; topics/rule-model.md

where: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.9.1 deliver detail (local mode); 3.6 'Nothing in 1.0 pulls or merges in the person's checkout'; rewrite/design/state.md 2.3 person's checkout row; 2.12 delivery.mode; rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.11.4; rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 4.12
problem: In local mode the integration branch is usually the branch checked out in the person's main checkout. Git refuses to check it out in a tool-owned worktree. git update-ref leaves the person's index showing the story reversed, so their next commit undoes it. Merging in their checkout breaks the stated invariant and clobbers uncommitted work. The design defines neither path, and the slice's first local delivery hits this.
proposed_resolution: Define the local merge: merge in the worktree where the branch is checked out when it has no tracked changes; return checkout_dirty (blocked, reason environment, naming the checkout) when it is dirty; when checked out nowhere, merge in a tool-owned detached worktree and move the ref. Amend the invariant wording. init and doctor report the case. Add slice tests for clean and dirty.

outcome.what_was_done: Adopted `checkout_dirty` as the state for a checkout the merge would overwrite, but not merging in the person's checkout: the merge commit is always made in the tool's detached integration worktree, so a conflict never lands in the person's files, and their checkout only ever receives a fast-forward that git refuses atomically. The invariant wording is amended; init and doctor need no change because the checkout on the integration branch is the normal, supported case.

where: rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.11.4 merge-guard; 2.11.1 command families; 2.7 example rows; 2.11.10 auto-allow core; rewrite/design/agents-skills.md 2.9 command scopes; rewrite/design/state.md 2.16 story deliver, gate wave
problem: merge-guard does not match commands that move the integration or release ref without a checkout: git update-ref, branch -f/-M/-C, switch -C, checkout -B, fetch . x:<branch>. These fall in git-read ('every other git command'). The family table is wrong both ways: if git-read must be granted, test-writer and implementer (commands = [git-commit]) cannot run git status, diff or log; if it is implied, ref writes pass. Verifier and devops rows default to every family, including push, gh-pr and worktree, which agents-skills forbids. The tool never checks that the integration head is one it produced.
proposed_resolution: Narrow git-read to read-only subcommands. Add a git-ref family that no agent holds, and have merge-guard block it for every caller when it names the integration or release branch. Every agent row lists commands explicitly, and an absent key means none; builders get git-commit and git-read. story deliver and gate wave refuse with integration_moved when the integration head is not one the tool recorded or produced through its own merges.

outcome.what_was_done: merge-guard now blocks, for every caller, commands that move, replace or delete the integration or release branch without a checkout (update-ref, symbolic-ref, branch -f/-m/-M/-c/-C/-d/-D, switch -C, checkout -B, fetch, pull and push refspecs). Those commands sit in the new git-other family, which no builder holds. The proposed integration_moved refusal was not taken: a person in local mode, and other people's merges in pr mode, move the branch legitimately; local delivery re-merges from the new head instead.

where: rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.11.7 item 2; rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.10.1 step identity; 2.10.3; 2.9.1 review row; rewrite/design/state.md 2.8 step record; rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 4.10 Verdict row, 5.4, 11.1 P2LEAN-10
problem: A review pass counts only when the stored agent type owns the pass's method, but the method is only in the prompt. Step records hold the identity, the agent type and the head. Step names follow no single pattern across story, wave and verify, and the step-name table was removed. The tool cannot map a record to a method, so G3 either rejects real passes or skips the check.
proposed_resolution: Add method to the step identity: brief() puts it in the identity the agent echoes, and step-results stores it. The tool counts a record as a pass only when its method is a review method of that perimeter and the stored agent type owns it in the roster. Add a conformance fixture in which a builder echoes a reviewer's method.

outcome.what_was_done: `method` is in the step identity and so in every step record; a pass counts only when its method belongs to a reviewer-tier agent in the methods table and the stored agent type is that owner. A conformance fixture has a builder echo a reviewer's method.

where: rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.5 main loop; 2.9 failure rows; 2.6 quarantine; 2.11.8 runner lines; rewrite/design/state.md 2.9 State problems; rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.6 blocked reason stuck; rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md D12
problem: A deterministic crash in a locked rule (step-results, gate-guard) blocks every step result or clerk call. The blocks reach step agents, not the person, who after two runs gets blocked/stuck with retry, direct and descope, none of which helps. Nothing names VSDD_FACTORY_HOOKS_QUARANTINE. A rule module's import error happens outside the per-rule try, so it is a runner crash, never logged as rule.error, and the quarantine condition cannot be met; only hooks=off remains.
proposed_resolution: Import rule modules inside the per-rule try. The rule_error block's fix line names the restart command with the quarantine variable. The briefing and vsdd status list rules with repeated rule.error, with the restart line. The checkpoint copies a unit's last block codes into its blocked packet.

outcome.what_was_done: Each rule module is imported inside its own rule's try, so an import error is that rule's rule.error and the quarantine condition can be met. The rule_error block's fix line names the restart with VSDD_FACTORY_HOOKS_QUARANTINE=<rule>, and the briefing's state-problems line and vsdd status list rules with repeated rule.error. Copying block codes into a blocked packet was not taken: the briefing line already reaches the person.

problem: Every gate checks that a story is recorded in the run it is given, but admission is recorded only in the admitting run. When a fast-route story ends awaiting_merge (D15: the first CI story, any dependency change) or a run dies mid-child, the resumed feature run either skips story-draft and has no units, or reruns gate plan --story, which 'changes nothing', so the child's gates refuse. proposed_resolution: The feature, wave, verify and maintain surveys return, and record in the new run, every story admitted to the open cycle that is neither delivered nor descoped. Re-admission records the story in the calling run. feature passes the survey units to runStories() when story-draft is done. problem: 1. A suite with no JUnit report at ingest gives a baseline with no failing-test identities, so the harness chore and the first bug fix see every inherited failure as new. 2. pipeline asks for the harness only when there is 'no suite'; state also asks when there is 'no JUnit report'. 3. Record whether identities were measured; when they were not, delivery of the harness chore re-measures them into the baseline, and that chore's own green gate requires only that the report is produced and its own tests pass. 2. where: rewrite/design/state.md 2.2 rule 6; 2.3 Push; 2.11 two machines and adoption; 2.9 State problems; rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 4.13, section 7, section 8 OPS-07
problem: Nothing fetches the state branch before the briefing or the survey. An existing second clone routes on stale state and redoes checkpointed work. Two machines can run the same wave at once, both build the same stories, and adoption lets one take over the other's open PR mid-delivery. Both reach conflicting closure-record pushes with no named repair.
proposed_resolution: The survey fetches and fast-forwards, or rebases, the state branch before preconditions, and the briefing reports when state is behind the remote. The survey writes and pushes a lease (scope, run, machine, time); another machine's survey refuses while it is fresh; checkpoints and deliveries refresh it and the checkpoint clears it. A push conflict opens blocked, reason environment, and status --fix retries the rebase.

outcome.what_was_done: Decision D33 settles the design, and the lease this finding proposed is not built. The fetch before a survey is the opening sync, without which no run starts (T-FRESH, package M1). What stops two machines running one wave is the work claim: a file on the state branch, made by a push the remote accepts from one clone only, with no expiry and no refresh (T-CLAIM and T-PUBLISH, package M2). A push that is not taken is judged by a fetch and ends as the sync's outcome, not as a blocked decision (T-PUSH, T-COMBINE). Nothing on the slice pushes or fetches, so S2b and S3 build nothing for it now.

where: rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.11.10 auto-allow core row; 2.11.1 shell.py; rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 5.4
problem: The built-in part of auto-allow requires a single segment, but the core prefix match of configured commands does not. A configured command followed by ;, &&, $(...), backticks, eval or sh -c with an opaque payload is approved without a prompt in the default permission mode, for exactly the commands the heuristic checks cannot read.
proposed_resolution: Approve a configured command only as one segment followed by plain argument tokens: no separators, substitutions, eval, sh -c, xargs or redirects. shell.py marks commands with substitutions as opaque, and auto-allow never permits an opaque command. Add cases.

problem: The route names 'feature with the oldest queued request', but nothing defines what next.args carries, and the feature survey can receive a request only as free text in --request-uri, which always writes a new request file. There are three readings and all fail. The request text duplicates the request and leaves the CR queued, so it is offered again after the release. 'CR-NNN' is stored as a new request whose text is the identifier. An empty args fails because request is required on a first run. Whether a request typed while another run holds the lock is recorded before the lock refusal is also unstated.
proposed_resolution: Define next for a queued request as {command: '/vsdd-factory:feature', args: {request: 'CR-NNN'}}. A request argument that is exactly a queued CR id is passed as --subject and activates that file instead of writing a new one. feature with no request and no amend takes the in-flight request, or else the oldest queued one. The survey writes a new request file before any lock check and returns 'queued' without taking the lock when a cycle is active. Apply this in pipeline 2.3, 2.4 and 2.9.4, state 2.5, 2.7 and 2.16, and blueprint 4.9, and add a fixture for a typed request that is queued and later activated once.

where: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.9.1 'Where a child's unit comes from', 2.9.4 story-draft and deliver rows, 2.9.5 readiness paragraph; rewrite/design/state.md 2.12 missing-commands bullets, 2.16 gate plan row, 2.8 cycle record (no base field); rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 3.4 row 4, 4.6

The fix story's worktree therefore lacks the test harness that the readiness chore later delivers, and it is never refreshed, because delivery rebases only on a conflict. When the route lists readiness stories, the fast route runs story-draft and deliver twice: first the readiness chores alone, then the change's own stories. plan schedule puts the test-harness chore in a first wave of its own, like the scaffold. where: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.9.8 coverage-and-baseline row before synthesize, 'What the baseline is for'; rewrite/design/state.md 2.8 baseline record, 2.12 'Missing commands are a state'; rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 4.12 missing commands, 4.13 baseline; rewrite/design/packaging.md E4 run (1)
problem: vsdd gate ingest measures the baseline (failing-test identities, lint, format) in a stage that runs before the architect writes toolchain.toml, and ingest is not among the workflows that refuse without commands. When init could not detect test, test_report or lint, the baseline lists nothing. After approval fills the commands, every inherited failure and lint finding counts as new and fails the gates of unrelated stories, and nothing measures again. An import gets a first-survey measurement, but an ingest does not. The E4 sample's custom JUnit runner is not in init's detection list, so E4 run (1) would fail its own assertion.
proposed_resolution: When gate ingest runs with test, test_report, lint or format_check unset, it records those measurements as 'not taken'. The first survey after the spec approval applies the toolchain and takes them, as for an import (as a job, see P3REQ-06). Readiness reads 'has a suite' from the taken measurement. Apply this in pipeline 2.9.8, state 2.8 and 2.12, and blueprint 4.13.

where: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 3.2 'Brownfield multi-repo' mapping, 2.9.11 synthesize row, 2.4 ingest route rows, 2.6 whole-set lock, 2.9.6/2.9.7 hub release; rewrite/design/state.md 2.8 closure row and baseline record (single _standing/units/ingest.json, decision spec), 2.5 toolchain row, 2.14, 2.16 survey row; rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 3.4 'Several repositories' row, 4.8, 4.13
problem: The design maps multi-repository brownfield to 'ingest with repo for each repository', but the second ingest fails at several points. Its done test reads the first ingest's closed ingest.json, so every stage reads as done. Its baseline would overwrite the first one's, and its decision would reuse the identifier spec in _standing. Once the first baseline is approved, the whole-set specification lock refuses its writes, because an ingest holds no amendment. The route never names it, since a baseline already exists. The gates compare against one baseline measured with one repository's commands, and toolchain.toml cannot fill per-repository commands. Which run opens the hub's single release decision is also unstated.
proposed_resolution: In a hub, ingest without repo covers every member in one run, storing one baseline object per repository in the ingest closure (each with its own integration head and measurements, read by the gates for stories with that repo). It writes toolchain.toml with a [[repo]] section per member, whose approval fills that entry's unset commands, and it ends at one spec decision. A member added later is ingested with repo in a run that holds an amendment. The route's ingest row becomes 'a member has no baseline'. In a hub, verify runs once at the hub and opens the one release decision. Apply this in pipeline 2.4, 2.9.8, 2.9.11 and 3.2, state 2.5, 2.8 and 2.14, and blueprint 3.4 and 4.13, and have E4 run (4) ingest two existing repositories.

where: rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 4.9 'Long commands', 7 fresh clone row; rewrite/design/pipeline.md amendment 4, 2.5 done test, 2.10.8 survey fields; rewrite/design/state.md 2.8 (survey re-measures; import baseline by first survey), 2.10 fresh clone row, 2.15 step 4, 2.16 survey row and job paragraph
problem: The survey re-measures every gate whose evidence is missing (on a fresh clone, every closed story's green gate and the plan baseline), and it takes an import's whole baseline: suite, lint, format, mutation per module and scanners. Yet it is not a long command. It has no job and no pending state, and it runs in one clerk Bash call capped at ten minutes, while already holding the lock it took before the done test. On any project with a slow suite, the retry meets its own lock or starts the measurement again from scratch.
proposed_resolution: Run the survey's measurements as the same keyed detached jobs the gate commands use. vsdd survey re-attaches like any long command and returns {ok, state: 'pending'} until they finish; the clerk already re-runs pending commands. problem:
Six facts the gates and the hook depend on are undefined:
1. How a JUnit test case maps to its file (the file attribute is optional).
2. Where the base commit's report comes from.
3. How green-by-design and wiring exemptions are marked.
4. What a stub marker is.
5. Assertion failure versus build error. A Python stub that raises NotImplementedError is a JUnit error, so the slice's sample story would fail the red gate twice.
6. How a criterion links to its tests for the demo table.
G2 and H5 would each invent answers, and the answers need not agree.
proposed_resolution:
Add a gate-inputs list to pipeline 2.9.1, mirrored in state.md 2.16, with the agent-side half in the failing-tests method:
1. Test identity is classname plus name. The file is the file attribute, else the classname mapped through the tests globs (init and doctor warn when neither exists).
2. The base report is measured once in a temporary detached worktree and cached as evidence keyed by the base sha.
3. A failure is <failure>, or an <error> of a constant list of not-implemented types; any other error fails the gate.
4. The stub marker is the fixed string VSDD-STUB.
5. A test is exempt when its name contains wiring or green_by_design.
6. Test names carry ac<N>, and the red record keeps the criterion-to-test map that gate demo uses.

outcome.what_was_done: The six gate inputs are defined: identity is classname::name; the base report is measured once per base commit in a temporary detached worktree and kept under local/evidence/_base; a red test is a <failure> or an <error> of a constant list of not-implemented types; exempt tests carry `wiring` or `green_by_design` and at least one new test must be red; a test's file is the file attribute or the classname mapped to a test file; the stub marker is VSDD-STUB; a test name carrying ac<N> covers AC-N and the red record keeps that map for gate demo.
outcome.where: commands/gate-red.md; commands/gate-green.md; commands/gate-demo.md; records/evidence.md; schemas/evidence-record.schema.json; agents/test-writer.md

problem:
A non-isolated workflow step starts every Bash call in the project root, so a builder commits with 'cd <worktree> && git commit' or 'git -C'. The payload's cwd is therefore the main checkout, which in local mode has the integration branch checked out.

Read literally, merge-guard ('while the integration branch is checked out') then blocks every builder commit. Liveness by 'cwd inside a worktree the run owns', the fallback for probe 28, never fires for steps.
proposed_resolution:
- Define the effective directory of a Bash call in hooks.md 2.5: the last cd target or git -C path, else cwd. Use it for ctx.story, merge-guard, auto-allow's worktree tests and liveness; liveness also uses target for file tools.
- Add two cases: 'cd <worktree> && git commit' with the main checkout on the integration branch is allowed; 'git commit' in the main checkout is blocked.

outcome.what_was_done: Ctx gains `where`, the effective directory of a call (the target's directory; for a Bash segment the directory of a cd, git -C or vsdd -C, else cwd), and `story`, `in_spike`, merge-guard, auto-allow and liveness use it. The two cases are stated: `cd <story worktree> && git commit` with the main checkout on the integration branch is allowed, and a bare `git commit` there is blocked.

A wrong frozen test therefore blocks with kind gate, and becomes a stuck decision after two runs.

where: rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.4 and packaging.md (differential test) vs state.md 2.4
problem: The reader is held to PyYAML, which implements YAML 1.1 (yes/no/on/off are booleans, 010 is octal, 12:30 is sexagesimal). The design never says which YAML semantics the subset must agree with, or that plain scalars YAML 1.1 would retype must be refused. The differential test only covers plugin-authored files (agents, skills, templates), never the agent-written artifacts that are the reader's real input. As designed, the test can pass while artifacts are misread.

outcome.what_was_done: The reader's semantics are pinned as built: refused, not misread. On every input it accepts it equals PyYAML's YAML 1.1 safe_load, and every plain scalar YAML 1.1 would retype is refused with the line number. The differential test is extended to artifact frontmatter in the fixture overlays and hook case files and to a corpus of inputs that must be refused; the first of these is added to the built test when those fixtures exist.

problem: The design says `encodeURIComponent` makes free text safe on a single-segment shell command. It does not: `'`, `(`, `)`, `*` and `!` stay raw, so a request containing an apostrophe, parentheses or an asterisk breaks or globs the clerk's command. Universal test 11 as specified (spaces, quotes, a semicolon) cannot detect this.

outcome.what_was_done: enc() is specified as built: encodeURIComponent plus the five characters it leaves raw (! ' ( ) *). Universal test 11 passes a request with both quotes, a semicolon, parentheses, an asterisk and an exclamation mark and requires that none appears raw.

where: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.7, 2.10.2; blueprint 4.10 (finding built from scenario scores)
problem:
The holdout finding's shape contradicts itself:

problem:
The table of platform behaviours the harness must copy omits several platform features:

- The `pipeline(items, ...stages)` signature, with stages receiving (prev, item, index).

It also states 'required within properties' where the platform rule is 'required ⊆ properties, required optional'. The builder implemented the omissions and the misreading.

where: rewrite/design/packaging.md 2.6, universal tests 4, 5 and 7; pipeline.md 2.11.1 step()

Tests 4 and 5 as specified therefore never reach a convergence loop, a spike or a child, so they cannot be the 'mechanical proof that convergence loops and spike limits terminate'. The test definitions must say that stubs echo the prompt's step identity and that the survey stub passes. P3BLD-19 covers only the survey half, for test 7.

outcome.what_was_done: Universal tests 4, 5 and 7 now say that every stub returns as `step` the identity its prompt gave it and that the survey stub passes with the units the test supplies, which is what the built tests do; test 4 also asserts that the loops ran.

where: rewrite/design/pipeline.md 2.10.8 (Close) and 2.5 (the checkpoint output is the workflow's return value)
problem: The checkpoint's output fields are listed without types, although the same object is returned as the workflow result, where `progress` is boolean and `decisions` are objects. The design should state that S_CLOSE is the workflow-result schema plus `ok`. Otherwise a builder chooses string types, as happened here, and the drive loop's `progress: false` test breaks.

outcome.what_was_done: The checkpoint output is typed: ok and error, plus status, progress, decisions and next exactly as the workflow-result schema types them, all required. The built S_CLOSE has the same types; its required list (ok, status, next) grows to all six when the literals are generated from the schema files.

where: rewrite/design/hooks.md section 2.2, launch.sh skeleton line here="${0%/*}"
problem: When launch.sh is invoked without a slash in $0 (e.g. 'sh launch.sh' run from inside py/), ${0%/*} yields 'launch.sh' with no directory, so sourcing find-root.sh fails. The real hook command always uses an absolute plugin path, but a bare-name invocation would break the launcher.
what_was_built: Implemented with a POSIX case guard: case "$0" in */*) here="${0%/*}" ;; *) here=. ;; esac. Proved with a bare-filename invocation of launch.sh beside its sources (gate exit 0).

outcome.what_was_done: Verified as built: launch.sh's POSIX case guard (case "$0" in */*) here="${0%/*}";; *) here=. ;; esac) survives a bare-name invocation; the launcher suites pass under sh, bash and dash.

problem: 'Stop at the user's home directory or the filesystem root' is ambiguous about whether $HOME and / are themselves examined as candidate project roots; the stated rationale ('a stray file there can never turn every project into a factory project') only holds if they are not.
what_was_built: Implemented the walk exclusively: $HOME and / terminate the walk before their .factory is tested. Consequence: a project rooted directly at $HOME is never detected; matches the stated intent and decision D24.

outcome.what_was_done: The exclusive walk (HOME and / terminate it before their own .factory is tested) is what the runner's resolver uses, via find_project_root; the runner in addition refuses a VSDD_FACTORY_ROOT whose real path is the real home or /, and the guard never tests the home directory.

where: packaging.md section 2.3, canonical check command 'cd next && uv run python tools/check.py'
problem: The first run syncs pytest/ruff/pyyaml from PyPI; in this sandbox (and per the spike, in assistant shells generally) PyPI is unreachable (TLS UnknownIssuer), so the canonical command fails before check.py starts even though check.py itself is standard-library only.
what_was_built: Verified 'uv run --project next --no-sync python tools/check.py' passes fully offline. Recommend documenting the --no-sync variant for disconnected environments and committing a generated uv.lock from a connected machine (B7/CI).

where: rewrite/design/packaging.md section 2.4 omitted-fields list (privacyPolicyUrl) vs claude plugin validate
problem: 'claude plugin validate' emits PRIVACY_URL_MISSING (a warning, verdict still passes) because the plugin declares remote MCP servers but no privacy policy URL. The design deliberately omits the field, so the warning is inherent to the manifest as specified.
what_was_built: Left the manifest per the design and recorded the warning. A later package (D3 or a maintainer) can add privacyPolicyUrl once a human supplies the organisational URL; any MIT-project GitHub URL would also satisfy it.

problem: hooks.md defines the reader to accept one level of nested mapping, while state.md's flat artifact frontmatter forbids nested maps and caps line length; the two constraints are stated against different artifacts and a builder could read either as the reader's contract.
what_was_built: Built the reader to the hooks.md superset (it is the owning design) and left flatness and the 200-character line cap to the artifacts registry (C2); both module docstrings state the subset relation.

outcome.what_was_done: No action at this depth: the frontmatter reader under next/ already implements the hooks.md superset with both module docstrings stating the subset relation, and tests/unit holds its tests. Nothing in the runner overrides it.

where: rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.4 scalar enumeration vs rewrite/design/state.md 2.4 value list
problem: state.md lists a date among flat frontmatter values but hooks.md's scalar list (string, integer, boolean, null) omits it.
what_was_built: The reader parses bare YYYY-MM-DD scalars to datetime.date (YAML-consistent, stdlib), documented in the module docstring; the differential PyYAML test compares parsed objects so dates agree.

outcome.what_was_done: No action at this depth: the reader's date scalar handling is in next/ from layer 2, documented in its docstring, with the differential test in tests/unit.

problem: It says scripts hold the schemas 'composed without $ref, because the platform only promises a root object with properties', while the single-source schema files themselves use $ref between files.
what_was_built: Kept $ref in the shipped files (blueprint 4.14: the files are the single source); vsdd.schema resolves refs through a file-name registry, and the B4a build inlines them when it generates the prelude literals.

outcome.what_was_done: Closed with evidence: the built prelude carries no $ref (grep over prelude.js: 0) because the build's _strip_schema_node inlines each sibling ref when it generates the literal, and topics/result-schemas.md now says exactly that — the files compose with refs, the literals never carry one. The apparent contradiction the finding named is dissolved in the sentence the topic already had.

problem: The probe asserted py/ carries no vsdd package ('that arrives with B3') and unconditionally mkdir'd one, so B3's arrival raised FileExistsError and broke the hooks lint tier.
what_was_built: Updated build_probe_case to import the real shipped py/vsdd package when present and keep the minimal stand-in only for the pre-B3 case; the probe now proves the real package imports under PYTHONSAFEPATH.

outcome.what_was_done: Verified as closed by B3's arrival: the sibling-import probe imports the real shipped py/vsdd package when present and keeps the minimal stand-in only for the pre-B3 case; the suite passes, so the hooks lint tier no longer trips on the package's existence.

problem: 'Commands are cut to 200 characters and passed through a redactor' is ambiguous about order; cutting first would leave secret material in the 200-char prefix.
what_was_built: Implemented redact-then-cut in events.py (no secret material survives, then the budget applies) and pinned the order in a test.

outcome.what_was_done: No action at this depth: redact-then-cut order is implemented in events.py with its pinning test in tests/unit, unchanged by this unit.

problem: The skeleton's step() consults an undeclared `budget.total` / `budget.remaining()`; no `budget` object, survey key, or blueprint-4.12 limit key defines a token budget
what_was_built: Modelled it as RUN.tokens_left + TOKEN_FLOOR, filled from an optional survey `config.tokens_left`; the unknown-limit-key test still enforces the key table. The design should add tokens_left to 4.12 or drop the token-budget clause

outcome.what_was_done: tokens_left as a survey limit key: the slice step() consults the platform budget object, so no key is needed on the story path this unit builds; the limits-table owner (S1 prose pass with W1) still decides whether the key joins the table.

problem: Test 3 (every agentType exists in <plugin>/agents/) and test 6 (the method file exists and the agent owns it) cannot pass before A1 builds the agent and method files, but B5 ships the tests
what_was_built: Test 3 checks each observed agentType against the generated ROLE table (roster), switching to file existence once agents/ is populated; test 6 asserts the Method-prefix always and defers file ownership. Should be stated in packaging.md 2.6 or B5's dependency row

outcome.what_was_done: Test 3's spec text now states the interim rule the built test implements: every agentType is a roster agent via the generated ROLE table until <plugin>/agents/ is populated, after which file existence is checked.

problem: Grammar ^([a-z_]+)= cannot parse decision keys containing hyphens (e.g. the blocked choice `open-spike name=...`) that section 2.6 of the same design documents
what_was_built: Implemented ^([a-z_-]+)= — a superset: every documented input parses identically and hyphenated keys resolve. Amend the design or restrict the key table

outcome.what_was_done: No drift remains: the amended topic states the names-gated grammar (a key=value word counts only for the workflow's own argument names), which the built ^([a-z_-]+)= implements exactly; every documented input, hyphenated keys included, parses identically, and universal test 12 pins both argument forms.

where: rewrite/design/packaging.md 2.5, marker guard (no file outside <plugin>/workflows/ contains a marker)
problem: Taken literally, the guard fires on tools/build.py and tools/check.py themselves, which must quote the marker strings to define and check them
what_was_built: Guard scans plugin, workflow-lib and tools, skipping the .py tool sources; noted as an interpretation for the amend step

outcome.what_was_done: The marker-guard sentence in build-step.md now names the exact scan scope the build enforces (the toy workflows' stamped regions, and the build's own sources and tests quoting the markers), replacing the unguarded 'no file outside <plugin>/workflows/'.

problem: The command is fixed literally as `uv run python tools/junit_runner.py`. `uv run` discovers ancestor pyprojects, so run in place (or inside any monorepo) it picks up next/pyproject.toml and tries to sync its dev dependencies from PyPI - observed failing with a TLS/network error (exit 2).
what_was_built: Used `uv run --no-project python ...` for all three commands in factory.toml and README.md. Identical behaviour in the fresh copy (the e2e deployment), immune to ancestor discovery, and no network ever needed; proven both in place and in the fresh repo.

where: rewrite/design/state.md 2.12 and 2.15 vs packaging.md 2.6 and the unit task
problem: state.md says factory.toml 'exists if and only if the project is initialised' and is created by vsdd init, while the unit requires shipping it filled in inside the sample. Committed naively, a fresh copy would look initialised with a broken .factory mount.
what_was_built: Shipped .factory/factory.toml in the sample and added .factory/ and .worktrees/ to the sample's .gitignore (the two exclusion lines init writes), so the product commit stays clean; make_sample_repo.sh -n drops .factory entirely for uninitialised scenarios.

outcome.what_was_done: init refuses a plain .factory/ holding a factory.toml: detect reports partial and init exits 1 with state 'partial' and next naming /vsdd-factory:status --fix (the S3R-6 correction), converting nothing. Moving the sample's file into the overlay stays with E1.

problem: The XML envelope is unspecified: bare <testsuite> root (Ant-style) or <testsuites> wrapper (pytest-style) both parse differently.
what_was_built: Wrote the pytest-style <testsuites><testsuite .../> wrapper; per-test identity is classname.dotted.module.Class + name, recoverable as the stable id gates freeze. Later gate packages should parse the wrapper form.

where: rewrite/design/packaging.md 2.6 (sample project) - fresh-copy script and path classes
problem: No design text names the fresh-copy script or says where project-local tool scripts fall in the seven path classes; tools/** would be classified by no glob.
what_was_built: Placed the script at next/tests/e2e/make_sample_repo.sh (POSIX sh, optional DEST target, -n/--no-factory, deterministic local git identity, asserts exactly one commit); in the sample's [paths], put tools/** under source.

outcome.what_was_done: Nothing owed to the classes table: the seven product classes are configured per project (classes.toml carries only their from_config keys and precedence), and layer 1 already put tools/** under source in the sample's factory.toml beside the fresh-copy script tests/e2e/make_sample_repo.sh. What remains is design text: packaging/sample-project.md (E1's file) does not yet name the script.
outcome.where: next/tests/e2e/make_sample_repo.sh, next/tests/e2e/sample-project/.factory/factory.toml [paths]; the design-text naming is taken by E1

where: rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.9 (table row 'uv cannot run') vs the proposed fix in U1-R3/U1-R4
problem: The proposed discriminator (`uv python find --no-python-downloads '>=3.11'`) inherits the session's UV_CACHE_DIR, so when the cache itself is broken the probe also fails and a perfectly healthy interpreter is misreported as 'no Python' — the exact conflation the finding was about. Found by running the real uv against a read-only cache while implementing R3.
what_was_built: The probe in launch.sh's interpreter_ok runs with its own writable UV_CACHE_DIR (${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/vsdd-factory/probe-cache), so 'is a Python at the floor installed?' is answered independently of 'is uv's cache usable?'. Documented in the launcher comment; guarded by a real-uv TestReadOnlyCache test asserting the uv_unusable message (not py_floor) with a read-only cache.

outcome.what_was_done: Verified as built: interpreter_ok's probe runs with its own writable UV_CACHE_DIR under the user's cache, so a broken uv cache cannot be misreported as a missing Python; the read-only-cache test asserts the uv_unusable message.

where: rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.2 illustrative skeleton (the rc case) vs U1-R5's expectation table
problem: The skeleton's `case 0) exit 0;; 10) exit 2;; *) fail ...` is mode-uniform, so a brief-mode launch failure with rc=10 exits 2 and rc=1 exits 0 with the down briefing — while a reader of R5 ('assert exit code and stderr for 0,1,2,10,13,137 in each of gate, brief and notify') might expect 2 for every failure in every mode. The two readings differ for brief/notify.
what_was_built: Kept the design's uniform mapping (0->0, 10->2, other codes through fail(), whose brief/notify arms absorb the failure with exit 0 and the down briefing) and encoded exactly that in the test matrix with a comment citing the skeleton; no launcher change was needed.

outcome.what_was_done: Verified as built: the uniform exit mapping (0->0, 10->2, other codes through fail()'s brief/notify arms) is what launch.sh does and what the test matrix asserts, with the mapping comment citing the design skeleton.

problem: The check can only answer 'would this file vanish on a fresh clone' where git itself runs; on a scratch copy outside a repository (how review-style negative tests tend to run) git check-ignore has nothing to consult.
what_was_built: The check returns early (passes) when `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` fails, with a comment; in a real checkout it enumerates every file under plugins/vsdd-factory/ and fails listing any ignored paths.

problem: The documents contradict each other on holdout findings: blueprint 4.10 exempts category 'holdout' from BOTH the location and grounding conditions; pipeline.md 2.11.1's judge() exempts only the location condition (its 'hard' still requires spec_ref || repro).
what_was_built: Followed blueprint 4.10 (authority per the task brief): the prelude's judge() keeps the exemption from both conditions, matching the pre-existing code and the walled-finding rationale; the test-10 fixture carries spec_ref so it is meaningful under either reading.

outcome.what_was_done: The contradiction is settled by the amendment, which the built judge() now follows: grounded === false makes a finding not hard (f.grounded !== false in the hard test), and holdout keeps its blueprint-4.10 exemption from the location and grounding conditions. Universal test 14 fails without the grounded test (a critical ungrounded finding must land in advisory).

where: rewrite/design/packaging.md 2.5 (400-line prelude cap) vs required additions from U3-R16 and U3-R20 (S_CLOSE composition, S_WAVE_GATE)
problem: The cap predates those required schemas; the prelude stood at 445 non-generated lines with every mandated composite present, and deleting design-mandated content was not an option.
what_was_built: Compacted composites and doc comments, and fixed the measuring tool: check.py's _strip_region left 5 phantom blank lines at the splice seams which the cap counted. After a fair seam-trim and compaction the prelude is at or under 400 real lines with all mandated content.

outcome.what_was_done: The cap is now checked against the fair measure (generated sub-blocks excluded) and the delivered schemas moved out of the hand-written region, so the prelude sits well under 400 real lines with every mandated function; the platform-constraints check passes.

problem: Annotated '-> bool' but returned None.
what_was_built: Corrected the annotation to -> None.

problem: relay() prefixes 'vsdd -C <dir>', so no prompt contains the contiguous substring 'vsdd checkpoint'; the pre-existing test 7 passed only because its survey stub returned an empty project_dir.
what_was_built: New assertions match 'checkpoint' rather than 'vsdd checkpoint', correct whichever project_dir a stub supplies.

outcome.what_was_done: Verified as built: the relay assertions match 'checkpoint' rather than 'vsdd checkpoint', correct for any project_dir a stub supplies; the node suite passes including test 7 and the close-relay tests.

problem: The specified `root=$(CDPATH= cd -- ...)` fails shellcheck with SC1007, and L-SH requires shellcheck to pass, so the design's own snippet violates its own lint. `CDPATH='' cd` passes. L-SH also names only launch.sh and bin/vsdd; find-root.sh is shipped shell too and should be covered.

outcome.what_was_done: cli-entry.md's bin/vsdd snippet now reads root=$(CDPATH='' cd -- ...) which passes shellcheck's SC1007, and the L-SH row of tables/lint-checks.toml covers every shipped shell source: py/launch.sh, py/find-root.sh and bin/vsdd. The built check.py shell_lint already checks all three, so the table now states what runs.

where: rewrite/design/packaging.md sections 2.3 and 2.12 (B0 skeleton, B1 'empty component folders') and BLUEPRINT.md 9.1
problem: Git cannot track empty directories, so the skeleton and component folders vanish on commit, and a layout check over them fails on any fresh checkout. The design should specify a placeholder such as .gitkeep, or make layout lint check only populated directories.

where: rewrite/design/packaging.md section 2.3 (the check command `cd next && uv run python tools/check.py`) and STATE.md's note that PyPI fails in the sandbox
problem: The first run syncs from PyPI. In the assistant sandbox, plain uv fails with UnknownIssuer, but `--system-certs` (UV_SYSTEM_CERTS=1) works: uv.lock was generated and the dependencies installed. The design should state the working form for assistant shells, so builders do not defer uv.lock or work around a check command that fails.

where: rewrite/design/hooks.md section 2.8 step 3 and the inline guard in section 2.3
problem: Both assume an absolute `gitdir:` path. git 2.48 and later can write relative worktree paths (worktree.useRelativePaths). Both also compare against $HOME as a raw string, which a trailing slash or a symlinked spelling defeats. The design should say that relative gitdirs are resolved against the worktree, and that HOME is normalised.

outcome.what_was_done: The guard normalises HOME (trailing slash stripped) and starts its walk only at an absolute path, matching vsdd.project's relative-gitdir handling; a state rooted at home adopts nothing. Stated in topics/hook-wiring.md and topics/caller-identity.md remain the owners of the gitdir rule; the guard's part is tested.

problem: Section 2.2 says hook.py exits 13 below the Python floor, but no row of the failure table maps launcher rc 13 to a message. The generic 'could not run (exit N)' row has no fix, although 2.2 says every message carries one. Also, the skeleton's fail() sends any mode other than gate or brief to exit 0, so an unknown or mistyped mode turns failures silent. The design should require unknown modes to fail closed.

outcome.what_was_done: Verified as built: an unknown hook mode fails closed with exit 2 and a message (TestUnknownMode), and the failure table's missing rc-13 row is covered by the launcher's explicit 13 case (defence in depth for hook.py's floor check).

where: rewrite/design/packaging.md section 2.4 (network.hosts and its hosts table)
problem: `*.githubusercontent.com` is justified only by uv downloading a Python interpreter. Blueprint 4.1 and the launcher's `--no-python-downloads` forbid that, so the entry has no stated reason. Separately, Playwright's browser-binary download hosts are not considered, should @playwright/mcp need to install a browser.

where: rewrite/design/packaging.md section 2.11 (the rewrite-mode CLAUDE.md: 'work only under next/; everything else is the system being replaced, to be read and not edited')
problem: rewrite/ is not the system being replaced. STATE.md says rewrite/STATE.md is updated at every step and that slice findings go to rewrite/design/slice-findings.md. The specified text forbids that to every agent that loads it, and should carve out rewrite/ for the orchestrating session.

where: rewrite/design/packaging.md section 2.4 and BLUEPRINT.md 5.4 ('the bundled browser server's entry carries the option that refuses file: addresses, and lint checks it')
problem: The builder's finding is confirmed against the @playwright/mcp 0.0.86 README. There is no option that refuses file: addresses: refusal is the default, and the only documented option, --allow-unrestricted-file-access, loosens it. The README also says this restriction is 'not a secure boundary', and the environment variable PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_ALLOW_UNRESTRICTED_FILE_ACCESS loosens it from the environment as well. L-MCP should be restated as: no loosening flag in args, no loosening variable in env. The wall rests on the hook check of 2.11.2.

`claude plugin validate` raises PRIVACY_URL_MISSING because the plugin bundles remote MCP servers. The validator says a 'Privacy' link in the README also satisfies it, so no organisational URL is needed. A README link to a privacy statement in the repository would clear the directory-profile warning while keeping the field omitted.

4.10 says gate output is 'either the gate result, or {ok, state: "pending"}'. pipeline.md's gate-result schema requires gate, subject, passed, sha, evidence and failures, yet also lists state 'pending'. 2.10.8 adds a 'retry' field that is not among the gate-result properties. The design does not say whether this is one schema with a union, which the stdlib checker cannot express, or two schemas.

outcome.what_was_done: Settled as two schemas, as the registry already names them: gate-result.schema.json is the ordinary gate result, pending-output.schema.json (renamed from the built gate-output, dropping the anyOf union) is the pending branch alone with ok, state and retry required by the relay rule. No script needed the union.

problem: hooks.md 2.6 says an unknown key or a bad value under [hooks] makes only that rule fall back to its defaults. hooks.md 2.9 says an invalid configuration means built-in defaults overall, and state.md 2.12 says unknown keys and wrong types are errors. The designs do not say whether a [hooks] fault invalidates the whole file or only the rule, or which module (config.py or H1) owns the per-rule check.

outcome.what_was_done: config.py owns the per-rule check (already built by the layer-2 catch-up): a fault in one rule's table resets that rule to its defaults, any other fault resets the whole file to defaults. The runner announces both: a faulting rule's rule_config falls back, hook_problems reach the SessionStart notice as config.invalid, and a failing strength is never a relaxation.
outcome.where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/hooks/model.py (rule_config), main.py (_notices); tests: next/tests/hooks/test_runner.py::test_applies_and_strength (faulty table resets that rule only), next/tests/hooks/test_ctx.py covers project.config_error

problem: 2.8 gives exact discovery rules for the shell: stop at $HOME and '/', follow a linked worktree's .git file to the main checkout, no symlink resolution. 2.5's per-path Python resolution says only 'walking up to the nearest state directory, falls back to the session's project'. Leaving the Python rules unstated invites the divergence in U2-R8. The Python resolver should be specified as the same algorithm.

outcome.what_was_done: The runner's per-path Python resolution calls vsdd.project.find_project_root with the caller's HOME — the same algorithm find-root.sh runs — and both resolvers already share tests/root_cases.py. New: the context resolution is asserted against the shared table, with the session project as the fallback.

where: rewrite/design/state.md 2.12 ([caps]) vs the build plan (B3, C2)
problem: 'Raise a cap to at most twice its default' needs the cap names and defaults, which live in artifacts.toml (C2). config.py (B3) validates [caps] and cannot know them, and no package is told to enforce the bound.

outcome.what_was_done: The validated raised cap is the cap: check_text reads [caps] and applies a project's raised value for the kind, and a file matched by caps.waived skips the size check altogether. test_raised_cap_applies_and_waived_skips covers raised-applies, waived-skips and the default cap firing.

where: rewrite/design/hooks.md 2.12 event example vs its field lists
problem: The example rule.block line carries 'story', but neither the required field list nor the type table's extra fields for rule.block name 'story'. A schema that the writer validates against must either list it or allow additional properties, and the design does not say which.

outcome.what_was_done: story and cwd are properties of the shipped event schema and the runner sends them on its rule events when known; the design's example rule.block line is the schema fixture, so the example, the schema and the writer agree.

problem: gated() renames the second attempt to `<name>-retryN`, and step() looks up OVERRIDE by `${wf}/${o.stage || name}`. In the design's own skeleton, a retried `ingest/map` or `ingest/analyze` therefore runs on the planner tier, which contradicts D5 and blueprint 4.2.

outcome.what_was_done: gated() keeps `stage: o.stage || name` on every attempt, and the pin is now behavioural: a universal test runs a gated step in workflow 'ingest' whose gate fails once; both attempts run on the OVERRIDE's builder tier (model sonnet), which only the stage passthrough explains — without it the retry resolves 'ingest/map-retry1' and falls back to the planner tier (fable). The former outcome cited a test that reads only the OVERRIDE table, which passes with the passthrough removed.
outcome.where: next/workflow-lib/prelude.js gated(); next/tests/workflows/universal.test.mjs 'a retried gated step keeps its stage and its override tier'

where: rewrite/design/packaging.md 2.5, the --check list ('no file outside <plugin>/workflows/ contains a marker')
problem: The rule cannot hold as written. outcome.what_was_done: Same closure as SL1-25: the guard's allowed files are named in the spec and implemented in build.py's allowed set (toys, harness, universal test, lint tests, tools), so --check holds as written against those files.

problem: Reviewer files must carry 'the finding key rule' byte for byte, but no single source file for it is named; severity.md holds only the table. packaging.md 2.5 says spike-runner and clerk take 'the variants the source file defines', while agents-skills.md 2.7 says spike-runner omits one bullet and the clerk carries a two-line block of its own. where: rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md 9.1, the B5 row; packaging.md 2.6, universal tests 3 and 6
problem: The builder's design finding 2 is confirmed. Tests 3 (every agentType exists in <plugin>/agents/) and 6 (the method file exists and the agent owns it) cannot pass until A1, yet B5 depends only on B4a and no interim rule is stated. The interim check should be exact roster membership read from roster.toml; the builder's interim regex accepts non-agents (U3-R14).
