problem: `safe()` is the design's guard for identifiers on command lines, but its regex admits a leading '-'. A typed identifier can therefore become an option of the vsdd command.

outcome.what_was_done: The spec's safe() literal admitted a leading dash; the built guard (first character alnum) does not. topics/prelude.md now carries the built regex, so a typed identifier can never become a vsdd option.

where: topics/worktrees.md (The base of a story branch); topics/evidence-lookup.md; commands/story-deliver.md (What it refuses, verdict binding); commands/gate-green.md; records/evidence.md
problem: Caused by P3SEAM-03 and P3OPS-02. Every measure now uses the fixed recorded base; patch_id is the diff from that base; delivery and green require a red record on a commit between the base and the head. story-deliver still rebases in pr mode and claims the patch id survives a clean rebase. After a rebase the red record's commit is not an ancestor of the head, so delivery refuses and green fails 'no red record'. The diff also includes stories merged meanwhile, so the patch id changes and every rebase goes review_stale.
proposed_resolution: On a rebase, delivery re-records delivery.base as the commit it rebased onto. The red lookup also accepts the latest red or re-freeze record whose frozen files' SHA-256 match the head and whose patch id equals the head's diff from the new base. State this once in worktrees.md and evidence-lookup.md. Add a G4a fixture: pr mode, integration moved, clean rebase, merged with no re-review.

outcome.what_was_done: Not at slice depth: the red lookup after a rebase stays G4a's (delivery re-records delivery.base) with S2a's lookup change. The pieces the fix needs are in place: gatelib's cached record is read by exact head, evidence() looks up red by ancestry between base and head, and patch_id(tree, base, head) is computed per record.
outcome.where: packages G4a and S2a (the rebase fixture and the lookup)

problem: delivery-data.schema.json, rewritten in this pass, says ok is 'False when the story was not merged and no person is being waited for', so ok is false for ci_failed, conflict and review_stale. story.js tests !d.ok first and returns blocked, so the delivery repair loop never runs.
proposed_resolution: Define ok as 'the command ran and reached a state': false only for refused, checkout_dirty and a command that could not run. List the ok value of each state in story-deliver.md.

outcome.what_was_done: delivery-data's ok is defined as 'the command ran and reached a state': false only for refused, checkout_dirty and a command failure; merged, awaiting_merge, ci_failed, conflict and review_stale are ok, so the delivery repair loop runs. story-deliver.md lists the ok value of every state; story.js's !d.ok first test now behaves as designed.

where: topics/verdicts.md (Items to account for); topics/story-script.md (review(round + 1, d.reviewed_sha, 2, d.changed_files, 0)); schemas/delivery-data.schema.json
problem: Caused by P3BLD-01. In a later review loop, verdicts.md takes the items to account for as the files changed from the converged commit to the reviewed head. story.js passes d.changed_files, which delivery computed before the repair commits, and delivery-data never defines changed_files. After a ci_failed or conflict repair the tool's list holds files the reviewers were not asked about, so the tool's verdict is not converged while the script's is, and delivery refuses.
proposed_resolution: Define changed_files as the files changed from reviewed_sha to the delivered head. After a repair, take the list from the gate green --since result (add changed_files to it). Use the same definition in the tool. Add a conformance fixture in which a repair touches a new file.

outcome.what_was_done: The one definition of 'the files changed': vsdd.state.verdicts.changed_files(project, since, head) with --no-renames, sorted, None when git cannot say; a later loop's items are changed(previous verdict head, its own first pass's head), and a loop whose items cannot be computed has no ok pass. Conformance case r06-repair-new-file; unit test test_changed_files_and_later_loop_items; test_items_equal_unit_acs holds the items to story_unit's ACs. The gate --since result is G2's and the script half is W2's, both taking this function.

problem: The open ledger entries that guide the F builders still describe the design as it was before the corrections. D31-4, left for F3, says 'a story that removes a feature flag always opens a merge decision' and that the spec row gains only flags=home-built, 'only accepted when ... source = home-built'. Both contradict the corrected design: F-APPROVE now requires flags=<source> for every source and accepts flags=decline -- <words> for an existing system; the removal question is no longer a wait at story deliver; and the question is asked only while flags.removal = human, before any story exists. The merge row itself (opened when a delivered story waits; approve performs the merge; reject closes the pull request and descopes the story) does not fit a decision opened by the maintain checkpoint with no story or pull request, with the id merge.flag-<stem> and a reject that needs until=<date>. D31-8 points F2 at F-ITEMS in tables/flag-checks.toml, but the check now lives in tables/flag-story-checks.toml and has four items that come back in later loops. D31-2 says the survey fills [flags] keys, but it now writes only [flags.approved]. An F3 builder following D31-4 would put back the always-wait that D31R-F-4 and D31R-D-21 removed.
proposed_resolution: Rewrite the problem and proposed-resolution text of D31-4, D31-8 and D31-2, or add triage notes that apply after triage/d31.json. D31-4, spec row: approve [variant] [topology] [flags=<source> | flags=decline -- <words>], required when the decision would accept the flag decision record. D31-4, merge row: opened by the maintain checkpoint before a cleanup story is written, only while flags.removal = human; id merge.flag-<stem>; approve lets the next maintain run write the cleanup story; reject needs until=<yyyy-mm-dd>; nothing waits at story deliver. D31-8: F-ITEMS is in tables/flag-story-checks.toml, with the items flag-off, flag-removed, flag-system and not-a-flag. D31-2: the survey writes [flags.approved].

outcome.what_was_done: Every open D31-<n> entry was read against the design as it stands and six were rewritten in sources/extra-d31.json, with their outcome texts in outcomes/d31.json and their notes and file lists in triage/d31.json. D31-4: the spec row takes flags=<source> for every source, or flags=decline -- <words>; the merge row gains the decision merge.flag-<stem> that the maintain checkpoint opens before a cleanup story is written, only while flags.removal = human, with approve letting the next maintain run write the story and reject needing until; nothing waits at story deliver. D31-8: F-ITEMS is in flag-story-checks.toml with four items; only checked counts; two come back in a later loop; not-a-flag is known only from the green evidence. D31-2: the survey writes [flags.approved] only. D31-1: four story keys, the stem cell, the lock value removed and the 12,000-byte toolchain cap. D31-3: two tables of factory.toml, with set_by deciding which accepts a key, and the four keys that may be empty. D31-6: points at the encoded form of a key. D31-5 already matched the design. D31-7 is closed and was left as it is.

problem: F-ON reruns the whole suite with the story's flag on and refuses any new failure against the baseline. It leaves out only tests whose names carry that flag's off or default token. A feature behind a flag usually replaces behaviour that existing tests assert; this is the case D31 says matters most, features added to existing code. With the flag on, those existing tests fail, they carry no token, and the baseline lists them as passing, so F-ON refuses the story. No duty tells the test-writer to put those tests in the off state, the implementer may not edit tests, and the only way out written in the design is flag_exempt, which drops the flag.
proposed_resolution: Add to the test-writer's duty for a story behind a flag: each existing test that asserts behaviour the on state replaces is moved to the off state. It sets the flag off through the test double and is renamed with the flag_off_<k> token and the flag-off criterion, so F-ON leaves it out and the removal story deletes it. Have F-ON's refusal name each failing existing test, so the repair goes to the tests stage. Add to the adversary's flag-off item that every test moved to off asserted only replaced behaviour.

outcome.what_was_done: Decided: the test-writer moves an existing test that the on state breaks, by renaming it; nobody edits or drops one. The move carries one of two tokens. flag_old_<k>: a criterion of a story behind the flag replaces everything the test asserts; the test is deleted when the flag is removed. flag_pending_<k>: the test asserts behaviour the product must keep that the flag's stories do not provide yet, which is the half-finished case of clause 2b. When: in the tests stage where the criteria show the need; otherwise after the green gate's run with the flag on (F-ON) names the test, through the existing test-defects step: the implementer changes code only where the code is at fault, else returns blocked with the test under test_defects, and the test-writer moves it and re-freezes. No stage, step or prompt is added. What checks the move. Programs: F-STATES holds a moved test to passing with no flag set and to naming the flag-off criterion, and refuses more missing base tests than new moved tests, so an existing test leaves the suite only by a move; F-ON leaves moved tests out of the on run, refuses a moved test that passes with the flag on (it is given its name back), names every other failing test and says whether the base held it, and refuses a turn-on story while a pending test remains; F-DEFINITION refuses a removal that leaves a test named for the off state. Reviewer: the adversary's item flag-off, which only checked satisfies, now covers each moved test (an existing test, assertions unchanged, old only where a criterion replaces it, no other existing test deleted, renamed or weakened); the item is also added to a turn-on story and comes back in a later loop that touches tests. The pull request body lists the moved tests by name. Walked through red, green and review for a feature added to existing code, for a feature built over several stories, for turning on and for removal. Not changed, and outside this finding: vsdd env start turns every live temporary flag on for wave and release evaluation, which includes a flag whose feature is unfinished.
outcome.where: rewrite/spec/tables/flag-story-checks.toml (F-STATES, F-ON, F-DEFINITION, F-ITEMS), rewrite/spec/tables/flag-duties.toml (test-writer, implementer, adversary), rewrite/spec/topics/flag-lifecycle.md, rewrite/spec/topics/feature-flags.md, rewrite/spec/workflows/story.md (D31 passage), rewrite/spec/registry.d/d31.toml (F2, F4)

where: rewrite/spec/tables/flag-checks.toml (header rule 'Cannot measure is a failure')
problem: The header rule says that while flags are on a check fails when a key it reads is empty, and never passes by default. The corrections added keys whose empty value is a valid choice that the rows treat as a report, not a failure. key_env is empty for a source with no secret key. key_patterns empty gives 'key shape not measured' (F-KEY). definition_patterns empty means one file per flag (F-DEFINITION). definitions_check empty gives 'definitions not validated'. F-CHOICE does not require any of the four. A builder who follows the header fails every green gate of a project with no key, or with no definitions command.
proposed_resolution: Narrow the header rule to the keys F-CHOICE requires, plus patterns that do not compile and scans that time out. State that key_env, key_patterns, definition_patterns and definitions_check may be empty, and that the row's unmeasured cell gives what the gate then reports.

outcome.what_was_done: The header rule now fails a check only for an empty key that F-CHOICE requires, a pattern that does not compile, or a scan stopped at its time limit. A second rule names the four keys that may be empty (key_env, key_patterns, definition_patterns, definitions_check) and says the check then does what its row says and prints the report its unmeasured cell names. Each of the four has a report: 'no key variable named' was added to F-KEY for an empty key_env; 'key shape not measured', 'definition value not measured' and 'definitions not validated' were already there. The adversary's check of the architect in review-specs now also compares each key the table leaves empty with the record's heading 'Definitions and keys', so an empty key is a reviewed choice.

problem: F5's delivers text includes F-CHOICE as advisory findings in the spec coherence check of vsdd gate sweep, but F5 depends only on F1 and G5. gate-sweep is built by G7, so F5's generated brief does not name the package it extends. This is the same class of problem D31R-F-14 fixed for F4.

problem: The state token is flag_on_<k>, flag_off_<k> or flag_default_<k>, with no letter or digit directly before or after it. Test names go on after the token with an underscore, so for the tidy keys checkout and checkout-v2 (encoded checkout_v2), the token flag_off_checkout also matches inside test_ac2_flag_off_checkout_v2_keeps_old_page. F-ON for checkout then leaves out checkout-v2's off and default tests, and F-STATES for a checkout story counts such a test as its own. F-RECORD refuses only keys whose encoded forms are equal, so the prefix collision that D31R-D-12 and D31R-D-17 closed for definitions comes back for tests.
proposed_resolution: End the token with a fixed terminator, for example the token followed by a double underscore or by the end of the name, and say so in F-STATES and in the test-writer's duty. The alternative is for F-RECORD to refuse a new key whose encoded form followed by '_' begins another record's encoded form.

outcome.what_was_done: A token now ends at the end of the name, at '__', or at a character that is not a letter, a digit or '_', so a single '_' after it belongs to a longer key and flag_off_checkout no longer matches inside flag_off_checkout_v2. The encoded form of a key is defined once, in the header of flag-checks.toml: lower case, each run of other characters written as one '_', none at either end. It can therefore never contain '__', which is what makes the terminator safe for every key, inherited ones included. F-RECORD refuses a new key whose encoded form is another record's, and F-REQUIRE refuses a story behind a flag whose encoded form another record shares. The alternative, refusing a key that begins another, was rejected: keys are never reused, so it would forbid 'checkout.v2' for ever once 'checkout' existed, and it could not cover two inherited keys.

problem: config/flags.md says that in the requested state 'every gate result and the release packet' print 'flags requested, flag system not chosen'. The flag-checks header says no flag check runs while flags are not on. The release list in topics/flag-lifecycle.md does not include the line. No package's delivers text names it either: F1 delivers the states only in vsdd status and the briefing. The line that replaced the F-6 deadlock therefore has no builder in gate results, and probably none in the release packet.
proposed_resolution: Name the line in F1's delivers as one helper that every gate result calls, add it to the release list of topics/flag-lifecycle.md (built by F3), or drop 'every gate result' from config/flags.md.

outcome.what_was_done: 'Every gate result' is dropped: config/flags.md now says the line is printed by vsdd status, the briefing and the release packet. flag-lifecycle.md 'The release' says that in the state requested the packet's section is that one line, and that in the state off there is no section. Both have a builder: F1 delivers the states in status and the briefing, F3 the flag lines of the release packet. The helper called from every gate result was rejected: no flag check runs in that state, a gate result is read by a script and not by a person, and it would add a flag dependency to every gate package for a line that has no reader there.

problem: flags.enabled has set_by = "person", which the table's header defines as 'written by a person in [flags], and by nothing else'. Yet the proposal carries enabled, F-CHOICE requires it, and F-FILL writes it into [flags.approved] with an exception. topics/project-configuration.md also restates that the survey keeps [flags.approved] 'equal to' the toolchain table and leaves out that exception. An F1 builder who writes the schema from set_by could reject enabled in [flags.approved] or in the toolchain file.
proposed_resolution: Make flags.enabled set_by = "proposal" with override = true, which is the existing meaning: a person's value in [flags] wins. Have project-configuration.md link to config:flags for the contents of [flags.approved] instead of restating them.

outcome.what_was_done: flags.enabled is now set_by proposal with override = true, and its meaning says it is the one key F-FILL does not copy as written. flags.require is the only key left with set_by person, and the header says a proposal that carries such a key is refused (F-CHOICE). The D31 passage of project-configuration.md no longer says what [flags.approved] holds; it links to config:flags, which links to F-FILL.

where: rewrite/spec/tables/flag-duties.toml (test-writer duty, the split sentence; adversary item flag-off)
problem: This round's design choice to split a test (test-writer duty: 'Split a test that asserts both kinds: the part the on state breaks is moved, and the rest keeps the name') does not fit the reviewer item that is supposed to cover it. The adversary's item flag-off asks that 'each test the diff moves has its assertions unchanged' and that 'the diff deletes, renames or weakens no other existing test'. A correct split fails both on their face: the moved part holds only some of the original's assertions, and the part that keeps the name has lost the assertions that moved, so it is an existing test the diff weakens. A reviewer that follows the item raises a finding on every correct split. Nothing checks what matters about a split either: that the two parts together keep every assertion of the original, unchanged. F-STATES's unmeasured cell hands exactly that question to the items flag-off and flag-removed. Also, 'both kinds' follows the sentence that defines `old` and `pending`, so it can be read as a test that asserts both an old and a pending part rather than a test the on state only partly breaks.
proposed_resolution: In the item flag-off of the adversary's duty, add: for a split test, the moved part and the part that keeps the name together hold every assertion of the original, unchanged, and the moved part holds only what the on state breaks. Exclude a split's remaining part from 'weakens no other existing test'. In the test-writer duty, write 'Split a test that the on state breaks only in part' instead of 'that asserts both kinds'.

outcome.what_was_done: The orchestrating session applied the proposed fix as written: the test-writer duty now says 'Split a test that the on state breaks only in part', and the adversary's item flag-off says that for a split test the two parts together hold every assertion of the original, unchanged, that the moved part holds only what the on state breaks, and that the part keeping the name is not a weakened test. Not confirmed by an independent check; the reviewer of package F4 reads it when the duties are built.

where: rewrite/spec/tables/flag-story-checks.toml (F-STATES, the criterion refusal for a new off or default test)
problem: The new refusal in F-STATES rejects a new off or default test whose name 'names one [criterion] whose text lacks the words flag off'. It takes which criteria a name names from gate-red's rule, which is a substring match ('its name contains ac<N>'). A test named for AC-12 therefore also names AC-1, and a token whose encoded key contains `ac` followed by a digit (the tidy form allows a key such as `hvac2-mode`, which encodes as `hvac2_mode`) makes every test that carries the token name that criterion. In a story with ten or more criteria whose flag-off criterion is AC-1x, or with such a key, an off test written as the duty says is refused because it also names a criterion without 'flag off'. The test-writer cannot rename its way out, because the state token is required. Before this round the check only asked whether a name named any criterion, so the loose match caused no refusal.
proposed_resolution: In F-STATES, define which criteria a name names for this refusal: each `ac<N>` that no letter or digit comes directly before and no digit comes directly after, read in the name once every token of the flag has been taken out. Leave gate-red's own map rule as it is, since that rule is on the thin slice path.

outcome.what_was_done: The orchestrating session applied the proposed fix as written: for the F-STATES refusal alone, a name names AC-<N> when, with every token of the flag taken out, it holds ac<N> with no letter or digit directly before it and no digit directly after it. The red gate's own map rule is left alone. Not confirmed by an independent check; the reviewer of package F2 reads it when the check is built.

problem: The removal duty this round added, for a removal that keeps the off behaviour, does not fit its check. The duty says to 'delete its on tests and the test of its definition, and take the token out of the names of the rest'. But the same duty has every off test 'set it off' through the test double, and at a removal F-DEFINITION refuses 'a test that sets it', as the item flag-removed does ('no test sets the key'). So a test-writer that follows the duty produces a removal the green gate refuses. Only the clause that keeps the on behaviour takes the flag setting out ('take the flag setting out of its on tests'). Also, the clause that keeps the on behaviour does not say what becomes of a pending test. Such a removal can be asked for on a flag that is not on, F-ON does not run on a removal story, and F-DEFINITION refuses any moved test that remains. The duty gives no way through, so the story ends blocked with no stated reason.
proposed_resolution: In the clause that keeps the off behaviour, add: take the flag setting out of the off tests (and out of any other test that sets the key), then take the token out of the names of the rest. In the clause that keeps the on behaviour, say what a pending test means. For example, a removal that keeps the on behaviour is refused while the flag has a pending test, as a turn-on is (state it in F-DEFINITION's removal refusal, so the message names the test). Or the test-writer returns blocked and names it.

outcome.what_was_done: Decided: a story removes a flag in one of two ways and says which in flag_change (artifacts/flag.md). remove keeps the behaviour of a value other than the default, which for a release flag is the on behaviour; withdraw keeps the behaviour of the default, so the feature is given up. This replaces 'the request says which behaviour stays', which no program could read. Each duty now fits its checks. Every removal leaves no test that sets the key: the tests of the behaviour that goes and the test of the definition are deleted, and the flag setting is taken out of every other test. remove deletes the off, default and old tests and writes the regression test. withdraw deletes the on tests and every other test that turns the flag on, gives each moved test its own name back and takes the token out of the names of the off and default tests. F-DEFINITION refuses, at the head of either, a test that sets the key or still carries a token of the flag, other than an on test after a remove. A pending test: F-STATES refuses a remove at its red gate while the base report holds a pending test of the flag, and names each, so the story stops before anything is built; flag-lifecycle.md 'Removal' gives the way through (the stories behind the flag provide what the test asserts, which gives it its name back, or the flag is withdrawn). Walking a withdrawal through red showed a second defect of the same clause: nothing the product does with no flag set changes, so no test can fail first and the red gate could never pass. F-STATES now asks a withdrawal for no red test, applies no red share, maps no test to a criterion and says so in its record, and it refuses a moved test of the base report that has not come back. The item flag-removed now also covers which tests the diff deletes and that a test brought back or renamed is unchanged; review-stories checks each flag_change against the request. F-REQUIRE holds both removals to kind fix, F-REMOVE counts either as an open removal, the record is removed after either, and the release packet says which behaviour stays. F4 gains a harness scenario for a withdrawal, and ledger entry D31-1 names the three values.

where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/schemas/implement-data.schema.json (test_defects description); rewrite/spec/topics/story-script.md (the test-defects prompt); rewrite/spec/tables/flag-duties.toml (implementer duty)
problem: The design choice 'no ledger entry was added: test_defects carries a test that F-ON names, with its shape unchanged' is right about the shape (path, test, reason). But the shipped schema describes the field as 'frozen tests the builder believes are wrong and may not edit', and the story script's prompt tells the test-writer 'The implementer reports these frozen tests as wrong'. A test that F-ON names is an existing test the story did not write, and it is not frozen. Moved tests are expressly not held among the frozen tests (F-STATES). So D31 uses a shipped field beyond its documented meaning, with no ledger entry to widen the description. D31-8 makes exactly that kind of change for the acs field. A builder or reviewer who reads the description could reject or ignore such an entry.
proposed_resolution: Add a ledger entry, left-for-builder for package F2: widen the description of test_defects in implement-data.schema.json to 'tests the builder believes are wrong and may not edit: frozen tests, and existing tests that the green gate's run with a flag on names'. The shape does not change. Leave the story script's prompt unchanged, so nothing on the slice path changes. F4's harness scenario, in which an existing test is moved once the run with the flag on has named it, already proves that the step works with that prompt.

outcome.what_was_done: Package F2, when it builds F-ON, widens the description of test_defects in next/plugins/vsdd-factory/schemas/implement-data.schema.json to: tests the builder believes are wrong and may not edit: frozen tests, and existing tests that the green gate's run with a flag on names. The shape (path, test, reason) does not change. The story script's prompt stays as it is, so nothing on the slice path changes; F4's harness scenario runs the moved-test path through that prompt. The design side is settled: the implementer's duty in flag-duties.toml and the D31 passage of workflows/story.md say that such a test travels under test_defects, and F2's delivers text names this entry. It can only be settled in code, because the schema is shipped under next/.

problem: The test-writer duty says that a moved test is renamed 'with a token and, in a story behind a flag, the flag off criterion', and the corrector's account says F-STATES checks that a moved test 'names the flag-off criterion'. F-STATES refuses only an off, default or moved test whose name 'names no criterion (ac<N>)', and its reads do not include the story's criteria. The item flag-off does not check the criterion either. So a moved test named for an on criterion passes every check, and gate demo's criterion table then shows a test of the old behaviour as evidence for the new one. The flag-duties header calls a duty with neither a check nor a reviewer a defect of that table.
proposed_resolution: In a story behind a flag, have F-STATES refuse a moved test (and, if wanted, an off or default test) whose name names no criterion whose text contains 'flag off', compared without case. F-REQUIRE already guarantees that such a criterion exists. Add the story's criteria to F-STATES's reads. Alternatively, drop 'the flag off criterion' from the duty and let any criterion do.

outcome.what_was_done: Neither proposed fix was enough alone. A moved test is an existing test, and in a product the factory built its own name already holds the ac<N> of the story that wrote it, so the criteria map would show it under that number whatever criterion the move added or left out. Decided: a moved test is evidence of no criterion. The duty no longer adds a criterion to a moved name, and F-STATES leaves moved tests out of the record's criteria map, so gate demo's table never shows a test of the old behaviour as evidence of the new one. For the tests the story writes itself, F-STATES now reads the story's criteria and refuses a new off or default test that names no criterion, or names one whose text lacks 'flag off'; the duty says the same. So that the rule also holds when a test gets its own name back, a moved name now has one form: the test's own name with __flag_old_<k> or __flag_pending_<k> added. A program can then tell which test a moved test was and when it has come back. F-STATES refuses a new moved test that the base report does not hold, refuses a missing test that the head does not hold as a moved test (this replaces the count of missing tests against moved tests), and treats a test that has come back as neither new nor evidence of a criterion. Which existing test a moved test was is no longer unmeasured; the item flag-off keeps what is a judgment (assertions unchanged, old only where a criterion replaces).

proposed_resolution: The orchestrating session changes 'F5 the planning gates' to 'F5 the planning gates and the sweep's spec coherence check'. Nothing else changes: G7 is built in step 3, before any F package.

F6 the wave, release and sweep jobs') is therefore right as it stands and needs no edit, and its order F1, F5, F2, F6 already builds F5 before F6. proposed_resolution: Decide which flags an evaluation turns on: only flags that have no pending test and whose stories in the wave are all delivered, with the others left at their default; say so where the override is defined and test it with a wave that holds one finished and one unfinished flag.

outcome.what_was_done: Recorded by the orchestrating session from the corrector's notes. No further round of design fixes is run on D31; the package named in the triage settles it when it is built.

proposed_resolution: For a removal or withdrawal story, have the Rollback section say that the way back is to revert the merge, and leave out the line about turning the flag off.
