where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/config.py and next/tests/unit/test_config.py (the shipped loader); rewrite/spec/tables/config-keys.toml; rewrite/spec/schemas/config.schema.json; the annotated example in rewrite/spec/topics/project-configuration.md
problem: The configuration key list exists in four places that must gain the flag keys together, and none has them: the shipped loader rejects [flags] as an unknown section, and config-keys.toml (15.7 KB) and config.schema.json (14.7 KB) are both too close to the 16 KB file limit to take the rows as they are. A [[repo]] entry may carry a flags table as well.
proposed_resolution: Teach the loader both tables from the rows of rewrite/spec/tables/flag-config-keys.toml: types and defaults, the four values of flags.require, compiled patterns, repo.flags, and the meaning of set_by. A key marked person (flags.require) is accepted only in [flags]. A key marked proposal is accepted in [flags.approved]; one that also has override = true (flags.enabled among them) is accepted in [flags] too, where a person's value wins. Compute the three states off, requested and on from the two tables. Ship accept and reject cases; add the section to the annotated example; for the two files at the size limit either split them or have them name flag-config-keys.toml as the home of the flag rows. outcome.what_was_done: The rows are settled in rewrite/spec/tables/flag-config-keys.toml, and the two tables of factory.toml, the three states and the patterns in rewrite/spec/config/flags.md. problem: Decision D31 adds no decision kind but changes two rows the table does not yet show. Row spec: approving a specification whose toolchain file says enabled = true, when the decision would accept the decision record that flags.decision names, needs the value flags=<source> with that file's source, whichever of the four sources it is; flags=decline -- <words> is accepted instead where the source is existing; a flags value on any other approval is refused (F-APPROVE in rewrite/spec/tables/flag-checks.toml; rewrite/spec/topics/flag-system-choice.md). Row merge: where flags.removal = human, the checkpoint of maintain opens one merge decision for each flag that is due for removal, with the id merge.flag-<stem>, before any cleanup story is written. No story and no pull request exist at that point, so the row's opened_when (a delivered story waits) and its note (approve performs the merge; reject closes the pull request and descopes the story) do not describe it, and its reject needs until=<yyyy-mm-dd> naming a day after today (F-APPROVE; F-REMOVE in rewrite/spec/tables/flag-release-checks.toml; rewrite/spec/topics/flag-lifecycle.md). A flag adds no wait at vsdd story deliver: a cleanup story merges as delivery.merge says, and where flags.removal = auto no decision is opened.
proposed_resolution: Row spec: write the approve choice as approve [variant=<id>] [topology=single or split] [flags=<source> | flags=decline -- <words>], with a note that a flags value is required exactly when the decision would accept the flag decision record, that it is stored in the decision's values, and that settling refuses it on any other approval. Row merge: add to opened_when that, where flags.removal = human, the maintain checkpoint opens merge.flag-<stem> for a flag that is due for removal, before a cleanup story is written; write the reject choice as reject [until=<yyyy-mm-dd>]; add to the note that for a removal decision approve lets the next maintain run write the cleanup story, and reject, which needs until, keeps the flag and makes it not due again before that day, with nothing merged, closed or descoped. The grammar of decide needs no change: flags and until are named values. Do not add a wait at story deliver, and do not open the decision when a person asked for the removal with a change request.

outcome.what_was_done: The two changes are settled in rewrite/spec/topics/flag-system-choice.md (the flags value of a spec approval, for every source, and flags=decline) and rewrite/spec/topics/flag-lifecycle.md (the merge decision merge.flag-<stem> that the maintain checkpoint opens before a cleanup story is written, only while flags.removal = human, with a reject that needs until), as the checks F-APPROVE and F-REMOVE. Package F3 edits the two rows of the decision table when it builds those checks, after S4 and G4b are complete. Nothing waits at story deliver.

where: rewrite/spec/tables/lint-checks.toml; the lint suite under next/tests/lint/

proposed_resolution: Add the lint check L-FLAG: every method the duty table names has a section headed Feature flags; no other method has one; every agent the table names lists the method. Ship the duty table as data beside the roster so the lint reads one source.

outcome.what_was_done: The check is stated in the header of rewrite/spec/tables/flag-duties.toml. Package F4 adds the L-FLAG row and its test when it writes the Feature flags sections of the method files, after the agent packages are complete.

problem: The identifier table lists every identifier scheme, and the flag key is a new one: it is the identifier of a flag record, its file stem is a function of it, and it is never reused. Test names carry a second function of it, the encoded form, which no two keys that tests can name may share.
proposed_resolution: Add a row for the flag key: any key existing code reads, held to the tidy form ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$ for a new flag; chosen by the story-writer; the file stem is the key with /, % and whitespace percent-encoded; never reused, because the record of a removed flag is kept. For the encoded form point at the header of rewrite/spec/tables/flag-checks.toml, which defines it; do not restate it.

outcome.what_was_done: The scheme is settled in rewrite/spec/artifacts/flag.md. Package F1 adds the row to the identifier table with the artifact kind.

problem: The registry's one-line summary of decisions.md still reads "The record of the adopted decisions D1 to D30, as decided." The file now also records D31, under a heading for decisions adopted after 2026-11-23. The workflow that wrote D31 was not allowed to edit registry.toml.
proposed_resolution: Change the summary to "The record of the adopted decisions, D1 to D31, as decided." and regenerate the briefs.

where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/schemas/story-unit.schema.json (the acs field); rewrite/spec/topics/verdicts.md (items to account for); rewrite/spec/tables/flag-story-checks.toml (F-ITEMS)
problem: F-ITEMS (rewrite/spec/tables/flag-story-checks.toml) adds four review items that are not acceptance criteria to the items a story's review must account for: flag-off:<key>, for a story behind a flag and for a story that turns one on; flag-removed:<key>; flag-system; and not-a-flag. The workflow script hands reviewers the unit's acs list, and the shipped schema describes acs as acceptance criteria only, so without a change the reviewers are never told of an item the tool's verdict then waits for, and the story cannot converge. These items differ from a criterion in three ways. Only checked counts for them: not_checkable leaves the item uncovered. flag-off and flag-removed are added again in a later review loop whose commits touch a file of class source or tests. And not-a-flag is known only once the green gate has run, because it is added when the green evidence lists a marked line, so it cannot come from a unit the survey built before that gate.
proposed_resolution: Have the survey and the admission commands append the items that the story's own keys decide (flag-off, flag-removed, flag-system) to the unit's acs, and widen the field's description to say so. Carry not-a-flag to the reviewers from the green gate's result, and have the tool's verdict add it from the green evidence. For a later loop, have the verdict and the script's list for that loop both carry flag-off or flag-removed when the loop's commits touch source or tests. Check that nothing reads every acs entry as AC-<N> (the criterion-to-test table is built from the red record's criteria map, not from acs); if a consumer does, carry the items in a field of their own and pass it in the review step's prompt instead. Prove with a harness scenario that a story behind a flag converges only when a reviewer marks flag-off checked, and that not_checkable does not converge it.

outcome.what_was_done: The items are settled as check F-ITEMS in rewrite/spec/tables/flag-story-checks.toml: four items, of which only checked counts, two added again in a later loop that touches source or tests, and one known only from the green evidence. Package F2 carries them to the reviewers and into the tool's verdict, widens the schema description, and proves with a harness scenario that a story behind a flag converges only when a reviewer marks flag-off checked.

problem: T-REMOTE says every fetch and every push names `refs/heads/<branch>` on both sides. For a fetch that is wrong. Tested with git 2.34.1 on Linux and 2.50.1 on macOS: `git fetch <remote> refs/heads/<b>:refs/heads/<b>` into the state branch, which is checked out in the mount, exits 128 ('Refusing to fetch into current branch'), so every sync would end `unreachable`; into a target branch that is not checked out it would move the person's own local branch. A fetch into the remote-tracking ref without a leading `+` exits 1 ('[rejected] (non-fast-forward)') after the remote was rewound, and the head rule makes a failed fetch `unreachable`, so T-HISTORY's `rewritten` is never reached. Fact 9's 'git fetch exits 0 and reports a forced update' holds only for a forced refspec (the configured one, or `+refs/heads/<b>:refs/remotes/<r>/<b>`). command:sync already says the sync writes the remote-tracking ref, so the two files disagree. Ledger D33-13, which is on the slice path, carries the same ambiguity to S3's target_head being built now ('fetches refs/heads/<branch> from that remote under the branch's own name').
proposed_resolution: Say in T-REMOTE that a push names refs/heads/<b> on both sides and a fetch is `git fetch <remote> +refs/heads/<b>:refs/remotes/<remote>/<b>`, never into refs/heads. Add to fact 9 that the `+` is what turns a rewind into a forced update with exit 0, and that without it the fetch exits 1. Amend D33-13 to the same refspec before S3 builds target_head, with a pr-mode test that the local integration branch did not move. M1's T-HISTORY test fetches a rewound branch and expects `rewritten`.

outcome.what_was_done: T-REMOTE now states the refs once, in two forms and no other, for the state branch, a target branch and a story branch alike: a push is git push <remote> <source>:refs/heads/<branch> (the source is refs/heads/<branch> or the id of a commit built on the remote's head), and a fetch is git fetch <remote> +refs/heads/<branch>:refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>, never into a ref under refs/heads/. The tool runs no git pull and no fetch without a refspec, so a local branch moves only as its own row says (the mount by the flush and a fast-forward, a story branch in its worktree, a target branch in pr mode never), and what a clone last saw is sync.remote_head or delivery.pushed, never the remote-tracking ref. Run on git 2.34.1 (Ubuntu 22.04) and 2.50.1 (macOS) in scratch repositories: a fetch into the state branch exits 128 inside the mount on both, and from the main checkout exits 128 on 2.50.1 but exits 0 on 2.34.1 and moves the branch under the mount; a fetch into a target branch that is not checked out moves the person's branch, or exits 1 when it holds a commit of its own; without the + a fetch after a rewind exits 1, with it 0 and a forced update (team-git-facts, facts 9 and 15). One full sync, one claim taken by two clones at once and one hand-off were then walked command by command with those two forms, three times on each version: every command exited as designed and no local or remote integration branch moved (fact 18). The walk of the hand-off showed one gap, now closed in T-BRANCH: a holder with no local story branch, or one behind delivery.pushed, creates it at that commit id or fast-forwards, and a listing says whether a story branch is on the remote at all, since a fetch of a branch that is not there fails as an unreachable remote does. command:sync, topic:team-sync and the worktrees passage point to T-REMOTE. Ledger D33-13, which S3 has built and closed meanwhile, now words the fetch as it was built, into the remote-tracking ref and never the local branch; what the built code still lacks, the leading + and two assertions, is the new entry D33-33 for S3 and G4a. Proof scenario 40 asserts that no fetch names a local branch.

problem: Fact 6 names `git diff --name-status` against the merge base as what the sync reads to decide each path. Porcelain diff detects renames by default, and a person's diff.renames setting can change that. Tested with git 2.34.1 and 2.50.1: one commit that removes claims/story.S-1.json and adds claims/story.S-2.json (a release and a take, pretty-printed JSON) is listed as the single line `R080 claims/story.S-1.json claims/story.S-2.json`. A path-by-path decision read from that output misses a removal and an addition, and can take a new claim for a change to the released one.
proposed_resolution: State in T-COMBINE and fact 6 that the two diffs are read with rename detection off (`git diff-tree -r --no-renames --name-status <base> <head>`, or `git diff --no-renames`), which lists D and A for the same commit, and add that case to M1's tests.

outcome.what_was_done: A head rule of table:team-checks now says that every list of the paths that differ between two commits is read with git diff-tree -r --no-renames --name-status -z, by one function of package M1 that T-INCOMING, T-COMBINE, T-HOLD, T-LOCAL and T-NOTICE read through; T-COMBINE's `reads` names it. Run on 2.34.1 and 2.50.1: with the two claim files written one key to a line, git diff --name-status and git show --name-status list the release plus take as one line, R092; git diff-tree -r lists D and A with or without --no-renames, whatever diff.renames is set to, and joins them only with -M; with the claims on three lines every command lists D and A, so the rename depends on how alike the files are; -z gives a path with a space and a non-ASCII letter whole (team-git-facts, fact 6). Proof scenario 41 runs the release-plus-take case.

problem: T-PUSH calls a refused push a lost race whenever the remote's head is no longer the commit the push was built on. A state branch rewound or replaced between the claim's sync and its push matches that test too. The sync goes back to step 3, where T-HISTORY can catch it, but T-PUBLISH and T-MINT build the commit again on the new head, push it, and on acceptance bring it into the mount through T-COMBINE, which merges the vanished commits back: the outcome T-HISTORY exists to prevent. The commits that arrived between the two heads also reach the mount without T-INCOMING or T-HOLD having run on them. clone.md defines sync.remote_head as the head 'at the last listing or fetch that succeeded', so T-PUSH's own fetch of a rewound head moves it, and the next sync's T-HISTORY test then passes and the rewind is undone silently.
proposed_resolution: A lost race requires that the new head contains the head the push was built on; otherwise every caller answers `rewritten`. After a lost race T-PUBLISH and T-MINT run the sync's steps 3 and 4 (T-HISTORY, T-INCOMING, T-HOLD) on the new head before building again. sync.remote_head is written only once T-HISTORY has accepted a fetched head. Add to proof scenario 7 a rewind between B's opening sync and its claim push.

outcome.what_was_done: T-HISTORY now defines sync.remote_head as the last head of the remote whose arrivals this clone checked and took into its mount, and says that the check itself reads it and never writes it. It is written in two places, each only after the mount holds the commit: by step 4 of the sync, once what arrived is checked and the mount is fast-forwarded, to the fetched head; and when a push of this clone is accepted, to the pushed commit and not to the remote's head. A fetch made to judge a push writes nothing in the mount or the clone record (T-PUSH says so where it makes that fetch), so after a lost race the field is still the push's base, and the repeated sync, and T-PUBLISH's and T-MINT's repeated opening sync, list what arrived from that base through T-INCOMING, whose `reads` now names the field. command:sync follows: step 3 ends `synced` without a fetch only when the listed head is sync.remote_head, the mount's head is that commit too, sync.unknown is empty and, in a full sync, the clone holds no claim that T-RELEASE has a sync remove; step 4 writes the clone record after the fast-forward and not before; step 5 returns to step 3 with the field as it was. The last two conditions of step 3 go past the proposal, because the shortcut also skipped step 4's own work: on a quiet remote a commit in sync.unknown was never settled, so a minting command stayed refused. record:clone, schema:clone, T-REMOTE's wording and the reason in topic:team-sync say the same by reference. Run on git 2.34.1 and 2.50.1 in scratch repositories, three rounds each (team-git-facts, fact 20): after a lost race, diff-tree from the push's base to the new head lists a record made by hand and the winner's claim, the same listing from the judged head to itself is empty, and the fast-forward of the mount to the accepted claim commit alone put that record into the mount; after a push that was taken while its answer was lost and a commit pushed on top, merge --ff-only of the pushed commit moves the mount to that commit and not to the remote's head, and the listing from the pushed commit names the later file. The full sync, the claim taken by two clones at once and the hand-off were walked again with this rule (fact 18). Proof scenario 2 gains both cases, with the broken record reported through T-INCOMING. Ledger D33-3 is reworded.

problem: A full sync removes, unasked, 'a story claim under which nothing was begun and for which no run is live', and every claim held for a run whose run is not live here. A claim a person has just taken with `vsdd claim take` matches both: the command starts no run, and this clone has no commit of that story. The next full sync is the opening sync of the very survey that claim-take.md says 'enters the claim as its own', so the claim is removed first, `taken_from` is lost, and the story is free to any clone until that survey's T-CLAIM takes it again. Whether 'begun' is measured on this clone's branch or on the remote's is not said; measured locally, it also frees a taken story whose old holder had pushed work.
proposed_resolution: Say that 'begun' is measured on the story branch on the remote as well as on this clone, and that a full sync does not remove a claim carrying `taken_from` until a run of this clone has entered it or a person releases it. Add the case to proof scenario 28.

outcome.what_was_done: T-RELEASE now defines 'begun' once: the story's branch on this clone holds a commit beyond the base its closure records, or its closure records a pushed head (delivery.pushed) other than that base. That reads what was pushed from tracked state, where the proposal asked for the remote branch, so no sync needs another network call. A full sync removes a run's claim or an unbegun story's claim only when its `run` names a run of this clone that is not live. vsdd claim take writes an empty `run` (T-TAKEOVER, schema:work-claim), so no sync removes a claim a person took over (the rule is keyed on the empty `run` and not on taken_from, which stays in the claim after a run has entered it), the opening sync of the survey that enters it included; it ends when a run enters it and writes its own id there, or by vsdd claim release. The checkpoint's removal of unbegun stories is limited to stories its run took or entered. commands/claim-take.md and claim-release.md say so, and proof scenario 28 has the case, also where the old holder had pushed nothing.

problem: `vsdd sync` is a job keyed by the command and the state branch, with no commit, and the decisions rule starts it detached and returns. Nothing ever collects that job's result, and the built job layer serves a finished, uncollected result to the next call with the same key (next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/gates/jobs.py, _serves; a record is pruned only after the retention days). So the next `vsdd sync` that a person or the main session runs, when the briefing says state is behind or unpublished, returns the earlier outcome of the hook's sync and runs no sync.
proposed_resolution: Start the rule's sync under a key of its own (for example the subject `settle:<decision id>`), or have `vsdd sync` attach only to a running job and otherwise start a new one. State it in the Team use passage of long-commands.md, with a test: a rule-started sync finishes, then `vsdd sync` fetches again.

outcome.what_was_done: The Team use passage of topic:long-commands now takes both halves of the proposal, because each covers a case the other does not. A sync's result is the state of the remote at one moment, so the job specification of a sync says that its worker marks its own result as collected: a call that started the job or attached while it ran is given the result, and any later call starts a new sync. That also covers a vsdd sync whose caller never came back after a pending answer. The sync the decisions rule starts is a job of its own, keyed by the command and settle:<decision id>, which names the one record its flush may commit; it does not attach to a vsdd sync that is running, since that one may have flushed before the settlement was written, and local/sync.lock puts the two in a row. command:sync and the Team use passage of rule:decisions point there. New ledger entry D33-31 gives package M1 the one field to add to the job layer, with its test. Proof scenario 43.

problem: A clone that was mounted while team use was off joins by itself at its next push once the fetched factory.toml has team use on (T-SOLO). Unlike T-SWITCH on the switching clone, nothing claims the stories this clone has in flight, and T-HANDOFF pushes the branch only of a story whose claim this clone holds. Its in-flight story therefore stays unclaimed and its branch stays on this clone, and another clone's survey takes the story as free and starts it again from its base: the double work clause 4b forbids. Proof scenario 17 gives B no story in flight.
proposed_resolution: When T-SOLO joins, it claims in the same sync, as T-SWITCH does, every undelivered story whose branch on this clone holds a commit beyond its base and that no other clone claims, and reports the others for a person. Extend scenario 17 with a story in flight on B.

outcome.what_was_done: T-SOLO: when a clone that was mounted with team use off finds a team formed, it runs the preflight, gets its record with how = joined, and before that sync ends claims the stories it has in flight exactly as T-SWITCH claims them: one commit, an empty `run`, every undelivered story whose branch here holds a commit beyond its base, and a story another clone already claimed reported for a person and not taken. T-SWITCH's `runs` cell, topic:team-claims and config:team say the same by reference. Proof scenario 17 gives B a story in flight: it is claimed in the joining sync and A's next survey lists it under `elsewhere`.

where: rewrite/spec/tables/team-checks.toml (head rule 'When a check runs'); rewrite/spec/config/team.md (On and off); rewrite/spec/topics/team-use.md (One clone); rewrite/spec/tables/team-delivery-checks.toml (T-DELIVERY)
problem: The head rule says a check runs only while team use is on 'with three exceptions' (T-JOIN, T-SOLO and the hand-commit checks). T-DELIVERY is a fourth: its row and ledger D33-17 ('All of it but the two claim refusals runs with team use off as well') run the host-module refusal, `queued`, the adoption of a merge made by the host or outside the tool, and `merged_by` in every pr-mode delivery. config/team.md's 'Off' list and team-use.md's 'One clone' line omit it. config/team.md also says 'No survey fetches' with team use off, while in pr mode the survey fetches the target branch (target_head) and T-NOTICE and T-BRANCH read after that fetch. With team use off `merged_by` is to hold 'the person and clone', but no clone record exists then.
proposed_resolution: Name T-DELIVERY, less its two team refusals, as an exception in the head rule, in config/team.md's 'Off' list and in team-use.md. Say that with team use off `merged_by` holds the person and no clone. Reword 'No survey fetches' as 'No survey fetches the state branch'.

outcome.what_was_done: The last section of topics/team-sync.md keeps no list of its own: it says that which of the checks the file explains act while team.enabled is false is stated once, at the head of table:team-checks, and keeps the sentence "With no remote there is nothing to sync and nothing changes." A search of every D33 file for the same statement found it in two more places, both corrected. command:sync said that with team use off the command does the state push "and nothing else, with T-SOLO"; it now points to the head rule for the checks that act on that push. T-SOLO said it "is the only thing that changes for a project with one clone", which the head rule contradicts (T-REMOTE's remote and refs, T-JOIN, T-ORDER, the hand-commit checks and T-DELIVERY in pr mode act too); it now says only that with no second clone the remote never moves and T-SOLO never runs. Ledger D33-3 said "nothing changes but T-SOLO" and is reworded. The statements left in topic:state-commits, topic:run-lock and record:lock describe T-SOLO alone and claim no list.

problem: A second sync 'waits for the first and then runs its own' on local/sync.lock, with no limit. `vsdd sync` run as a job has ten minutes for each network call, so a survey, a checkpoint or `vsdd decide` that starts behind it waits past the 60-second budget that T-FRESH and command:sync give a sync inside a foreground command to keep it inside the Bash tool's default limit.
proposed_resolution: Count the wait for local/sync.lock against the caller's 60-second budget; when it runs out the caller answers `busy` and changes nothing. Add a case: a slow `vsdd sync` job holds the lock while a survey starts.

outcome.what_was_done: command:sync, step 1 and the section on time: a second sync waits for local/sync.lock inside its own budget and answers `busy` at its end, having changed nothing. In a foreground command the 60 seconds cover that wait and all network calls together; a sync job has ten minutes for the wait and for each call. The `busy` row of the outcome table names the case and what to do. T-FRESH says the opening sync's budget covers the wait. Proof scenario 42 holds the lock with a slow sync job while a survey starts.

problem: The outcome of a story-branch push is judged only by its exit status; T-PUSH's measurement covers the state branch alone. T-NEVER puts the branch back at its pre-rebase head 'when the remote refuses' the forced push. If that push was accepted and its answer lost (a time limit or a dropped connection, fact 3) and the tool takes it as refused, the remote holds the rebased commits while delivery.pushed and the local head hold the old ones. T-BRANCH then finds the rebased copies reachable from neither, records the holder's own commits as hand commits, merges them in and makes them `hand:` items: the doubled history D33R-S-5 named, which the `git cherry` filter S-5 proposed, and the correction dropped without a reason, would have caught.
proposed_resolution: Judge every push of a story branch as T-PUSH judges a state push: after any push that did not report success, fetch the branch and compare; if the remote head is the pushed commit the push was accepted and delivery.pushed is set to it. In T-BRANCH also drop an arrived commit whose patch id is already on the local branch (git cherry). Add a case: a forced push accepted under a post-receive hook that outlasts the client's limit.

outcome.what_was_done: T-BRANCH now judges every push of a story branch that did not report success by the measurement of T-PUSH, at a checkpoint, a release of the claim and a delivery alike: after a fetch, a pushed head contained in the remote head was accepted and delivery.pushed becomes it; a remote head equal to delivery.pushed was not taken; any other head means something arrived; when the fetch fails as well nothing is recorded or put back. T-NEVER puts the branch back only when a fetch shows the remote did not take the push, and rebases only from the head the remote holds, so delivery.pushed is the head before a rebase. Two things the tests showed are corrected with it. A remote head that contains this clone's head but not delivery.pushed is this clone's own push with a lost answer or record, where the old test read it as a branch somebody replaced; replaced now means the remote head contains neither. And git cherry has its reason: where a rebase never reached the remote and a teammate's commit arrived, merging it into the rebased branch exits 0 and leaves each of the holder's commits in the history twice, so the branch is first put back at delivery.pushed, and only when git cherry shows that every commit this drops has its patch there; otherwise the unit is blocked as a conflict (team-git-facts, fact 17; 2.34.1 and 2.50.1). The filter in the form proposed, dropping arrived commits by patch id, is not taken: once pushes are judged by a fetch the holder's copies no longer arrive, and a dropped commit would still come in as an ancestor of any teammate commit merged under its own id. T-HANDOFF, topic:team-delivery, the story-deliver passage and ledger D33-17 follow. Proof scenario 44 has the hook that outlasts the client's limit.

problem: New, from the correction of d33-fix-2-C1-2. The head rule of table:team-checks used to give every hand-commit check a local condition ('wherever the branch they read has an upstream'). It now says when each acts 'is stated in its own runs cell and nowhere else'. T-NEVER's runs cell says 'At every git command the tool runs on a branch that is on the remote'. That is a property of the remote, and the cell gives no local test for it. T-BRANCH's cell gives one (delivery.pushed recorded, or an upstream), but only for T-BRANCH. A builder who follows T-NEVER's row literally would list the remote before the tool rebases or squashes a story branch. In local mode, which rebases branches that were never pushed, that is a network call config/team.md ('Off') and proof scenario 23 ('no listing of the remote') forbid. Where the listing cannot be made, the head rule's 'cannot measure is a failure' would refuse the delivery.
proposed_resolution: Write T-NEVER's runs cell as a test read without the network: a story branch for which T-BRANCH's runs cell has the remote asked (its closure records delivery.pushed, or it has an upstream), and a target branch that has an upstream. Say that no listing is made to decide it. Proof scenario 23 then covers T-NEVER as well: a local delivery that rebases makes no listing.

outcome.what_was_done: Left for the package that builds it, after the two correction rounds this design gets; nothing of D33 is on the thin slice path. Resolution for the builder, who corrects the spec file in the same change: state T-NEVER's runs cell as a test read without the network: a story branch for which T-BRANCH's runs cell has the remote asked (delivery.pushed recorded, or an upstream), and a target branch with an upstream; say that no listing is made to decide it; and have proof scenario 23 cover a local delivery that rebases with no listing.

problem: New, from the correction of d33-fix-2-C1-2. Two statements were added: the head rule of table:team-checks says when each hand-commit check acts 'is stated in its own runs cell and nowhere else', and topics/team-delivery.md says the same. The correction also reports that the D33 passage of commands/survey.md 'restates no condition'. Yet that passage still says 'Wherever the target branch has an upstream it lists the hand commits on it (T-NOTICE)', and the D33 passages of commands/gate-wave.md and commands/gate-release.md open with 'Wherever the target branch has an upstream, with team use on or off'. Each copies T-NOTICE's runs cell. The copies agree with the cell today, but the 'nowhere else' claim is false, and a change to T-NOTICE's condition would leave three command files wrong (spec rule 1).
proposed_resolution: In the three D33 passages, replace the condition with a link: 'where T-NOTICE's runs cell has it act' ([[table:team-delivery-checks]]). Change only those passages, because survey.md is read on the slice path.

outcome.what_was_done: Left for the package that builds it, after the two correction rounds this design gets; nothing of D33 is on the thin slice path. Resolution for the builder, who corrects the spec file in the same change: in the D33 passages of commands/survey.md, commands/gate-wave.md and commands/gate-release.md, replace the restated condition ('wherever the target branch has an upstream') with a link to T-NOTICE's runs cell; change only those passages.

problem: New, from the correction of D33R-C-3. T-HISTORY now says sync.remote_head 'is written in two places only': step 4 of the sync, and an accepted push. Neither place covers the moment a clone record is made. vsdd init writes the record when a clone joins (T-JOIN; record:clone, 'Written by'), and the schema requires remote_head. T-SWITCH and T-SOLO's join make the record inside a sync whose T-HISTORY and T-INCOMING read the field before step 4 writes it. A record that is remade has lost it. Before the correction, 'the head at the last listing or fetch that succeeded' gave init's fetch and the switching sync's fetch a value. Now no file says what a new record holds, what the `rewritten` test compares, or which files T-INCOMING checks on a clone's first team sync. The rule is also stated more than once. record:clone says when the field is written 'is T-HISTORY's to say' and then repeats that a judging fetch does not change it. The schema description repeats both halves, and T-PUSH repeats 'That fetch changes nothing in the mount or the clone record' beside T-HISTORY's 'A fetch made to judge a push writes nothing'. Adding a third writer would mean editing four places.
proposed_resolution: In T-HISTORY, name the value a new record starts with: the merge base of the mount's head and the fetched head, written once the mount holds it. For T-JOIN at vsdd init that is the head it mounted; for T-SWITCH, T-SOLO's join and a `remade` record it is what this clone last shared with the remote. A rewrite that happened before then is the case T-HISTORY's `unmeasured` cell already names. Keep T-HISTORY as the one statement of when the field is written. Cut record:clone and the schema description to the field's one-line meaning with a link to T-HISTORY. Drop T-PUSH's copy and have T-PUSH link to T-HISTORY. Add to proof scenario 17 a record that fails its check and is on the remote when B joins at its push: B's sync reports it through T-INCOMING.

outcome.what_was_done: Left for the package that builds it, after the two correction rounds this design gets; nothing of D33 is on the thin slice path. Resolution for the builder, who corrects the spec file in the same change: in T-HISTORY name the starting value of sync.remote_head in a new clone record: the merge base of the mount's head and the fetched head, written once the mount holds it (for T-JOIN, the mounted head); keep T-HISTORY as the one statement of when the field is written, cut record:clone and the schema description to a one-line meaning with a link, have T-PUSH link to T-HISTORY instead of restating it, and add to proof scenario 17 a failing record on the remote when the second clone joins, which its sync reports through T-INCOMING.

problem: New, from the correction of d33-fix-2-C1-2. T-BRANCH's runs cell now has the survey look for a story branch only where the closure records delivery.pushed or the local branch has an upstream. Take a first push whose answer was lost and whose judging fetch failed. Nothing records delivery.pushed, and git sets the upstream of `push -u` only on a reported success, so the branch has neither. The last paragraph of the same row still says that in this case 'the result lists the story as not pushed, and the next survey measures'. For a first push the next survey does not measure: the runs cell excludes the branch. The adopted design choice says such a push is caught at the next push, but no file says so, and the row contradicts itself.
proposed_resolution: Reword the last sentence of T-BRANCH's refuses: the next survey measures where the runs cell has it look, and a first push whose answer and fetch were both lost is measured at the next push of the branch, which is judged as every push is. Add that case to proof scenario 44: the next push of the branch finds the commit the remote took, records it as delivery.pushed, and reports no hand commit. The alternative is to have the tool write the branch's upstream configuration before the first push, so that the runs cell covers it (fact 21 shows for-each-ref reads the configuration with no remote-tracking ref). That would change T-REMOTE's first-push sentence too.

outcome.what_was_done: Left for the package that builds it, after the two correction rounds this design gets; nothing of D33 is on the thin slice path. Resolution for the builder, who corrects the spec file in the same change: reword T-BRANCH's last sentence: the next survey measures where the runs cell has it look, and a first push whose answer and judging fetch were both lost is measured at the branch's next push, which is judged as every push is; add that case to proof scenario 44. (The alternative, writing the upstream configuration before the first push, would change T-REMOTE's first-push sentence; take it only if the proof shows the first form leaves a branch unmeasured.)

problem: The correction of D33R-S-2 added to T-MINT that, once a sync has settled a lost answer as accepted, 'a command that mints that kind of id, run again, returns that id, takes the entry off the list and mints nothing'. That rule keys on the kind of id alone, and a `settled` entry holds only the commit, the paths it carried and whether the remote took it. So the next command of that kind run for a different request (a second idea, another change request, another spike) gets back the earlier id and file and mints nothing: the new request is dropped. This lasts until the entry's retention ends (state.retain_runs_days). From the kind alone a program cannot tell a repeat of the same request from a new one.
proposed_resolution: Return the settled id only when the request matches what was minted: the file the command would write, less its id and its times, equals the minted file, or a digest of the request stored in the settled entry matches. Otherwise mint as usual and leave the entry for vsdd status and the briefing to show. Add to proof scenario 30 a different change request filed after the settled lost answer, which gets a new id and a new file.

outcome.what_was_done: T-MINT no longer keys on the kind of id. When a minting push ends `unknown`, the clone record lists the commit with its request: the SHA-256 of the kind of id and of every value the caller gave for the new file, and of nothing the tool adds (the id, a time, the run, the clone, the person). The entries of sync.unknown are now objects {commit, request}, the sync copies the request into the `settled` entry, and the digest is defined once, in record:clone, and computed by one function of package M3 for every minting command, with a test that the same request has the same digest under any id and on any day and that another title or text has another. After its opening sync, which settles every unknown commit, a minting command looks in `settled` for its own request. An entry the remote took is the lost answer: the command returns that id, removes the entry and mints nothing. An entry the remote did not take is removed and the command mints. A command with any other request mints as usual and leaves the entries, so a second idea or change request is never answered with the first one's id. The stored digest was chosen over comparing the file the command would write with the minted one, because it is one function for six commands and needs no list, per kind of file, of the fields to leave out. T-MINT's `unmeasured` cell states what remains: a request worded differently after a lost answer is minted again, and the settled entry stays listed for a person. schema:clone, T-PUSH's `unknown` case, ledger D33-16 and the deliverables of M3 follow. Proof scenario 30 gains a different change request filed after the settled lost answer: it gets a new id and a new file, and vsdd status still lists the entry. No git command is concerned.

where: rewrite/spec/tables/team-delivery-checks.toml (T-BRANCH, runs); rewrite/spec/tables/team-checks.toml (head rule, when a check runs); rewrite/spec/topics/team-delivery.md (Commits made by hand); rewrite/spec/config/team.md (Off)
problem: Two statements written in this correction disagree on when T-BRANCH acts. The head rule of table:team-checks says the hand-commit checks run 'wherever the branch they read has an upstream', which git answers locally. T-BRANCH's runs cell now says it runs 'wherever the story branch is on the remote' and that a listing (`git ls-remote --exit-code`, exit 2 for an absent branch) says whether it is. A builder who follows the row lists the remote for every story this clone holds, in every survey. That includes team use off and local mode, where story branches are never pushed and have no upstream. config/team.md ('Off': nothing waits on the network that did not wait before) and proof scenario 23 do not allow that network call. topics/team-delivery.md restates the upstream form of the condition as well.
proposed_resolution: State the condition once, in T-BRANCH's runs cell. The listing is made only for a story whose closure records `delivery.pushed`, or whose local branch has an upstream (the branch may since have been deleted on the remote). A story branch this clone created and never pushed is not on the remote, so it needs no listing, and with team use off in local mode no listing is made. Have the head rule refer to that cell for the hand-commit checks' condition, and have topics/team-delivery.md link to it instead of restating it. Add to proof scenario 23 or 38 that a survey in local mode runs no ls-remote.

outcome.what_was_done: T-BRANCH's `runs` cell is now the one statement of when the remote is asked about a story branch: only where the story's closure records delivery.pushed or the local branch has an upstream, both read without the network (tracked state, and %(upstream:remotename) of git for-each-ref). Such a branch is looked for on the remote and fetched where it is there; where it is not, nothing arrived. A branch with neither has no push on record and the remote is not asked about it, so a project in local mode makes no network call, and its first push is judged by a fetch as every push is, which finds whatever is there. The head rule of table:team-checks no longer says "wherever the branch they read has an upstream" and refers to each row's `runs` cell; topic:team-delivery and the D33 passages of command:survey and command:story-deliver link to the cell and restate no condition. Two things the git runs showed are corrected with it (2.34.1 and 2.50.1, three rounds each; team-git-facts, facts 19 and 21). git ls-remote matches a pattern at the end of a name: with only keep/refs/heads/story/S-6 on the remote, a listing of refs/heads/story/S-6 exits 0, so the exit status alone does not say that the branch is there. A new head rule has every listing read by the exact ref name, through one function of package M1, and T-HISTORY reads through it as T-BRANCH does. And the upstream stays recorded after the branch is deleted on the remote, where the listing exits 2 and a fetch 128: T-BRANCH gains a fifth blocked case, the branch gone while this clone does not hold the commit delivery.pushed names. Proof scenario 23 asserts no listing of the remote in local mode, and scenario 38 that no listing names a story branch before its first push. Ledger D33-17 follows. One gap seen here and not closed is recorded as the new entry D33-34 for package M4: the listings and fetches the survey makes for held stories have each a time limit but no shared budget, and no row says what the survey does with a story whose branch could not be read.

problem: A story branch would be pushed onto the integration branch. T-HANDOFF pushes 'the story branch to its upstream as a fast-forward'. T-REMOTE reads a branch's push target as its upstream (%(upstream:remotename) %(upstream:remoteref)). Fact 3 names `git worktree add --track -b` as the way that upstream is set. But a story branch is cut from the remote head of the integration branch (team-delivery.md: 'a story's base is the remote head read when its branch is created'), and git gives a branch made that way the integration branch as its upstream. Run in a scratch repository with git 2.50.1: `git worktree add --track -b story/S-1 ../wt shared/develop` gives story/S-1 the upstream `shared refs/heads/develop`. Pushing story/S-1 to that upstream ref was accepted as a fast-forward and moved the remote's develop. Git's default branch.autoSetupMerge does the same without --track. So every checkpoint on a team would put unreviewed story commits on the shared branch, outside a pull request and CI (clause 4f). That breaks T-NEVER ('never pushes to a target branch outside a delivery or a release'), and only a protected branch stops it. A clone with two remotes (a fork layout) has no rule at all for a story branch's first push: T-REMOTE refuses a branch with no upstream.
proposed_resolution: Say that a story branch's push destination is always `<remote of the integration branch's upstream>` plus `refs/heads/story/<id>`. Never use the story branch's recorded upstream ref. The worktree library creates story branches with --no-track. The first push uses `push -u <remote> story/<id>`. T-REMOTE refuses any push of a story branch whose destination ref name differs from the branch name. Correct fact 3: --track sets the start point as upstream. Add a ledger entry for S3's worktree library, which is being built now, and for M3: create story branches without tracking, and push them by explicit refspec. Add a test that the remote's integration branch is unchanged after a checkpoint pushes a story branch.

outcome.what_was_done: T-REMOTE now takes only the remote from an upstream and never a ref: every fetch and push names refs/heads/<branch> on both sides, a story branch is created at a commit id (no upstream), is pushed under its own name to the remote of its target, and gets its own name as upstream at that first push; an upstream that names another ref is refused. T-HANDOFF pushes under the branch's own name and a test asserts that no checkpoint, release of a claim or sync moves the remote's integration branch (also proof scenario 29). The upstream fact was rerun on git 2.34.1 and 2.50.1 and corrected (team-git-facts, fact 4). New ledger entry D33-25 for S3 (on the slice path: keep creating the branch at a commit id, and assert it has no upstream) and M3; D33-13 now fetches the target by its own name and refuses a differing upstream ref.

where: tables/team-checks.toml (the rule 'A check runs only while team use is on'); tables/team-delivery-checks.toml; tables/team-config-keys.toml (team.enabled)
problem: Clause 6 (cope with teammates who commit by hand, without the plugin) is delivered only when team.enabled is true. T-NOTICE, T-BRANCH, T-ITEMS, T-GAP and T-NEVER follow the head rule of team-checks.toml: a check runs only while team use is on. The key's meaning is 'True when more than one clone runs the factory on this repository'. The most common case of clause 6 is one person running the factory while teammates commit by hand. That project correctly leaves team.enabled false, by the key's own definition, and so gets none of these checks. Its hand commits are not listed or made review items. A story branch that holds one may still be rebased, because T-NEVER is a team check.
proposed_resolution: Make the hand-commit checks independent of team.enabled. Run T-NOTICE, T-ITEMS, T-GAP and T-NEVER whenever the target branch has a remote, or always, since the first-parent check needs no remote. Keep only the claim-dependent half of T-BRANCH (commits from another clone) under team use. Say so in the head rule as a third exception beside T-JOIN and T-SOLO, and in team-delivery.md. Add a scenario to proof-team.md with team.enabled false and C committing by hand.

outcome.what_was_done: The five checks of hand commits (T-NOTICE, T-BRANCH, T-ITEMS, T-GAP, T-NEVER) no longer read team.enabled. They run wherever the branch they read has an upstream, which is the only way a teammate reaches the product; with no remote none runs. It is the third exception in the head rule of team-checks and is stated at the head of team-delivery-checks; only T-WAVE and the two claim refusals of T-DELIVERY stay under team use. Proof scenario 38 runs the hand-commit scenarios with team.enabled false. Consequence stated in config/team.md: a project with one clone and a remote now has commits made by hand reviewed.

where: tables/team-checks.toml (T-JOIN, T-SOLO); config/team.md (On and off); topics/state-directory.md (Team use)
problem: T-JOIN and T-SOLO force new behaviour on projects that do not use team use, and they conflict with the existing design. (a) A person working alone who clones the project on a new machine is refused by `vsdd init` and must type `vsdd init --only-clone` in a terminal. D1 says it 'costs you one /vsdd-factory:setup per clone'. state-directory.md says 'A fresh clone: one command mounts the state' and that init 'With a state branch on the remote ... mounts that'. compaction-and-cold-start.md and resume.md describe a fresh clone resuming after setup alone. (b) A solo user who alternates two machines must turn team use on. T-SWITCH refuses that in local delivery mode, so a solo local-mode user cannot use a second machine at all. The old design allowed it: run-lock.md and lock.md say the second machine fetches, rebases and retries. (c) With team use off, `vsdd status --fix` now pushes state and the push stops instead of rebasing. The designer lists (a) as open question 1, but team-use.md, config/team.md and state-directory.md state it as decided.
proposed_resolution: Leave solo mounting as it is. With team.enabled not true, T-JOIN mounts and prints one line: the state was written by another clone, and if that clone is still in use, turn team use on. T-SOLO remains the guard at the push. Alternatively keep T-JOIN and mark it in team-use.md and config/team.md as awaiting the person's answer to open question 1, and do not present it as decided. In either case, say which of the existing statements (D1's cost, state-directory Mounting, compaction-and-cold-start's fresh clone, lock.md 'Two machines') change, and record the change for S1 and S2b in the ledger.

outcome.what_was_done: T-JOIN no longer refuses while team use is off: vsdd init mounts as it did before D33 (decision D1 holds) and returns a notice that another clone wrote the state, which setup shows. The flag --only-clone is gone. T-SOLO stays as the guard, in the checkpoint's push and vsdd sync only (vsdd status --fix does not start pushing with team use off), names two ways on (turn team use on; or, for one person who moved machines, combine with git and push), and lets a clone join by itself when a team was formed around it. The one statement of the earlier design that changes with team use off, the unasked rebase and retry at the state push, is named in the Team use passages of state-commits.md, run-lock.md and records/lock.md. Ledger entries D33-14 (S1, M6) and D33-3 (S2b, M1) carry it.

problem: Clause 4c requires that 'a run starts from what the team has already pushed, not from a stale local copy'. T-FRESH lets a run start when the remote cannot be reached, if this clone already holds all its claims, marked refreshed: false. Such a run starts from a local copy that may be stale. It cannot see a teammate's settlement of the unit's decisions, a take-over of the claim, or a change to factory.toml such as a raised team.min_plugin. The design states this allowance as decided. It is not among the open questions, although it relaxes a clause the user wrote. Git's limits allow a refusal here, which is what the clause asks for.
proposed_resolution: Default to the clause: with the outcome unreachable, refuse every survey that would write tracked state, and keep only report-only runs. If offline continuation is wanted, make it an open question for the person, and mark it in team-use.md as an exception to 4c awaiting the answer. Fix D33R-F-5 in either case.

outcome.what_was_done: T-FRESH now refuses every survey unless the opening sync ended synced, also for a run whose claims the clone holds: there is no offline continuation and no refreshed field. Clause 4c is the user's and is kept as written; team-sync.md says what it costs. Proof scenario 5.

where: tables/claim-checks.toml (T-SETTLE); topics/team-records.md (A decision opened on one clone and settled on another)
problem: The guarantee 'No run ever acts on a settlement that a sync has not confirmed, so the two answers cannot both take effect' (T-SETTLE: 'every survey syncs before it reads decisions') is false under T-FRESH. A decision typed in a session is settled on the clone with no network. If clone A is offline, its person settles finding.<story> for a story A holds while B's person settles it differently and pushes. A's next survey ends unreachable, starts anyway because A holds the claim, and reads A's own unpublished settlement as settled. A's run acts on it. A's later sync sets that settlement aside, but its effect has already happened. Proof scenario 6 tests only a merge decision, and delivery needs the network, so the gap is not exercised.
proposed_resolution: In T-SETTLE and the survey: a settlement listed in the clone record's sync.unpublished counts as open, not settled, for every survey whose outcome is not synced. The run returns needs_human, naming the unpublished settlement, until a sync confirms it. Add to proof-team.md: A offline settles finding.<story>, B settles it differently online, and no work on A's answer reaches tracked state.

outcome.what_was_done: T-SETTLE: a settlement counts only once the remote holds it. The function that settles lists the decision in sync.unpublished of the clone record under the lock it settles under, the sync removes it when the commit is contained in the remote's head, and until then every gate, survey, route and delivery reads the decision as open; status and the briefing show it as settled here, not yet published. Proof scenarios 25 (finding.<story> settled while the remote is out of reach) and 26 (during a live run). Ledger entry D33-28 (M3, S4).

where: topics/team-sync.md (When someone edits state by hand); tables/team-checks.toml (T-INCOMING unmeasured); topics/state-commits.md (What flush does, step 4)
problem: The remedy the design names for what it cannot measure would stop the factory. team-sync.md and T-INCOMING say that 'a repository that needs more protects the state branch and requires signed commits there'. The flush commits state 'without signing' (state-commits.md step 4). The sync's merge commit, the claim commit of T-PUBLISH and the mint commit are built with commit-tree, and the design says nothing about signing them. On a remote that requires signed commits on the state branch, every state push is declined with [remote rejected]. T-REMOTE then reports refused and does not retry, so no claim can be taken and team use cannot run.
proposed_resolution: Choose one. (a) With team use on, the flush and every commit the sync builds sign when the clone's git configuration asks for it (commit.gpgsign and a signing key), with a time limit and no prompt, and doctor checks signing. Add a probe for signing inside a hook and a detached job. (b) Drop the signed-commit remedy from team-sync.md and T-INCOMING, and say that a state branch requiring signed commits is not supported. Either way, add a ledger entry for S2b, because the flush is built.

outcome.what_was_done: The remedy is dropped. State commits stay unsigned on a team, as decision D2 decided, and team-sync.md (A remote with its own rules) now says what the factory needs of the repository: direct pushes of unsigned commits to the state branch, so a rule that requires a signature or a pull request there declines every push and is not supported; such a push ends refused with git's line (T-PUSH) and vsdd doctor says what is needed. The other option, signing, was not taken because it reverses D2. No ledger entry for S2b: the flush does not change.

problem: T-JOIN says `vsdd init --only-clone` is a flag 'which only a person may run', but nothing makes it person-only. init is run by the setup skill, so the main session's model calls it. HUMAN_ONLY (tables/callers.toml, matched on the longest subcommand) has 'init --fresh' but not 'init --only-clone'. D33-4 adds only sync, claim release and claim take. A model that meets the `solo` answer can run --only-clone itself. That mounts a second clone's state with team use off, which is exactly the unannounced second writer that T-JOIN exists to stop.
proposed_resolution: Extend D33-4, or add an entry for H6 and M1: add 'init --only-clone' to HUMAN_ONLY. Pin it in the lint. Add a case: the main session's `vsdd init --only-clone` is refused by gate-guard, and the same flag typed in a terminal mounts the state. As claim take does, the command should also refuse a call that carries a caller marker or has no terminal.

outcome.what_was_done: Fixed by removing what needed protecting: vsdd init has no --only-clone flag any more (D33R-F-3), so there is nothing a model could run in a person's place. D33-4 says that only claim take joins the person-only list.

where: topics/state-commits.md (Team use: 'it holds flush.lock'); ledger entry D33-3
problem: The sync is specified as holding flush.lock, with no limit on what it does while holding it. Every writer of tracked records takes the same lock with a 3-second wait in the built store (store.locked; decisions.py settle_decision, cycles.py, runs.py, gate_evidence.py). The flush waits 5 seconds. The sync makes git calls with a 60-second time limit each (gitrun.py), and a push can be tried five times. A sync that holds flush.lock across the network therefore makes concurrent writers fail with StoreBusy while it runs. These include the settlement in the decisions rule, which has a 4-second deadline and fails closed, and evidence and run-record writes in a live run. T-SETTLE runs exactly that case: a detached sync during a live run.
proposed_resolution: Say that the sync holds flush.lock only for the local steps: flush, building the combined or isolated commit, and the fast-forward of the mount. The fetch and the push run outside it, because a push of a commit id needs no lock. After the push, the mount is moved under the lock again. Put this in team-sync.md and D33-3, with a test: a settlement typed while a sync waits on a slow remote succeeds.

outcome.what_was_done: command:sync now gives the order of the sync and says that flush.lock is held for the three local steps only and never across a listing, a fetch or a push; a local step that finds the mount's head moved repeats; whole syncs of one clone are serialised by local/sync.lock. state-commits.md and ledger entry D33-3 say the same, with the test (a settlement and a closure write succeed while a slow remote holds a sync's fetch open; proof scenario 14).

problem: The sync's outcomes do not fully map to what may run. (a) T-FRESH names unreachable, diverged, blocked and refused, but not unpushed or busy. It says what a run on claims already held does only for unreachable. (b) T-PUBLISH says that after acceptance 'the mount is moved to it'. The claim commit is built on the remote's head, and the mount may hold commits that were never pushed: a PreCompact flush in the middle of a run, an earlier unpushed outcome, or a mint inside a live run (T-MINT). A fast-forward is then impossible. The step needed is to combine with the claim commit, which the text does not say. T-MINT does not say its commit is built alone on the remote's head, as T-PUBLISH's is. (c) Scenario 4 expects the checkpoint to end 'unpushed' with the remote out of reach, but sync.md defines that case as unreachable, because the fetch fails first.
proposed_resolution: Give T-FRESH one line per outcome (synced, unpushed, unreachable, diverged, blocked, refused, busy), each saying both whether new claims are allowed and whether a run on held claims may start. In T-PUBLISH and T-MINT, say that the commit holds only the claim or the new file, is built on the remote's head, and is merged into the mount by the sync's merge, built without touching the mount and then fast-forwarded. Make scenario 4's end condition match sync.md.

outcome.what_was_done: T-FRESH has one rule for every outcome (no run unless synced) and command:sync lists each outcome with what a person does. T-PUBLISH and T-MINT build an isolated commit on the remote's head, never write the file in the mount first, and the mount takes the accepted commit by a fast-forward or through T-COMBINE; the mounted branch is never moved to a commit that does not contain its head. Scenario 4 of the old proof is now scenario 5 and expects unreachable.

problem: T-HOLD runs 'At every sync' and ends 'A run of this clone on that unit', releasing its lock. That includes the detached sync that the decisions rule starts from a hook. team-use.md justifies `vsdd sync` as a separate command because `status --fix` 'also releases locks ..., which a job started by a hook must not do'. The lock is scoped to the repository and branch, not to the unit. So ending 'the run on that unit' ends a whole wave run because one of its stories was taken over. T-CLAIM's write-path refusal (claim_not_held) already stops the run from writing to that unit.
proposed_resolution: Have T-HOLD, in a sync started outside a survey or checkpoint, only set aside and record the loss. The run's own later writes then fail through claim_not_held, and its checkpoint releases the unit. Only the survey and checkpoint syncs end a run, and only one that works on nothing but the lost unit. A wave run continues with its other stories.

outcome.what_was_done: T-HOLD ends no run and releases no lock. It withholds, sets aside and reports the loss; a live run meets claim_not_held at its next tracked write to the lost unit (T-CLAIM) and ends at its own checkpoint, and a run with other units goes on with them. So a sync a hook started changes no lock, which keeps the reason team-use.md gives for vsdd sync true.

problem: The claim that nothing waits rests on two unstated limits. (a) The survey is a foreground command, not a job. Its opening sync plus a claim push, at 60 s per git call (gitrun.py) and with up to five push attempts, can pass the Bash tool's 2-minute default. A call past its timeout is moved to the background and killed at the step's final response (platform-proven-2, item 43), possibly between the accepted claim push and the lock or the mount move. (b) GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 stops only git's own terminal prompt. ssh host-key and passphrase prompts, and credential helpers that open a window or a browser, are outside it and are bounded only by the time limit. Fact 8 was checked only for a missing remote.
proposed_resolution: State the network time limit of one sync, and choose it so that a survey stays inside the Bash default with its other work. Alternatively make the opening sync a job the survey re-attaches to. Run the tool's git calls with ssh in batch mode (core.sshCommand with BatchMode=yes, unless the person set their own) and with credential helpers non-interactive. Add a probe with an ssh remote that wants a passphrase, from a hook and from a Bash call.

outcome.what_was_done: command:sync states the limits: 30 seconds for each network call, 60 for all of a sync's calls inside a foreground command, and T-FRESH gives the claim 30 more, which keeps the survey inside the Bash default; a clone too far behind runs vsdd sync, which is a job. Every network call runs with standard input from /dev/null in a session of its own, GIT_ASKPASS and core.askPass empty, SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never, credential.interactive=false, and the whole process group is killed at the limit (team-sync.md, Credentials; ledger entry D33-29). Checked against a throwaway sshd with git 2.34.1 and OpenSSH 8.9 (team-git-facts, fact 10); M1 keeps it as a test and the proof has it as scenario 16.

where: topics/team-sync.md (The git facts this rests on); commands/doctor.md (Team use)
problem: The sync rests on `git merge-tree --write-tree`, which first appeared in git 2.38. The facts were checked on macOS with git 2.50.1 only, while the design supports macOS and Linux (platform.md: Linux open). Ubuntu 22.04 LTS ships git 2.34, which cannot run the combine. The design leaves 'the oldest git it supports' to M1, so whether team use works on a supported Linux is not known until M1 is built.
proposed_resolution: State the git floor in team-sync.md now: at least 2.38 for merge-tree --write-tree, checking the exit status and output form named in fact 5 against that version. Have doctor and T-VERSION refuse team use below it. Run the nine facts once on a Linux git at the floor, as the platform probes do.

outcome.what_was_done: The floor is stated: git 2.34 (T-VERSION), refused below by the preflight, which the sync, init, status and doctor share. It is 2.34 and not 2.38 because the sync no longer uses git merge-tree --write-tree: it decides each path itself and merges a text file alone with git merge-file. All fourteen facts were run on Linux with git 2.34.1, and all but the ssh and askpass part of fact 10 on macOS with 2.50.1 as well (topics/team-git-facts.md); M1 keeps them as tests that CI runs at the floor.

where: topics/team-claims.md (A wave on a team); tables/claim-scopes.toml (story.<id>, cycle)
problem: Clause 4a asks that two people can work on different stories 'or different stages' without blocking each other. (a) team-claims.md says a wave run 'takes each story it starts'. claim-scopes.toml says the wave's survey claims 'each story it returns as a unit'. The wave survey returns every free story, so one wave run claims the whole wave at once and a teammate can take none of its stories until that run's checkpoint. (b) Every cycle-level workflow (spec, plan, feature, wave, verify, release, multi, ingest, maintain) takes the one cycle claim. In one cycle, an amendment cannot run while another clone drives the wave. That may be the right choice, but it is not stated as a choice against 4a.
proposed_resolution: Make the two texts agree. Prefer claiming only the stories the run will start (up to its story limit), and keep the rest free for a standalone story run elsewhere. In team-use.md's 'What was decided', say which stages run in parallel on a team, which are serialized by the cycle claim, and why.

outcome.what_was_done: The story scope's `when` now claims the batch the run's first call of runStories() will start: the free stories among the first N units that call would start, N being the smaller of limits.stories_per_wave_run and the agent fit, which the survey works out with the formula and the reserve of runStories(), counting its own limits.step_attempts agents as spent. The survey returns N to the script as the limit stories_per_run, so the script cannot start a story outside the claimed batch, and a test runs both on a table of limits and asserts that the stories started are the ones claimed or already held. T-WAVE says the same by reference and states the one residue in its unmeasured cell: a script other than wave that spends agents between its survey and its first batch can lower the fit, and a story claimed and not started then stays claimed until that run's checkpoint. New ledger entry D33-32 (B4a keeps the reserve where the survey can read it; M2 builds the function). Proof scenario 33 gains the case in which the agent budget fits one story.

where: topics/team-claims.md (What can be claimed); tables/claim-scopes.toml (header and the open row)
problem: The rule 'a workflow that takes the lock takes a claim; spike, discover and a report-only maintain, which take no lock, take none' is stated twice: in team-claims.md and in the header of claim-scopes.toml. The open row of the same table contradicts it: the open claim is taken by 'the discover assess checkpoint'.
proposed_resolution: State the rule once, in claim-scopes.toml, with the stated exception: discover takes the open claim when its assess checkpoint opens a cycle. Have team-claims.md link to it.

outcome.what_was_done: The row of the parallel-work table now reads 'They take no claim for their run; the rule and its one exception are in table:work-claim-scopes', so the rule and its exception (opening a cycle takes `open`, discover included) stay in the head of that table alone.

problem: T-CLAIM refuses 'A write to a closure record ... for a unit whose claim in the mount does not name this clone'. The head rule says 'Cannot measure is a failure'. Read together, a unit with no claim file at all is refused, which covers the standing closures of spike, discover and a report-only maintain, workflows that take no claim. On a team those workflows' checkpoints would fail with claim_not_held.
proposed_resolution: Word the clause as: refused when a claim file covering the unit exists and names another clone, or when the unit's workflow takes a claim and this clone holds none. Units of claimless workflows are written as on one clone. Add the passing case for a report-only maintain.

outcome.what_was_done: T-CLAIM's write refusal now has two cases: a claim on the scope stands and names another clone; or the run's workflow takes that scope and this clone does not hold it. A workflow that takes no claim is refused in the first case only. The cycle scope no longer covers the units and decisions of spike and discover.

where: tables/team-checks.toml (T-COMBINE); topics/team-sync.md (How two clones' pushes combine)
problem: (a) T-COMBINE treats a path as a code-written record when it is in 'class control and the classes inside it'. Other code-written classes are outside control: holdout-evaluations, research-inputs and requests (write = code in the shipped classes.toml). These fall to git's text merge, which can combine two JSON records line by line into one that neither clone wrote. (b) notes.json, the one record team-sync.md says several clones write with no claim, keeps the remote's version and sets the other aside. That drops a note a person asked to keep from shared state, although the same file says 'A person's words are never dropped by a program'.
proposed_resolution: Classify by the class's write mode from classes.toml (code versus agent or person), not by containment in control. Merge notes.json as a union of notes up to its cap of five, with the overflow set aside, or make each note its own file.

outcome.what_was_done: T-COMBINE classifies each path by the write mode of its class in the shipped class table, not by lying under control, so holdout evaluations, research inputs, requests, ideas and spikes are records too. notes.json has a rule of its own: the remote's notes followed by those this clone added since the merge base, cut to the cap from the oldest end, with nothing set aside (proof scenario 13). One file per note was not taken: notes.json is a built record on the slice path.

problem: README rule 5 says to be machine-readable where a program reads the table. T-HOLD reads 'the covers of each scope ([[table:claim-scopes]])', but covers is prose ('The story's branch on the remote; its closure record; the opening of its decisions; ...'). The file column mixes a path with prose in parentheses. The schema lists scope ids story.<id>, cycle, spec, open and open.hotfix, while the table has four rows and gives open.hotfix only as a parenthetical file name.
proposed_resolution: Give each row machine-readable fields: covers_paths (globs relative to .factory/), covers_acts (decision kinds whose opening it covers, cycle creation, wave moves) and file plus a standing_file. Add open.hotfix as a row or a variants field. Leave the prose in why.

outcome.what_was_done: Each scope now has fields a program reads: file (a path only), workflows, held, covers_paths with not_paths, covers_new with not_new (files only the holder may create, which is how a decision is opened by the holder and settled by anyone), covers_branch and cycle_kinds. The prose covers column is gone, and T-CLAIM, T-HOLD and T-RELEASE read those fields. open.hotfix is a row of its own.

problem: T-ORDER makes follows universal: each decision record names 'the decision of its kind that was latest when it was opened'. 'The latest decision of a kind is the one no other record follows; two such records are reported as a state problem and the route answers human'. Decisions of per-story kinds (merge, finding.<story>, blocked.<story>) are opened legitimately at the same time by two clones holding two stories. Both follow the same earlier record, which gives two heads and a false state problem wherever anything asks for the latest of such a kind.
proposed_resolution: Store a follows chain only for kinds opened under one exclusive claim (spec, brief, plan, release, ideas), and the spec link only on a merge decision. Say that per-story kinds have no 'latest' and that no code asks for one.

outcome.what_was_done: T-ORDER: follows is stored only by a decision whose id carries no subject; a decision about a story or a wave stores none, because two clones open such decisions at once and nothing asks for the latest of them; a merge decision stores spec. Open cycles are ordered by kind and id. Proof scenario 27 opens two merge decisions at the same moment and expects no state problem. Ledger entry D33-7.

problem: T-HANDOFF copies the red record (commit, frozen files, tests, criteria) into the story's closure, whose cap is 16,000 bytes, beside its stages, verdict, flaky list and the new delivery fields. A story with many tests or frozen files can pass the cap. T-HANDOFF then refuses the release, and the story can never be handed on. Clause 3's 'continues from what has been pushed' then fails for exactly the larger stories.
proposed_resolution: Carry the red copy in a record of its own, for example cycles/<cycle>/units/story.<id>.red.json, in class control, with its own cap sized from the evidence record's. Have the evidence lookup read that file.

outcome.what_was_done: The red record travels as a tracked record of its own, cycles/<cycle>/red/<story>.json, with the fields, the schema and the cap of the evidence record it copies, so a record that could be written locally always fits; it is no longer inside the closure. The evidence lookup reads it (records/evidence.md, evidence-lookup.md, T-HANDOFF; ledger entry D33-11). The path is not under units/, where the closure store would read it as a closure.

problem: The adversary 'reads that commit's diff' for each hand:<12 hex> item, but it has no shell (READ, REPORT, SPAWN, RESULT) and is given only 'the latest diff patch'. Nothing says who writes one patch per hand commit, where, or how it is given. The wave's range diff mixes the hand commit with delivered stories.
proposed_resolution: Have the gate that lists hand_commits (T-NOTICE) write one diff patch per hand commit beside its evidence. Add the patch path to each hand: item in the review's given inputs, and say so in T-ITEMS and in the item's text.

outcome.what_was_done: T-NOTICE has the gate write the patch of each hand commit beside its evidence as hand.<sha12>.patch, T-BRANCH does the same for a story branch, and T-ITEMS gives each hand: item to the reviewer with that path. The adversary's passage says it reads that file. Ledger entry D33-23.

where: packaging/proof-team.md; tables/team-checks.toml (header: 'the proof runs the check on two clones')
problem: The head rule says the proof runs every check on two clones. Several checks are in no scenario: T-INCOMING (C edits a record on the state branch by hand, the case clause 6 also implies for state), T-WHO (a clone with no git identity), T-LOCAL (a path under local/, or an absolute path in factory.toml), T-GAP (a hand commit that changes specified behaviour) and T-DELIVERY's adoption of a pull request merged outside the tool.
proposed_resolution: Add one scenario for each, with its end condition. Alternatively reword the head rule to say which checks only the package's own cases hold.

outcome.what_was_done: The proof now has 39 scenarios and names in brackets the checks each runs; every one of the 28 checks is run by at least one. Added among others: a record edited by hand on the state branch (10), no identity (21), one machine's data (22), spec-gap from a hand commit (34), a pull request merged outside the tool (37).

where: packaging/proof-team.md (What it gates); skills/setup.md (Team use); config/team.md
problem: proof-team.md says team use 'is not offered by setup ... until this proof passes', but no mechanism holds that. setup.md and config/team.md make setup show the two lines that turn it on, and they are built with K1 and M1 before M5.
proposed_resolution: Make setup's team lines part of M5's delivery (or of a step after M5), and say so in the build plan. Alternatively drop the sentence and let the user documents carry the warning.

outcome.what_was_done: The sentence has a mechanism: the passage of the setup skill that offers team use is delivered by package M5 once the proof passes, K1 builds setup without it (ledger entry D33-30), and the documents packages come after M5 in the order of work. proof-team.md, skills/setup.md, config/team.md and the build plan say so.

problem: Clause 4f says stories reach the shared branch 'through pull requests and CI'. T-SWITCH and T-DELIVERY require delivery.mode = pr but accept delivery.ci = none. With that setting, a team's pull requests merge without the factory waiting for any CI.
proposed_resolution: Either refuse team use with delivery.ci = none, naming the line, or state in team-delivery.md why a team may run without CI, which clause 5 would leave to the repository. In that case, list it as a point for the person.

outcome.what_was_done: T-SWITCH refuses to turn team use on, and T-DELIVERY refuses a delivery on a team, while delivery.ci is not required. Clause 4f says pull requests and CI, and team-delivery.md gives the reason CI is required: on a team the target moves under teammates' merges, and the pull request's checks are what measures the merged result before it lands.

where: topics/team-use.md (clause table, row 2); tables/team-checks.toml (header rule on Git hosts); ledger entry D33-18
problem: (a) Row 2 says the shipped Python imports no network module, 'so git is the only way out'. But pr mode, which team use requires, runs the host's command-line tool. notify.command can run anything, and T-DELIVERY reads pull-request state from the host.
