(b) The head rule says 'Nothing a check reads names a Git host, a vendor or a remote', yet T-DELIVERY reads through the delivery library, which is bound to one vendor until D33-18 is built. D33-18 then proposes 'one configuration key' naming the implementation, which conflicts with that rule and with team-config-keys' 'No key holds ... the name of a Git host'. (c) T-SWITCH checks only delivery.mode, so a team on a host with no implementation fails at its first delivery instead of at the switch.
proposed_resolution: Reword row 2: coordination goes only through git, and delivery also reaches the host's pull-request service through one module (D33-18). State in the head rule that the host module is the one exception and that no other check reads a host. Say where the implementation key lives (delivery, not team), or detect the host from the module's own probe. Have T-SWITCH and doctor ask the module whether it can serve the remote.

outcome.what_was_done: Row 2 of the clause table now says that claims, decisions, state and hand-off travel only as fetches and pushes of branches, and that delivery opens and merges the pull request clause 4f asks for through one host module that carries nothing else. The head rule of team-checks names that module as the one exception. There is no configuration key for it, so nothing a program reads names a host: the tool asks the module whether it can serve the remote, and T-SWITCH, T-DELIVERY and the doctor refuse or report when it cannot (ledger entry D33-18, rewritten).

problem: Clause 7 says the multi-repository layout is not meant by D33. multi-repo.md nevertheless asserts how the two combine ('The two combine at the hub: the state branch, and so the claims, are the hub's ...'). No check, package duty or proof scenario backs this, and member repositories' hand commits, story branches and remotes under T-NOTICE, T-BRANCH and T-REMOTE are not designed.
proposed_resolution: Replace the passage with: team use with the multi-repository layout is outside D33 and is not supported until it is designed and proved. Alternatively raise it as an open question.

outcome.what_was_done: multi-repo.md now says that decision D33 covers one repository only and that how team use combines with a hub is not designed and not proved. It is enforced: T-SWITCH refuses to turn team use on while factory.toml holds a [[repo]] entry (proof scenario 19).

where: topics/run-lock.md (A story branch on the remote; Team use); topics/resume.md
problem: The step-3 survey plan, which S3 is building now, includes 'adoption of a remote story branch and the conflict unit'. On a team that rule 'gives way to the claim', and a remote branch with unknown commits becomes T-BRANCH's hand commits instead of a conflict. No ledger entry tells S3 to keep adoption replaceable, and none tells M2 or M4 to replace it. M4's delivers does not name it either.
proposed_resolution: Add a D33 ledger entry for S3 (on the slice path) to keep 'adoptable or owned elsewhere' behind one function of the survey that takes the claim state as an argument, changing nothing on one clone. Add it to M4's delivers (or M2's) to replace that function's team branch with the claim and T-BRANCH.

outcome.what_was_done: New ledger entry D33-26 for S3 and M4: adoption is built as one function that is given the story's claim state, and M4 supplies the team branches; M4's delivers names it and run-lock.md says why. It is not marked as on the slice path: the plans leave adoption of a remote story branch for the widening (step-3 survey.md, step-4 survey-2.md).

where: ledger entries D33-19 and D33-7 (rewrite/findings/triage/d33.json, outcomes/d33.json)
problem: Ledger bookkeeping. D33-19's outcome says 'with S2c's owner', but its triage lists only M1 and M2, so S2c's by-package list has no D33 entry, although S2c owns the briefing and the status report. D33-7's where names cycles.py ('cycles_open sorts by opened'), but its resolution addresses only decision ordering. cycles_open still orders two tracked records by time, which T-ORDER refuses.
proposed_resolution: Add S2c to D33-19's packages. Extend D33-7's resolution to cycles_open, for example ordering by the main cycle and then hotfix cycles by kind, or saying the order is only for display, and give it a test.

outcome.what_was_done: D33-19 is triaged to S2c as well as M6 and M2. D33-7 now covers cycles_open (ordered by kind and id) with a test, and is triaged to S2a, S4 and M3.

problem: sync.md makes `vsdd sync` 'A job command keyed sync', but long-commands.md, which lists the commands that run as jobs and defines the key as 'a hash of the command, its subject and the commit', neither lists sync nor allows a key without a subject or commit. long-commands.md has no Team use passage.
proposed_resolution: Add sync to the list in long-commands.md with its key rule (command only, so a second call attaches), in a Team use passage. Add a ledger entry for G1's job layer.

outcome.what_was_done: long-commands.md has a Team use passage that lists vsdd sync as a job with its key rule: the command and the name of the state branch, with no commit. No ledger entry for G1 was needed: the built job layer already allows a key with an empty commit and requires only a subject, which the state branch's name is (jobs.py, job_key and _spec_problem).

where: packaging/build-plan.md (Order of work, items 6 and 7); registry.d/d33.toml (M1)
problem: (a) Item 6 says 'T1 is therefore built before M1', but item 7, which comes after item 6, lists T1 among the operator tools, so the order is self-contradictory. (b) M1 is large for one builder. It carries the whole sync engine (fetch, incoming checks, merge-tree combine by path class, isolated commits, the push loop) plus eight checks, the clone record, the loader keys, init with --only-clone, doctor, status and briefing lines, and seven and a half ledger entries. The precedent D31R-F-13 flagged F2 for less. T-FRESH, which M1 builds, needs claims, which M2 builds.
proposed_resolution: Move T1 into item 6 ahead of M1, or drop T1 from M1's dependencies and give the doctor lines to a later package. Split M1: one package for the sync engine and T-COMBINE, T-INCOMING and T-REMOTE, and one for the setting, the clone record, T-JOIN, T-SOLO, T-VERSION, T-LOCAL, init, doctor, status and briefing. Move T-FRESH's claim clause to M2.

outcome.what_was_done: The dependency on T1 is dropped: package M6 delivers one preflight function and T1 prints its lines when T1 is built (D33-22), and the build plan says so. M1 is split by adding package M6 (settings, the clone record, joining, the preflight and the report lines), built first, so M1 is the sync alone; a new id was used instead of renaming M1, so no brief or ledger entry had to move. T-FRESH has no claim clause any more, so M1 needs nothing of M2.

where: topics/team-delivery.md; topics/team-records.md; config/team.md; topics/team-use.md; tables/team-delivery-checks.toml; tables/team-checks.toml; tables/claim-checks.toml
problem: README rule 1, one fact in one place, is broken in several places. 'Local delivery remains for a project with no remote, for a project with one clone that chooses it, and for the thin slice' appears word for word in team-delivery.md and T-DELIVERY. The definition of a hand commit is in team-delivery.md and in the header of team-delivery-checks.toml. The table of where each act is recorded (team-records.md) restates T-WHO's refuses cell. The list of what stays on the machine is in config/team.md, team-records.md and T-LOCAL. The refusal of absolute paths in factory.toml is in config/team.md and T-LOCAL. The detached-sync settlement is in T-SETTLE, team-records.md and rules/decisions.md. 'No claim expires because git has no liveness' is in six files. team-use.md says each fact is 'in the file the table names, and nowhere else'.
proposed_resolution: Keep each fact in its check row (or in the one topic named), and replace the other statements with a link and a reason. For example, team-delivery.md keeps why local delivery stays and links T-DELIVERY for when.

outcome.what_was_done: T-TAKEOVER is the one statement that no claim expires and no program decides a holder is gone. topics/team-claims.md and topics/team-use.md now give only the reason (git has no notion of a live clone, two clocks cannot be compared) and name the row; records/work-claim.md says only that `at` decides nothing and that how a claim ends is T-TAKEOVER's and T-RELEASE's; commands/claim-take.md links instead of restating. A search of every D33 file for the fact finds it in T-TAKEOVER only.

problem: 'Claim' already means a fixer's claim about a finding: schema:claim, and claim_checks in the adversary's review data, the story and wave scripts and prelude-converge. The record was named work-claim to avoid that, but the table claim-checks, the check T-CLAIM, the table claim-scopes and the commands `vsdd claim take` and `vsdd claim release` reuse the bare word. claim-checks (checks of work claims) and claim_checks (a reviewer's checks of fixer claims) are near-identical names for different things, which builders and reviewers will confuse.
proposed_resolution: Use work-claim throughout the new names: tables work-claim-scopes and work-claim-checks, the check T-WORK-CLAIM or T-HOLDER, and commands `vsdd work take` and `vsdd work release`, or keep the commands and rename only the tables. Update the glossary entry.

outcome.what_was_done: The two tables are renamed work-claim-checks and work-claim-scopes, the status field is work_claims, and the glossary says how the two senses are told apart. Not taken: renaming the commands vsdd claim take and vsdd claim release and the check T-CLAIM. No command or check of the other sense exists, so they cannot be confused, and the glossary says that in commands and T- names the word means a work claim.

problem: The record of D33 shortens clause 4 to labels ('parallel work, no double work, current state (...), shared decisions, attribution, ... matching setups') and drops the user's definitions that the design is mapped against: 'different stories, or different stages, without blocking each other or corrupting shared state'; 'everyone can see who is working on what, and two machines cannot both take the same story, wave or specification change'; 'can be seen and answered by a teammate on another machine'; 'which person started a run, approved a specification, settled a decision or merged'; 'a compatible plugin version and the same project settings'. A decision record is the fixed text later reviews check against, and the labels are weaker than the clauses.
proposed_resolution: Write clause 4's seven items into Decided as the user gave them, one short sentence each, keeping the rest of the record.

outcome.what_was_done: The D33 record now gives the eight clauses, and the seven items of clause 4, in the user's words.

problem: The design tells a lost race from a remote's rule by git's reason text, and git does not give that distinction. T-REMOTE says a push refused 'for a reason other than "fetch first"' is not retried and ends `refused`, as 'a rule of the remote that only a person can change'. T-PUBLISH retries only on 'fetch first', and any other failure means 'no claim and no run'. commands/sync.md repeats 'from the fetch on "fetch first"'. T-MINT repeats after 'a refused push'. topics/team-sync.md fact 1 says '[remote rejected]' marks a remote rule, 'so the two are told apart'. Tested with git 2.50.1 on a local bare repository and two clones. 'fetch first' appears only when the remote had already moved before the pushing clone connected. When two pushes are truly concurrent, both clients see the same advertised head, and the loser gets `[remote rejected] (failed to update ref)`, with 'cannot lock ref ... is at X but expected Y' on stderr. That happened in 40 rounds out of 40 with no hook, and again with a pre-receive hook that held both connections open. A rule-declined push shows `[remote rejected] (pre-receive hook declined)`. So under the rule as written, the loser of every real race is reported as blocked by a remote rule and is never retried. Two checkpoints at once leave one clone `refused`. A claim race for two different stories leaves the loser with no claim and no run, when it should have retried. The loser of a claim race for the same story does not name the holder, so proof scenario 1's end condition fails. Exclusivity still holds; the retry and the reported cause do not.
proposed_resolution: Classify every refused push by measurement, never by its reason string. After any refusal, fetch the branch. If the remote head is no longer the commit the push was built on, the push lost a race: repeat from the fetch (T-PUBLISH, T-MINT, the sync). If the head is unchanged, the remote declined it: report `refused` with git's line. Correct team-sync fact 1, and add a fact for `[remote rejected] (failed to update ref)` in a concurrent push. M1's test makes the race deterministic with a pre-receive hook that sleeps, and asserts that the loser retries.

outcome.what_was_done: New check T-PUSH: no push is judged by the reason git prints. After any push that did not report success the tool fetches and compares commits: contained in the remote's head is accepted; a remote head other than the one the push was built on is a lost race, repeated from the fetch; an unchanged head is refused with git's line. T-PUBLISH, T-MINT and the sync use it. Reproduced with git 2.34.1 and 2.50.1: the loser of 20 simultaneous pushes of 20 got [remote rejected] (failed to update ref) (team-git-facts, fact 1). Proof scenarios 1 to 3 make the race and the declined push happen every time with a hook on the bare repository.

problem: T-PUBLISH treats every failed push as 'no claim and no run', and its `unmeasured` cell says 'Nothing: the remote's answer to the push is the measurement'. The answer can be lost after the remote has acted on the push. Tested: a bare remote whose post-receive hook takes 5 s, and a client push run under a 2 s time limit, as the built helper (gitrun.py) runs every git call with a time limit. The client's push timed out, yet the remote branch held the client's claim commit. The same happens when a connection drops after the ref update. The clone then holds a claim it believes it lacks. For a `cycle` claim that blocks every other clone's wave, plan, verify and release in that cycle. `vsdd status --fix` removes only a run claim 'whose run has ended without a checkpoint', and this run never began. For T-MINT the command reports failure for an id the remote accepted. Running it again mints a second number, which leaves two change requests or two fix stories for one request.
proposed_resolution: Measure the outcome whenever the answer did not arrive (a timeout, a dropped connection, any failure the refetch of D33R-S-1 does not explain). Fetch and test `git merge-base --is-ancestor <pushed commit> <remote head>`. If the commit is contained, the claim or id is held, and the command proceeds or returns it. If the fetch fails too, record the commit as `outcome_unknown` in the clone record and refuse new claims until a sync settles it. The briefing shows it. `status --fix` releases a claim of this clone that no run record names. Change both `unmeasured` cells to say this.

outcome.what_was_done: (a) T-RELEASE: a full sync now also removes an `open` or `open.hotfix` claim of this clone when the mount holds no cycle record of the scope's kinds that the remote lacks, which is the case of a lost answer and of a command that died before it wrote the record. No opening can be in progress then, because a command that takes a claim, mints an id or opens a cycle holds local/sync.lock for its whole act (command:sync, step 1), and the file lock is released when a process dies. T-PUBLISH's unmeasured cell is corrected to match. (b) The sync result gains `settled`: each commit that left sync.unknown, what it carried and whether the remote had taken it; the clone record keeps the list (record:clone, schema:clone) and vsdd status and the briefing show it. T-MINT goes one step past the report, so that it is a program and not a person that prevents the duplicate: a command that mints that kind of id, run again after its answer was lost and the id accepted, returns that id and mints nothing. Proof scenarios 4 and 30 are extended.

problem: Nothing detects that the state branch was rewound, force-pushed or deleted. The design's own rule, 'cannot measure is a failure', is not applied to the state branch: T-NOTICE covers only the target branch. Tested: a third copy force-pushed the state branch back past A's claim. On B, `git fetch upstream state` exited 0 and printed '(forced update)'. `git merge-tree --write-tree` of B's state and the rewound remote exited 0, and its tree held the dropped claim again, so the next sync silently undoes the rewind. A clone that fetched only after the rewind saw no claim and could claim the same story: double work. A deleted state branch makes `git fetch` exit 128, the same code as an unreachable remote, so the clone reports `unreachable`. Runs on held claims then start 'not refreshed', and the next push recreates the branch with exit 0 ('[new branch]'). T-PUBLISH's premise that 'only the holder removes its claim' is also unchecked. A claim file deleted with plain git by anyone else arrives as a change made on one side only and is taken silently; T-INCOMING only reports it.
proposed_resolution: Make it a step of the sync. Before combining, test that the clone record's `remote_head` is an ancestor of the fetched head. If it is not, the state is a new state `rewritten`: nothing is combined or pushed, and both heads and the commits that vanished are named for a person. Tell a missing branch from an unreachable remote with `git ls-remote --exit-code <remote> refs/heads/<state branch>`, which exits 2 when the ref is absent (tested). The state is then `missing`, and nothing but T-SWITCH or init creates the branch. When a claim this clone holds disappears in a commit this clone did not make, report it and end the run as T-HOLD does. Add to T-REMOTE's `unmeasured` cell, and to the doctor, that the repository should forbid force-pushing and deleting the state branch. Add a proof scenario for each case.

outcome.what_was_done: New check T-HISTORY, a step of every sync. missing: the remote answers and has no state branch (git ls-remote --exit-code exits 2), and no sync creates it again. rewritten: the head the clone last saw is not contained in the fetched head while the mount still contains it; nothing is combined or pushed and both heads and the vanished commits are named. T-HOLD and T-INCOMING report a claim removed or changed by a commit that is not its holder's. team-sync.md and the doctor say the repository should forbid forced pushes and deletion of the state branch. Reproduced (fact 9); proof scenarios 7, 8 and 9.

problem: T-NEVER promises the tool never force-pushes over a person's commit, and its `unmeasured` cell says 'Nothing'. Delivery still 'pushes the story's own branch with --force-with-lease' after a rebase (commands/story-deliver.md), and T-NEVER allows rebasing a branch without a known hand commit. A bare --force-with-lease takes its lease from the remote-tracking ref, which any fetch moves, including an editor's background fetch or the person's own `git fetch`. Tested: holder A pushed story/S-1; teammate C pushed a hand commit to it; A fetched, rebased and pushed with a bare --force-with-lease. The push was accepted as a '(forced update)', and C's commit was no longer on the remote branch. The same push with --force-if-includes was refused with '[rejected] (remote ref updated since checkout)', and the hand commit stayed. The test T-NEVER plans, 'the hand commit's id is still on the branch afterwards', passes unless it fetches between the commit and the push.
proposed_resolution: On a team, every forced push of a story branch names the expected value the tool itself last read and checked: `--force-with-lease=refs/heads/story/<id>:<sha>` together with `--force-if-includes`. Better still, once a story branch has been pushed, update it only by merging the target in, as T-NEVER already does for a branch with a hand commit, so that nothing is forced at all. Add a T-NEVER test that fetches between the teammate's push and the tool's push.

outcome.what_was_done: T-NEVER: the one push the tool forces, after its own rebase of a branch with no hand commit, names the head it expects, --force-with-lease=refs/heads/story/<id>:<delivery.pushed>, the head T-BRANCH just read and checked; a lease without that value is never used. When the remote refuses, the branch is put back at the head written down before the rebase and T-BRANCH brings in what arrived. Reproduced: the named lease was refused with stale info and the hand commit stayed, a bare one overwrote it (fact 12). The test fetches between the teammate's push and the tool's (proof scenario 36). Not taken: --force-if-includes, which the named value makes unnecessary, and never rebasing a pushed branch, which would change how the verdict's patch id is kept after a rebase in the delivery design.

problem: T-BRANCH counts as hand commits all the commits the local branch lacks whenever 'the remote head is not this clone's head or an ancestor of it'. That also matches the holder's own commits after it rebases. Delivery rebases on a conflict, and T-NEVER allows a rebase of a branch with no hand commit; if the push that follows fails or the run ends, the local and remote heads diverge. Tested: A pushed story/S-1, the target moved, and A rebased locally. `merge-base --is-ancestor` of the remote head and the local head exited 1. The one commit the local branch lacked was A's own pre-rebase commit, with the same patch id as the rebased one. Merging it in as T-BRANCH says exited 0 and left the change twice in history. The holder's own commit is then recorded in `delivery.hand_commits`, made a `hand:` item for review, and may fail green as if a teammate had changed a frozen test.
proposed_resolution: Record the head of each story branch the tool pushes, in the local store and in the closure. T-BRANCH treats as foreign only the commits on the remote branch that are not reachable from the last head this clone pushed, or fetched and checked. It drops any commit whose patch id is already on the local branch (`git cherry`). Add a T-BRANCH case: rebase locally, fail the push, then survey.

outcome.what_was_done: The closure records delivery.pushed, the head the holder last pushed or last brought in and checked. T-BRANCH counts as arrived only the commits on the remote branch reachable from neither that head nor the local head, so the holder's own commits after an unpushed rebase are not taken for a teammate's (git rev-list <remote> --not <pushed> <local> gave none; fact 13). A remote branch that no longer contains delivery.pushed is a conflict for a person. Proof scenario 36 rebases, fails the push and surveys. git cherry is not needed: the tool always runs T-BRANCH before it rebases.

problem: Read together, three passages deliver a story to the integration branch without a pull request. T-HANDOFF 'pushes the story branch to its upstream as a fast-forward'. T-REMOTE reads 'the upstream that git records for the branch (its remote and its ref)' before every push. team-sync fact 3 says `git worktree add --track -b` sets that upstream. A story branch is cut from the target's remote head. Tested: `git worktree add --track -b story/S-1 <path> shared/main` gave story/S-1 the upstream 'shared refs/heads/main'. A push to that ref was a fast-forward of main (`refs/heads/story/S-1:refs/heads/main`), and so was a plain `git push` under push.default=upstream. On a repository that does not protect main, the checkpoint would publish an unreviewed story onto the shared branch, against clause 4f. The slice's `create_story` creates the branch at a commit and so sets no upstream; the risk lies in what M1 and M3 add.
proposed_resolution: T-REMOTE takes only the remote from a branch's upstream. A story branch is always pushed to `refs/heads/story/<id>`, named explicitly, and never to its upstream ref. Story branches are made with --no-track, and their upstream is set to `<remote>/story/<id>` at the first push. Correct fact 3 so that it does not suggest --track from the target. A test asserts that no checkpoint, release or claim release ever moves the integration branch.

outcome.what_was_done: Same correction as D33R-F-1: only the remote is taken from an upstream, a story branch is created at a commit id and pushed as refs/heads/story/<id> to the remote of its target, an upstream that names another ref is refused, and a test asserts that no checkpoint, release of a claim or sync moves the integration branch. Fact 4 states what was reproduced, including that a plain push under push.default=upstream moved the integration branch.

problem: T-PUBLISH builds the claim commit on the remote's head, and 'only after the remote accepted the commit is the mount moved to it'. That move is a fast-forward only when the mount holds nothing unpushed. T-FRESH refuses a new claim after `unreachable`, `diverged`, `blocked` or `refused`, but not after `unpushed` or `busy`, both of which leave unpushed commits in the mount. Tested: with one unpushed state commit in A's mount, a claim commit built on the remote head was pushed and accepted, and `git merge --ff-only <claim commit>` then failed ('Not possible to fast-forward'). A builder who moves the branch with update-ref instead orphans the unpushed state commits: a lost update. Also tested: `merge --ff-only` refuses over a modified tracked file even when its content equals the target's. So anything published must first be committed through the mount's own index, not only through a temporary one. T-FRESH also says nothing of a run on held claims after `diverged`, `blocked`, `unpushed` or `busy`.
proposed_resolution: Before T-PUBLISH builds a claim commit, the mount's head must be the remote head (ahead 0). Otherwise it syncs first and refuses if that fails. Alternatively, it combines the accepted claim commit into the mount through T-COMBINE, never by update-ref. Add `unpushed` and `busy` to T-FRESH's refusals of a new claim, and state per outcome what a run on held claims does. State in team-sync that the flush commits through the mount's index, and that 'without touching the mount' applies to the merge only.

outcome.what_was_done: T-PUBLISH takes a claim only after a sync that ended synced, and the mount takes the accepted commit by a fast-forward or through T-COMBINE; T-COMBINE says the mounted branch is never moved to a commit that does not contain its head. T-FRESH refuses a run after every outcome but synced, unpushed and busy included. team-sync.md says that what a clone publishes is first committed by the flush through the mount's own index, that only the combined commit is built without touching the mount, and that a claim or a minted file is never written in the mount first because git refuses to fast-forward over a file with the same content (fact 7).

problem: T-SETTLE and topics/team-records.md say 'nothing acts on a settlement before a sync has confirmed it: every survey syncs before it reads decisions'. A sync that fails confirms nothing, and T-FRESH lets a run on held claims start after `unreachable`. That survey reads decisions from the mount, which holds the local, unpublished settlement. Take A, offline, holding S-1, whose person settles `finding.S-1` as fix. Meanwhile B's person settles it as descope and pushes. A's run acts on fix. When A comes back online, T-SETTLE keeps B's descope and sets A's aside, but A's closure already records the work. The two answers have both taken effect, which team-records says cannot happen. No check enforces the sentence; it is advice.
proposed_resolution: Make confirmation a property the decisions reader checks. A settlement counts as settled only when the state commit that settled it is contained in the clone record's last fetched `remote_head`. Until then it reads as open with the note 'settled here, not yet published'. A survey that started with `refreshed: false` therefore stops at such a decision. Add a proof scenario: settle offline, run on a held claim, and the run stops at the decision.

outcome.what_was_done: Same correction as D33R-F-5, and stricter than proposed where the proposal assumed a run could start offline: no run starts without a sync that ended synced (T-FRESH), and a settlement listed in sync.unpublished reads as open to every reader until the remote holds it (T-SETTLE). Proof scenario 25: settled out of reach on A, settled differently and pushed by B, and no run on A ever acted on A's answer.

problem: The team section says the sync 'holds flush.lock, not the run lock', and ledger D33-3 adds that this is so 'no read-modify-write of a tracked record can straddle it'. The sync's fetch and push run under the git helper's time limit, 60 s by default in gitrun.py. Built code: `store.locked` waits 3 s for flush.lock and then raises `StoreBusy`; `settle_decision` takes flush.lock, and so does every closure write. While a sync is on the network, a decision a person types fails inside the hook's four-second deadline, and an agent's record write fails `busy`. The flush 'waits up to 5 seconds and then leaves the work to the holder'. When the holder is the decisions-and-claims-only sync, which runs while a run is live (T-SETTLE), the checkpoint's closures and claim removals are not in the commit that holder makes. Nothing says what a sync does when another sync of the same clone holds the lock. This is the failure for two sessions on one machine: one types a decision while the other's run checkpoints.
proposed_resolution: The sync holds flush.lock only around its local steps: the flush commit, the combine and fast-forward, and writing the clone record. It never holds it across a fetch or a push. The network steps run unlocked, and the local step afterwards fails safe if the head moved meanwhile (update-ref with the expected old value, or ff-only). A flush that finds a sync holding the lock waits for that local step instead of leaving its work. A checkpoint's sync waits for another sync of the same clone, then runs its own. Add a test: settle while a sync's fetch is held open by a slow remote.

outcome.what_was_done: Same correction as D33R-F-8: flush.lock for the local steps only, never across the network; a local step that finds the head moved repeats, because the fast-forward fails without changing anything; one sync per clone through local/sync.lock, a second waiting and then running its own. A flush therefore waits no longer for a sync than for another flush and does its own work. Test and proof scenario 14.

problem: Fact 8 and T-FRESH claim that because every git call 'runs with terminal prompts off and a time limit ... it fails ... Nothing waits'. GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 governs git's own prompts, not ssh's. Tested with OpenSSH 10.2 against a throwaway local sshd, in a terminal, with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. `git ls-remote` over ssh printed the host-key question and waited. Run through subprocess.run with a 4 s time limit, as gitrun.py runs git (stdin inherited), git was killed at 4 s while the ssh child stayed alive and still held the prompt in the terminal. The same call with stdin from /dev/null in a new session (start_new_session) failed at once with 'Host key verification failed.' A Bash tool call here has no controlling terminal, so the case is a person's terminal: `vsdd sync`, `vsdd decide`, `vsdd claim take` (terminal only) and `vsdd claim release`.
proposed_resolution: Run every git call that may reach the network with stdin from /dev/null, in a new session (no controlling terminal), and kill the whole process group at the time limit. Correct fact 8 to say what GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT does and does not cover. M1's test runs a fetch over ssh to a local sshd with an unknown host key, from a terminal, and asserts an immediate failure and no leftover process.

outcome.what_was_done: Every network call runs with standard input from /dev/null in a session of its own and the whole process group is killed at the time limit; askpass programs and credential helpers are covered as well (team-sync.md, Credentials; ledger entry D33-29 for the git helper). Fact 10 says what GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT does and does not cover, as reproduced with git 2.34.1 and OpenSSH 8.9 against a throwaway sshd from a pseudo-terminal. M1 keeps it as a test; proof scenario 16.

problem: Claims exclude each other only when every clone's state branch upstream is the same repository. Nothing in the design says so or checks it, and forks are not mentioned. Tested: a mirror of the shared repository, standing in for a fork. A clone of the shared repository and a clone of the copy both pushed a claim for S-1 as a fast-forward, and both were accepted. The shared repository held A's claim and the copy held B's. Both state branches have the same root commit, so git cannot tell two copies of one history apart. T-JOIN would admit B, because the copy's factory.toml says `team.enabled = true`. The result is the double work clause 4b forbids, and it is silent. It is also not said where story branches go in a fork workflow. T-BRANCH cannot see a teammate's fork, and a story base read from a fork's stale main is wrong.
proposed_resolution: State the condition, since a program cannot measure it. In T-REMOTE's `unmeasured` cell, in setup and in the doctor, say that every clone's state branch and story branches must have the one shared repository as their upstream. When a clone has several remotes, setup asks the person which one is shared and sets the state branch's upstream there. The doctor lists, for each branch the factory uses, the remote's URL, so a person can compare clones. Say that a fork workflow pushes the state branch and story branches to the shared repository, or declare fork workflows out of scope for 1.0.

outcome.what_was_done: The condition is stated where it cannot be measured: T-REMOTE's unmeasured cell and team-sync.md (One shared repository) say that every clone pushes its state and story branches to the one repository the team shares, and that working through a fork a person alone can push to is not supported. When several remotes hold the state branch vsdd init mounts nothing until --remote names one, and setup asks the person which is the shared repository (T-JOIN, D33-12). The doctor prints the address each factory branch is pushed to, without any user or password part. Reproduced with a mirror (fact 14); proof scenario 18.

problem: On a team, stories reach the shared branch only through pull requests. Yet T-NEVER keeps 'the tool never pushes to a target branch outside a delivery or a release', and the release still moves target branches itself: the merge of `hotfix/<version>` back into the integration branch, and the release branch. Decision D33 expects the repository to enforce who may merge, and a repository set up that way protects the integration branch. Its rules then refuse the release's direct push. T-REMOTE reports `refused` and stops, and the design gives the release no other route, so a hotfix cannot be completed on the kind of repository D33 assumes. The 'integration lock' that the merge-back waits for is a file lock on one clone and serialises nothing with other clones' deliveries.
proposed_resolution: In `pr` mode, and so on every team, the hotfix merge-back and any release commit on a branch the repository protects go through a pull request, using the same host module as delivery (ledger D33-18). Record the pull request and its merged sha in the release closure so that T-NOTICE recognises them. Drop the integration lock from the team path.

outcome.what_was_done: In pr mode vsdd release moves no shared branch by a push of its own: the merge of hotfix/<version> back and a release commit go through pull requests opened and merged by the delivery's host module, each recorded in the release closure so that T-NOTICE does not count it; the integration lock is named as a lock of one clone (commands/release.md, T-NEVER). New ledger entry D33-27 for G7 and M4. Proof scenario 39 uses a bare repository that declines direct pushes to the integration branch. That hosts let a rule refuse direct pushes to a branch was confirmed in the hosts' documentation.

problem: T-COMBINE is right that a code-written record changed on both sides keeps the remote's version. But the git facts present `git merge-tree --write-tree` as the combining mechanism ('so do changes to different parts of one text file') without saying it must never decide a record. Tested: A changed `status` in a decision record and B changed `settled_on` and `note` further down the same file. `merge-tree` exited 0 and wrote a record neither side wrote, schema-valid, with status from A and settled_on and note from B. With nearer edits it exited 1 and still wrote a tree, with conflict markers inside the JSON. A modify/delete pair (a claim released here, taken over there) gave 'CONFLICT (modify/delete)'. A builder who trusts merge-tree's exit status merges two valid records into one that is wrong. Proof scenario 13 tests text only.
proposed_resolution: State in team-sync, and in T-COMBINE, that the sync decides every path from the two diffs against the merge base before it builds the tree. A record takes the remote's blob, and only text paths go through merge-tree; its exit status is never the test for a record. Add a proof scenario: two edits to one decision record, far enough apart that git merges them; at the end the remote's version stands and the other is set aside.

outcome.what_was_done: T-COMBINE decides every path from the two diffs against the merge base before any tree is built: a record is taken whole from the remote, only a text path is merged, one file at a time with git merge-file, and no path is decided by the exit status of a merge of the whole tree, which the sync no longer runs. team-sync.md gives the reason and fact 6 the reproduction (two edits to one decision record merged with exit 0 into a record neither side wrote). Proof scenario 11.

problem: Shallow clones (common in CI) are not mentioned. Tested on a --depth 2 clone. `merge-base --is-ancestor` with a commit outside the shallow history exited 128, not 1. A first-parent count from the head gave 2 where the true count was 6. `merge-tree --write-tree` across the boundary failed with 'refusing to merge unrelated histories' (exit 128). T-NOTICE would then report `history_rewritten`, a wrong cause, or count too few hand commits; T-BRANCH would misjudge containment; the sync would fail with no named cause.
proposed_resolution: Make it a refusal of the sync and a line of the doctor. When `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` is true, team use refuses, naming the shallow clone and `git fetch --unshallow`. T-NOTICE and T-BRANCH treat exit 128 from an ancestry test as cannot-measure, with its own reason.

outcome.what_was_done: T-REMOTE, in the preflight, refuses team use in a shallow clone and names git fetch --unshallow. T-NOTICE fails with history_unmeasured, and T-BRANCH returns a conflict, when git cannot answer an ancestry test, and the head rule says an error where a yes or a no was asked is neither. Reproduced: exit 128 and a first-parent count of 2 for 27 (fact 8). Proof scenario 19.

problem: T-WHO, and team-sync fact 9, read `user.name` and `user.email` from git's configuration, but git stamps commits with GIT_AUTHOR_NAME and GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL when they are set in the environment. Tested: with only environment identity, `git config user.name` exited 1, so T-WHO would refuse a clone that git commits from without trouble. With both set, the configuration named one person and the commit's author was the other, so a claim's `holder` and its state commit's author can disagree. The built helper passes GIT_AUTHOR_* through.
proposed_resolution: Read the identity git will actually use: `git -c user.useConfigOnly=true var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT` (and GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT). Tested: with nothing configured it exits 128 instead of inventing an identity from the system account, and with environment identity it returns that identity. Write the result into the claim, the decision and the delivery. Correct fact 9.

outcome.what_was_done: T-WHO reads the identity from git itself, git -c user.useConfigOnly=true var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT and the same for the committer, and writes that into the claim, the decision and the delivery, so a record and its commit name the same person. Fact 11 is corrected as reproduced. Ledger entry D33-8; proof scenario 21.

problem: The state branch's growth is not addressed. Every survey that takes a claim pushes a commit, every combine adds a merge commit, and team-claims makes the branch's history the record of who held what, so nothing is ever pruned from it. T-INCOMING checks 'every commit that arrives' file by file. A clone away for a month checks every intermediate commit, where the tree it will build on is what matters. Nothing measures the sync's cost as the history grows.
proposed_resolution: State that the history is kept and grows by design. T-INCOMING checks the arriving tree once, plus the trailers of each arriving commit for the report. M5 measures a sync on a state branch with a large history (for example 50,000 commits), and the doctor reports the branch's size.

outcome.what_was_done: team-sync.md says the state branch's history is kept and grows by design, and how the sync's cost is kept independent of its length: it lists before it fetches, T-INCOMING checks the tree that arrived once and not each commit, and the combine reads two diffs. Proof scenario 15 measures a sync on 50,000 commits, and the doctor reports the branch's length.

problem: The design names no delivery state for a pull request that the host will merge later, as with a merge queue or a merge the repository's rules defer. Delivery's states are merged, awaiting_merge, ci_failed, conflict, review_stale, refused and checkout_dirty. `awaiting_merge` opens a `merge` decision for a person, which is wrong when nothing waits on a person. When the host merges, the commit it makes was built on a target head the tool never saw. T-DELIVERY's adoption rule then decides, and a changed patch id closes the story `unreviewed`. The design does not say this is the expected path for such repositories.
proposed_resolution: Add a delivery state `queued`: the host has accepted the pull request and will merge it, no decision opens, and the next survey or delivery polls it. Say that the adoption rule of T-DELIVERY is how a merge made by the host is recorded, and that a patch id that differs makes the merge a hand commit for the wave's review.

outcome.what_was_done: T-DELIVERY has the state queued for a pull request the host will merge by itself later: no decision opens, the run ends partial, the story keeps its claim and the next survey or delivery asks again. A merge the host made is adopted with merged_by.how = host when the patch id is the reviewed one and is closed unreviewed, as a hand commit for the wave's review, when it is not. Ledger entry D33-17 adds the state to the delivery data and the story script. That hosts offer a merge queue and a merge when checks pass was confirmed in their documentation.

problem: T-HANDOFF pushes the story branch, so it carries only committed work. Uncommitted changes in the story worktree at a checkpoint, or at `vsdd claim release`, stay on the clone. Yet claim release frees the story as fully handed over, and team-records tells the next holder it continues from what was pushed. Work made before the checkpoint is then lost, where the design says only work made after the last checkpoint can be.
proposed_resolution: T-HANDOFF reports uncommitted changes in a story worktree in the checkpoint result. `vsdd claim release` refuses while the story worktree has uncommitted changes, naming them.

outcome.what_was_done: T-HANDOFF lists in the checkpoint result each story worktree that holds uncommitted changes, and vsdd claim release refuses while the story's worktree holds any, naming them. The unmeasured cell says that changes never committed do not travel. Proof scenario 29.

problem: A clone is named to people only by sixteen random hex characters. A person with two machines, the case of one person on two clones, sees on one machine that a claim is held by themselves on clone 5f0c2a9d81b3e746, and cannot tell which machine that is or whether it is gone. Clause 4b asks that everyone can see who is working on what.
proposed_resolution: Give the clone record a label that the person gives when the clone joins or switches (defaulting to the host name), carry it in the claim beside the id, and print it in status and the briefing. The label is shown only and decides nothing.

outcome.what_was_done: The clone record has label: the machine's host name unless the person gives another with vsdd init --label or vsdd sync --label, which setup offers when a clone joins. It is copied into each claim as holder.label and printed by status and the briefing beside the person; it is shown only and decides nothing. Because it is shared in claims, the record says that a person who does not want the host name shared gives another.

problem: Two facts are defined twice and differently. (a) claim-scopes gives `open` as held 'act', 'for one command', while T-RELEASE has the checkpoint remove it. If the claim ends with the command, its removal can be published before the new cycle record: while a run is live, a sync started outside it (the detached decision sync, or `vsdd sync` from the main session) 'commits and pushes decision records and claims only'. A second clone then finds neither the claim nor an open cycle and opens a second cycle, the case the `open` claim exists to stop. (b) team-claims says a wave run 'takes each story it starts', while claim-scopes says the wave survey takes a claim 'for each story it returns as a unit'. Read the second way, one wave run holds every free story of the wave for as long as it runs.
proposed_resolution: Define `held` in claim-scopes only. Make `open` held until the push that carries the new cycle record. A claims-only sync never publishes a claim removal while the records that claim covers are uncommitted. Say which story claims a wave survey takes.

outcome.what_was_done: held is defined only in work-claim-scopes.toml. open is held until the push, made by the command that opens the cycle, that carries the new cycle record, and is removed in that commit. T-RELEASE says a removal is committed only together with every change under the paths its scope covers, so a partial sync never publishes one ahead of its records (command:sync defines full and partial). A wave survey claims only the stories it can start (D33R-F-13). Proof scenario 31.

problem: T-CLAIM's store check refuses 'a write to a closure record ... for a unit whose claim in the mount does not name this clone'. Some units take no claim at all: `spike`, `discover` and a report-only `maintain`. Read literally, the check refuses their closures on a team. It also does not say what happens when two clones write the same unclaimed closure at once.
proposed_resolution: Apply `claim_not_held` only to units that a scope in claim-scopes covers. Say that two clones writing one unclaimed closure end as T-COMBINE says: the remote's version stands, and the other is set aside and named.

outcome.what_was_done: Same correction as D33R-F-15, and T-CLAIM and T-COMBINE say what happens when two clones write one unclaimed closure: the remote's version stands and the other is set aside and named.

problem: T-INCOMING checks each arriving file against this plugin's registry. A newer plugin, still at or above `team.min_plugin`, that writes a path kind this plugin does not know therefore stops the unit on older clones as if its record were corrupt, with the route answer `human` and no word about versions. T-VERSION calls a newer writer only a report.
proposed_resolution: When a file fails the registry check and its commit's `Plugin:` trailer is newer than this plugin, report it as 'written by plugin <v>; upgrade', distinct from a broken record. Say whether the unit stops; stopping is the safe answer, with the right cause given.

outcome.what_was_done: T-INCOMING: when a file fails its check and its commit carries a Plugin: trailer newer than this plugin, the cause given is that it was written by plugin <version> and this clone must be upgraded, not a broken record; the unit stops the same way, which is the safe answer. T-VERSION points to it. Proof scenario 20.

problem: Package order. M2 delivers T-CLAIM, whose rows include a refusal of `vsdd story deliver`, a command package G4a builds, but M2 does not depend on G4a. M2 also delivers `vsdd claim release`, which must perform T-HANDOFF and refuse when it fails, but T-HANDOFF is built by M3, which depends on M2. M2's brief therefore cannot be completed as listed.
proposed_resolution: Move T-CLAIM's delivery refusal to M4, which depends on G4a, or add G4a to M2's dependencies. Build claim release's hand-off with M3, or move T-HANDOFF into M2.

outcome.what_was_done: The refusal of a delivery by a clone that does not hold the story is T-DELIVERY, built by M4, which depends on G4a. vsdd claim release is built by M3, with the hand-off it depends on (its registry entry and file name M3). M2 no longer lists either.

problem: `notes.json` is named as the one record that several clones write with no claim, and under T-COMBINE the remote's version stands. Any two notes that people on two clones add between syncs collide, and one person's note is set aside every time. That is noise and a lost write by design, for a file whose entries are independent.
proposed_resolution: Store each note as a file of its own (for example `notes/<clone>-<n>.json`) and count the cap of five across the directory, so that two notes never collide.

outcome.what_was_done: Two notes added on two clones are both kept: T-COMBINE merges notes.json as the remote's notes followed by those this clone added since the merge base, cut to the cap from the oldest end, and sets nothing aside. One file per note was not taken, because notes.json is a built record on the slice path and its storage may not change. Proof scenario 13.

where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/config.py (the one key list, SPECS); rewrite/spec/tables/config-keys.toml; rewrite/spec/topics/project-configuration.md (the annotated example)
problem: Decision D33 adds the section [team] with two keys, team.enabled and team.min_plugin. The loader's one key list has no such section, so a factory.toml that turns team use on is rejected as holding an unknown key, on every clone. The key table and the annotated example do not list the keys, and the meaning of state.push ("State is pushed only by vsdd checkpoint") stops being true: the survey, a settlement and the claim commands also push.
proposed_resolution: Add the two rows of rewrite/spec/tables/team-config-keys.toml to config.SPECS, to the key table and to the example, each with its default (false, empty), and reword state.push. Leave the cross-key refusals (team use with state.push false, with delivery.mode local, with delivery.ci none, with a [[repo]] entry, or with no remote) to the sync, T-SWITCH: the loader cannot see a remote.

where: rewrite/spec/records/config-fingerprint.md (the list of gate-bearing sections); the hook runner's fingerprint code when H1 widens
problem: The hook runner announces a change to a gate-bearing section of factory.toml that arrives from another clone. [team] is not in its list, so a teammate who turns team use off, or lowers team.min_plugin, changes every clone's behaviour unannounced.
proposed_resolution: Add [team] to the fingerprinted sections, with a case: the section changes in an arriving commit and the next session announces it once.

outcome.what_was_done: Package M6 adds the section when it adds the keys (D33-1).

where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/commits.py (flush); next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/store.py (locked: flush.lock with a wait of 3 s); rewrite/spec/topics/state-commits.md (Push); rewrite/plans/step-3/records.md D11; rewrite/plans/step-3/survey.md D19
problem: The flush and the state push were built and planned for one writer. (a) Where the clone has no git identity the flush commits as vsdd-factory <vsdd-factory@example.invalid>, which on a team hides who acted. (b) Its commit carries Run: and Code-Head: but neither the clone nor the plugin version, so nothing says which clone or version wrote state. (c) Code-Head: is the local integration branch's head, which in pr mode lags the remote. (d) It commits every changed file, with no way to publish a settlement or a claim alone while a run is live. (e) The push is designed as a rebase of the mounted state branch, allowed only while the run lock is held; a sync must also run outside a run and while an agent has uncommitted files in the mount, where a rebase cannot run. (f) The record stores and the function that settles a decision take flush.lock with a wait of three seconds, and a second flush waits five and then leaves its work to the holder; a sync that held that lock across a fetch or a push would make a typed settlement and a record write in a live run fail busy, and would leave a checkpoint's closures out of the commit.
proposed_resolution: When the sync is built: the flush takes an optional path filter; with team use on it refuses a clone for which git has no identity (T-WHO) and adds the trailers Clone: and Plugin:; Code-Head: becomes the fetched head of the target branch; state commits stay unsigned (decision D2). The push is vsdd.state.sync (rewrite/spec/commands/sync.md): it builds the combined commit path by path with a temporary index, never by a merge of the whole tree, and fast-forwards the mount. It takes flush.lock for its local steps only (the flush; the check, combine, fast-forward and clone record; the outcome) and never across a listing, a fetch or a push; a local step that finds the mount's head moved repeats. Whole syncs of one clone are serialised by local/sync.lock: a second sync waits for the first inside its own time budget (in a foreground command 60 seconds for the wait and all network calls together) and answers busy at its end, having changed nothing; a command that takes a claim, mints an id or opens a cycle holds the lock for its whole act. Every fetch goes into the remote-tracking ref (git fetch <remote> +refs/heads/<branch>:refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>) and never into a local branch, and every push of the state branch names the head it was built on (--force-with-lease=refs/heads/<branch>:<that head>), so that it only adds to that head (T-REMOTE, T-PUSH). A branch is looked for on the remote by its exact ref name, through one function, because git ls-remote matches a pattern at the end of a name (the listing rule at the head of rewrite/spec/tables/team-checks.toml). sync.remote_head is the last head of the remote whose arrivals the clone checked and took into its mount: it is written only after the mount holds the commit, by the local step that checked what arrived and fast-forwarded the mount (to the fetched head) and when a push of the clone is accepted (to the pushed commit, not to the remote's head); a fetch made to judge a push writes nothing, so after a lost race the repeated sync checks every commit between the push's base and the new head (T-HISTORY, T-INCOMING). The sync ends synced without a fetch only when the listed head is sync.remote_head, the mount's head is that commit too, sync.unknown is empty and, in a full sync, the clone holds no claim that T-RELEASE has a sync remove (rewrite/spec/commands/sync.md, step 3). With team use off the push changes only as the head of rewrite/spec/tables/team-checks.toml lists: T-SOLO, where a push that finds the remote moved stops where it used to rebase and retry, and T-REMOTE's choice of remote and refs. The slice builds no push, so nothing is built differently now. Tests: a settlement and a closure write succeed while a slow remote holds a sync's fetch open; a survey that starts while a sync job holds the lock answers busy inside its budget; a state branch rewound between a fetch and a push is answered rewritten and the removed commits are not pushed back; a record that fails its check, pushed by the clone that beat this clone's push, is reported by the repeated sync before the mount takes it; a listing answered only by a branch whose name ends in the state branch's ref name is read as missing.

outcome.what_was_done: Package M1 makes the change to the flush and builds the sync, with S2b's owner, when the build widens. The flush as built is right for one clone.

where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/policy/walls.toml ([callers]); the person-only list (HUMAN_ONLY, carried by rewrite/spec/tables/callers.toml until H6 moves it)
problem: Three new subcommands have no group in the wall table: sync, claim release and claim take. A subcommand in no group cannot be run by any caller, and claim take must be refused for every caller, the main session's model included, because taking a claim over is a person's act.
proposed_resolution: Add sync and "claim release" to the group author, which the main row holds, and "claim take" to the person-only list that gate-guard reads. Nothing else joins that list: vsdd init has no person-only flag for team use. Extend the lint pins and add one case each: the main session runs sync; an agent's claim take is refused.

outcome.what_was_done: Each package adds its command's line in the same change as the command, when the build widens: M1 sync, M2 claim take, M3 claim release. H6's owner keeps the person-only list where gate-guard reads it.

problem: The survey object has no place for elsewhere (stories another clone holds, with their holders) or hand_commits; the checkpoint result has none for the sync's outcome, for a story branch the remote did not accept and for a story worktree that holds uncommitted changes; the status object has none for work claims and the sync. The shipped schemas are open, so the fields would validate, but the prelude carries the survey schema as a literal and an undeclared field is not part of the contract a script may read.
proposed_resolution: Add the fields, all optional with empty defaults, with fixtures, and run tools/build.py so the prelude is regenerated: elsewhere and hand_commits in the survey object; sync, not_pushed and uncommitted in the checkpoint result; work_claims and sync in the status object (named in full, because claims already means a fixer's claims in review data). There is no field for a run that started without a fetch: none does. No workflow script needs to read them: a story held elsewhere is simply not among the units.

outcome.what_was_done: Package M2 adds the fields when it builds the claim, with the build step of B4a.

where: rewrite/plans/step-3/survey.md 3.1 and 3.2 (the order of the survey and of the checkpoint); rewrite/spec/commands/survey.md ("Order of the checks")
problem: The survey is planned as: caller marker, every precondition, flush, lock, admission. On a team the preconditions must be read on fetched state, so a sync comes before them, and a claim comes after the lock; the checkpoint gains the hand-off and the removal of claims before its push. The planned order (preconditions, then flush) is right for one clone and wrong for two: a stale clone would pass "the story is admitted" for a story a teammate has delivered.
proposed_resolution: When team use is built the survey becomes: marker, sync (a full one: flush, list, fetch, combine, push), and only if it ended synced (T-FRESH): preconditions, lock, claim (T-CLAIM, through T-PUBLISH), admission. The checkpoint becomes: map results, hand-off (T-HANDOFF), remove claims (T-RELEASE), sync, release the lock; it ends the run whatever the sync's outcome. With team use off the order stays as planned.

outcome.what_was_done: Package M2 inserts the steps, with S3's owner and M1's sync, when the build widens. The unit being built now keeps the planned order; its steps are already separate calls, which is all the insertion needs.

where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/decisions.py (latest_decision sorts by opened; spec_approved reads it); next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/cycles.py (cycles_open sorts by opened); rewrite/spec/topics/decisions.md ("every approved merge decision that is newer than the latest approved spec decision")
problem: The latest decision of a kind is found by comparing the opened times of records, open cycles are ordered by their opened times, and dependency detection is specified as a comparison of a merge decision's time with a spec decision's. On a team those times are written by different machines whose clocks need not agree, so "the specification is approved" can be read from the wrong record and two open cycles can come out in the wrong order. The 90-day retention of settled decisions in the standing cycle compares a record's time with the local clock in the same way.
proposed_resolution: A decision whose id carries no subject stores follows: the decision of its kind in the same cycle that was latest when it was opened. A decision whose id carries a subject (a story or a wave) stores none: two clones open such decisions at the same moment, and nothing asks for the latest of them. A merge decision stores spec, the spec decision in force. latest_decision returns the record that no other follows, and two such records are a reported state problem. cycles_open orders by the cycle's kind and then its id. Retention by age may keep reading times: pruning early or late changes no decision. Each ordering function, cycles_open included, gets a test whose times contradict the links.

outcome.what_was_done: Package M3 adds the links and changes the functions, with the owners of S4 and S2a, when the build widens. On one clone the built ordering is right.

where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/decisions.py (settle_decision, decision_open); next/plugins/vsdd-factory/schemas/decision-record.schema.json (settled_by is session, terminal or import; settled_by_session)
problem: A decision record says how it was settled (session or terminal) and in which session, and nothing about who: no person and no clone. A session id means something on one machine only. Decision D33 requires the record to say which person approved a specification or settled a decision.
proposed_resolution: settle_decision takes the person and the clone's id as keyword arguments with empty defaults and writes settled_by_person and settled_on; the terminal command and the decisions rule pass them. The person is the identity git itself gives for a commit made in that clone (git -c user.useConfigOnly=true var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT), not the two configuration keys, because git takes the identity from the environment first. Nothing compares them with anything.

outcome.what_was_done: Package M3 adds the fields when the build widens. The keyword arguments default to empty, so no caller built for the slice changes.

where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/schemas/decision-record.schema.json, closure-record.schema.json, cycle-record.schema.json (built by the records unit, in its fix stage)
problem: Decision D33 adds fields to tracked records: settled_by_person, settled_on, follows and spec to a decision; delivery.pushed, delivery.merged_by, delivery.landed and delivery.hand_commits to a closure. On a team a newer plugin writes them and an older one on another clone reads them, inside one schema number of factory.toml. The three schemas are open today. If a review round closes one with additionalProperties: false, every older clone will refuse the record as corrupt and its flush will refuse to commit it. An earlier finding (AU-T2-14) asked for exactly that tightening on the configuration schema, so the risk is real.
proposed_resolution: Keep the three tracked record schemas open, at the top level and inside stages, verdict and delivery, and pin it with a test beside the schema fixtures, as the rules unit pins the finding schema. Say in each schema's description that a later version may add a field. This changes nothing the slice does.

outcome.what_was_done: The tracked record schemas stay open to added fields and the openness is pinned. Nothing set additionalProperties false, so no schema text beyond the descriptions changed; each of decision-record, closure-record and cycle-record now ends its description with 'A later version may add a field: read records that carry an unknown field, never refuse them (decision D33)' (closure names stages, verdict and delivery). The notes file ships no schema (its kind's schema is None in commits.record_kinds), so there was nothing to open there. New test_tracked_record_schemas_stay_open_to_added_fields walks each raw schema and fails naming the JSON path of any additionalProperties: false at any depth, and asserts each description carries the sentence. New fixture valid_future-fields.json per schema carries one unknown top-level field (settled_by_person and follows on the decision; rebased_on on the closure; reopened_on on the cycle) and unknown fields inside the nested objects (signed_off_by inside a decision's values; reviewed_by_panel inside a closure stage, waived_total inside its verdict, pushed and merged_by inside its delivery; the cycle record has no nested objects, noted in the test). New test_tracked_record_store_round_trip_keeps_unknown_fields validates each fixture and proves write_record/read_record (schema-checked both ways) preserve every unknown field. Verified both tests fail with additionalProperties: false added to cycle-record (the walk names $.additionalProperties; the round trip refuses 'unknown property reopened_on'). Ran tools/build.py: 0 file(s) regenerated — none of the three schemas is a prelude literal, so no generated copy changed.

where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/runs.py (_new_id: r-<date>-<minute>-<2 of 36>); the closure's admitted_by and delivery.run (rewrite/plans/step-4/delivery.md 3.4); the Run: trailer of a state commit
problem: A run id is unique on one clone: the store retries until the directory name is free there. Two clones can mint the same id in the same minute (one chance in 1,296 for each pair of runs). The id is written into tracked closures (admitted_by, delivery.run) and compared for equality: the checkpoint reads delivery.state where delivery.run is its own run, so a collision makes one clone read another's delivery outcome as its own.
proposed_resolution: When team use is built, every tracked field that names a run stores the clone's id beside it, and the comparisons use both. The alternative, four characters of the clone's id inside the run id, is one function (_new_id); the schema gives the id no pattern, so either can be done at any time.

outcome.what_was_done: Package M3 makes the change, with S2a's owner, when the build widens. On one clone the id is unique.

where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/gate_evidence.py (the red lookup reads local records only); next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/commits.py (record_kinds); rewrite/plans/step-4/gates.md; rewrite/plans/step-4/ORDER.md section 7 ("red evidence cannot be restored at an earlier commit")
problem: Evidence is local. A clone that continues another clone's story past its red gate has no red record: the story's position reads ready, the tests-first rule blocks every write to source, the green gate fails with "no red record", and the red gate cannot pass again on a branch whose tests already pass. So a story cannot be handed on once it is past red, which decision D33 requires ("picking up work that was begun on another machine continues from what has been pushed"). The record cannot ride inside the story's closure: a story with many tests would pass the closure's cap of 16,000 bytes and could then never be handed on.
proposed_resolution: The checkpoint and vsdd claim release write the story's latest passing red or re-freeze record to a tracked record of its own, cycles/<cycle>/red/<story>.json, with the fields, the schema and the cap of the evidence record it copies (8,000 bytes), so a record that could be written locally can always travel. The flush's record_kinds registers it in the same step. evidence(project, "red", subject) falls back to it when no local record exists, under the same rule: its commit lies between the story's base and its head. The tests-first rule and the green gate already read through that lookup. Green, demo and the review's cover are measured again as designed.

outcome.what_was_done: Not at slice depth: evidence stays local in the slice, so the travelling red record (cycles/<cycle>/red/<story>.json) is M3's to add with G2's owner for the lookup fallback, when the build widens to team use (decision D33).
outcome.where: package M3 (team hand-off), with G2 owning the lookup fallback

where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/mount.py (detect reads refs/remotes/origin/factory-artifacts; mount_state adds origin/factory-artifacts); next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/cmd_init.py (_branch_tip); rewrite/spec/topics/state-directory.md (the table of conditions)
problem: A remote is named in code. On a clone whose remote has another name, detect answers none where the truth is unmounted, and vsdd init creates a second, unrelated state branch instead of mounting the one on the remote. Two histories of state then exist that no push or merge can combine. A team's clones need not agree on what they call the remote.
proposed_resolution: detect and init look for the state branch under every remote: the loose ref refs/remotes/<any>/factory-artifacts and the matching lines of packed-refs, still by file reads only. When more than one remote holds it, init mounts nothing and lists them, and the option --remote <name>, which setup passes after asking the person which is the repository the team shares, says which to use. The mount sets the state branch's upstream to that remote, which is all the sync reads afterwards (T-REMOTE). The test mounts from a remote that is not called origin, and from a clone with two.

outcome.what_was_done: S1's owner makes the change when the build widens, before or with package M6, whose T-JOIN builds on it. The slice's sample has one remote named origin or none, so nothing it does changes.

where: rewrite/plans/step-3/survey.md 3.3 (target_head: "in pr mode it runs git fetch origin <branch> and reads the remote head"); its test test_target_head_local_and_pr
problem: The worktree library, which is about to be built, is planned to fetch the target branch from a remote named in code. Every later caller (story admission, delivery in pr mode, the wave gate) reads the target through this one function, so the name would be built into all of them.
proposed_resolution: Build target_head so that in pr mode it takes the remote from the branch's upstream (git for-each-ref --format='%(upstream:remotename) %(upstream:remoteref)' refs/heads/<branch>), fetches refs/heads/<branch> from that remote into the remote-tracking ref refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>, never into the local branch, and reads that ref (T-REMOTE in rewrite/spec/tables/sync-checks.toml). It takes only the remote from the upstream: an upstream whose ref is not refs/heads/<branch> raises a WorktreeError that names the branch and the git command that corrects it. With no upstream and exactly one remote it uses that remote; otherwise it raises a WorktreeError that names the branch and the git command that sets the upstream. The pr case of the test uses a remote that is not called origin. Local mode, which is all the slice runs, is untouched. The leading + of the refspec and two further assertions are entry D33-33.

outcome.what_was_done: target_head in pr mode takes the remote from the target branch's upstream (git for-each-ref --format='%(upstream:remotename) %(upstream:remoteref)'), fetches refs/heads/<branch> under the branch's own name and reads the remote-tracking head; an upstream whose ref is not refs/heads/<branch>, and a missing upstream with zero or several remotes, raise WorktreeError('git') naming the branch and the correcting command. No remote name is in code; the test's remote is 'gitea'. Local mode is untouched.

True: it runs the preflight, mounts, and writes the clone record with how = joined and the label of --label. Otherwise it mounts as it does today and returns a notice, which setup shows: this state was written on another clone, and if both are going to run the factory, team use is turned on first on the clone that has the project. There is no flag that only a person may pass. T-SOLO, in the sync, is the guard at the first push.

where: rewrite/plans/step-3/state-core.md section 1 (vsdd new with next_id, left for the widening); rewrite/spec/tables/identifiers.toml ("Sequential, by vsdd"); the commands new, story new-fix, spike open, review prepare and the idea register
problem: An id is minted as the next free number in the local tree, and the command file says why that is safe: "there is one state directory". On a team there is one per clone. Two clones mint the same id: S-0.07 in the standing epic from a wave's fix round and from a critical fix beside it; the same CR number for two queued requests; the same spike id; the same report path. Git then sees one path added twice, and for a story two cycles hold closures for one id.
proposed_resolution: With team use on, a command that mints an id which more than one claim could mint (an epic, a story of the standing epic, a change request, an idea, a spike, an on-demand review report) does so inside a sync (T-MINT): it takes the next free number in the fetched tree, builds one commit on the remote's head that adds the new file alone, and pushes it as a claim is pushed; the file reaches the mount with that commit. The push is judged by T-PUSH: a lost race repeats from the sync with the number taken again. After an answer that was lost the clone record lists the commit with its request, the SHA-256 of the kind of id and of every value the caller gave for the new file and of nothing the tool adds (rewrite/spec/records/clone.md), computed by one function for every minting command. The opening sync of any later command settles the commit, so nothing is minted while it is unknown. A command whose own request equals a settled entry's is given the id back when the remote took the commit, and mints when it did not; either way it removes the entry. A command with any other request mints as usual and leaves the entry, so a lost answer does not become two files for one request and a second request of the same kind is never answered with the first one's id. next_id takes the tree to scan as an argument, so a caller can pass the fetched one. Ids of the specification classes are minted only under the spec claim, and the stories of an epic belong to the run that holds its cycle; they need nothing. A number an agent picks for itself is caught at the sync as one path added twice (diverged).

outcome.what_was_done: Package M3 adds the rule to each minting command as that command exists; S1's owner gives next_id the argument when it builds vsdd new. Nothing on the slice mints an id.

where: rewrite/plans/step-4/delivery.md (pr mode left for the widening: push, rebase with --force-with-lease; 3.3 the refusal list; 3.4 the closure's delivery keys); rewrite/spec/commands/story-deliver.md; next/plugins/vsdd-factory/schemas/closure-record.schema.json and delivery-data.schema.json; the story script's delivery loop
problem: Delivery in pr mode is not built yet, and decision D33 makes it the only delivery a team has. When it is built it must carry what D33 adds. Refusals: this clone does not hold the story's claim; local mode or delivery.ci = none on a team; a host the module cannot serve. Closure keys: delivery.pushed, delivery.merged_by, delivery.landed, delivery.hand_commits. A state for a pull request the host will merge by itself later, queued, which opens no decision. The rule for a pull request merged by the host or outside the tool. The story branch pushed under its own name to the remote of its target, never to an upstream ref. No rebase or forced push of a story branch that holds a hand commit. And the planned bare --force-with-lease after a rebase is unsafe: it trusts the remote-tracking ref, which any fetch moves, so it overwrites a commit a teammate pushed in between (checked with git 2.34.1 and 2.50.1).

Package M4 then adds the refusal rows to the one refusal list (checks.py), the keys to the closure, queued to the delivery data and to the story script's delivery loop (the run ends partial), and T-BRANCH, which looks for a story branch on the remote only where the closure records delivery.pushed or the local branch has an upstream, both read without the network, so that a branch never pushed costs no network call and local mode makes none; which reads delivery.pushed to tell what arrived from the holder's own commits, treats a remote head that contains this clone's head as this clone's own push, and puts a rebase the remote never took back at delivery.pushed, under a git cherry guard, before it brings in a teammate's commit, and returns the unit blocked where the branch is gone from the remote and the clone does not hold the commit delivery.pushed names. All of it but the two claim refusals runs with team use off as well.

outcome.what_was_done: G4a builds pr mode with that one function and that push when the build widens; package M4 then adds the rows, the keys and the state, with W2's owner for the script. Local mode, which the slice builds, is unchanged.

where: rewrite/spec/commands/story-deliver.md and topics/governed-delivery.md (the merge through one vendor's command-line tool); next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/policy/walls.toml (the command family for it); rewrite/spec/rules/merge-guard.md; rewrite/spec/commands/doctor.md; rewrite/spec/packaging/sandbox-needs.md and plugin-manifest.md (one vendor's hosts)
problem: Delivery in pr mode is specified through one vendor's command-line tool, which the design, the wall table, a hook rule, the doctor and the list of hosts all name.
