origin: d33-fix-2, second pass (seen while correcting d33-fix-2-C1-2)
problem: T-FRESH says the opening sync (60 seconds) and the claim (30 seconds) together keep the survey inside the Bash tool's default limit of two minutes. The survey makes more network calls than those two: in pr mode the fetch of the target branch (T-NOTICE), and for each story the clone holds whose branch was pushed a listing and a fetch (T-BRANCH). Each has the time limit of a network call, but nothing bounds them together, so on a slow remote a clone that holds several pushed stories passes the limit, and the survey is not a job. Nor does any row say what the survey does with a story whose branch could not be listed or fetched: the head rule only says that it is `unreachable` and never 'nothing arrived'.
proposed_resolution: Give those calls one stated budget and one outcome. Either list every held story branch in one call (git ls-remote <remote> 'refs/heads/story/*', read by exact ref name) and fetch those that moved in one fetch with several refspecs, or give the calls a shared budget inside what the opening sync and the claim leave. A story whose branch could not be read inside it is not worked on in this run: its unit is returned blocked with the reason `environment`, the others go on, and the next survey measures again. State this in T-BRANCH and correct the sentence of T-FRESH. problem: The B6-R7 fixes hold for the forms that finding named, but the workflow lint still misses other ways a hand-written region can pin a tier. Each of these passes workflow_problems with 0 problems (probed in a scratch copy): (a) RUN['tier'] = 'reviewer' and Object.assign(RUN, { tier: TIER.reviewer }), because TIER_TABLE_ASSIGN_RE matches only the spelling RUN.tier; (b) const x = TIER followed by RUN.tier = x.reviewer || null, an alias the adoption form accepts; (c) a hand-written workflow('vsdd-factory:story', { story: id, tier: TIER.reviewer }), which the child adopts through its own RUN.tier = a.tier || null (runStories puts tier: RUN.tier after ...extra, so it overrides an extra tier; a direct call has no such override); (d) since TIER_KEY_RE was narrowed to quoted literals, { model: big ? 'opus' : 'sonnet' }, a model chosen between literals, which was rejected before the narrowing. Separately, _strip_comments_and_strings lets a ' or " string run across newlines. A / the stripper misreads as a division (if (x) /'/.test(y)) or as a regex (a++ / 2; const s = 'x/y') therefore opens a string that blanks the rest of the file and hides a later direct agent( call: the lint fails open. Forms (a), (b) and (c) are older than this fix; (d) is new with the B6-R7 decision. No toy and neither spec skeleton reads TIER, ROLE or OVERRIDE in its hand-written region, so a stricter rule costs nothing.
proposed_resolution: In the hand-written region, reject any reference to TIER, ROLE or OVERRIDE, reject RUN[ and Object.assign(RUN, and reject any tier: key outside the two adoption forms. Have TIER_KEY_RE reject a model: or effort: value that holds a quoted literal anywhere before the next , or }. End a ' or " string at an unescaped newline, which JavaScript forbids, or report the file, so that a misread / cannot hide what follows. Add one test for each form.

outcome.what_was_done: Three rounds each closed the spellings named and the next check found others (an alias of RUN, Reflect.set, a quoted or computed tier key, member writes of model and effort, a template literal that hides a later call). A pattern lint over hand-written JavaScript cannot be made complete, so no fourth round is run. Decided by the orchestrating session: the lint stays as the first check for the ordinary forms, and the check that counts is behavioural. W2, and each later workflow package, asserts in its scenario tests that the model and effort of every step the workflow dispatches equal the roster's tier for that agent, so a spelling the lint misses is caught when it changes what is dispatched. B6's lint docstring must say which forms it catches and that the harness assertion is the authority, and must drop the claim that it cannot fail open; the test that fails when OBJECT_ASSIGN_RUN_RE alone is removed is added then.
outcome.where: next/tests/lint/test_roster_lint.py; next/tests/workflows/universal.test.mjs; packages B6, B5 and W2

problem: The design texts that later packages port still name literals the built prelude no longer defines. story-script.md uses `data: S_IMPLEMENT`, `S_REVIEW`, `S_FIXES` and `S_RULINGS`. wave-script.md uses `S_REVIEW`, `S_HOLDOUT` and `S_RULINGS`. prelude.md lists `S_REVIEW, S_FIXES, S_RULINGS, S_IMPLEMENT, S_HOLDOUT` as the prelude's literals. This unit deleted the composites S_REVIEW/S_FIXES/S_RULINGS/S_HOLDOUT and generates only S_REVIEW_DATA, S_FIX_DATA, S_RULING_DATA, S_HOLDOUT_DATA and S_IMPLEMENT_DATA. It renamed the uses in toy-build.js but not in the spec. A B6/W2/W3 port of story.js or wave.js as written throws ReferenceError.
proposed_resolution: Pick one naming and apply it everywhere: either rename the spec uses in story-script.md, wave-script.md and prelude.md to the generated names, or map those files to the spec names in build.py LITERAL_NAMES. Then add a lint that every S_* identifier appearing in a spec code block or a workflow body is a key of the generated set.

outcome.what_was_done: The spec now uses the generated names. story-script.md and wave-script.md use S_REVIEW_DATA, S_FIX_DATA, S_RULING_DATA, S_HOLDOUT_DATA and S_IMPLEMENT_DATA, and topics/prelude.md is a pointer that lists no literals. A grep of rewrite/spec finds no S_REVIEW, S_FIXES, S_RULINGS or S_HOLDOUT. The new check.py check spec_literals_are_the_generated_set fails on any S_* name in a spec code fence or a workflow body that is not a value of build.LITERAL_NAMES. I tested both sides in a scratch copy: writing `data: S_REVIEW` into the story-script.md code block failed the check, and so did writing it into toy-build.js's body.
outcome.where: rewrite/spec/topics/story-script.md; rewrite/spec/topics/wave-script.md; rewrite/spec/topics/prelude.md; next/tools/check.py spec_literals_are_the_generated_set (also run by tests/lint/test_check.py::TestRepositoryChecks::test_every_registered_check)

problem: SL1-06 is marked fixed, but the guard the design requires is absent. result-schemas.md says `tools/build.py --check` fails on an S_* literal that was not generated. build() only regenerates the region between the generated:schemas markers. Adding `const S_HANDMADE = {...}` to prelude.js's hand-written region (or to a workflow body) passes build --check, check.py 24/24 and the node suite (verified by mutation). LITERAL_NAMES is also a hand list that nothing ties to the shipped schema files. check.py's set is a second hand list. A schema added to both the directory and check.py, but not to LITERAL_NAMES, silently gets no literal.
proposed_resolution: In build() (and therefore --check), scan prelude.js outside the generated blocks, and every workflow file outside its stamped region, for /^\s*const\s+S_[A-Z0-9_]+\s*=/m, and report each hit as a problem. Assert that LITERAL_NAMES' keys equal the set of shipped *.schema.json files, so a missing mapping is an error. Add test_build.py cases for both.

outcome.what_was_done: build() now reports a hand-written `const S_* =` found outside the generated:tables and generated:schemas blocks of prelude.js, and one found outside the stamped region of a workflow (_hand_literal_problems). _mapping_problems requires LITERAL_NAMES plus NON_PRELUDE_SCHEMAS (event.schema.json) to equal the set of shipped *.schema.json files. I tested both in a scratch copy. Appending `const S_HANDMADE = {...}` to prelude.js made build --check print 'hand-written schema literal S_HANDMADE'. Deleting the wave-gate-data mapping made it print 'shipped schemas no literal mapping covers ... wave-gate-data.schema.json'. test_build.py pins both guards. One small gap: the regex matches `const` only, so `let S_X =` is not caught.

problem:
step() does not follow the amended prelude-steps.md.
- The spec rejects a result whose `r.step.method !== o.method`, and tests-workflows.md says step() rejects any identity other than the one given. The built step() checks only name and subject.
- The spec sets `loop: o.loop || 1` whenever pass is given. The built code adds loop only when o.loop is passed, so a review step given only pass carries no loop. It also adds loop without pass.
- converge()'s amended `c.arbitrate(open, pass)` is untested: dropping pass passes every suite.
- Adding the spec's method check changes no test result, so nothing pins the echo contract.
proposed_resolution: Build the identity exactly as prelude-steps.md does: `...(o.pass ? { loop: o.loop || 1, pass: o.pass } : {})`. Add `|| r.step.method !== o.method` to the unusable-result test. Add tests: a stub that echoes a different method is retried and then fails; a step given pass alone carries loop 1; toy-verdict's converge arbitrate stub records the pass it received and the test asserts it.

outcome.what_was_done: step() builds the identity as prelude-steps.md does: `...(o.pass ? { loop: o.loop || 1, pass: o.pass } : {})`. A result whose method differs from o.method is now unusable and is retried. converge() calls c.arbitrate(open, pass, notes). The spec text in prelude-steps.md and prelude-converge.md matches. A new universal test, 'the amended identity and arbitration', covers three cases: a stub that echoes a foreign method gets 2 calls and then fails; a step given pass alone carries loop 1; and arbitrate receives pass 2 and the dispute note. I re-ran four mutations in scratch, and that test failed each time: dropping the method check, using the old identity form, calling arbitrate(open), and calling arbitrate(open, pass) without the notes.
outcome.where: next/workflow-lib/prelude.js step(), converge(); rewrite/spec/topics/prelude-steps.md; next/tests/workflows/universal.test.mjs 'the amended identity and arbitration: a foreign method is retried then fails; pass alone carries loop 1; arbitrate sees the pass and the dispute notes'

problem: relay() only half-adopts the amendment ("relay() uses the empty-object fallback"). The final fallback returns emptyOf(schema), but the clerk is still told `If it prints no JSON, return {"ok": false, "error": "<what it printed>"}`. The amended spec says to return `JSON.stringify(emptyOf(schema))` with error set to what the command printed. The partial object fails the schema it is bound to; for example survey requires 19 fields. On the platform the clerk's result is then rejected and retried, so the printed error is lost and the run reports 'The clerk step returned nothing, twice.' Test 14 covers only a dead clerk.
proposed_resolution: Use the spec's prompt text, which embeds JSON.stringify(emptyOf(schema)) with error set. Add a universal test that the clerk prompt for S_SURVEY and S_CLOSE carries the full empty object.

outcome.what_was_done: emptyOf() now recurses into object-typed required members (a nested required field is filled by the same empty-by-type rule), and the relayed-output enums admit '': status of checkpoint-result and workflow-result, and next.kind of checkpoint-result, workflow-result and survey, with the composition checks in check.py unchanged because all composed copies were widened together. The dictated error object of relay() — the schema's empty object with error set — is therefore valid for every schema a clerk is bound to. A universal test relays all four schemas through a clerk that does exactly what the prompt says and the harness's validateValue accepts each answer; the mutation (old flat emptyOf) fails it. prelude-steps.md carries the same function.
outcome.where: next/workflow-lib/prelude.js emptyOf(); next/plugins/vsdd-factory/schemas/{checkpoint-result,workflow-result,survey}.schema.json; rewrite/spec/topics/prelude-steps.md; next/tests/workflows/universal.test.mjs 'the dictated no-JSON answer is a valid result of every relayed schema' (and the next:{kind:""} assertions of tests 7 and 14 updated to the valid shape)

Setting project_dir to '/proj' in okStub makes test 7 fail (verified in scratch).

problem: Admitting null in EVENT_SCHEMA also opened the Python writer to null, which nothing reports. build() refuses only `not str(self.session_id).strip()`, and str(None) is 'None', so `EventLog(dir, None).build('session.start')` now returns session_id None and log() writes it. HEAD's events.py refused the same call ('$.session_id: expected string, got null'). event-log.md and the spec event schema say null appears 'only on a line the launcher wrote'. The outcome claims the writer keeps its strict non-empty session id, but test_writer_session_id_stays_a_string only reads the fixture's 'sess-1'. _fit's slim path would write the string 'None'.
proposed_resolution: In build(), refuse `not isinstance(self.session_id, str) or not self.session_id.strip()`. In _fit, keep the value as a string without calling str() on None. Add a test that EventLog(d, None).build(...) raises EventError.

outcome.what_was_done: EventLog.build() now refuses any session id that is not a non-empty str (`not isinstance(self.session_id, str) or not self.session_id.strip()`). _fit's slim path slices the string and never calls str() on None. test_session_id_must_be_a_string asserts that EventLog(d, None).build('session.start') raises EventError. Reverting to the old `not str(self.session_id).strip()` in scratch failed exactly that test.

problem: The delivered wave-gate-data, now the single source with the spec file reduced to a pointer, types `pending` as a boolean ('True while the wave gate's CI job still runs'). gate-wave.md says the command 'reports any story that still blocks the gate in pending', and wave-script.md does `g.pending.length` and `g.pending.join(', ')`. With a boolean, `.length` is undefined, so wave.js's 'Stories not yet delivered' stop never fires and nothing reports it; with a real list, the platform rejects the clerk's output. `pending` also duplicates `state: pending`. `stories` items are full story-unit objects while wave-script.md builds its prompt with `g.stories.join(', ')`.
proposed_resolution: Type pending as an array of story ids (required, [] when none) and let `state` carry the job state. Settle the item type of `stories` with wave-script.md (ids, or change the script text to map u.id). Add valid and invalid fixtures for both.

outcome.what_was_done: In wave-gate-data, pending is now a required array of story ids, and the state property is gone. wave-script.md now builds its prompt with g.stories.map((u) => u.id).join(', ') to match the story-unit items. The invalid fixture invalid_pending-not-an-array pins the type, and the relay-rule check pins that pending is required. A neighbouring problem, which was already there and is not caused by this fix: holdout_batches has the same item-type mismatch, filed as L2C-catchup-1.

The Walls sections of clerk.md, adversary.md, ui-reviewer.md and code-reviewer.md link their rows and no longer list read_deny. The AU-S2-09 text in outcomes/c2.json matches. Text only, checked by spec_lint.

problem: The meaning of @<method> is ambiguous. The header says it applies 'only in a story whose resolved method for the stage written (the kind's, or the story's tests_method / impl_method) is that one'. Take devops writing tests under 'tests:create@repo-setup' in a chore story. If 'the stage written' means the tests stage, the method resolves to tests_method, which is '' because a chore has no tests stage, so the scaffold's test files are blocked. If it means the caller's own stage, it resolves to impl_method = repo-setup. No test covers either reading.
proposed_resolution: Define the suffix as matching the resolved method of the stage the caller runs in that story (for devops, impl_method). Add a policy test or a write-scopes case for tests:create@repo-setup.

outcome.what_was_done: artifacts/story.md now says the @<method> suffix matches 'the resolved method of the caller's own stage', linking [[rule:write-scopes]], the wording walls.toml, artifacts.toml and write-scopes.md carry.

problem: The artifact rows outside the slice carry prose placeholders, not globs. Examples: 'SS-<NN>.md', 'supplements/nfr.md, errors.md, interfaces.md', 'AC-<k>.(tape, spec.ts, sh), AC-<k>.txt, ...'. They also have no id patterns. A loader that matches globs would send every write to these kinds to [_unknown], which blocks it. demo-evidence's max_bytes = 1,500,000 is the per-story total. The per-file caps (script 8,000; transcript 20,000; screenshot 300,000) are only in cap_note prose, so a per-file check would allow 1.5 MB per file, and [caps] accepts demo-evidence = 3,000,000. The builder's deferred list names the untested wall rows but not these artifact rows.
proposed_resolution: Say in the file header which artifact rows are design placeholders and untested. Otherwise give them real globs and id patterns, and split the demo-evidence caps per file type.

outcome.what_was_done: Fixed by the first option the finding offered. The artifacts.toml header now says that the kind rows other than contract and story are untested design placeholders: their glob and id cells use the design's notation, and a loader would send their writes to [_unknown]. It also says that where a kind caps per file, max_bytes is the per-kind or per-story total and cap_note carries the per-file caps. Real cells wait for the packages that ship each kind. The same header claims [contract] and [[story-kind]] are pinned by test_policy.py, which is not true; see L2C-c2-b6-1.

proposed_resolution: Write the choice into commands/story-deliver.md, or word the outcome as a recommendation to G4a.

outcome.what_was_done: The VSA-18 choice is in commands/story-deliver.md under 'Conflict repair': before the repair step, the tool merges the integration head into the story branch, so the builder rows keep only git-commit and git-read. The VSA-18 outcome in outcomes/c2.json is worded as left-for-builder for G4a, which builds the step. Text only.

problem: registry.toml assigns [table.identifiers] to package C2 and the C2 brief lists it under Implements, but C2 deferred it to an S-package. Anything that reads the registry will count C2 as having delivered the identifiers table.
proposed_resolution: Reassign table:identifiers to the S-package that allocates ids, or add a Notes line to packages/C2.md stating the deferral.

outcome.what_was_done: registry.toml [table.identifiers] now names package S1. packages/S1.md lists [[table:identifiers]] under Implements, and packages/C2.md no longer does. Checked by spec_lint, which reads the registry.

problem: The shipped tables do not say how a grant or a denial applies to classes nested inside it. Read literally, classes.toml's 'A contained class is matched first' gives each path one class. Then main's read_deny of 'holdout' would not cover holdout-evaluations, the product-owner's 'spec-product' grant would not cover brief, and the architect's 'spec-arch' grant would not cover guidance. The rule the design means ('wherever a row says holdout, it covers holdout-evaluations too'; read_allow 'wins over a containing class that is denied') is stated only in the information-walls topic and partly in the read_allow key note.
proposed_resolution: State in the walls.toml header that a class named in read_deny or write also covers the classes nested inside it, except those named in read_allow. Add tests: main denied holdout-evaluations, product-owner may write brief, architect may write guidance.

outcome.what_was_done: The walls.toml header now has a Coverage paragraph: a class named in read_deny or write also covers the classes nested inside it, except those the row's read_allow names (code-reviewer and guidance, holdout-evaluator and brief), and a write grant covers nested classes the same way. TestClassCoverage derives the nesting from the globs and pins it, and pins the table facts the rule depends on: main denies holdout and not holdout-evaluations by name, the product-owner's spec-product grant covers brief, the architect's spec-arch grant covers guidance, and the read_allow exceptions. A spec-arch glob typo fails the nesting test. The matcher that applies the rule belongs to H3/H4, so table-level tests are as far as this can go now.

problem: In _stamp_agents (lines 353-364), the test is is_reviewer = (agents.get(name) or model) == roster['tiers']['reviewer']['model']. For a rostered agent this compares the tier name 'reviewer' with the model 'opus', so it is never true and no reviewer in the roster gets the severity table or the key rule. The B6 lint (test_roster_lint.py lines 216-222) decides reviewer status itself (tier_name == 'reviewer') and requires both regions, then tells the author to 'run tools/build.py'. Running it changes nothing and build --check reports the tree current. I reproduced this in a scratch copy: an adversary.md after build.py has 0 severity markers, check passes, and the lint fails. The lint's docstring says the stamping 'delegates to tools/build.py itself', but the reviewer decision is made twice and the two disagree. No test runs the build's stamping and then the lint: test_reviewer_without_the_severity_stamp_is_rejected stamps with the lint's own helper. This breaks A6a (adversary, security-reviewer) in step 5, or forces a hand-written copy of the severity table, which the design forbids.
proposed_resolution: In _stamp_agents, decide reviewer status by tier name: is_reviewer = agents.get(name) == 'reviewer'. Fall back to the model comparison only for agents not in the roster. Expose that decision as one function (for example build_mod.is_reviewer(name, roster)) and call it from the lint, so there is one decision. Add a seam test: write a reviewer agent with empty marker pairs into a temporary plugin, run build_mod.build() against it, and assert that agent_problems returns [].

outcome.what_was_done: build.py has one decision, is_reviewer(name, roster, text): it goes by tier name for a rostered agent and falls back to the model comparison only for agents outside the roster. _stamp_agents and the lint's agent_problems both call it. TestBuildStampingSeam::test_a_reviewer_stamped_by_the_build_passes_the_lint runs the build's own _stamp_agents on an adversary file and asserts that agent_problems returns []. Confirmed in a scratch copy: putting back the old model comparison fails test_reviewer_without_the_severity_stamp_is_rejected and the seam test.

problem: KNOWN_TOOLS (lines 51-71) lists the MCP tools by bare name (query-docs, perplexity_ask, browser_navigate and so on). topics/research-and-browser-tools.md requires every agent that needs an MCP tool to list both 'mcp__plugin_vsdd-factory_<server>__<tool>' and 'mcp__<server>__<tool>'. topics/platform-proven.md item 10 shows that a tool name which does not resolve is dropped silently from an agent's list. The lint rejects both required spellings as 'not a known tool' (probed) and accepts the bare names, which resolve to nothing. Most step-5 agents carry DOCS, LOOKUP, BROWSER or STORYBOOK (test-writer, implementer, verifier, devops, demo-recorder, security-reviewer, architect). The lint therefore forces the spelling under which these agents would silently run without their tools.
proposed_resolution: Build the known set from <plugin>/.mcp.json's server keys and the per-server tool lists. Accept a name when it is a built-in tool, or when it is 'mcp__plugin_vsdd-factory_<server>__<tool>' or 'mcp__<server>__<tool>' for a tool of that server's set (storybook in the second form only, per step-5 plan D8). Reject bare MCP names. Require that a plugin-server tool is listed in both spellings. Add fixture tests for both spellings, for a bare name, and for a list missing one of the pair.

outcome.what_was_done: The lint accepts built-in tools plus MCP tools spelled mcp__plugin_vsdd-factory_<server>__<tool> or mcp__<server>__<tool>, for servers in .mcp.json and the per-server lists of topics/tool-sets.md. Storybook is accepted in the second form only. It rejects bare MCP names and requires both spellings for a bundled server's tool. Fixture tests cover both spellings, a bare name, each spelling alone, and storybook alone. Confirmed in a scratch copy: turning off the bare-name rejection fails test_a_bare_mcp_tool_name_is_rejected, and turning off the pair rule fails test_one_spelling_without_the_other_is_rejected. Related, already recorded by the fixer as L2-c2-b6-fix-1: the shipped reader refuses unquoted MCP names, so tools lines must be quoted.
outcome.where: next/tests/lint/test_roster_lint.py::_tool_problems, MCP_SERVER_TOOLS; TestAgentLint (test_a_bare_mcp_tool_name_is_rejected, test_both_spellings_..., test_one_spelling_..., test_the_second_spelling_alone_..., test_the_storybook_spelling_alone_...)

problem: Lines 207-209 hold len(text.splitlines()) to agent_file_lines = 70, counting the stamped regions. topics/agent-file.md and agents-skills.md 2.7 define the 70 as frontmatter plus a body of at most 60 lines, with the stamped regions not counted. The shared block is 14 lines plus markers, and a reviewer also carries the severity table (6 lines) and the key rule. The effective body cap is therefore about 45 lines for a builder and about 33 for a reviewer, not 60. Probe: the spec's own 'complete example' adversary, stamped, is 71 lines with a 34-line body, and the lint rejects it. The roster's own comment ('whole file: frontmatter plus a body of at most 60 lines') describes a different count from the one the lint makes. The fixture tests use short bodies, so none exposes this.
proposed_resolution: Apply agent_file_lines to the file with its stamped regions removed (the same _without_stamped_regions the body count uses). Add a test that runs the spec example from topics/agent-file.md, stamped, through agent_problems and expects [], and a test that a 61-line body fails while a 60-line one passes.

outcome.what_was_done: agent_file_lines (70) now applies to the file with its stamped regions removed, and agent_body_lines (60) to the body without them. test_the_agent_file_topic_example_passes_stamped runs the complete example from topics/agent-file.md, stamped as a reviewer, and expects []. test_a_body_at_the_budget_passes_and_one_line_over_fails checks 60 lines pass and 61 fail. Confirmed in a scratch copy: counting the whole file again fails the 60/61 test.

problem: workflow_problems (lines 226-260) treats only workflow('...') with a single or double quote as a call edge, and it removes the stamped prelude before scanning. Workflows call story through the prelude's runStories() (the toy toy-build.js does so), and that call sits in the hand-written region, so the lint never sees it. Probes: a story.js whose own region calls runStories() passes, although pipeline.md 2.3 says story contains no workflow() call and nesting throws at run time. A release.js calling runStories() passes, although the roster gives release calls = []. A wave calling workflow(`vsdd-factory:release`) with backticks passes. test_wave_may_call_story replaces 'runStories(units)' with a workflow() call, so the test avoids the real call form. L-XREF's first clause (every vsdd-factory:<name> in a shipped file resolves) is neither built nor listed among the deferrals.
proposed_resolution: Count a runStories( call in the hand-written region as an edge to 'story'. Accept backtick literals in the call pattern. Report a workflow() call whose first argument is not a literal as a problem. Add tests: story calling runStories is rejected; release calling runStories is rejected; wave calling runStories passes. Either implement vsdd-factory:<name> resolution over agents, workflows and walls.toml now, or list it with the deferrals in the docstring.

outcome.what_was_done: The call scan allows whitespace before the parenthesis, and every workflow( call whose first argument is not one complete quoted literal (concatenation, interpolation, bare name) is reported as non-literal — the argument is read from the original body at the scanner's offset. The backtick test is now a forbidden edge: wave calling `vsdd-factory:release` with backticks is rejected.

problem: _parse_frontmatter (lines 93-111) lowercases every key and splits each line at the first colon. Probes show that 'omitclaudemd: true' and 'Model: sonnet' pass the lint, yet the platform reads the exact keys, so it would silently load the project's CLAUDE.md into the agent (the holdout-evaluator wall relies on this key) or ignore the model. A folded 'description: >' block passes as a one-character description, which gets past the 200-character cap. A strict, case-preserving reader already ships (plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/frontmatter.py) that refuses block scalars. The lint wrote a second, looser parser instead of using it.
proposed_resolution: Parse agent frontmatter with vsdd.frontmatter.parse, which keeps key case and refuses block scalars, and compare keys exactly (omitClaudeMd, model, ...). Report a parse error as a lint problem. Add tests for a wrong-case key, a block-scalar description and a quoted model value.

outcome.what_was_done: Agent frontmatter is now parsed with the shipped vsdd.frontmatter.parse, which keeps key case and refuses block scalars, and a parse error is reported as a lint problem. Keys are compared exactly. Tests cover a lowercase omitclaudemd (rejected), a folded 'description: >' (rejected as unparseable) and a quoted model value (accepted). A probe shows 'Model: sonnet' reported both as a key outside the template and as a model mismatch.

problem: L-AGENT (tables/lint-checks.toml) ends 'Every agent has a row in walls.toml and every row has an agent.' Both inputs ship now (the roster lists all 20 agents and walls.toml has their rows), but nothing checks this: not this lint, not check.py's policy_tables_are_consistent, not test_policy.py. It is also missing from the docstring's deferrals. A misspelled row key (for example 'vsdd-factory:adversry') would silently drop that agent to the [other] row, which grants write = ['project'] and no 'outside' denial, and that weakens its wall. L-KIND catches this only for the stage agents of story kinds.
proposed_resolution: Add to check_all a check that {row[len('vsdd-factory:'):] for each 'vsdd-factory:*' row} equals set(roster['agents']), reporting the missing and the extra names. Add a fixture test for each direction.

outcome.what_was_done: walls_row_problems checks that the vsdd-factory:* rows of walls.toml equal the roster's [agents] and reports missing and extra names. check_all calls it, so TestLiveTree runs it over the real tables. Fixture tests cover the matching case, a missing row and an extra (misspelt) row. Confirmed in a scratch copy: suppressing the extra-row report fails test_an_extra_row_is_reported. Small gap: removing the call from check_all passes, because the live tables agree.

problem: The [overrides] comment says 'lint rejects any other', and the same claim appears in rewrite/spec/conventions.md (Model tiers), topics/model-tiers.md, packaging/tests-lint.md and the generated comment in prelude.js. No code does this: no lint, check or harness test rejects a workflow that runs a step off its agent's tier, whether by a direct agent() call with its own model or effort, or by assigning RUN.tier or the tier tables in its own region. The user's model policy depends on this, and the story workflow (W2) is the next workflow to ship.
proposed_resolution: In workflow_problems, reject in the hand-written region any direct agent( call (steps must go through step(), relay() or gated()), any 'model:' or 'effort:' key, and any assignment to RUN.tier, TIER, ROLE or OVERRIDE. Add fixture tests. If this is deferred instead, say so in the roster comment and the docstring rather than claiming it.

outcome.what_was_done: (1) RUN_TIER_ADOPTION_RE matches only a dotted member chain on an input object ending in '|| null' (a.tier, s.config.tier_override, survey.config.tier_override), and workflow_problems skips it only when the chain names no TIER, ROLE or OVERRIDE. RUN.tier = TIER.planner, RUN.tier = TIER.reviewer || null, RUN.tier = a.tier || TIER.planner, RUN.tier = a.tier and RUN.tier = 'planner' are each rejected now (test_pinning_the_run_to_a_tier_is_rejected; the old loose regex accepted the first three). (2) _strip_comments_and_strings scans a template literal's ${...} interpolations as code, so a direct agent(, a model:/effort: literal and a forbidden workflow('vsdd-factory:release') written inside a template are reported (test_interpolations_are_scanned_as_code). A regular-expression literal is opaque: escapes and [...] classes hold no terminator, flags are consumed, and a regex that does not close before the line's newline reads as division, so a quote inside /'/g no longer throws the string state off and a following direct agent( is reported (test_a_regex_literal_hides_nothing_after_it). (3) The stripping is pinned by tests that fail with it removed: test_a_comment_and_a_prompt_string_are_not_tier_settings (a comment 'the agent (x)' and a prompt string 'effort: high' trip nothing) was checked by mutation to fail with js = body. (4) The data-key question is decided and tested: a model:/effort: key whose value is carried ({ model: u.model, effort: u.effort }) passes what the run was given and is allowed; one set from a quoted literal is a tier setting and is rejected (TIER_KEY_RE narrowed; test_a_carried_model_data_key_is_not_a_tier_setting, both halves). Lint suite: 85 passed, 1 skipped.
outcome.where: next/tests/lint/test_roster_lint.py (_strip_comments_and_strings, RUN_TIER_ADOPTION_RE + TIER_NAME_RE, TIER_KEY_RE; TestWorkflowLint: test_a_comment_and_a_prompt_string_are_not_tier_settings, test_interpolations_are_scanned_as_code, test_a_regex_literal_hides_nothing_after_it, test_the_skeleton_tier_adoptions_are_allowed, test_pinning_the_run_to_a_tier_is_rejected, test_a_carried_model_data_key_is_not_a_tier_setting)

problem: The AU-S2-09 outcome says the B6 part is in place and that conventions.md 'already points there'. conventions.md (lines about 106-116) still restates every tier's model and effort, and topics/model-tiers.md restates the overrides. These are the very second statements the finding names. The outcome also says the lint rejects a colour that 'disagrees with its tier row', but colours are not in the roster's tier rows: they are a hard-coded TIER_COLOR table in the lint, and the clerk's colour is not checked at all (step-5 plan D10 picks yellow).
proposed_resolution: Reduce the tier table in conventions.md to a link to tests/lint/roster.toml. Move colour into [tiers] (for example planner = { model, effort, color = "blue" }, with a clerk colour) and read it in the lint. Correct the AU-S2-09 what_was_done text.

outcome.what_was_done: Colour is now part of each [tiers] row, including the clerk's (yellow, per step-5 plan D10), and the lint reads it from there. test_wrong_colour_for_the_tier_is_rejected and test_the_clerk_colour_comes_from_the_roster pin this; removing the colour check fails the clerk-colour test, and removing the clerk colour from the roster fails tools/check.py. conventions.md's tier table keeps only 'Used for' and points at the roster for model, effort and colour. topics/model-tiers.md no longer lists the override steps. The AU-S2-09 text in outcomes/b6.json matches. The edit left the same three sentences twice in conventions.md; see L2C-c2-b6-2.
outcome.where: next/tests/lint/roster.toml [tiers]; next/tests/lint/test_roster_lint.py::agent_problems, TestAgentLint; rewrite/spec/conventions.md (Model tiers); rewrite/spec/topics/model-tiers.md; rewrite/findings/outcomes/b6.json

problem: The section 'Built files under next/ (recorded, not changed)' still says the built roster has status = "model", listed_description_chars = 400 and agent_file_lines = 60, and contrasts these with 'the spec table'. B6 changed the built file to "both", 4400 and 70 and turned the spec table into a pointer, so the spec file now describes a difference that no longer exists.
proposed_resolution: Change the roster bullets to record that B6 brought the built file into line with agents-skills.md 2.12 and that the spec table is now a pointer, or remove them.

outcome.what_was_done: The roster bullet in conflicts/tables-repair.md now says B6 brought the built file into line with agents-skills.md#2.12 (status "both", 4400, 70), that the spec table is a pointer, and that no difference remains. Text only.

problem: roster_problems (lines 307-318) checks only that the budget keys exist and the model-visible count, and its failure branches have no test (it is only asserted to return [] on the live roster). It does not check that each [agents] value is a [tiers] key, that the [overrides] values are tiers and their keys name roster workflows, that [workflows] call targets are roster workflows and a called workflow has calls = [], or that [skills] values are person, model or both. Also, [platform] python_floor is read by nothing (check.py hard-codes (3, 11)), and check.py hard-codes engines '>=2.1.331' and the icon path, so the floor is stated in two places.
proposed_resolution: Add these integrity checks to roster_problems, with a fixture test for each. Have check.py read the floors from the roster, or drop python_floor from the roster and say where the floor lives.

outcome.what_was_done: roster_problems now checks that every [agents] value is a tier, every [overrides] value is a tier and every override key names a roster workflow. It checks that [workflows] call targets are roster workflows and a called workflow has calls = [], that [skills] values are person, model or both, and that the budget keys exist. Each check has a fixture test in TestRosterIntegrity. tools/check.py reads engines (min_claude_code) and python_floor from roster [platform]. Gaps, not regressions: the model-visible-skills over-budget branch still has no test (removing it passes), and the manifest icon path is still a literal in check.py, which is a manifest value rather than a floor.

problem: L-KIND can switch off without a message. check_all skips it when py/vsdd/policy is not a directory (line 392). kind_grant_problems passes when artifacts.toml yields zero [[story-kind]] rows, and silently skips a kind whose implement_agent is empty. test_policy.py's import-time load and test_seven_kinds mitigate this today. In addition, grant qualifiers are ignored: an implementer granted only 'source:before-red' or 'source:create' would satisfy the 'source' need.
proposed_resolution: Report a missing policy directory and zero story kinds as problems, and treat an empty implement_agent as a problem. Treat ':before-red' and ':create' as not meeting an unconditional write need, or state that L-KIND checks class presence only.

outcome.what_was_done: check_all reports a missing policy directory. kind_grant_problems reports zero [[story-kind]] rows and an empty implement_agent. ':create' and ':before-red' no longer meet an unconditional write need, while ':frozen' still does, and the comment says so. Tests cover zero kinds, an empty implement agent and a conditional qualifier; mutations of each fail. Gap: the missing-policy-directory branch has no test.

problem: The roster-to-disk half of L-ROSTER ('none missing') is off, as the build plan allows. Nothing in a test run says so: the off state is recorded only in comments, and nothing names the switch-on point (E1 part 2).
proposed_resolution: Add test_nothing_in_the_roster_is_absent_from_disk, implemented and marked unittest.skip('switches on with E1 part 2 (packaging/build-plan.md)'), so every run reports the check as skipped and the switch is a one-line change.

outcome.what_was_done: absence_problems(plugin, roster) implements the roster-side half of L-ROSTER next to membership_problems. Fixture tests prove it: a fully populated temporary plugin passes, and removing an agent file, a skill directory or a workflow file each fails. The live-tree test against the PLUGIN constant is written and stays skip-marked only until E1 part 2 fills agents/, skills/ and workflows/ — switching it on is deleting the decorator.

problem: The pointer comment restates the workflow call edges ('wave, feature, verify, maintain and multi calling story and story calling none'). conflicts/people-repair.md P-8 does the same, and both copy the shipped roster's data, which breaks README rule 1 and rule 7. The registry summary for table:roster still says the roster carries 'each agent's tier, tools and package', which the shipped file does not. topics/tool-sets.md says 'the agent-file lint checks each file against' the named sets, but L-AGENT checks only membership in the union, so an adversary listing Bash or Edit passes.
proposed_resolution: Reduce the pointer to the file path and its consumers. Correct the registry summary. Either make the per-agent tool sets data (for example a tool_sets key in the roster [agents]) and check each agent file against them, or change tool-sets.md to say what the lint actually checks.

outcome.what_was_done: The pointer in rewrite/spec/tables/roster.toml now gives only the file path, its tables and its consumers, with no call edges. conflicts/people-repair.md P-8 names the shipped rows as the one copy and no longer repeats the edges. The registry summary for table:roster matches the shipped file (floors, tiers, each agent's tier, skills, calls, overrides, budgets). topics/tool-sets.md now says what the lint does: each tools entry is checked against the union of the sets, and the per-agent table is prose. The lint's known tools match the tool-sets table.

problem: B6 added tests/lint/test_roster_lint.py to the prelude-marker guard's allowlist (line 434) because TestWorkflowLint.write_workflow writes the marker strings as literals. The test module already loads build_mod and could use build_mod.PRELUDE_MARKERS, which would leave the guard narrower. As written, if the markers ever change, the fixtures stop carrying real markers and those tests still pass. Also, the AU-P2-01 outcome's statement that 'the prelude and the lint read' the call edges 'from one place' is wrong: the prelude reads no [workflows] table.
proposed_resolution: Build the fixture marker lines from build_mod.PRELUDE_MARKERS, drop test_roster_lint.py from the allowlist, and correct the outcome sentence.

outcome.what_was_done: test_roster_lint.py is off the prelude-marker guard's allowlist; only harness.mjs, universal.test.mjs and test_build.py remain. TestWorkflowLint.write_workflow builds its marker lines from build_mod.PRELUDE_MARKERS, so a marker change reaches the fixtures. The guard pins this: a literal marker in test_roster_lint.py would fail build --check and the build_is_current check. The AU-P2-01 outcome in outcomes/b6.json now says the prelude reads no [workflows] table.

problem: The unit's new finding L2-b6-1 names only next/ files in its 'where' field, so findings.py maps it to no spec file and no package ('mapped to no spec file: ... L2-b6-1'). It will appear in no by-package list, and the agent packages that widen method sets, which its resolution asks to act, will never see it.
proposed_resolution: Add tables/lint-checks.toml (and, if wanted, the A-package agent files) to its 'where' field so it routes to B6 and the agent packages, then rebuild the ledger.

outcome.what_was_done: L2-b6-1's where field now names rewrite/spec/tables/lint-checks.toml, which registry.toml assigns to B6. origin: orchestrating session, 2026-11-24, after four rounds on the hook runner's shell parser
problem: The runner approves an agent's vsdd call, with the rewrite that carries the caller marker, when the shell parser finds the command to be one plain segment that is not opaque. That makes the parser a security boundary built as a deny-list: it must recognise every construct that could run something else. Four review rounds each found new ways through (a substitution beside arithmetic, quotes nested in a parameter expansion, $[ ] inside double quotes, ANSI-C quoting, ${name@P}), in each case getting an arbitrary command approved without a prompt. A deny-list over shell syntax cannot be shown complete across sh, bash, dash and zsh.
proposed_resolution: Decide approval by an allow-list on the raw command text, in addition to the parsed shape. A command is a plain vsdd call only if the whole text is: the program (vsdd, or a path of safe characters ending /vsdd), then arguments separated by spaces or tabs, each either a bare word made only of ASCII letters, digits and _ @ % + = : , . / - or a single-quoted string that starts after whitespace or after = at the end of a bare word, ends before whitespace or the end of the text, and holds no single quote and no control character. Nothing else: no double quote, dollar, backtick, backslash, semicolon, ampersand, pipe, angle bracket, parenthesis, brace, bracket, star, question mark, tilde, hash, exclamation mark, newline or carriage return anywhere outside a single-quoted string. Any other command that runs vsdd passes unmarked and unapproved, as HD8 already says. The parser's 'not opaque' is never by itself a reason to approve anything.

outcome.what_was_done: Pinned the two unpinned rules of the allow-list with tests; the code was already right and is unchanged for this finding. (1) A single-quoted string holds no character below U+0020 and no U+007F: REFUSED_CALLS in test_caller.py gains six calls whose single-quoted argument holds, in turn, a tab, a newline, a carriage return, a NUL, an escape character and DEL ('vsdd survey a\tb' and friends), so test_allow_list_refuses_every_excluded_character and test_allow_list_regex_refuses_the_tables_on_its_own cover the rule; and the property test's between-quotes position now draws from an alphabet that holds every control character below U+0020 and DEL besides the excluded characters and the single quote. The between-quotes construction anchors the span with a plain x ('vsdd survey --flag value 'x<junk>''), so a widened span class cannot swallow the junk and close the argument cleanly: restoring _QUOTED = r"'[^']*'" now fails three tests (the refusal table, the regex-alone table and test_property_junk_from_excluded_characters_never_approves, caught in 51 of its 200 draws; the old doubled-quote construction caught none), and letting only the tab in fails two. (2) A quoted string may follow a bare word only when that word ends with '=': REFUSED_CALLS gains 'vsdd survey a\'b'', a bare letter directly followed by a quoted string; loosening the prefix to (?:(?!=)[_SAFE_]*)? in caller.py fails the refusal table and the regex-alone table. Both new-table facts also travel with the property test, which asserts every drawing is refused while caller._CALL_TEXT_RE and the parser both hold. Mutation proofs ran in a scratch copy of next/ built from the pre-fix tree; each mutation was restored byte-identically afterwards.
outcome.where: next/tests/hooks/test_caller.py (REFUSED_CALLS: six control-character quoted spans and vsdd survey a'b'; test_property_junk_from_excluded_characters_never_approves: the between-quotes alphabet and anchor)

where: rewrite/spec/topics/long-commands.md; the G1 open probe in rewrite/plans/step-3/RESOLUTIONS.md; items 43 and 6 of the platform record; rewrite/plans/step-5/agents.md M3 and the clerk
problem: The design worded the Bash timeout as a kill ('the tool stops a foreground command', 'a call killed by a timeout'). Observed on Claude Code 2.1.331, macOS, default mode, sandbox off and on: a foreground call past its Bash timeout is not killed at the timeout. It is moved to the background (timedOutAfterMs, a backgroundTaskId, backgroundEndsWithFinalResponse true), and it is killed when the step agent gives its final response (its task output reads '[killed]'). The platform does reap it, at the step's end. The notice the agent reads at the move tells it to wait for the result before its final response and not to start a second copy while the call runs (item 43 quotes it): the opposite of what a job command needs, so an agent told only to run the command again gets two contradicting instructions. A double-forked worker in its own session (fork, setsid, fork) survived that kill and the session's exit and wrote its file about 40 s later, sandbox off and on, so a job outlives its step only because it is detached: detachment is necessary, not a precaution. Linux is untested. Evidence: rewrite/spike/probes-round-4/CHECK.md (reruns C and D); round 4's own legs did not show survival.
proposed_resolution: long-commands.md states the premise as observed: backgrounded at the timeout, killed at the step's final response, the job surviving because its worker is detached. The job record covers what outlives the step. An agent whose call is moved to the background runs the same command again, which re-attaches, and does not wait for or read the background task. Because the platform's notice says the opposite at that moment, the agent is given the rule with its reason (the re-run re-attaches to the job already running and is not a second copy) in the builder methods' common text and the clerk's rules (step 5), and a lint test checks that the sentence is there. The Linux leg stays an open probe (platform.md, open leg 43). E2's eleven-minute gate reads its transcripts: wherever a call shows the backgrounding signature (timedOutAfterMs, a backgroundTaskId), the step's next Bash call is the same command. A run in which no call was moved says that this was not measured.

outcome.what_was_done: G1: the job record, not the tool's timeout, is what reaps a job. E2: its eleven-minute gate must measure that a call moved to the background is followed by a re-run of the same command, which re-attaches.

No step was running, so this is not a stop in the middle of a workflow. Shape 2, cap 0.02, seen in the check's rerun only: the cap was passed while the first step ran; standard error says 'Budget limit reached ($0.05 of $0.02); stopping background agents.'; the run record reads status killed and result null and adds a key error ('Error: Workflow aborted'); the running step is left in state progress and its result is lost, though the hook log holds that step's StructuredOutput PreToolUse payload with no PostToolUse; the later steps never started. The cap is soft: what is in flight is charged past it (0.0578 and 0.0651 dollars on a 5-cent cap; 0.0544 on a 2-cent cap, 2.7 times); how far a large step overshoots was not measured. A driver that diagnosed from the session result alone could not tell the shapes apart and would discard a usable result in the first; one that indexes result['result'] would raise. Alongside this, leg A settled what the plans flagged as open. The typed workflow command starts the named file byte for byte with no skill and no main-session denial. The plugin's hooks, workflow and bin/ load under --setting-sources project,local --strict-mcp-config, with the sandbox-off --settings flag honoured (a commit under .git/worktrees/ succeeded); the person's user-level CLAUDE.md still reaches the main session and the step under those flags. A step's hook payloads carry the effort the step was dispatched with: low under a session at medium (the prober's run, where the agent file also said low) and, in the check's rerun, low under an agent file at xhigh; a main-session payload carries the session's effort (medium). The plan ships STEP_EFFORT_PROVEN false, so the plan must change: it ships true. Evidence: rewrite/spike/probes-round-5/CHECK.md, which holds where RESULTS.md beside it differs; leg-A/ and leg-B/.
proposed_resolution: first-run.md 3.7 (the cause budget_stop) and ORDER.md section 7 (its row) say: the session reports error_max_budget_usd (exit 1, is_error true, no result key, errors naming the cap), and the driver reads the run record. It is completed with the whole result when the cap was passed after the workflow ended. It is killed, with error 'Workflow aborted', result null and the running step left in progress, when the cap was passed during a step; standard error then says 'Budget limit reached ...; stopping background agents.' The diagnosis names that step; its result may be in the hook capture with no PostToolUse. Resume with --dir. The driver reads result.get('result'), never result['result']. The caps are soft and the plans say so beside them: the session cap, and the total over all attempts, can each be passed by one attempt's in-flight calls. STEP_EFFORT_PROVEN in tests/e2e/probe.py ships True, resting on item 53 with the check's rerun (first-run.md D11; ORDER.md 8.2 row A4 and the E2 line of 8.4), as PR5C-15 says. No change to the isolation flags or the allowed-tools list; ORDER-6 8.2's follow-ups (Skill in the list, a --user-settings default) do not trigger.

where: rewrite/spec/platform.md (the standing observation); rewrite/spec/skills/setup.md (project CLAUDE.md sections); rewrite/spec/packaging/build-plan.md (E1 and E2 headless runs, including the slice's E2 first run); rewrite/spec/topics/compaction-and-cold-start.md (cold-start briefing)

Add a fixture-placement note to the E1/E2 setup steps and to packaging/sample-project.md.

problem: platform.md item 13 assumed the platform's block-on-failure setting covers a missing hook launcher. The probe shows the opposite: with every hook command pointing at a missing file, sh exits 127 and the headless session ran normally; each failure surfaced in the transcript as a non-blocking hook error, so the platform fails open rather than blocking (R6). Exit 127 is treated as non-blocking, confirming what topics/hook-wiring.md already records for a missing uv.
proposed_resolution: Keep the self-guarding launcher exactly as designed (it is load-bearing, not defensive padding): run.sh must translate a missing interpreter or missing files into exit 2 with a loud message. platform.md item 13 is corrected to fail-open in this build. No code change.

outcome.what_was_done: The self-guarding command is built as designed, with HD12's two precautions (the walk starts only at an absolute path; HOME is stripped of a trailing slash): exit 2 with the reinstall message in a factory project, silent 0 elsewhere, the down-briefing JSON with systemMessage in brief, silent 0 in notify, and the launcher's own code when the launcher is present. Verified under sh, bash and dash.

where: rewrite/spec/rules/auto-allow.md; rewrite/spec/topics/rule-model.md; rewrite/BLUEPRINT.md section 10 item 27 (finding P3COV-07's stated rule)
problem: Pairing a hook command rewrite (updatedInput) with permissionDecision ask does not run the call in a headless session in the auto permission mode (R10a-c; all three sessions ran in auto): the call never executed (side-effect file not created) and the permissionDecisionReason text was surfaced to the model as the call's outcome, which the model reported as the command's printed output. An ask paired with a rewrite is therefore unusable in unattended runs and its reason text can be mistaken for command output.
proposed_resolution: Adopt the P3COV-07 rule only where a person is present: in unattended paths (headless, workflow steps, dispatched agents) every rewrite pairs with allow, and a rule that cannot permit the call refuses it plainly instead of answering ask. The rule model should also keep reason strings distinct from tool output in wording, so a surfaced reason cannot be mistaken for a result.

outcome.what_was_done: Same pairing rule: in unattended paths (agent_id set, StructuredOutput, auto/bypassPermissions) every rewrite pairs with allow; the main session in a prompting mode gets ask, not a rewritten call that cannot run. Reason strings are prefixed so they cannot be mistaken for command output.

problem: WebFetch refuses undotted hostnames outright (R5): 'WebFetch cannot fetch localhost or other hostnames without a dot. To reach a local server, use Bash with curl instead.' The dotted workaround does not work either: WebFetch to http://127.0.0.1:8139 upgraded the request to HTTPS and returned HTTP 502 against the plain-http server (check rerun C9), so a plain-http loopback fixture is unreachable through WebFetch. A walled agent restricted to WebFetch cannot reach a localhost fixture at all; of the two routes the original resolution offered, only the shell is left, and it was not tested.
proposed_resolution: Localhost fixtures for walled agents travel through the shell, where the walls already apply per the item-9 fallback; the shell route itself is untested, so the e2e-wall work must verify it. The 127.0.0.1-through-WebFetch route is refuted and stays dropped. Record both the undotted-hostname refusal and the http-to-https upgrade in the browser-tools topic so the e2e walls expect them.

outcome.what_was_done: For A3 (the agents that read a local fixture) and E1 (the wall probes): a localhost fixture is reached through the shell (curl), where the walls already apply, never through WebFetch, which refuses an undotted host and upgrades 127.0.0.1 to HTTPS; the wall probe verifies the shell route.

outcome.what_was_done: The orchestrating session added H3 to P3SEAM-24's packages in triage/a.json, with a note that states the acceptance for the read-only reviewer half and points at decision D2 of the hook-runner-b plan, not at decisions.md.

problem: The S3R-hook-runner-b-6 fix's _union drops 'outside' whenever project, own-worktree or tmp is present. The literal form enters _forms only when it is anchored under the project root, and _classify then returns before tmp or outside. So the literal form never yields 'outside', and the drop fires in one case only: a symlink inside the project whose destination is outside. There it removes the destination's real 'outside'. Probe: src/link -> /etc/hosts gives ctx.classes ('source', 'project', 'unclassified'), while ctx.classes_of(ctx.target) gives ('unclassified', 'outside'). Before the fix, ctx.classes gave ('unclassified', 'outside'). walls.toml denies 'outside' to the architect, ux-designer and story-writer, and spike-bounds denies it to the spike runner. A read-walls rule (H3) reading ctx.classes would let such an agent read any file outside the project through a symlink in the project, or in the spike's own worktree, where the runner may create one. That contradicts rule-model's 'class matching tests both the literal and the resolved path' and the paths.py docstring's 'judged by its destination'. No test pins the drop: removing it keeps all 7 test_classes tests green.
proposed_resolution: Remove the 'outside' drop from _union, so the union keeps every class of both forms. Add a test case: a symlink in the project pointing outside the project, the plugin directory and tmp, asserting 'outside' is in ctx.classes. If walls need per-form answers (read_allow's 'a class that contains the path'), also expose the literal and the resolved classes separately for step 4.

outcome.what_was_done: The 'outside' drop is gone from _union: the union keeps every class of both forms, so an in-project symlink whose destination is outside the project, the plugin directory and tmp answers 'project' and 'outside' together, and a read-walls rule (H3) reading ctx.classes sees the destination's outside. The plan 3.1 interfaces keep their names and signatures (ctx.classes, ctx.classes_of, paths.classes_of); no per-form split is exposed — the literal and resolved classes are available separately only inside paths.py — because walls' read_allow shape is a step 4 question; expose it there if it is wanted. test_in_project_symlink_outside_stays_outside links src/wall-peek to /etc/hosts and asserts ('unclassified', 'project', 'outside'); restoring the drop fails it, and it was the only test noticing.

problem: When lock_release raises StoreBusy, records puts the entries it did release on busy.released. See locks.lock_release, and outcome S3R-records-C2-2: 'exc.released holds the entries actually released'. liveness reads busy.entries instead, finds nothing and logs no lock.released. It also returns [], although those entries were removed from lock.json and their runs ended. test_release_logs_a_busy_store raises its own StoreBusy subclass that carries .entries, so the test pins a shape records never raises. A probe in a scratch copy raised StoreBusy with .released=[{run: <id>}] from lock_release. The result was zero lock.released events and only runner.liveness_error. The builder reported this seam as a departure that follows records' contract, but the attribute name does not match.
proposed_resolution: Read the released entries from getattr(busy, 'released', None). In the test, raise a plain StoreBusy with .released set the way locks.py sets it. Better, drive the real lock_release with two entries of one session, one of whose run_end is held busy. Close S3B-hook-runner-b-2 against records' name 'released'.

outcome.what_was_done: liveness._released_under_busy reads getattr(busy, "released", None) — the attribute locks.lock_release sets (records outcome S3R-records-C2-2) — so the entries a partly successful release removed are logged as lock.released and returned. test_release_logs_a_busy_store now raises a plain StoreBusy carrying .released the way locks.py sets it, instead of a bespoke subclass carrying .entries; the drive-the-real-lock_release variant is additionally pinned by the test test_session_end_logs_released_entries_when_a_run_end_is_busy added with the records fix round.

problem: P3SEAM-24 and the refresh half of P3OPS-20 are marked fixed, citing the --run, step.run and story-worktree cases of test_lock_refresh. problem: The tmp test compares a realpath'd path with Path(tempfile.gettempdir()), which is not resolved. On macOS gettempdir() is /var/folders/.../T, and /var is a symlink to /private/var, so every real temporary path resolves to a location outside it. Such a path is classed 'outside', never 'tmp'. Probe: Path(tempfile.gettempdir())/'vsdd-probe.txt' gave ('unclassified', 'outside'). classes.toml makes tmp always writable, so write-scopes (H5) built on this would block writes to the temporary directory on macOS. test_computed_classes passes only because its fake temporary root sits under pytest's tmp_path, which is already resolved.
proposed_resolution: Resolve the temporary directory once, with os.path.realpath(tempfile.gettempdir()), and use that in both tmp checks. Add a test that classes a file under the real gettempdir(), not a fake root built from tmp_path.

outcome.what_was_done: paths.py resolves the temporary directory through one helper (_tmp_root: os.path.realpath(tempfile.gettempdir())) for both the tmp check and the outside complement, so a real temporary file on macOS (/var/folders/... under the /var symlink) classes as tmp, not outside. test_real_temporary_directory_is_tmp writes a real mkdtemp file and asserts ('unclassified', 'tmp'); with the unresolved comparison restored it fails.

problem: tmp is added to every path under the temporary directory, including the project's own state and product paths when the project itself lies there. classes.toml's closing comment treats project, tmp and outside as separate regions: outside means outside the project, the plugin directory and tmp. tmp is always writable, so in a project under /tmp every path, runs and brief included, would carry an always-writable class. On Linux, a supported platform, pytest's tmp_path is under /tmp, which is not a symlink. There test_state_classes_innermost_first and test_product_class_by_precedence fail. Simulated here by setting TMPDIR to a resolved directory, they return ('brief', 'spec-product', 'tmp') and ('tests', 'project', 'tmp'). The suite is green on macOS only because of S3R-hook-runner-b-3, and fixing that finding alone makes these tests fail on macOS too.
proposed_resolution: Give tmp only to a path outside the project root: test the project first, then tmp, then outside, as the closing comment orders the regions. Add a test whose project root lies under a monkeypatched temporary directory. Run test_classes.py once with TMPDIR set to a resolved directory.

outcome.what_was_done: classes_of classifies by region: the project first (state classes, or the product class and project), then tmp only for a path outside the project root, then outside — the separate regions of classes.toml's closing comment. A project lying under the temporary directory gives every path its own class alone, never tmp. test_project_inside_temporary_directory_is_not_tmp makes the project under a real mkdtemp directory and asserts the product path stays ('unclassified', 'project') and the state path ('config',); on Linux this is what made test_state_classes_innermost_first and test_product_class_by_precedence fail before, and both hold again there and here.

problem: Plan 3.1 promises that a policy table that does not load raises PolicyInvalid, giving the rule that read the field the code policy_invalid. Only the state-directory branch calls hooks.policy.tables(). The product branch goes straight to S1's path_class, which loads classes.toml through vsdd.policy.load and lets FileNotFoundError or TOMLDecodeError escape. Probe with classes.toml unreadable: a gate rule reading ctx.classes for src/a.rs was blocked as rule_error ('FileNotFoundError: classes.toml missing'), not policy_invalid. The test covers only a state path (brief.md).
proposed_resolution: Call tables() at the top of classes_of, so a broken table raises PolicyInvalid on every branch; it is cached, so this costs nothing. Alternatively, re-raise OSError and ValueError from path_class as PolicyInvalid. Add a product-path case to test_invalid_policy_is_the_rules_fault.

outcome.what_was_done: classes_of calls the cached hooks.policy.tables() at the top whenever a project governs, so a table that does not load is PolicyInvalid on every branch, and _product_classes re-raises the OSError/ValueError of the load path_class makes itself as PolicyInvalid (the FileNotFoundError 'classes.toml missing' of the probe). test_invalid_policy_is_the_rules_fault gains the product-path case: the shipped tables load for the runner but vsdd.policy.load is made to raise for classes.toml, and the fixture rule reading ctx.classes on src/main.rs is refused with policy_invalid, not rule_error.

problem: rule-model.md's target row, taken from hooks.md 2.5, says that class matching tests both the literal and the resolved path. ctx.classes classes only the resolved target. paths.classes_of applies os.path.realpath to whatever it is given, so even ctx.classes_of(ctx.target_literal) cannot answer for the literal path. Probe: with .factory/specs/product/brief.md a symlink to src/x.rs, both forms gave ('unclassified', 'project'), and 'brief' appeared in neither. A write-scopes or tests-first rule built in step 4 on ctx.classes would judge a write through a symlink only by where the link points. The builder did not report this departure.
proposed_resolution: Class the literal path in its absolute form, without realpath, as well as the resolved path, and have ctx.classes return the union of the two, keeping innermost-first order. Alternatively, give classes_of a resolve flag and document that rules must call it for both forms. Either way, add a symlink case to test_classes.py. If the design is to change instead, amend rule-model.md and say so in the plan.

outcome.what_was_done: Fixed for the case the finding named. What remains is a path that goes through a directory symlink inside the project and is spelled through an alias of the project root: only its resolved form is classed. Left for H4, which builds the first rule that decides on a path's classes: before the realpath fallback, walk the literal path's parents and anchor at the first ancestor whose realpath equals the resolved root, with the confirmer's probe as the test.

problem: P3OPS-20 is recorded as 'fixed', but its own text says the clear half, whether a workflow survives /clear, is left for B8 and then H9. Plan 6 records that half as left-for-builder. As written, the ledger shows the whole finding closed. PR4C-15, left-for-builder, does carry the probe.
proposed_resolution: Record P3OPS-20 as left-for-builder for B8, with the refresh half noted as done, or point the outcome at PR4C-15 explicitly so the clear half cannot be lost.

outcome.what_was_done: The revised P3OPS-20 outcome below records it as left-for-builder: the refresh half is done, the clear half waits for the B8 probe (still open after round 4, platform item 46) and then H9, and the probe is pointed at PR4C-15, which carries it.

problem: The test asserts only exit 0 and isinstance(lock_entries(...), list). It would pass if the release deleted the entry without ending its run, or if it took the whole platform budget. Its docstring promises 'promptly and says so', and it checks neither. A probe of the same setup took 0.6 s, kept the entry, left the run not ended, and logged runner.liveness_error with StoreBusy.
proposed_resolution: Assert that the launch takes under about 1.0 s, that the session's entry is still in lock.json with its run's 'ended' empty, and that a runner.liveness_error naming StoreBusy is logged.

outcome.what_was_done: test_flush_lock_held_never_blocks_session_end now asserts the three things its docstring promised: the launch returns inside 1.5 s (the 0.5 s RELEASE_WAIT on top of the launcher's start-up; the probe measured 0.6 s), the sess_end entry is still in the lock table with its run's ended empty, and a runner.liveness_error naming StoreBusy is logged. The assertions fail against a release that wedged, deleted the entry without ending the run, or spent the whole platform budget.

problem: run_of recognises a vsdd segment by segment.program == 'vsdd'. caller.is_vsdd_call uses os.path.basename(segment.program) == 'vsdd'. A call by path, such as '.../bin/vsdd gate --run <id>', therefore gets the caller marker but passes no run to lock_seen. The two predicates for one fact disagree.
proposed_resolution: Use the basename test, ideally through one helper shared with caller.py, and add a path-form case to test_lock_refresh.

outcome.what_was_done: liveness.run_of reads the segment program through _is_vsdd_program — os.path.basename(program) == 'vsdd', the same test caller.is_vsdd_call applies — so a vsdd call made by path refreshes. The shared-helper half is reported, not done: py/vsdd/hooks/caller.py belongs to the concurrent records fix round this week, so the helper stands in liveness.py for the caller owner to adopt; the path-form case ./vsdd gate --run is in test_lock_refresh_belongs_by_run_and_story.

problem: run-lock.md lists among the calls that belong to a run any call whose target path or effective directory lies in a worktree the run owns. For Bash, rule-model gives one effective directory per segment: a cd, git -C or vsdd -C prefix. The refresh passes ctx.story, which for Bash is read from the payload cwd only. So 'cd .worktrees/S-3.01 && cargo test', or 'vsdd -C .worktrees/S-3.01 ...', run from the project root does not count by story. The session match, after item 28, covers subagents today, so nothing is lost on the slice, but the spec and the code disagree.
proposed_resolution: Pass the story of the first segment whose effective directory is in a story worktree (ctx.story_at(segment.where)), or reword run-lock.md to say the payload cwd for Bash.

outcome.what_was_done: liveness passes the story of the first Bash segment whose effective directory sits in a story worktree (_story_of walks command.segments with ctx.story_at(segment.where), ruling-model's per-segment where, falling back to ctx.story for other tools), so 'cd .worktrees/S-3.01 && ...' from the project root counts. run-lock.md keeps its wording; the test case is in test_lock_refresh_belongs_by_run_and_story.

problem: classes.toml defines own-worktree as the union of the worktree that holds the caller's working directory and, for a spike runner, the worktree its open ledger entry records. That includes the throwaway platform worktree a spike runner is given. The code uses containing_worktree, which answers None outside .worktrees/, so a platform worktree (.claude/worktrees/<id>) is never own-worktree, and the ledger half is absent. Neither gap is stated in paths.py or the plan.
proposed_resolution: Say in paths.py's docstring, and in the spike-bounds package brief, that the ledger union and platform worktrees arrive with spike-bounds. Then build them there, with a test.

outcome.what_was_done: The gaps are stated where the reader stands: the paths.py module docstring says containing_worktree answers None outside .worktrees/, so the platform's throwaway worktree is never own-worktree at this depth, and that the ledger union and the platform worktree arrive with spike-bounds (H8); the spike-bounds brief gained the same sentence at its write-scopes bullet, to build and test them there. Building them now would add a ledger read to every rule call of the slice for a rule (spike-bounds, H8) that is not built yet.

problem: registry.py's module docstring still says two duties are wired with no rule, PreToolUse on Bash and SessionStart. There are now four, adding StructuredOutput and SessionEnd. hooks/__init__.py, a hook-runner file, lists the package's modules without paths and liveness. rule-model.md says own-worktree is computed 'by `where`, which defaults to the payload `cwd`'. In that file `where` is the Ctx field for the effective directory, which classes.toml says own-worktree is deliberately not.
proposed_resolution: Update the registry docstring. Ask the hook-runner owner to add the two modules to __init__.py. In rule-model.md, say 'by the caller's working directory (the payload cwd), or the directory passed to classes_of'.

outcome.what_was_done: The registry.py docstring says four duties wired with no rule: the caller marker, the session-start briefing and notices, and the two lock-liveness duties. rule-model.md now says own-worktree is decided 'by the caller's working directory — the payload cwd — or the directory passed to classes_of', no longer colliding with Ctx.where. Reported for the hook-runner owner: hooks/__init__.py (owned by the hook-runner unit, not this one) still lists no paths or liveness module; its Modules list wants two lines — vsdd.hooks.paths (the path classes of a call's target) and vsdd.hooks.liveness (lock liveness: refresh and release).

problem: The plan's classes_of has two branches only: in the state directory the matching classes of classes.toml, elsewhere S1's path_class or unclassified. The reference class (.reference/**, a globs class that is neither a state-directory class nor one of the seven product classes) falls through the elsewhere branch and answers unclassified, which is the class the design reserves for a product path that matches no [paths] glob, with the block message pointing at a [paths] line that would not help.
proposed_resolution: When write-scopes (H5) is built, either teach path_class to return reference for .reference/** paths matched relative to the project root, or have the elsewhere branch of paths.classes_of add the non-product, non-state glob classes of classes.toml beside path_class's answer. Nothing on the slice reads the class yet.

outcome.what_was_done: The reference class (.reference/**) answers unclassified from classes_of. Left for H5 with write-scopes, as the builder proposed: teach the elsewhere branch to answer it, or fold it into path_class.
