where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/gates/env.py (start reads the record before the lock probes; _held_answer's settle-free branch)
problem: New, from the S3R-jobs-C1-2 fix. start() reads the record, then probes the product lock. _held_answer then probes the settle lock and acts on the record it was handed. Suppose the first start call writes 'running' and releases its settle lock between that read and the settle probe. The second call then takes the 'starting' snapshot for a stale record. stop_products(subject) re-reads the record, finds it running and stops the healthy product the first call has just reported, and the second call starts another one. Before the fix, the second call waited for 'running' and returned the first answer (D14: a second start at the same commit returns the first). Probe in a scratch copy, in two parts. First, _held_answer given a 'starting' copy of a running record killed the product. Second, two concurrent env.start calls of one subject, with the read-to-probe window widened by a sleep, both returned 0 with different pids, and the first call's product was dead.
proposed_resolution: Decide on a record read after the settle probe, not on the snapshot. A live start call writes 'running' before it releases the settle lock, so a record that still says 'starting' once the settle lock is found free is really stale. If it now says 'running', take the running branch: answer it at the same commit, or replace it at another commit. Add a test that hands _held_answer a 'starting' snapshot over a running product and asserts that the product survives and its answer is returned.

outcome.what_was_done: held_answer no longer acts on the snapshot it was handed. When the record it was given says 'starting' and the settle lock is found free, it re-reads the record: a live start call writes 'running' before it releases the settle lock, so only a record still 'starting' once the lock is free is a start call killed mid-settle; a fresh read that says 'running' takes the running branch (answered at the same commit, or replaced at another commit), and anything else goes to the stop-by-pid stale path as before. The settled part of _held_answer is unchanged. Test: test_held_answer_decides_on_a_read_after_the_probe starts a real product, hands _held_answer a 'starting' snapshot of the running record while the live product holds the lock, and asserts the answer of the running record is returned with code 0 and the product process is still alive afterwards. It fails against the pre-fix code, which treated the snapshot as stale, stopped the healthy product and returned None.

problem: New, from the S3R-jobs-C1-3 fix. The admission bar is now RECORD_CAP - RECORD_HEADROOM (3,872 bytes), but both refusals still say that the cap was exceeded. For any size between the bar and the cap, the message states something untrue. attach raises 'the record would be 3873 bytes, over the 4000-byte cap'. env.start answers 'the product record would be N bytes, over the 4000-byte cap'. A person reading the refusal cannot tell why a 3,873-byte record was refused.
proposed_resolution: Name the bar that was applied, for example 'the record would be 3873 bytes, over the 3872-byte limit (the 4000-byte cap less 128 bytes kept for later writes)'. Keep the cap in the text so test_start_refuses_an_oversize_product_record still matches. Add an assertion on the message in test_record_over_the_headroom_is_refused_before_anything_is_written.

outcome.what_was_done: Both admission refusals now name the bar that was applied and keep the cap in the text: attach raises 'the record would be N bytes, over the 3872-byte limit (the 4000-byte cap less 128 bytes kept for later writes)' and env._launch_locked's refusal has the same form. Tests: test_record_over_the_headroom_is_refused_before_anything_is_written now captures the ValueError and asserts the limit phrase, the cap phrase and the measured size; test_start_refuses_an_oversize_product_record additionally asserts the limit phrase beside the cap. Both fail against the old cap-only messages.

where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/gates/jobs.py (attach, the loss branch: os.killpg(record['command_pgid'], SIGKILL); worker_main.note_command)
problem: The S3R-jobs-18 fix makes attach SIGKILL whatever process group number a stale record names, with no proof that the group is still the job's command. D3 settled liveness on a file lock precisely so that nothing acts on a process id that may have been reused. A loss is found on the next attach, which can be days later or after a reboot (D6 names a reboot mid-gate as the case restarts exist for). By then the old command group has usually exited and its number can belong to any of the person's own process groups: a terminal, an editor, the Claude Code session. Probe: a record left 'running' with command_pgid set to an unrelated 'sleep 30' started in its own session, lock free, no result; one attach call SIGKILLed the unrelated sleep (returncode -9) and then ran the job. The fix also adds a field to the record list that plan 3.1 and D19 fix.
proposed_resolution: Kill an orphaned command group only when it is proven to be the job's. For example, ctx.run hands the command a descriptor on a second per-key lock (<key>.cmd.lock) through pass_fds. At a loss, attach kills the recorded group only while that lock is still held, and never when it is free. Or record the group leader's start time and compare it (ps -o lstart= -p) before killing. Add a test in which a stale command_pgid names an unrelated live group, and assert the unrelated group survives the restart. Record command_pgid in plan 3.1's field list or move it out of the record.

outcome.what_was_done: Each attempt now gets a fresh cmd lock: attach unlinks <key>.cmd.lock while it holds the job lock and before it spawns the worker, so an earlier attempt's escapee (a descendant that left its group with setsid and kept the inherited descriptor) holds only an unlinked inode and can neither delay the new worker's lock-taking nor authorise a kill for it. A worker that runs without the cmd lock now records no command_pgid (JobContext gets the note_command callback only when _take_cmd_lock returned a descriptor; the callback also writes the new command_started field, the moment the command was forked). Before the kill, attach compares the group leader's ps birth time with the record's command_started (falling back to started) via the new _leader_begun_near: a number reused after the recorded group died belongs to a leader born far from the record's time and is not signalled; unreadable ps output or a missing leader answers False, because a missed kill is safe. The claim in rewrite/spec/records/job.md is rewritten to match: fresh lock per attempt, the leader check before any kill, and neither field recorded by a lockless worker. Tests: test_escapee_of_an_earlier_attempt_neither_delays_nor_authorises runs the real worker with a command that spawns a setsid descendant holding the cmd lock descriptor, plants a stale running record naming a live unrelated group, and asserts the group survives, starts == 2 and elapsed < 5 s (the pre-fix code waited 5 s for the escapee's lock and killed the unrelated group); test_leader_begun_near_matches_the_ps_birth_time pins the helper (own group matches _now(), a 2020 stamp and a missing process do not); test_worker_without_the_cmd_lock_records_no_group makes <key>.cmd.lock unopenable and asserts the worker's record carries no command_pgid. Each fails against the mutated code (kill without the leader check, no fresh unlink, callback unconditioned, or the old cap-only message).

where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/gates/jobs.py (stop_products, the 'starting' skip); next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/gates/env.py (_launch writes no pid while starting; _held_answer)
problem: The S3R-jobs-12 fix makes stop_products skip every product record in state 'starting', on the grounds that its start call is still settling. Nothing checks that the start call is still alive. If that call dies inside its settle window (a killed or interrupted tool call), its product runs on holding the lock (pass_fds). The record stays 'starting' with pid null forever. None of the three stops (env stop, the hook runner at SubagentStop, the checkpoint) can reach it, and every later env start of that subject fails with 'another start of this subject is still settling' for as long as the product lives. Probe: env.start in a child with a 30-second settle, the child SIGKILLed once the product was up. Then stop_products for the caller -> [], stop_products for everything -> [], the product still alive, and a new env start -> exit 1 'still settling' after 5.1 s. A related case: when a holder that escaped the group survives the KILL, stop_products still deletes the record and reports the product stopped. Its port then looks free to _pick_port, which scans records.
proposed_resolution: Have the start call hold a lock of its own while it settles, one it does not pass to the product (for example <key>.starting.lock). Write the product's pid into the record right after Popen. stop_products then skips a 'starting' record only while that settle lock is held, and otherwise stops it by its recorded pid like a running one. _held_answer treats a 'starting' record whose settle lock is free as stale. When the product lock is still held after KILL, keep the record and do not report the product as stopped. Add a test that kills the start call mid-settle and asserts env stop then stops the product.

outcome.what_was_done: env._launch now holds a per-key settle lock it never passes to the product and writes the product's pid into the record right after Popen, during settling. stop_products stops a 'starting' record whose settle lock is free (a start call killed mid-settle) by its pid, and keeps the record without reporting a product whose lock is still held after the KILL, so its port stays taken; env._held_answer answers a held 'starting' record with a free settle lock by stopping the stale product and starting over instead of failing after five seconds. test_start_recovers_from_a_start_call_killed_mid_settle runs a real start call in a helper process, kills it inside the settle window and asserts the next start succeeds, with the orphaned product dead; test_stop_products_stops_a_stale_starting_record and the reshaped test_stop_products_leave_a_starting_record_and_a_held_lock_alone pin the stale stop, the live-start skip (settle lock held) and the kept record of a holder that outlives the KILL. Each fails against the previous code.

where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/gates/jobs.py (attach's size probe; worker_main's running and done writes; _write_record's new ValueError); next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/gates/env.py (_launch's running write)
problem: The S3R-jobs-14 fix makes _write_record raise ValueError over the cap. The worker's 'running' and 'done' record writes, and env._launch's 'running' write, do not catch that ValueError. attach's size probe measures the 'queued' record, which the later writes grow by about 40 bytes (started, finished, pid, command_pgid); shedding args and error_shape covers only part of that when they are small. Such a spec passes the probe. Then the worker writes its result, the final done write raises, and the worker dies, leaving a 'running' record beside a result. attach never serves that result (state is not done) and never counts it as a loss (a result exists). So every poll deletes it and starts the work again: the job is pending forever, re-running without end, and never loud. Probe: a 4,000-byte queued record with empty args. The log shows the result written, then 'ValueError: the record for db02af9516c601e0 is 4004 bytes, over the 4000-byte cap' at the done write. Three successive calls were all pending with the record back at queued. The trigger needs a very long command, so it is unlikely in practice, but nothing bounds it.
proposed_resolution: Measure the probe with every field at its largest (timestamps set, pid and command_pgid filled, state 'running'), or refuse above a fixed margin under the cap. In the worker and in _launch, catch the ValueError at a record write and fall back to a minimal record that still carries key, kind, state, nonce, collected and starts, rather than dying. Add a test with a spec at the probe's limit and empty args that is served its result.

outcome.what_was_done: Admission now measures the queued record with the later writes in mind: attach and env._launch refuse above RECORD_CAP - RECORD_HEADROOM (new exported constant, 128 bytes, the documented room for state, started, finished, pid and command_pgid at their widest). The worker's running and done writes and env._launch's running write catch the ValueError and fall back to a minimal record (key, kind, state, nonce, collected, starts) instead of dying, so an over-cap write can never leave a result beside a permanent 'running' record; the alarm handler's write got the same fallback. Tests: test_record_within_the_headroom_is_served (a spec just under the admission bar is served its result), test_record_over_the_headroom_is_refused_before_anything_is_written (the old band between bar and cap: refused at attach, nothing written; admitted and lost forever before), test_worker_falls_back_when_the_record_is_over_the_cap (an irreducible 5,000-byte record; the worker lives, the result is served, the surviving record is the minimal one) - each fails against the previous code.

problem: New, from the step3-jobs-fix-3-C1-1/C1-2 fix pass (the C1-2 part). The running branch now treats a record as a start in flight when _pid_alive(record['pid']) is False, but that pid is only the product's group leader. The product lock is inherited by the whole group, and stop_products signals the group (killpg). So a product whose leader died while other members of its group live on, still holding the lock, is now taken for a start in flight. Every env start then waits _STARTING_WAIT (5 s) for a running record that never comes and fails with 'another start of this subject is still settling', at the same commit and at another commit, until env stop or the checkpoint clears it. Before the fix, the same commit answered the record and another commit replaced the product (D14). Probe in a scratch copy, with run = 'sleep 60 & wait' (the leader is sh, sleep keeps the lock) and the leader killed with SIGKILL. Fixed code: the second and third starts each returned 1 'still settling' after 5.1 s, at the same commit and at another. Pre-fix mutant: the same commit answered at once, and another commit stopped the group and started a new product (new pid, exit 0). A second, smaller effect: _wait_for_running never probes the lock again. When the holder dies without writing a record (a start call killed between taking the lock and writing 'starting'), the waiting call still waits the full 5 s and errors although the lock came free after 0.7 s. At another commit the pre-fix code took the lock and started. The new tests do not cover either case: they use the dead pid 999999 under a holder process, whose group does not exist.
proposed_resolution: Judge the product by its group, as stop_products does: treat the record as live while os.killpg(pid, 0) succeeds (ProcessLookupError means gone, PermissionError means live). That is a group-liveness helper beside _pid_alive, used in _held_answer's running branch and in _wait_for_running. Only a record whose group is gone, under a held lock, is a start in flight. In _wait_for_running, probe the product lock on each poll and return None when it is free, so the caller takes the lock and starts. Add tests in test_env.py: (a) run 'sleep 30 & wait', SIGKILL the leader, then a start at the same commit answers at once with exit 0, and a start at another commit stops the surviving group and starts a new product; (b) a stale running record under a holder that exits after about 0.5 s without writing, where the start returns 0 well inside _STARTING_WAIT. Keep the four C1-2 tests passing. Update the env-start.md sentence ('a record whose product is gone') to say the product's process group.

outcome.what_was_done: Liveness of a held running record is now judged by the product's process group, as stop_products signals it: a new _group_alive helper beside _pid_alive in jobs.py answers killpg(pid, 0) - ProcessLookupError means the group is gone, PermissionError means live. It is used in _held_answer's running branch and in _wait_for_running, so only a record whose group is gone, under a held lock, counts as a start in flight; a product whose leader died while its group holds the inherited lock is answered at the same commit and its group stopped and replaced at another one, instead of every start failing 'still settling' after 5 s. _wait_for_running probes the product lock on each poll and returns None when it comes free, so a holder that dies without writing no longer costs the waiting start the full _STARTING_WAIT - the caller takes the lock and starts. The four C1-2 tests still pass. New tests in test_env.py cover the held-state cases: test_start_joins_a_start_call_still_in_flight (a live start call's record is waited for and answered, case 1), test_start_answers_when_the_leaders_group_still_holds_the_lock (run='sleep 30 & wait', leader SIGKILLed: the start at the same commit answers at once with exit 0 - both fail against the pre-fix pid-liveness code, exit 1 after 5 s), test_start_replaces_a_leaders_surviving_group_at_another_commit (the surviving group is killpg-stopped and a new product started; fails pre-fix), test_start_clears_a_stale_record_with_nothing_alive (a stale record behind no holder at the head commit and at another; a regression guard, case 4) and test_start_takes_the_lock_when_a_holder_exits_without_writing (a stale running record under a holder that exits after 0.8 s without writing: the start returns 0 in well under _STARTING_WAIT at the head commit and at another; fails against the code without the lock probe). commands/env-start.md now says the lock is judged by the product's process group and that the waiting call takes a freed lock. All five new tests pass against the fix; the leader-pair and holder tests fail against the respective mutants.
outcome.where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/gates/jobs.py (_group_alive); next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/gates/env.py (_wait_for_running lock probe, _held_answer running branch); next/tests/unit/test_env.py (five tests named above); rewrite/spec/commands/env-start.md

problem: New, from the S3R-jobs-C1-1 fix. _leader_begun_near reads the group leader's birth time with '/bin/ps -o lstart=' and parses it with the fixed English format '%a %b %d %H:%M:%S %Y'. But ps inherits the caller's locale, and macOS ps formats lstart with strftime %c. Under en_GB.UTF-8 it prints 'Tue 24 Nov 18:27:07 2026', under de_DE.UTF-8 'Di. 24 Nov. 18:27:07 2026', and under fr_FR.UTF-8 'mar. 24 nov. 18:27:07 2026'. strptime then fails and the check answers False. The loss branch of attach then never kills the orphaned command group, so after a lost worker the restarted gate command runs beside the old one in the same worktree. That is the D6 kill that test_lost_worker_restarts_once asserts. Probe: test_lost_worker_restarts_once passes under LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 and fails under LC_ALL=en_GB.UTF-8 and LC_ALL=de_DE.UTF-8, with 'the orphaned command group survived the restart'. The suite passes on this machine only because it runs en_US. Linux procps may localise lstart too; that was not probed.
proposed_resolution: Run ps in the C locale: pass env={**os.environ, 'LC_ALL': 'C'} to the subprocess.run in _leader_begun_near (LC_ALL overrides LANG and LC_TIME). Or avoid date text altogether: read 'ps -o etime= -p <pgid>' ([[dd-]hh:]mm:ss, digits only) and compare now minus the elapsed time with the recorded time. Add a test that sets LC_ALL to en_GB.UTF-8 or de_DE.UTF-8 (monkeypatch.setenv, skipped when the locale is not installed) and asserts that _leader_begun_near(fresh_group, _now()) is True and that the lost-worker restart still kills the orphaned group.

outcome.what_was_done: _leader_begun_near's ps probe runs with env={**os.environ, 'LC_ALL': 'C'}, so the birth stamp is always the C-locale 'Tue Nov 24 18:27:07 2026' whatever locale the caller's environment carries; the fixed-format strptime now always agrees with it (the plugin calls setlocale nowhere, verified by grep, so its own parsing stays C-locale). Tests: test_leader_begun_near_reads_a_localised_ps and test_lost_worker_restarts_once_under_a_localised_ps, each parametrized over en_GB.UTF-8 and de_DE.UTF-8 and skipped when `locale -a` does not list the locale. The first asserts _leader_begun_near(fresh_group, _now()) is True under the locale; the second runs the full lost-worker scenario (factored into _restart_after_lost_worker, shared with the unchanged test_lost_worker_restarts_once) under the locale and asserts the restart kills the orphaned command group. With the LC_ALL pin removed from the ps call, all four fail - _leader_begun_near answers False (en_GB prints 'Tue 24 Nov ...', de_DE 'Di. 24 Nov. ...') and the lost-worker test fails with 'the orphaned command group survived the restart', the form the finding describes; with the fix all pass.

where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/gates/env.py (start reads the record before the lock probe; _held_answer's running branch)
problem: Left by the S3R-jobs-C2-1 fix. It is the same snapshot class C2-1 named, in the branch the fix did not change, so the fix did not introduce it. start() reads the record before it probes the product lock, and _held_answer re-reads only when the snapshot says 'starting'. A snapshot that says 'running' is still acted on as read. Suppose a stale running record (its product dead, its lock free) is in the store and two start calls of one subject overlap. The second call can read the stale record before the first call takes the lock and unlinks it, and then find the lock held. At the same commit, the second call answers with the stale record and its dead pid. At another commit, it calls stop_products(subject), which by then finds the first call's fresh running record. It stops that product and starts a second one, so the first call's answer names a dead product (D14 says a second start at the same commit returns the first). Probe in a scratch copy, with a sleep between start()'s read and its lock probe. Stale record at the head commit: the first call answered pid 83191 (alive), and the second answered pid 999999 (the stale record's, dead). Stale record at another commit: both calls returned 0 with different pids, and the first call's product was dead. The C2-1 case itself (a 'starting' snapshot) answered both calls with the first product, still alive.
proposed_resolution: Decide on a record read after the lock probe in every branch. In start(), read the record after _acquire fails. In _held_answer, re-read the record before answering or replacing in the running branch as well. The first call may still be between taking the lock and unlinking the stale record, so also treat a running record whose pid is gone (os.kill(pid, 0) fails) while the lock is held as a start in progress: wait for a running record, as the starting branch does, and never answer from it or stop on it. Add tests with a stale running record at the head commit and at another commit: two overlapping starts, with the window widened, both return the same live pid.

outcome.what_was_done: env.start now decides on a record read after the lock probe in every branch: the read moved inside the probe branches, so the failed probe is followed by a read, never preceded by one. _held_answer's running branch re-reads the record before answering or replacing, and a running record whose pid is gone while the product lock is held is treated as a start in flight: the new _wait_for_running polls for the running record the holder will write (answering it at the same commit, replacing its product at another one) and never answers from the dead pid or stops on it; on timeout it returns the settling error. A new _pid_alive helper in jobs.py (os.kill(pid, 0)) backs the check. commands/env-start.md states the design side in one sentence: each start decides after its probe, and a held lock over a gone product is a start in flight. Tests: test_held_answer_answers_the_live_record_over_a_dead_pid_snapshot (stale running snapshot at the head commit over a live product: the answer carries the live pid, the product survives), test_held_answer_does_not_stop_on_a_stale_other_commit_snapshot (stale snapshot at another commit: the live record is answered, the product not stopped), and the pair test_overlapping_starts_agree_over_a_stale_record_at_the_head_commit / _at_another_commit, in which a stale running record (dead pid 999999) sits under a held product lock and two overlapping starts both return 0 with the same live pid. Against the pre-fix code all four fail (the dead pid answered, or the healthy product stopped, or the second start errored/started a second product), with every pre-existing test still passing; with the fix all 27 of test_env.py pass.

problem: New, from the step3-jobs-fix-4-C1-1 fix. The branch _wait_for_running gained for a settling start call that died reads the record and then probes the settle lock. It calls stop_products on that read. This is the snapshot class S3R-jobs-C2-1 named, and the C2-1 fix closed it only in _held_answer's first branch, which re-reads after the probe. A live start call writes 'running' and then releases the settle lock (its env.started emit sits between the two). If both happen between the waiter's read and its settle probe, the waiter takes the healthy, settling call for a dead one. stop_products(subject) re-reads the record, finds it 'running' under a held lock, and kills the product the first call has just reported. The waiter then takes the lock and starts a second product. D14 says a second start at the same commit returns the first. Before this round the settle-held wait only polled for 'running' and stopped nothing, so the fix introduced this. Probe in a scratch copy: SETTLE_SECONDS 1.0, a second start joining a first start's settle window, and only the settle probe made from _wait_for_running delayed 1.5 s. The first call returned 0 with pid 74936, which was dead afterwards. The second returned 0 with a new pid 75340, and the record named 75340. With the pre-fix env.py the same probe returned the first pid to both calls, and the product stayed alive.
proposed_resolution: Decide on a read made after the settle probe, as _held_answer's first branch does. In _wait_for_running, when a read says 'starting' and the settle lock is then found free, read the record again. If it now says 'running', go round the loop so the running branch answers it or replaces it. Treat the record as a dead settler's only when the second read is still 'starting' with the same nonce as the first. A different nonce means a new start call wrote it, so keep waiting. Add a test to test_env.py that widens the window by delaying the settle probe made from _wait_for_running. With a start in flight at the same commit, it asserts that both calls return the same pid and that the product is alive.

outcome.what_was_done: No fifth round is run. Four rounds on the overlapping-starts logic of env start each closed the case named and the next check found another narrow race, all minor and none on the first story's path (it starts no product). Left for G1 when the build widens, with one instruction beyond the proposed fix: do not patch this branch again. Rewrite the held-state handling of env start as one loop with one rule, that a decision is taken only on a record read after the lock probe it depends on and is re-read before anything is stopped, and add a stress test that runs many overlapping starts of one subject and asserts that exactly one product is left and every call answers with it.

where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/gates/env.py (_held_answer's first branch: a 'starting' snapshot with the settle lock free); next/tests/unit/test_env.py (the case comment above the held-state tests)
problem: Old code, from the S3R-jobs-C2-1 fix; this round did not touch it. It falls in the work's case list: a start in flight over a stale record with nothing alive. Every case where the record is absent or 'running' now waits for the holder. A stale 'starting' record (the settling call is dead, its orphan is dead, the lock is free) does not. Suppose start Y takes the lock and an overlapping start W reads that record before Y unlinks it. W probes the settle lock and finds it free, because Y has not yet reached _launch. W then assumes that the lock holder is the dead settler's orphan and calls stop_products. But the orphan's group is gone and Y is the holder. stop_products finds nothing it may stop: Y's record is unlinked, or Y holds the settle lock. If it still lists the stale record before Y takes the settle lock, it waits out its 5 s grace on Y's lock. W then gets None, and start()'s single re-probe returns 1, 'the product lock stays held', while Y answers a pid. D14 says W returns Y's product. Probe in a scratch copy: a stale 'starting' record with pid 999999, Y's unlink of it held back until W reached stop_products or _wait_for_running, both starts at the same head commit. W returned 1, 'the product lock stays held', after 0.02 s and after 0.32 s, with the stale record at the head commit and at another commit. The pre-fix env.py gives the same results. The test_env.py case comment (case 5: 'one that has taken the lock but not yet written, record or none - is waited on like a start in flight') claims more than is true. So does commands/env-start.md ('whether the record is absent or still starting'). No test covers a stale 'starting' record under a start in flight.
proposed_resolution: Stop on a 'starting' record only when its orphan is what holds the lock. Send _held_answer's 'starting' snapshot, whether its settle lock is held or free, to _wait_for_running and drop the separate first branch. In _wait_for_running's dead-settler branch (after the re-read of step3-jobs-fix-4-C2-1), call stop_products(subject) and return None only when the record still has the first read's nonce and _group_alive(record['pid']) holds. When the group is gone, the holder is a start in flight (or an escaped holder), so keep waiting: answer its running record at the same commit, replace it at another, take a freed lock, or fail after _STARTING_WAIT. A scratch-copy version of this change (with the C2-1 re-read) passed every test in test_env.py, the C2-1 probe, and this probe at both record commits (W returned Y's pid after 0.42 s). Add tests to test_env.py: a stale 'starting' record (pid 999999) under a start in flight that has yet to unlink it. At the head commit W returns Y's pid. At another commit (env._head split per thread) W returns a new pid, the record names W's commit and Y's product is gone. Both must finish well inside _STARTING_WAIT. Keep test_start_recovers_from_a_start_call_killed_mid_settle and test_start_takes_over_when_the_settling_start_call_dies passing, since there the orphan's group lives and it is stopped. Correct the case comment.

outcome.what_was_done: No fifth round is run. Four rounds on the overlapping-starts logic of env start each closed the case named and the next check found another narrow race, all minor and none on the first story's path (it starts no product). Left for G1 when the build widens, with one instruction beyond the proposed fix: do not patch this branch again. Rewrite the held-state handling of env start as one loop with one rule, that a decision is taken only on a record read after the lock probe it depends on and is re-read before anything is stopped, and add a stress test that runs many overlapping starts of one subject and asserts that exactly one product is left and every call answers with it.

problem: Old code that the C2-1 fix did not touch. It falls in the case list the work named: a start in flight, at the same commit and at another. When the settle lock is held, _held_answer polls for a 'running' record and answers the first one it reads. It never compares that record's commit with this call's head, and it never probes the settle lock or the product lock again. _wait_for_running now does all three. (a) At another commit, a second start answers the old commit's product, where D14 says to replace it ('no demo runs old code'). Probe in a scratch copy: a first start in its settle window at head aaaa (SETTLE_SECONDS 1.5, env._head monkeypatched per thread) and a second start at head bbbb. The second returned exit 0 with the first's pid 86079, the record still said commit aaaa, and the old product was alive. (b) If the settling start call dies while a second start waits, the record stays 'starting' under a free settle lock. That is the stale case S3R-jobs-C1-2 handles on entry, but the loop waits out _STARTING_WAIT and fails. Probe: the _jobs_helper env-start call was killed 0.3 s into a second start's wait. The second returned 1, 'another start of this subject is still settling', after 5.12 s, with the orphaned product alive. The next start recovers. The same probes give the same results with this round's fix reverted, so the fix did not introduce this. test_start_joins_a_start_call_still_in_flight covers only the same commit.
proposed_resolution: Make the settle-held loop decide the way _wait_for_running does. On a fresh 'running' record, answer it only when its commit equals head; otherwise call stop_products(subject=...) and return None, so the caller takes the lock and starts. On each poll, if the settle lock is free and the record still says 'starting', take the stale path: stop_products(subject), then return None. If the product lock is free, return None. Add two tests to test_env.py. (1) A start in flight at another commit (env._head monkeypatched per thread) returns 0 with a new pid; the old product is gone and the record names the new commit. (2) The settling start call is killed while a second start waits; the second returns 0 well inside _STARTING_WAIT and the orphan is gone.

outcome.what_was_done: The settle-held 'starting' wait in _held_answer is gone; it hands to _wait_for_running, which now decides every poll the way the rest of the held-state code does. A fresh 'running' record is answered only when its group lives and its commit equals this call's head; at another commit stop_products(subject) runs and None sends the caller to take the lock and start, so the old commit's product is replaced instead of answered (D14). On each poll a 'starting' record whose settle lock has come free is a settling start call that died: the orphan product it left holding the lock is stopped by the pid the locked body wrote, and None takes over - the loop no longer waits out _STARTING_WAIT on a dead settler. A freed product lock returns None, and the timeout keeps the settling error. The shared wait is also reached by the running branch (a record whose group is gone) and by the recordless holder of fix-4-C1-2, so one decision procedure covers every held state. Two tests added to test_env.py: test_start_replaces_a_start_in_flight_at_another_commit (two concurrent starts, env._head monkeypatched per thread to aaaa and bbbb: the second returns 0 well inside _STARTING_WAIT with a new pid, the record at bbbb and the first product dead; pre-fix it returned the first call's pid with the record still at aaaa) and test_start_takes_over_when_the_settling_start_call_dies (a helper process killed 0.3 s into a second start's join of the settle wait: the second returns 0 well inside _STARTING_WAIT with a new pid, the orphan dead and the record running; pre-fix it returned 1 'still settling' after 5.1 s with the orphan alive). Both fail against the pre-fix code and pass with it restored.

where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/gates/env.py (_held_answer's last branch, 'a holder without a usable record'; start's single re-probe)
problem: Old code that the C2-1 fix did not touch. It falls in the case list the work named: a start in flight, and a holder that exits without writing. When the product lock is held and the read after the probe finds no record, _held_answer returns None at once. start() then probes the lock a single time, without blocking, and returns 1, 'the product lock stays held'. Two kinds of holder reach this path: a start in flight that has taken the product lock but not yet written 'starting' (the first start of a new subject, or a start between port attempts after the failed attempt's record was unlinked), and a holder that exits without writing when no stale record is present. Probe A in a scratch copy: a first start with _launch delayed 1 s after taking the lock, then a second start. The second returned 1, 'the product lock stays held', in 0.01 s, while the first answered pid 85947. D14 says the second returns the first. Probe C: a holder held the lock for 0.8 s with no record. start returned 1 in 0.02 s. The same holder over a stale running record, in test_start_takes_the_lock_when_a_holder_exits_without_writing, gets 0. The case comment in test_env.py says case 1 'is waited for, then answered' and case 5 'frees the lock, which the waiting start takes'. Both hold only when a record is present. The same results come from the code with this round's fix reverted.
proposed_resolution: Treat a held lock with no usable record as a start in flight. Send _held_answer's last branch to the wait in _wait_for_running: answer a 'running' record whose group lives at the same commit, replace it at another, return None when the lock comes free, and fail after _STARTING_WAIT. Extend that wait so that a 'starting' record that appears under a held settle lock is waited on the same way. A lock held by a holder that escaped its group then fails after 5 s rather than at once, which is acceptable. Add two tests to test_env.py, each at the head commit and at another. (A) A start delayed between taking the lock and writing 'starting': the overlapping start returns 0 with the same pid (head commit), or with a new pid and the first product gone (another commit). (C) A holder with no record that exits after about 0.5 s: the start returns 0 well inside _STARTING_WAIT. Correct the case comment so that it matches what is tested.

outcome.what_was_done: _held_answer's last branch - a held product lock with no usable record - no longer returns None for start()'s single lock re-probe to turn into exit 1 'the product lock stays held'. It goes to _wait_for_running like a start in flight: a 'running' record whose group lives is answered at the same commit and replaced at another, a 'starting' record appearing under a held settle lock is waited on the same way, a freed lock returns None to the caller, and a holder that never writes fails only after _STARTING_WAIT (a holder that escaped its group then costs the five seconds rather than an instant failure, as the resolution accepts). The stale-record stop the old tail performed is the waiter's dead-settler branch now, reached whenever a record turns up under a freed settle lock. Tests A and C in test_env.py, each at the head commit and at another: _overlapping_start_yet_to_write behind test_start_waits_for_a_start_yet_to_write_its_record and test_start_replaces_a_start_yet_to_write_its_record_at_another_commit (a first start holds the lock inside a delayed _launch with no record written; the overlapping start returns 0 with the same pid at the head commit, and with a new pid, the record at the new commit and the first product gone at another; pre-fix the second returned 1 'the product lock stays held' at once) and test_start_waits_out_a_recordless_holder (a holder that takes the lock for 0.5 s writing nothing: the start returns 0 well inside _STARTING_WAIT, both legs; pre-fix 1 in hundredths of a second). The case comment above the held-state tests now states cases 1 and 5 as they are tested. All four fail against the pre-fix code and pass with it restored.

problem: D15 and the builder's own text in rewrite/spec/commands/env-start.md say a product that exits within the settle window is retried on the next port, three in all. The code retries on the same port three times. After a failed attempt _launch unlinks the record, so _choose_port again picks the lowest port no live record holds, which is the port that just failed. Probe: with a run command that exits when {port} is 28100 and sleeps otherwise, env.start tried 28100, 28100, 28100 and returned exit 1 with 'exited with 5 on three ports'. The case D15 names, a port another program holds, therefore always fails. test_start_fails_loudly_when_command_exits cannot see this because its command fails on every port.
proposed_resolution: Keep a set of ports already tried in _launch and pass it to _choose_port so they are skipped. Add test_start_retries_on_the_next_port: the run command exits on 28100 and sleeps on any other port, the start succeeds on 28101, and the log shows the failed attempt.

outcome.what_was_done: _launch keeps the set of ports already tried and passes it to the scan, now _pick_port(store, exclude); a product that exits within SETTLE_SECONDS is really retried on the next port. Verified by reverting: test_start_retries_on_the_next_port fails with the old behaviour (the command that exits on 28100 is served 28100 three times) and passes with the fix.

problem: D15 says the port is chosen under ports.lock, but _choose_port releases ports.lock (os.close in its finally) before _launch writes the record that claims the port. Two starts for different subjects can both see the port as free. Probe: three concurrent env.start calls on one project gave [28100, 28100, 28101] in one of five trials, and each record names its port. Parallel stories that start demos at the same time are exactly this case. The products collide on one port, or one dies late, after the settle window has passed.
proposed_resolution: Hold ports.lock from the choice until the 'starting' record that names the port has been written, for example by having _choose_port write the record while it still holds the lock. Add a test that runs several concurrent starts and asserts distinct ports.

outcome.what_was_done: ports.lock is now taken in _launch and held from the port scan until the 'starting' record naming the port is written, so a concurrent start scanning under the lock sees the claim; the scan itself is _pick_port, which takes no lock. test_concurrent_starts_claim_distinct_ports starts four products in four threads and asserts four distinct ports; with the release moved back before the record write the test failed twice in four runs.

problem: When a job keeps dying, attach writes the failure result with record.collected = False and returns it. The next call is therefore served the same stale failure without measuring, which breaks D5 ('a result is served once'; a failing gate is never returned without measuring again). Probe: after the loud failure, a second attach with a now-working command returned the old 'lost its worker twice' failure, and only the third call ran the work. test_job_that_keeps_dying_fails_loudly makes no second call.
proposed_resolution: Write collected: True in that branch. The call returns the result, and other waiters still receive it through the unchanged nonce. In test_job_that_keeps_dying_fails_loudly, add a second attach and assert that it runs the work again.

outcome.what_was_done: The 'lost its worker twice' failure is written with collected: True, so the next call re-measures instead of being served the stale failure; waiters still receive it through the nonce. The loud-failure test counts runs through a file: exactly two runs for the first call, and a second attach runs the work again.

problem: The cap of one restart is tracked per call. Calls last at most 240 s (100 s by default) and a gate lasts minutes, so a job that dies every time, but later than one call's wait, is restarted by each new call forever and never reported. The intent of D6 ('a job that dies every time is loud') is not met. Probe: with run_shell running 'sleep 1.5; kill -9 $PPID' and calls of wait=1, six calls in a row returned pending with starts = 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, never ok: false. With real gates each restart costs a whole run, and the clerk re-runs pending without end. The plan's loop says 'if this call has already restarted once', so this is a gap in the plan that the code inherits. The record already carries starts.
proposed_resolution: Decide the loud failure from the record as well as the call: a loss found when record.starts >= 2 writes the failure result (with collected: True, see S3R-jobs-3) instead of restarting. Add a test in which the job dies after the call's wait and successive short calls end in ok: false within two starts.

outcome.what_was_done: The loss branch also caps from the record: a loss with record.starts >= 2 writes the failure result, so a job that dies later than any one call's wait is still restarted only once in its life. test_loss_cap_comes_from_the_record drives three wait=1 calls against a worker that dies two seconds in: starts reaches 2 and the third call is loud, not pending.

problem: The D9 backstop is signal.alarm(limit + 30) with no SIGALRM handler. Its default action kills the worker without writing a result and without killing the running command's process group. The job is then seen as lost and restarted, runs its whole limit again, and is reported as 'the job lost its worker twice and kept dying' rather than as the time limit. Probe: a work function that sleeps in Python (outside ctx.run) with limit_seconds=1 returned after 62 s with starts = 2 and the lost-twice error. With S3R-jobs-4 it restarts forever. Nothing tests the backstop.
proposed_resolution: Install a SIGALRM handler in worker_main that kills guard['pgid'], writes the time-limit failure result ({**error_shape, ok: false, error: 'ran longer than <n> minutes (limits.gate_minutes); log: ...'}), writes done and exits. Make the 30-second margin a module constant so a test can shrink it, then test a work function that overruns outside ctx.run.

outcome.what_was_done: worker_main installs a SIGALRM handler (the margin is the module constant ALARM_MARGIN = 30, overridable per payload for tests): it kills the running command's group, writes the time-limit failure naming the log, writes done, emits job.done and exits. test_alarm_backstop_ends_an_overrun_outside_ctx_run runs worker_main through the helper with run_sleep (a work function that never calls ctx.run), limit 1 and margin 1: the worker ends in seconds and the result file carries the exact limit failure. Reverting the registration made the test fail.

problem: Plan 3.3 promises the failure text 'ran longer than <n> minutes (limits.gate_minutes)'. ctx.run instead builds the message from int(self._deadline - started), the time left when the current command started, not the job's limit. Probe: limit_seconds=2 gave 'ran longer than 1 seconds'. A 60-minute gate gives 'ran longer than 3599 seconds', and a second command that times out with ten minutes left gives '599 seconds'. The message never says minutes in practice. test_time_limit_stops_the_job checks only the substrings 'longer than' and 'limits.gate_minutes', so it cannot fail on this.
proposed_resolution: Give JobContext the job's limit_seconds from the payload and build _limit_message from it. Assert the exact text in the test (for example with limit_seconds=60 and a monkeypatched deadline, or by checking the formatter for 60 and 120).

outcome.what_was_done: The job's limit_seconds is carried into JobContext and _limit_message is built from it, so a 1-second limit says 'ran longer than 1 seconds (limits.gate_minutes)' and a 60-minute gate says minutes; ctx.run no longer reports the seconds that happened to be left when its command started. The time-limit test asserts the exact failure text, and _limit_message(3600) is pinned to 'ran longer than 60 minutes (limits.gate_minutes)'.

problem: Plan 3.2 promises that a failure made by the job layer is {**error_shape, ok: false, error: '<one line naming the log>'}. Only the lost-twice failure names the log. The time-limit failure ('ran longer than 1 seconds (limits.gate_minutes)') and the crash failure ('the job crashed: KeyError: 'command'') do not, so a caller is told the traceback is in the log without being told where the log is. The crash text also embeds str(exc) as it is, which can span several lines. The builder did not report this as a departure.
proposed_resolution: Append '; log: <path>' to every job-layer failure and collapse newlines in the exception text. In test_time_limit_stops_the_job and test_work_crash_keeps_command_shape, assert that the log's path appears in the error.

outcome.what_was_done: Every job-layer failure now goes through _job_failure: newlines collapsed, and the text ends with '; log: <path>'. The time-limit, crash and lost-twice failures all name the log; the time-limit and crash tests assert the path and that the error is one line.

problem: The record is read, changed and rewritten by two processes without a lock. The worker writes the result file, reads the record, then writes it with state done. An attach that sees the result in that gap writes collected: True, and the worker's write then puts collected: False back, so the next call is served the old result without measuring (D5). In the other order, attach's write from its stale read turns a 'done' record back into 'running' with the lock free, and list_jobs (S2c's status) then reports a finished job as running. Probe: with the gap widened by a one-second sleep in a scratch copy, the record ended done/collected: False and two collected calls ran the work once. Without the sleep the gap is short but real (attach polls every 0.2 s).
proposed_resolution: Serve a result only when record.state == 'done', which is the worker's last write; after it, only attach writes the record. Or keep collected in its own file (create it with O_EXCL and the nonce), or serialise record updates with a lock. Add a test that monkeypatches a pause between the result write and the done write and asserts the result is served once.

outcome.what_was_done: A result is served only from a record whose state is 'done' - the worker's last write, which is the last word on collected and nonce. With that ordering, attach's collected write happens after the worker's final write and can no longer be undone, and no stale read is written back over a done record. test_result_is_served_only_when_done holds the key lock, writes the result file while the record still says running, and asserts the result is not served until the record turns done (reverting the gate made it fail).

problem: The test cannot fail. It looks for state 'queued' on the second job right after attach has written that state, before the worker could take a slot. With _take_slot changed to return at once (no semaphore at all), all 19 job tests still pass (mutant run in a scratch copy). limits.parallel_gates, the semaphore the package brief names, therefore has no working test.
proposed_resolution: Assert the cap itself. While the first job runs (for example sleep 2), poll for at least a second that the second record never reaches 'running'. Afterwards assert second.started >= first.finished from the records.

outcome.what_was_done: test_semaphore_caps_running_jobs now runs both jobs to completion on two threads with parallel_gates = 1 and asserts, while the first runs, that the second's record never says running, and that second.started >= first.finished. The old assertions (pending plus a queued record attach writes before any slot is taken) are gone; with _take_slot a no-op the new assertions trip.

problem: The nonce rule of D5 (every call waiting on a job receives its result) has no test that can fail. With _serves changed to ignore the nonce, all 19 job tests still pass (mutant run in a scratch copy): the second waiter starts a fresh job, and the assertion starts == 1 still holds, because every fresh start that follows no loss has starts == 1. The plan's 'one run' and 'the command ran once' are never counted.
proposed_resolution: Count the runs as test_collected_result_is_not_served_again does (the command appends to a file) and assert exactly one run, in both test_two_waiters_get_one_result and test_same_command_twice_starts_one_job.

outcome.what_was_done: Both tests count runs through a file. test_two_waiters_get_one_result asserts exactly one run behind the two results (breaking the nonce rule makes the second waiter start a new job - two runs); test_same_command_twice_starts_one_job asserts the command ran exactly once.

problem: The module docstring says 'The worker makes the descriptor non-inheritable'. It does not. pass_fds clears close-on-exec on the lock descriptor, and a probe in the worker showed fd 3 inheritable: a child started with close_fds=False listed it. The builder's reported departure credits PEP 446, but PEP 446 does not cover a descriptor passed through pass_fds. The D3 invariant holds today only because subprocess defaults to close_fds=True. Any work function that uses os.system, posix_spawn or close_fds=False would hand the job lock to a child that can outlive the job.
proposed_resolution: Put the descriptor number in the payload and call os.set_inheritable(fd, False) in worker_main. Fix the docstring. Add a test in which a work function starts a child with close_fds=False that outlives the worker, and assert the job's lock comes free.

outcome.what_was_done: The worker payload carries lock_fd and worker_main calls os.set_inheritable(lock_fd, False); the module docstring now says the descriptor arrives inheritable through pass_fds against PEP 446's default and that close_fds is what shields child commands. The helper gained a worker mode, and test_worker_marks_the_lock_non_inheritable passes the descriptor through pass_fds and asserts the worker left it non-inheritable.

problem: Lock files are unlinked while a process may still hold them. stop_products on a product still 'starting' finds the lock held but pid null, so it kills nothing, deletes the record and lock file, and reports {pid: null}. The starter then rewrites the record as running, and the product runs on an unlinked lock: every later _lock_held says false, so it can no longer be stopped or listed and its port is handed out again. The same happens after a KILL that leaves a setsid'd descendant holding the lock, and in a prune that races a re-attach of a seven-day-old key (a second inode, two workers).
proposed_resolution: Unlink a lock file only after acquiring it, which proves no holder is left; otherwise leave the file in place. In stop_products, skip or wait out records in state 'starting', as env.start's _held_answer already does.

outcome.what_was_done: _delete_key removes the record, log and result files, then takes the lock file (flock) before unlinking it (_unlink_lock_if_free), so a held lock is never removed under a live holder; prune re-checks the lock at unlink time and skips the key if a re-attach took it; stop_products leaves records in state 'starting' alone - the start call that holds the lock is still settling and cleans up after itself. Tested: stop_products with a starting record leaves record and lock intact, and a stop with the lock held by another process removes the record but not the lock file.

problem: D17, and the builder's edit to env-start.md, say that a story id runs in its story worktree and anything else in the integration worktree. _worktree_dir uses classify_worktree(subject) for any kind, so a 'spike-x' subject runs in .worktrees/spike-x (probe confirmed). The story-worktree path, the one step 5's demo uses, has no test: every test_env case uses 'demo-N' and so the integration worktree. A probe shows it works today.
proposed_resolution: Use the classified worktree only when its kind is 'story', or else amend D17 and env-start.md to name spikes. Add test_start_runs_a_story_in_its_worktree: S-9.01 with its worktree runs there, and without it the answer is negative even though _integration exists.

outcome.what_was_done: _worktree_dir uses the classified worktree only when its kind is 'story'; anything else, a named spike included, runs in the integration worktree, as env-start.md and D17 say. test_start_runs_a_story_in_its_worktree pins the story path (started.txt lands in .worktrees/S-9.01 and not in _integration); test_start_runs_anything_but_a_story_in_the_integration_worktree pins spike-x in the integration worktree.

problem: The 4,000-byte cap is partly enforced. _write_record drops args and error_shape, then writes the record even if it is still over the cap (its comment says 'before giving up'). Product records, whose command and cwd come from configuration, are never checked. attach also creates the store directory before it refuses an over-cap spec, although the plan says nothing is written. test_bad_spec_is_refused accepts any '*.lock' entry as 'nothing written', so it would not notice a stray lock file.
proposed_resolution: Validate before the mkdir. Make _write_record raise, or truncate deterministically, when the cap is still exceeded, and apply the cap to product records too. In the test, assert that the store directory does not exist after the refusals.

outcome.what_was_done: The two missing tests are in. test_write_record_refuses_even_after_shedding calls jobs._write_record with an irreducible record (the 3,850-byte command field is not one of the shed fields) and asserts ValueError with nothing written, then pins the shedding side: a record over the cap only through args and error_shape is written without them. test_start_refuses_an_oversize_product_record gives factory.toml a run command of RECORD_CAP + 500 bytes and asserts env.start answers code 1 naming the cap, with no record left behind. Both fail against the previous code (removing the raise in _write_record, or the size check in env._launch, makes each fail).

problem: A kill between mkstemp and os.replace leaves '.<key>.json.<random>' or '.<key>.result.json.<random>' in the store, and nothing removes it. _key_paths skips every name that starts with '.', so prune never removes these temporary files, and they build up across restarts.
proposed_resolution: In prune, delete dot-prefixed temporary files of the _atomic_write form that are older than a short age (for example one hour), and add a case to test_list_jobs_and_prune.

outcome.what_was_done: _key_paths no longer skips dot-names of the _atomic_write temporary form (.'key'.json.<rand> and .'key'.result.json.<rand>): they count towards their key's newest mtime, so prune removes them, alone or beside their key. test_prune_removes_abandoned_temporaries asserts an eight-day-old temporary is removed and a fresh one kept.

outcome.what_was_done: test_the_five_job_events_are_written drives attach (job.started, job.done), a killed worker (job.lost), env start and env stop with one session id and reads the EventLog back: all five D21 types present, each line carrying session_id, id, command and detail. A schema drift that makes _emit drop events now fails the test.

problem: When a worker is SIGKILLed (by the OOM killer, by a person, or as in test_lost_worker_restarts_once), its configured command's process group runs on, because it has its own session and nothing records its group. The restart then runs a second copy of the same gate command in the same worktree beside the first, and the two can write the same output and evidence files.
proposed_resolution: Record the running command's process group in the record (ctx.run already knows it from guard['pgid']). In the loss branch of attach, killpg that group before starting the new worker. Extend test_lost_worker_restarts_once to assert that the first sleep is gone.

outcome.what_was_done: The job record gains a command_pgid field, written by the worker when ctx.run starts the command (through a JobContext on_command hook); attach's loss branch killpg's it SIGKILL before restarting, so no second copy of the gate command runs on in the worktree. test_lost_worker_restarts_once now asserts the record names the group and that the group is dead shortly after the restart while its own sleep still had seconds to run. Interface note: the record's field list grows by command_pgid (null until a command runs).

problem: The prelude's emptyOf() gives status "" and next {} for a relayed command that printed no JSON, and neither passes the shipped checkpoint-result or survey schema: status has an enum without the empty string, and next requires kind. relay() tells the clerk to return that object, which the platform's schema check would refuse. The Python side avoids it with Command.failure.

problem: New, caused by the S3R-records-9 fix. flush now commits only the rels listed by 'git diff --cached --name-only -z'. That command detects renames by default (diff.renames, git 2.9+), and --name-only then prints only the new name. So when one tracked state file is deleted and a similar one added in the same flush (a story or spec file renamed or renumbered, or any delete plus add over 50% similar), the deleted path drops out of commit_rels. The commit carries only the new file, and the deletion stays staged ('D '). Every later flush then returns state 'failed', because 'git add -A -- <path>' refuses a path that is in neither the index nor the worktree ('pathspec ... did not match any files'). No state file can be committed until someone runs git by hand in .factory. Probe (git 2.50.1): commit stories/E-1/S-1.01.md, rename it to S-1.02.md. The second flush is 'committed' with files ['stories/E-1/S-1.02.md'], status 'D  stories/E-1/S-1.01.md'. The third flush is 'failed'. Before the filter (commit_rels = state_rels) the same probe committed both paths and the next flush was clean. A deletion staged by a killed flush hits the same add failure; that was there before this round, and the same change fixes it.
proposed_resolution: Pass --no-renames to the 'git diff --cached --name-only' that builds commit_rels. Stage existing paths with 'git add -A --' and paths gone from the worktree with 'git rm --cached -q --ignore-unmatch --', so a deletion that is already staged is not refused. Tried in a scratch copy: the rename probe commits both paths and the next flush is clean; a killed flush's staged deletion commits; test_state_commits.py still passes. Add tests for (a) a committed story renamed to a similar file: state committed, both paths in HEAD's change, tree clean, next flush clean; (b) a committed file deleted and its deletion staged by hand before flush: state committed, tree clean.

outcome.what_was_done: Three changes in commits.py _flush_locked. (1) The `git diff --cached --name-only -z` that builds commit_rels now runs with --no-renames, so a delete-plus-add pair of a renamed state file lists both its paths and the deletion is committed together with the addition; before, rename detection printed only the new name, the staged deletion rode on, and every later flush failed on `git add -A -- <gone path>` ('pathspec did not match any files'). (2) Staging splits the valid rels: paths still in the worktree stage with `git add -A --`, paths gone from the worktree with `git rm --cached -q --ignore-unmatch --` (the same 40-path chunks), so a deletion already in the index — staged by a killed flush or by an earlier flush — no longer refuses. (3) The changed set also unions _staged_paths(root), the index's own leftovers read as `git diff --cached --name-only --no-renames -z` before staging: a staged rename is one 'R' record in status, which both changed_paths and _deleted_paths pass over, so a killed flush's staged rename would sit committed-never while flush reported 'clean'. Audit of every other git command in commits.py for rename, deletion, space, non-ASCII and already-staged: status --porcelain=v1 -z -uall and the two diffs are NUL-separated and never C-quoted, so spaces and non-ASCII come back whole (a rename pair in status is consumed and covered by the staged-diff union); add/rm --cached and commit --only take the paths as argv members, no shell; config user.email, rev-parse, merge-base take no paths. Tests (test_state_commits.py): test_flush_commits_a_renamed_story is the finding's probe — the second flush is 'committed' with both S-1.01.md and S-1.02.md in files, the tree is clean and the next flush clean; test_flush_commits_a_deletion_already_staged; test_flush_commits_a_rename_a_killed_flush_staged (status shows 'R ' and flush still commits both paths); test_flush_commits_a_renamed_name_with_space_and_accents runs a decision packet named 'nächste Runde.md' through status, staging, the diff and the commit pathspec. Each test was shown to fail against its reverted fix in a scratch copy of the tree.

problem: New, caused by the S3R-records-C1-1 fix. When flush.lock is busy, lock_release now keeps the entry and returns normally, without StoreBusy. Plan records.md 3 says 'StoreBusy after wait, which bounds the whole call', and the docstring was rewritten to match the new behaviour. Callers can no longer tell 'released nothing because flush.lock was busy' from 'nothing matched'. cmd_lock misreports both ways. Probe: with another process holding flush.lock, 'vsdd lock release --force' took 3.02 s and exited 0 with {ok: true, released: [], holder: null, error: ''}, while lock.json still held the entry and its run was not ended. Without --force, the caller's own session entry is kept and reported as 'another session's live run holds the lock', exit 1. The SessionEnd caller (wait=0.5, PL3-8) gets the same silent result and has nothing to log.
proposed_resolution: Keep the bounded per-entry wait. After writing the kept entries, raise StoreBusy when any matching entry was kept because its run_end was busy, carrying the entries that were released (for example exc.released), so lock.json and the run records still agree. In cmd_lock, catch StoreBusy and exit 1 with an error that says a flush is running and to retry, never holder null. Test: with flush.lock held, lock_release(session=..., wait=0.5) raises StoreBusy within about 0.6 s with lock.json unchanged, and 'vsdd lock release --force' exits non-zero naming the busy flush.

outcome.what_was_done: locks.lock_release: an entry whose run_end cannot take flush.lock within the wait budget is still kept and lock.json is written with the kept entries (lock.json and the run records agree), and after the file lock is freed the call raises StoreBusy whose `released` attribute carries the entries that were released — busy is no longer silent and the plan line 'StoreBusy after wait, which bounds the whole call' holds again. Caller note: `lock_release` must now be caught for StoreBusy; exc.released holds the entries actually released. cmd_lock._run wraps both the --force and the selector path: a StoreBusy returns exit 1 with `released` as far as it got, `holder` set to a kept entry (never null) and an error that says a flush is running and to retry — distinct from the 'another session's live run holds the lock' message. Tests: test_lock_release_wait_bounds_the_whole_call (test_state_locks.py) now expects StoreBusy within 1.0 s at wait=0.5 with lock.json unchanged and the run still live; new test_cmd_lock_release_while_a_flush_holds_the_lock (test_state_cmds.py) asserts `vsdd lock release --force` exits 1, holder is the kept live entry, the error names the flush, lock.json keeps its entry and its run, and the same command succeeds once the flush.lock holder dies. Both fail against the reverted behaviour (verified in a scratch copy).

problem: The S3R-records-3 fix put run_end under flush.lock with the default 3 s wait. lock_release and run_begin call run_end while they hold lock.flock, so lock_release's wait no longer bounds the call. Plan records.md 3 says 'StoreBusy after wait, which bounds the whole call', and RESOLUTIONS PL3-8 sets wait=0.5 to fit H1's 1 s SessionEnd deadline. Probe: with another process holding flush.lock (as a flush does during its git commit), lock_release(session='sess-A', wait=0.5) took 3.00 s, then raised StoreBusy and released nothing. With several matching entries it waits 3 s each. A busy run_end mid-loop leaves the earlier runs ended while lock.json still names them. run_begin likewise holds lock.flock for up to 3 s per run_end, and during that time lock_seen (1 s wait) returns False.
proposed_resolution: Give run_end a wait parameter. In lock_release, pass the time left from wait to each run_end and raise StoreBusy before writing anything once the budget is spent. Better still, write lock.json first and end the runs afterwards with the remaining budget, so a busy flush never leaves an entry pointing at a run it ended. Test: with flush.lock held by another process, lock_release(wait=0.5) returns or raises within about 0.6 s, and lock.json and the run records agree afterwards.

outcome.what_was_done: Interface change, flagged: runs.run_end grew a keyword, run_end(project, run_id, *, now=None, wait=3.0) — default unchanged, so existing callers are unaffected. lock_release now times the whole call from before it takes lock.flock and passes each run_end only the budget left; an entry whose run cannot be ended within it stays in lock.json (its run is still live), so the call returns what it released, lock.json and the run records agree, and nothing waits 3 s per entry inside a 0.5 s SessionEnd budget. Verified the test fails against the pre-fix behavior (elapsed ~3 s).
outcome.where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/{runs,locks}.py; next/tests/unit/test_state_locks.py::test_lock_release_wait_bounds_the_whole_call (flush.lock held: returns within 1 s, entry and live run agree; once flush.lock frees, the same release ends the run and empties the lock)

problem: The C1-1 fix sets GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1 on flush's add, rm --cached and commit calls. git refuses that when GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS=1 or GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS=1 is also set ('fatal: global 'literal' pathspec setting is incompatible with all other global pathspec settings', exit 128). gitrun.git passes the inherited environment through and strips only the repository-locating GIT_* keys, so a person who exports either variable gets state 'failed' from every flush that has changes, and hooks inherit it too. Probe: in a scratch copy, one new decisions/plain.md flushed with GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS=1 (or GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS=1) in os.environ gives 'failed: git add -A -- ... exited 128', and the next flush fails the same way. With _LITERAL_PATHSPECS emptied (the code before the fix) both commit. GIT_NOGLOB_PATHSPECS=1 is accepted.
proposed_resolution: In commits.py, make _LITERAL_PATHSPECS {"GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS": "1", "GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS": "0", "GIT_NOGLOB_PATHSPECS": "0", "GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS": "0"}; git reads "0" as off. In scratch this made both probes commit and kept test_state_commits.py at 20/20, also with both variables exported for the whole run. Add a test in test_state_commits.py that monkeypatches GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS=1 and GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS=1 into os.environ and asserts that flush commits a new packet and that the glob-neighbour case still leaves a.md out of HEAD.

outcome.what_was_done: _LITERAL_PATHSPECS in commits.py now forces the other three global pathspec settings off with literal on ({GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS: 1, GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS: 0, GIT_NOGLOB_PATHSPECS: 0, GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS: 0}); gitrun's full.update(env) lets the zeros override a person's 1s, so git no longer exits 128 ('literal' incompatible with all other global pathspec settings) when GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS=1 or GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS=1 is inherited. The finding's other git-environment question answered in the same places: the repository-locating keys (GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES, GIT_COMMON_DIR) are stripped for every call by gitrun._REPO_LOCATING_KEYS, now pinned by a test; GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/SYSTEM and the author and committer variables pass through by design and only shape the commit's metadata (test_flush_without_git_identity already covers identity). Tests in test_state_commits.py: test_flush_with_conflicting_pathspec_environment monkeypatches GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS=1 and GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS=1 into os.environ, flushes a valid [ab].md beside an over-cap a.md, and asserts committed-not-failed, a.md rejected and out of HEAD, and a clean later flush; test_flush_ignores_inherited_repo_locating_environment sets GIT_DIR to a foreign bare repo plus GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_INDEX_FILE and asserts the state branch advances, the foreign index is never created and the foreign repo receives nothing. Verified the first test fails with GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS forced to 1 in the dict (flush returns failed). Spec: topics/state-commits.md step 4 now says the other global pathspec settings are forced off and why.

problem: flush hands state paths to 'git add -A --', 'git rm --cached ... --' and 'git commit --only --' as pathspecs, and git reads a pathspec's glob characters (* ? [ ]) and a leading ':' as patterns and magic. So a valid file whose name has glob characters also stages and commits every file the pattern matches, including files flush just rejected. Probe (scratch copy, git 2.50): cycles/product-1/decisions/a.md is over PACKET_CAP and rejected (over_cap), and cycles/product-1/decisions/[ab].md is a valid packet. flush returns 'partial', with a.md listed in rejected and only [ab].md in files, but 'git show HEAD:cycles/product-1/decisions/a.md' succeeds and status is clean: the rejected file was committed through the '[ab].md' pathspec. The new 'rm --cached' staging of gone paths has the same exposure: deleting a glob-named file unstages whatever tracked files its pattern matches. This was already there before this round (add and commit --only already took pathspecs). It is reported here because S3R-records-C2-1 asked for an audit of every git command in commits.py for awkward file names, and that audit closed with 'paths go to git as argv members, nothing else needed changing'. Passing a path as an argument does not stop git reading it as a pattern. Also, test_flush_commits_a_renamed_name_with_space_and_accents only adds a file and stages its deletion; it never renames anything. A confirmer probe of a real rename of 'nächste Runde.md' to 'über nächste Runde.md' does commit both paths and the next flush is clean.
proposed_resolution: Run the three path-taking git commands in _flush_locked with git's global '--literal-pathspecs' option (git --literal-pathspecs add / rm / commit; for commit it goes after the -c options and before 'commit'), or set GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1 in their env. In a scratch copy, this made the probe pass and test_state_commits.py still passed (19 of 19). Add a test: a rejected a.md next to a valid [ab].md, where flush must not commit a.md. Rename the space-and-accents test, or make it a real rename.

outcome.what_was_done: The three path-taking git calls in _flush_locked (add -A, rm --cached, commit --only) now run with GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1 in their env (module constant _LITERAL_PATHSPECS), so a record name's glob characters and a leading ':' are never read as a pattern; the env form keeps the commit's -c options position-free. Verified the new test fails with the env blanked (scratch pytest plugin): without the fix the rejected a.md rides into HEAD through the '[ab].md' pathspec. New test test_flush_does_not_commit_a_rejected_neighbour_of_a_glob_name: over-cap a.md beside a valid [ab].md — flush is partial, a.md named with over_cap, [ab].md committed, a.md absent from HEAD and still in status. test_flush_commits_a_renamed_name_with_space_and_accents is now a real rename (nächste Runde.md -> über nächste Runde.md committed, then renamed): both paths committed, old name gone from HEAD, tree clean, next flush clean — it exercises the rm --cached staging too. Spec: topics/state-commits.md step 4 now says the path-taking git calls run with literal pathspecs and why.

problem: The S3R-records-C2-2 fix attaches the partial success to StoreBusy as the attribute 'released'. The SessionEnd caller that hook-runner-b is building, liveness._released_under_busy, reads getattr(busy, 'entries', None) instead. Neither plan records.md 3, hook-runner-b.md 4 nor the spec names this attribute, so each unit picked its own name. Probe (scratch copy): session sess-A holds two lock entries; the first run_end succeeds and the second raises StoreBusy. lock_release raises with busy.released == [entry a:develop] and lock.json keeps only b:develop. liveness._released_under_busy(busy) returns [], so the 'lock.released' event for the entry that really was released is never logged. Separately, the lock_release docstring now ends '— a caller cannot distinguish busy from nothing matched (finding S3R-records-C2-2)'. That describes the problem that was fixed as if it were current behaviour.
proposed_resolution: Settle on one attribute name and write it down where both units read it: StoreBusy.released, which records ships, in plan records.md 3 and topics/state-api.md (the orchestrator's files). Then have hook-runner-b's liveness read 'released'. Add a test that runs through both units: two entries, a busy second run_end, and SessionEnd logs lock.released for the first. Reword the docstring to say that the exception lets a caller tell busy from nothing matched.

outcome.what_was_done: The seam attribute is named: StoreBusy.released for the entries released, and lock_release now also attaches StoreBusy.kept for the entries held back because their run_end was busy (locks.py). The lock_release docstring no longer says a caller cannot distinguish busy from nothing matched — it says the exception is how a caller tells them apart and names the kept entries. hooks/liveness.py._released_under_busy reads 'released' (the rename was landed by the hook-runner-b builder in this tree while this fix ran; verified in place and aligned tests with it). Cross-unit test test_session_end_logs_released_entries_when_a_run_end_is_busy: two entries of one session, first run_end succeeds, second is busy, real lock_release through liveness.release with a stub ctx — it returns the first entry, logs exactly one lock.released for its run, logs runner.liveness_error, and leaves the kept entry with its run live; verified it fails when _released_under_busy reads 'entries' again. test_release_logs_a_busy_store's fake StoreBusy now carries 'released'. Spec: topics/state-api.md names StoreBusy.released and StoreBusy.kept as the seam's contract and says the session-end caller logs the released entries as lock.released. Still open for the orchestrator: the same one-clause naming in plan records.md 3 and hook-runner-b.md 4 (rewrite/plans/ is not mine to edit).

problem: cmd_lock._run now catches every StoreBusy and reports 'a flush is running; the release could not end the runs of the entries it matched'. StoreBusy also comes from lock_release's own 'locked(project, "lock.flock", wait=3.0)' when another lock release or a run_begin holds lock.flock. Then no flush is involved and nothing was matched. Probe (scratch copy): with lock.flock held by another process, 'vsdd lock release --force' exits 1 after about 3 s with that flush error. The reported holder is also lock_entries()[0], which can be an unrelated session's entry rather than the entry kept because run_end was busy.
proposed_resolution: Tell the two causes apart. Only the busy-run_end StoreBusy carries 'released', or lock_release can attach the kept entries as well.
