Report 'a flush is running' and name a kept-busy entry as holder only in that case. For a lock.flock timeout, say the run lock is busy because another release or survey holds it. Test both: flush.lock held and lock.flock held.

outcome.what_was_done: Added the missing two-entry test: test_cmd_lock_release_names_a_kept_entry_not_the_first_lock_entry writes lock.json with sess-other's live entry first (scope repo-a:develop) and the caller's sess-mine entry second (scope repo-b:develop), holds flush.lock in a subprocess, and runs 'vsdd lock release' with sess-mine's caller marker. It asserts exit 1, released empty, holder.session == 'sess-mine' (the kept entry from StoreBusy.kept, not lock_entries()[0]), 'flush' in the error, and lock.json keeping both entries in order with both runs still live. Replacing the holder with _names(lock_entries(inv.root)[0]) again — the mutation the confirmation probed — fails exactly this test (sess-other named) while the other six in the file still pass, so the test now pins what the code does.

problem: closure_update starts a new record with dict(_EMPTY_CLOSURE). That is a shallow copy, so every new closure shares one module-level 'stages' dict. A mutate that writes record['stages'][...] on a new record changes the template itself, and every later new closure in the same process starts with those stage entries. Probe: a new closure for story S-1 got stage 'draft', then a new closure for S-2 (mutate does nothing) was written with stages {'draft': ...}, and _EMPTY_CLOSURE['stages'] now holds 'draft'. A checkpoint that writes several units in one call, or any pytest session of the survey or checkpoint units, gets closure records with stages that never ran. Stage order is data (revise clears from a stage onward). No test creates two new closures.
proposed_resolution: Build the fresh record inside closure_update ({'schema': 1, 'workflow': workflow, 'subject': subject, 'cycle': cycle, 'state': 'open', 'stages': {}}) or use copy.deepcopy. Add to test_closures: a new closure whose mutate adds a stage, then a second new closure that must have empty stages.

outcome.what_was_done: closure_update builds the fresh closure record inline (literal dict with its own stages) instead of copying the module-level _EMPTY_CLOSURE, which is gone. No new closure can inherit a predecessor's mutation.
outcome.where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/cycles.py; next/tests/unit/test_state_cycles.py::test_two_new_closures_are_independent (two new closures in one process; the second must have empty stages, both orders)

problem: lock_seen reads lock.json without the file lock, updates 'seen' in that copy, then takes lock.flock and writes the old copy back without reading it again. Anything that changed the lock in between is lost. Probe 1: a lock_release(session=) that runs between the read and the write is undone. The released entry comes back with a fresh 'seen' and still points at the run that the release had ended. Probe 2: a stale takeover by another session's run_begin is overwritten. The lock names the old, ended run again, and the new run holds no entry. run_begin refuses any other session for 20 minutes, and the new run's checkpoint lock_release(run=) releases nothing. hook-runner-b will call lock_seen on every guarded call and lock_release on SessionEnd, so both can happen in normal use. The plan's 'reads once and takes no file lock' covers only the no-write path.
proposed_resolution: Keep the unlocked read for deciding whether a write is due. When it is, read lock.json again under lock.flock and set 'seen' only on entries that still match by (scope, run). Never write back the unlocked copy. Add a test that monkeypatches the locked write to run a release or a takeover first, then checks that the release or takeover survives.

outcome.what_was_done: test_lock_seen_refresh_does_not_undo_a_concurrent_release now begins the run with now='2026-11-24T12:29:00Z', a full write-interval before lock_seen's 12:30:00 stamp, so the refresh is due and lock_seen reaches the locked re-read and write that the race injection surrounds. No code change: the re-read under lock.flock was already correct.

problem: D1 says flush.lock covers 'every read-modify-write'. records/lock.md and topics/run-lock.md say writes to machine records are atomic 'under flush.lock'. These read-modify-writes take no lock: run_admit, run_set and run_end (run.json), settle_decision (the decision record) and cycle_write (a tracked record). Two processes can therefore lose an update. For example, the survey's run_admit of a story races a run_set(agents=) or a run_end from a SessionEnd release, the story drops out of 'stories', and every gate then refuses story_not_in_run. Two settles of the same decision can both succeed. run_open checks path.exists() and then writes, so two lock-free runs (spike) opened in the same minute with the same random suffix overwrite each other. store_step's read-then-write collision check has the same gap. The builder did not report this departure.
proposed_resolution: Do run_admit, run_set, run_end, settle_decision and cycle_write under store.locked(project, 'flush.lock') (run_end is called under lock.flock, which comes first, so the order holds). Create the run directory with mkdir(exist_ok=False) and retry with a new id on FileExistsError. Add a two-process test for run_admit against run_set.

outcome.what_was_done: run_admit, run_set, run_end, settle_decision and cycle_write hold store.locked(project, 'flush.lock') around their read-modify-writes (ordering lock.flock then flush.lock, as D1 says). run_open creates the run directory with mkdir(exist_ok=False) and retries on collision. store_step keeps no lock: its records are written once by rename (D1: a step never waits on a flush), and the collision check judges the stored file, which a rename cannot tear. store_step's refusal for an unknown run moved to run_not_live (see S3R-records-24).
outcome.where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/{runs,decisions,cycles}.py; next/tests/unit/test_state_runs.py::test_concurrent_admits_from_real_processes (four real subprocesses, twenty-four admits, every story present)

problem: decision_status and settle_decision check staleness against the file list stored in the record, not against the current spec file set. The plan says 'the kind's digest no longer matches', and topics/digests.md says 'the survey recomputes the digest'. Probe: approve spec, add .factory/specs/architecture/SS-02.md, and spec_approved still returns (True, ''), so an unapproved contract passes the survey precondition. Deleting a covered file makes decision_status, spec_approved and settle_decision raise digest_missing_file instead of reading 'stale' (probe: spec_approved raised). Because of this, test_spec_approved's check that a brief or guidance edit does not stale the approval cannot fail: those files are new after approval, and the stored list never contains them.
proposed_resolution: For kind 'spec', compare record['digest'] with spec_digest(project)[0]. That covers added, removed and changed files. A missing file under the stored-list rule should read 'stale' rather than raise. Test an added contract file and a deleted one (both stale), and edit an existing brief.md and conventions.md that were present at approval (still approved).

outcome.what_was_done: Staleness is computed by one helper, _stale: a spec decision is compared against spec_digest(project)[0], the current specification file set, and a missing covered file reads as stale (caught StoreRefused), never as digest_missing_file; other kinds digest the stored list as before. decision_status and settle_decision share it. brief and guidance stay outside the set, so the former unfalsifiable check can now fail.
outcome.where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/decisions.py; next/tests/unit/test_state_decisions.py::test_spec_staleness_follows_the_current_set (an added contract stales; a deleted file stales at status and at settle; brief and guidance edits do not)

problem: The plan promises that KINDS limits topology to one of single or split, and that only key and item may repeat. settle_decision checks neither. Probe: 'spec approve topology=banana variant=a variant=b' settled as approved with values {'topology': 'banana', 'variant': 'a b'}. The survey and plan stages read topology and variant from an approved spec decision.
proposed_resolution: Give Choice an allowed-values map (topology: {single, split}) and mark only key and item as repeatable. Refuse bad_key for a value outside the set and for a non-repeatable key given twice. Add both cases to test_settle.

outcome.what_was_done: Choice gained values (allowed values per key); spec approve carries topology=(single, split). settle_decision refuses a value outside its key's set with bad_key, and a repeated key whose mode is not _REPEAT (only key and item repeat) with bad_key, both before note_required.
outcome.where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/decisions.py; next/tests/unit/test_state_decisions.py::test_topology_values_and_repetition (topology=banana variant=a variant=b refuses; key= repeats; variant= does not)

problem: The plan says KINDS carries 'for open-spike and skip the reason the decision must carry'. tables/decision-kinds.toml has 'open-spike name=<name> (for spike_limit)' and 'skip (for an optional environment check)'. Choice has no reason field, and settle_decision never compares the record's reason. Probe: a blocked decision with reason 'stuck' was settled with 'skip' as approved. decision_open's bad_reason only refuses an empty reason, so a blocked decision opened with reason 'nonsense-reason' was accepted. The record schema documents four reasons (spike_limit, environment, stuck, reviewer).
proposed_resolution: Add Choice.reasons (open-spike: spike_limit; skip: environment), and have settle_decision refuse bad_choice, listing the choices valid for this reason, when the record's reason is not among them. decision_open should refuse bad_reason for a blocked reason outside the four. Test both.

outcome.what_was_done: Choice gained reasons; KINDS gates open-spike on spike_limit and skip on environment (the annotations the table carries). settle_decision refuses bad_choice when the record's reason does not allow the choice. decision_open refuses bad_reason for a blocked decision whose reason is not one of spike_limit, environment, stuck, reviewer (BLOCKED_REASONS).
outcome.where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/decisions.py; next/tests/unit/test_state_decisions.py::test_blocked_reason_gates (a stuck decision refuses skip and open-spike; a nonsense reason refuses at open; skip settles on environment)

problem: resolve_decision's second pass, 'else the one record', searches every cycle directory, closed cycles included. The plan and topics/decisions.md say a bare id is sought in the open cycles and _standing, and is ambiguous only 'when two cycles are open'. Probe: with cycle product-0 closed and holding a settled 'release', a bare 'release' resolves to the closed cycle. Once product-1 also settles its 'release', decision_read(root, 'release') raises ambiguous [release@product-0, release@product-1]. Every cycle has brief, spec, plan and release decisions, so after the first cycle closes, bare-id reads and settles of settled decisions refuse ambiguous. That is the situation D9 was written to avoid.
proposed_resolution: Restrict both passes to cycles_open(project) plus _standing. A qualified id@cycle still reaches a closed cycle. Add the closed-cycle case to test_resolve_prefers_open.

outcome.what_was_done: test_closed_cycles_are_not_searched rewritten to discriminate. Its unknown case now opens 'plan' only in the closed cycle hotfix-1.2 and expects the bare read to refuse unknown (the old case asked for 'plan', which existed in no cycle); its resolution case settles all three releases — both closed copies and product-1's — and expects the bare read to resolve to product-1 rather than be ambiguous (the old case left the open cycle's release open, so the open-first pass answered either way). Verified: restoring the all-cycles search fails both assertions.
outcome.where: next/tests/unit/test_state_decisions.py::test_closed_cycles_are_not_searched (no code change; decisions.resolve_decision was already right)

problem: The builder's spec edit says flush 'never raises: every failure comes back as the result', and the PR4C-08 outcome claims it. flush catches only StoreBusy and GitError. With run='' (the PreCompact hook's call), _live_lock_run reads lock.json and each run.json through read_record, and a corrupt or schema-failing file raises StoreCorrupt out of flush. Probe: a lock.json of '{broken' made flush raise StoreCorrupt. test_flush_never_raises only patches git.
proposed_resolution: In _live_lock_run, treat StoreCorrupt as no live run (the trailer falls back to '-'). Also wrap _flush_locked so any unexpected exception becomes state 'failed' with the cause in error. Add the corrupt-lock case to test_flush_never_raises.

outcome.what_was_done: _live_lock_run treats StoreCorrupt from lock.json or any run.json as no live run (the trailer falls back to '-'), and flush wraps its whole locked body so an unexpected exception comes back as state failed, never a raise. The spec (as edited) already said flush never raises; no spec change was needed.
outcome.where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/commits.py; next/tests/unit/test_state_commits.py::test_flush_with_corrupt_lock_json ('{broken' in lock.json, then in run.json) and ::test_flush_surprise_is_a_failure (a RuntimeError inside the flush body)

problem: D11 and flush's docstring say it stages deletions, but deletions are never committed. flush takes its changed set from S1's changed_paths, which keeps only '??' and M/A/T/C flags and drops 'D'. Probe: after a committed decision record and packet were deleted, git status showed ' D' for both, changed_paths returned [], and flush returned state 'clean'. A deleted tracked state file stays uncommitted indefinitely while flush reports a clean tree. No test deletes a tracked file.
proposed_resolution: Have flush collect deletions as well, either from a deletions-aware helper agreed with state-core or by reading 'D' records itself through gitrun, and pass them to 'git add -A --'. Skip validation for deleted paths. Add a test that deletes a committed record, expects 'committed', and expects the file gone from HEAD.

outcome.what_was_done: flush runs _record_problem (and so _cap_problems) only for rels that still exist — the same `present` list check_paths already got — so a deleted decision record and packet no longer stat a missing .md into state 'failed'. Beyond that, the commit pathspec is now what staging left that differs from HEAD (`git diff --cached --name-only`), so an 'AD' file — a new file staged by a killed flush and deleted since — neither breaks `commit --only`'s pathspec nor lands in the commit, and the result's `files` reports the paths actually committed. Note for consumers of flush's result: `files` can now be narrower than the valid set when staged files cancelled themselves.
outcome.where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/commits.py; next/tests/unit/test_state_commits.py::test_flush_commits_deleted_decision_record_and_packet (committed record and packet deleted: state committed, both gone from HEAD, tree clean, later flush clean) and ::test_flush_staged_then_deleted_new_file (the AD case)

problem: D11's fallback ('where git has no identity, vsdd-factory') never runs. The identity check is run_git(base, 'config', 'user.email'), and gitrun.git raises GitError on git's exit 1 when the key is unset. Probe: with no global or local identity, flush returned 'failed: git config user.email exited 1'. On a machine or CI runner with no git identity, every flush fails. The tests always have an identity, because _repo.make_project sets one.
proposed_resolution: Call git(base, 'config', 'user.email', check=False), or catch GitError there and treat it as no identity. Add a test that unsets the identity (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL pointed at an empty file, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, local keys unset) and expects 'committed' with author vsdd-factory.

outcome.what_was_done: The identity probe runs git config user.email with check=False: exit 1 is the answer (no identity), and flush continues with the vsdd-factory -c overrides. The unreachable fallback is reachable.
outcome.where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/commits.py; next/tests/unit/test_state_commits.py::test_flush_without_git_identity (local unset, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM pointed at empty files; the commit is authored vsdd-factory <vsdd-factory@example.invalid>)

problem: P3SEAM-15 is marked fixed, but the completeness check has two holes. First, it skips earlier re-freeze records and compares only with the latest non-re-freeze red record, while the plan says 'the latest earlier red record' and the finding requires 'the tests added in the fix pass'. Probe: red(a,b), then refreeze(a,b,c), then refreeze(a,b) was accepted and c dropped out of the frozen set. Second, it compares with the latest earlier red record whatever its result, so a failing red record with no 'frozen' makes any re-freeze pass. Probe: red(a,b), then a failing red, then refreeze([]) was accepted.
proposed_resolution: Compare with the latest earlier red record that is passing or a re-freeze (the set the lookup would return), including re-freezes. Add both sequences to test_refreeze_incomplete.

outcome.what_was_done: The re-freeze completeness check compares against the latest earlier red record that is passing or a re-freeze, re-freezes included; failing red records are skipped, and the walk stops at that record instead of skipping earlier re-freezes.
outcome.where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/gate_evidence.py; next/tests/unit/test_state_gate_evidence.py::test_refreeze_chaining (red(a,b), refreeze(a,b,c), then refreeze(a,b) refuses naming tests/c.py; red(a,b), a failing red, then refreeze([]) refuses naming tests/a.py)

problem: The plan's error tree is StoreError with subclasses StoreRefused, StoreBusy, StoreCorrupt and DecisionRefused(StoreRefused). Only DecisionRefused is named as a StoreRefused. In the code StoreBusy and StoreCorrupt also subclass StoreRefused, so a consumer built to the plan that catches StoreRefused to report a refusal (exit 1) will also swallow a busy file lock or a corrupt store as an ordinary refusal. The builder did not report this departure.
proposed_resolution: Make StoreBusy and StoreCorrupt subclass StoreError directly, and add an assertion of the tree to test_store_refusals. Alternatively, report the change and get the plan and the consuming units (survey, jobs-b, hook-runner-b) to agree to it.

outcome.what_was_done: StoreBusy and StoreCorrupt now subclass StoreError directly, as the plan's error list has it; only StoreRefused (and DecisionRefused under it) is a refusal. Consumers that must react to busy or corrupt catch them by name (locks, commits already did). Interface change, plan-conforming: code that caught StoreRefused to also swallow busy or corrupt must catch StoreError.
outcome.where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/store.py; next/tests/unit/test_state_store.py::test_error_tree (the tree asserted: Busy and Corrupt are StoreErrors, not StoreRefused)

problem: _has_holdout_finding refuses walled_not_built when any string anywhere in the result contains '.factory/holdout/', including summary, data and step. The plan says 'a finding under .factory/holdout/', and topics/walled-findings.md says a finding whose location lies under it. A builder whose summary says it did not read .factory/holdout/ cannot store its result, and the same retry is refused again. A finding located at 'holdout/...' (state-relative) is not caught. The test passes data={'evidence': '.factory/holdout/HS-001.md'}, which is not a finding location, so the test fixes the over-broad behaviour in place. The unused 'root' argument suggests a narrower check was intended.
proposed_resolution: Check only finding locations: each finding in data.findings (and any other finding list the result schemas define) whose 'location' starts with '.factory/holdout/' or 'holdout/'. Test a summary that mentions the path (stored) and a finding located there (refused).

outcome.what_was_done: The walled check reads only findings' locations: a finding dict whose location.path lies under .factory/holdout/ or holdout/ (both spellings) refuses walled_not_built; summaries and other strings anywhere in the result no longer trip it, so a step that mentions the wall stores.
outcome.where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/steps.py; next/tests/unit/test_state_steps.py::test_store_step (located findings refuse in both spellings; a summary and a data note mentioning holdout store; the old over-broad fixture rewritten)

problem: test_evidence_lookup does not cover two branches the plan lists ('green by head, then patch id'; red must 'descend from the closure's delivery.base'). In a scratch copy, replacing the red base-descent condition with True and the green patch-id match with False left every test in test_state_gate_evidence.py and test_state_locks.py passing. The test's own comment admits no green matches by patch id. Discovering gates from vsdd.gates.gate_*.py files is also untested: the test calls register_gate directly, though the plan's case is 'a function registered by a gate_x.py module comes back'.
proposed_resolution: Add the following cases. A green record at head1 that matches after an amend or rebase gives the same diff (same patch_id, different sha). A passing red record on a commit before delivery.base, which is an ancestor of the head, must not be returned. A temporary vsdd.gates package with a gate_x.py that calls register_gate must come back through registered_gate('x').

outcome.what_was_done: Added the mutation-catching tests: green matches by patch_id after an amend (tree identical, commit id moved); a red record on a commit before the base is rejected while a record on the base counts; and discovery through vsdd.gates.gate_*.py (a stub package registers at import and registered_gate finds it; a failing gate module is loud and leaves the loaded mark unset).

problem: AU-S2-06, AU-P2-03 and AU-S2-04 are spec-duplication findings (the record or table should define, and the topics should link), but they are marked fixed for code structure (one module each; KINDS and resolve_decision as 'the one copy'). The duplication is still in the spec. records/lock.md 'Taking and releasing' and its closing atomic-writes paragraph repeat topics/run-lock.md almost word for word. topics/human-stops.md still lists the decision choices (lines 67 and 78). The <id>@<cycle> rule is written in conventions.md:152, topics/decisions.md:29, topics/hotfix-cycle.md:14 and commands/decide.md:31. AU-P2-03 also covers facts that belong to other packages (gates, spike limits, holdout thresholds, tier override). The builder's own AU-S2-04 text says the spec consolidation is still to come, and hook-runner.md already treats AU-S2-06 as spec text.
proposed_resolution: Reset all three to open, or to left-for-builder naming the spec documentation pass, with a note that this unit's code holds one copy. Do not record them as fixed until the spec files are reduced to links.

outcome.what_was_done: AU-S2-06, AU-P2-03 and AU-S2-04 reset from fixed to left-for-builder naming the spec pass: the code halves stand, but records/lock.md, human-stops.md and the four id@cycle statements are still duplicated, and only the spec pass can reduce them to links.

problem: P3OPS-07 and P3REQ-07 are marked fixed, but this unit built only the store half: run_admit, run_open(stories=) and run_require, which are tested. The resolutions also need the surveys to re-record admitted, undelivered stories in the new run, plus a harness scenario that kills a fast route after admission. survey.md claims those parts (test_admit_again_same_unit_new_run) and has not been built. The builder's own text for P3REQ-07 says so.
proposed_resolution: Mark both left-for-builder naming the survey (S3), and let the survey's outcome close them.

outcome.what_was_done: P3OPS-07 and P3REQ-07 moved from fixed to left-for-builder naming S3 (survey): the store half is built and tested, the re-recording of admitted stories in a new run (test_admit_again_same_unit_new_run) is the survey's.

problem: AU-P2-11, AU-S2-15 and P3COV-11 are spec-text fixes (cite BLUEPRINT 11.2 and record the open offers; rewrite the stale mapping rows). They are marked left-for-builder, which means the design is settled and code must follow. No code follows from them, so the status takes them out of the open count while nothing has dealt with them.
proposed_resolution: Leave the three open (or route them to the spec pass), not left-for-builder.

outcome.what_was_done: AU-P2-11, AU-S2-15 and P3COV-11 moved from left-for-builder back to open, so the spec-text fixes stay in the open count until the spec pass takes them.

problem: PR4C-05 is marked fixed partly for keeping the store's own schema check in store_step. No test would fail without it: in a scratch copy, removing schema='step-record' from store_step's write left test_state_steps.py and test_state_locks.py passing. The schema_invalid refusal of store_step is not exercised.
proposed_resolution: Add a store_step case with an invalid status (or a missing summary) that expects schema_invalid and no file written.

outcome.what_was_done: The kept schema check has its test: a result whose status the step-record schema refuses is stored by no one, and the step directory is unchanged after the refusal.
outcome.where: next/tests/unit/test_state_steps.py::test_store_step (status 'hardly' refuses schema_invalid; before == after for the run's step files)

problem: Decision ids are path segments but are never validated. A bare id in resolve_decision, decision_read and settle_decision, the id part of id@cycle, and the subject in decision_open all go straight into cycles/<c>/decisions/<id>.json. The plan's common rule says unsafe_id. Probe: decision_open(subject='../../../escape') wrote the record at cycles/product-1/escape.json, outside decisions/, then raised FileNotFoundError (not a StoreError) while writing the packet, leaving a partial write. 'decide ../../x' returns unknown rather than unsafe_id. safe_segment also allows '..' inside a segment, which the plan's 'without ..' excludes.
proposed_resolution: Validate every dot-separated part of the id with safe_segment, or apply the regex to the whole id, before any path is built, in _decision_path and decision_open. Reject '..' inside a segment. Test the traversal case.

outcome.what_was_done: The '..' refusal moved into store.safe_segment itself (the literal segments _standing, _base and _ still pass; '..' anywhere else in the segment refuses unsafe_id), so runs, steps, cycles, closures, evidence subjects and decisions all live under the one rule the docstring and plan records.md 3 state. decisions' duplicate _segment is dropped; its call sites use safe_segment directly.

problem: Two writes can be left half done by a kill. decision_open writes the record atomically, then the packet with Path.write_bytes, which is neither atomic nor first. A kill in between leaves an open decision with no packet or a truncated one, and the briefing and the person then see a question with no context. evidence_write writes the .log with write_text and copies the .xml with copyfile, both in place and after the record.
proposed_resolution: Write the packet first, through the same tmp-and-replace path as write_record, then the record, which is the commit point. Write .log and .xml through a tmp file and os.replace.

outcome.what_was_done: No code change: the packet-first order and the tmp-and-replace side files were already in the code; the missing tests are added. test_packet_written_before_the_record kills the packet write (write_via_tmp patched to raise on .md) and asserts neither packet nor record exists and a bare read refuses unknown. test_log_replace_failure_leaves_the_old_log makes os.replace fail on the .log and asserts the old .log is intact, no partial file sits beside the record, and the temporary file in local/tmp is cleaned up. Both fail against the reverted write order/in-place write.

problem: flush calls check_paths(root, None, ...), which checks every artifact in the state tree on every flush. PL3-3 and the plan say check_paths(root, rels, ...), and topics/state-commits.md says 'validates each changed or new file'. Problems in unchanged files are computed and then thrown away. The spec's 'well under 2 seconds on the 2,000-contract corpus' assumes only the changed set is checked.
proposed_resolution: Pass the changed state paths (the rels check_paths expects) instead of None.

outcome.what_was_done: No code change: flush already passes the changed rels. The discriminating test is added: a spy wraps artifacts.check_paths across a flush where only notes.json changed, and asserts the received list holds exactly that changed, existing rel and not the story artifact committed by the previous flush (which a check_paths(root, None) would have included).

problem: flush runs 'git add' on the valid paths and then a plain 'git commit', which commits the whole index. If a flush is killed after 'git add' and before the commit, the staged blobs stay in the index. If one of those files is then edited into an invalid state, the next flush rejects it but still commits the old staged blob. A file that was not checked in its final form gets committed, against 'a file that fails is left uncommitted'.
proposed_resolution: Commit only the valid paths ('git commit --only -m ... -- <paths>' in chunks, or run 'git reset -q -- <rejected>' before committing). Test with a pre-staged file that is rejected.

outcome.what_was_done: flush commits with commit --only -- <the valid paths>, so the whole index no longer rides along: a blob staged by a killed flush whose file was since rejected stays out of the next commit.
outcome.where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/commits.py; next/tests/unit/test_state_commits.py::test_flush_leaves_a_now_rejected_stale_blob_out (the story staged valid, broken in the worktree, then flushed: not in HEAD, the note beside it committed)

problem: Several tests cannot fail on the point they name. test_flush_partial_and_busy accepts state 'committed' when the flush lock is held, waits the real 5 s although its comment says it turns the wait down, and never checks that nothing changed. test_run_trailer_from_the_live_lock checks the trailer only if result['commit'] is set. test_flush says 'the product index and worktree were never touched' but checks git status of .factory, not the product repository. test_settle is described as 'every refusal code, in order', but it never gives a call that two refusals would hit, so the order is untested, and ambiguous and stale are not reached through settle_decision there.
proposed_resolution: In the busy test, monkeypatch commits.FLUSH_WAIT, expect exactly 'busy', and check that HEAD and status are unchanged. Assert the commit unconditionally in the trailer test. Run git status on the product root. Add order cases: not_open together with a bad choice gives not_open, and stale together with a bad choice gives stale.

outcome.what_was_done: The busy test patches FLUSH_WAIT to 0.2 s, expects state busy with commit '' and HEAD unchanged, and waits no real 5 s. The trailer test asserts state committed and reads the log unconditionally. The product-unouched check snapshots and compares the PRODUCT root's status (git -C root), not the state tree's. test_settle gained combined-refusal cases: not_open before bad_choice, stale before bad_choice, bad_choice before bad_key, bad_key before note_required.

problem: store_step refuses an unknown run with 'run_unknown', which is not among its promised codes (bad_identity, run_not_live, schema_invalid, over_cap, step_exists, walled_not_built). A run that does not exist is not live (run_live is false), and the step-results rule will map the promised codes. Separately, _replace_ok's 'identical content' test compares only step, status, summary, head and data. A second empty-agent_id write that differs in artifacts, gates, blocked, spike_request or grounded therefore counts as identical and replaces the record.
proposed_resolution: Refuse an unknown run as run_not_live, naming 'no such run' in the message. Compare the whole record, apart from the fields the store adds, for the identical-content case.

outcome.what_was_done: store_step refuses run_not_live for an unknown run too (an unknown run is not a live run; run_not_live is a promised store_step code). _replace_ok compares the whole record for identical content - artifacts, grounded and data included - beside the hook's own additions, which must still match.
outcome.where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/steps.py; next/tests/unit/test_state_steps.py::test_store_step_unknown_run_is_run_not_live and ::test_step_collision (identical whole record replaces across hook fields; one differing field refuses)

problem: The note store goes past the slice and does not match the spec's shape. topics/status-report.md shows notes as objects {at, text}, and spec schemas/notes.schema.json infers the same shape. read_notes keeps only string entries and silently drops object entries. write_notes, which nothing calls because vsdd note is deferred, writes bare strings. The task asked only that {"notes": []} read as no notes.
proposed_resolution: Keep read_notes but return the entries as stored (objects with at and text), and remove write_notes until vsdd note is built against the {at, text} shape.

outcome.what_was_done: read_notes returns the entries as stored, so the {at, text} objects the status report shows survive; write_notes is removed (unused beyond its own test, and beyond the slice until vsdd note is built). Interface change: cycles.write_notes is gone.

problem: patch_id returns git patch-id's whole output line, the patch id plus a zero commit id. Probe: 'e40938dd...cd6a 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'. The lookup compares it with itself, so the lookup works. But the stored delivery.patch_id and evidence patch_id are not patch ids, and any writer that stores git's first field will never match.
proposed_resolution: Return the first whitespace-separated field only, and describe it so in the evidence-record and closure-record schemas.

outcome.what_was_done: No code change: patch_id already returns the first whitespace-separated field. The test now asserts the shape directly: re.fullmatch('[0-9a-f]{40}', patch_id(...)) on a non-empty diff, which git's whole output line (id plus zero commit id) would fail.

problem: _ensure_gates_loaded swallows every ImportError from import_module('vsdd.gates'), including one raised inside an existing vsdd/gates/__init__.py, although the plan says only a missing vsdd.gates is swallowed. It also sets _GATES_LOADED before importing the gate modules, so if one gate_*.py raises, the first lookup raises and every later registered_gate call in that process silently returns None for the gates that were not loaded.
proposed_resolution: Catch ModuleNotFoundError only when exc.name == 'vsdd.gates'. Set the loaded flag after every module has imported, or record the failure and raise it again on later lookups.

outcome.what_was_done: No code change: the catch is already ModuleNotFoundError narrowed to exc.name == 'vsdd.gates'. The discriminating test is added: a shipped fake vsdd.gates whose gate_absent.py imports a module nobody has makes registered_gate raise ModuleNotFoundError and leave _GATES_LOADED False — under the reverted broad `except ImportError` the lookup would silently return None instead.

problem: records/run.md (edited by the builder) lists 'the id itself' among the run record's fields, and run_open stores 'id'. runs_list, steps_list and flush all read record['id']. The schema has no 'id' property and does not require it. A run.json without id passes the schema, and steps_list then calls steps_dir(project, '') and raises unsafe_id.
proposed_resolution: Add 'id' (pattern r-YYYYMMDD-HHMM-xx) to run-record.schema.json and to its required list, with a fixture.

outcome.what_was_done: run-record.schema.json requires id (string, minLength 1, described shape r-<YYYYMMDD>-<HHMM>-<2 of [0-9a-z]>). The shipped checker has no pattern keyword and its registry refuses one, so the shape is stated in the description and enforced by the store's _new_id; both valid fixtures and the two invalid fixtures now carry id, and a new invalid_missing-id fixture pins the requirement.

problem: tables/event-types.toml defines decision.refused with extra fields 'decision, choice'. cmd_decide logs it with 'reason' only, so the log cannot say which decision or choice was refused. A failure of the event log after a successful settle (EventError or OSError) would also crash the command after the record was written.
proposed_resolution: Log decision.refused with decision=<id as typed>, choice=<choice> and the refusal code, and catch log failures after settling so the exit code reflects the settle.

outcome.what_was_done: No code change: the logging was already fixed. The tests now hold it there: test_cmd_decide asserts decision.recorded carries decision='release' and choice='approve' and decision.refused carries decision, choice and code='bad_choice' (it checked event types only); the new test_cmd_decide_log_failure_after_settle makes EventLog.log raise OSError after the settle and asserts exit 0 with the record settled — un-guarded logging crashes the command instead.

problem: write_record treats a path as a local (compact) record when '.factory' and 'local' both appear anywhere in its parts, rather than when the path lies under .factory/local/. A tracked record in a cycle or unit named 'local' would be written compact, and the tracked-record indent rule would silently break for it.
proposed_resolution: Decide compact by the part that follows the first '.factory' component being 'local'.

outcome.what_was_done: write_record decides compactness by the component that follows .factory (helper _under_local), so a project directory merely named local no longer flips a tracked record to compact form.
outcome.where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/store.py; next/tests/unit/test_state_store.py::test_compact_only_under_factory_local (a root named local: tracked indented, .factory/local compact)

problem: run_begin's refusal returns stale_at = the holder's last 'seen' (or 'taken'), not the time the holder becomes stale (seen plus state.lock_stale_minutes). The name and the briefing's purpose (telling the person when the lock can be taken over) suggest the latter, and the plan does not define it.
proposed_resolution: Return the time the lock goes stale under stale_at (and keep seen in holder), or rename the field 'seen'. State which in the plan and in topics/run-lock.md.

outcome.what_was_done: run_begin's refused take returns stale_at as seen plus state.lock_stale_minutes, the moment the holder expires, not the last-seen time (an unreadable stamp reads back as itself); the minutes factored into lock_stale_minutes. topics/run-lock.md now states it. The plan file under rewrite/plans/ is outside this task's editable set, so the plan sentence is recorded here instead of edited.
outcome.where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/locks.py; rewrite/spec/topics/run-lock.md; next/tests/unit/test_state_locks.py::test_run_begin_stale_at_is_the_expiry (12:20 expiry at the default, 12:30 with lock_stale_minutes=30)

problem: KINDS restates tables/decision-kinds.toml by hand (D10). No check ties the two together. test_kinds_table hard-codes the verbs, so a change to the table, for example a new choice or a key, drifts silently from the code that enforces it. The same fact is now stated in two places.
proposed_resolution: Add a lint or unit check that parses tables/decision-kinds.toml and compares each kind's choice lines (verb, keys, note marker, status list) with KINDS, or generate KINDS from the table with tools/build.py.

outcome.what_was_done: test_kinds_match_the_shipped_table now also parses '<key>=<a> or <b>' from every table line and holds Choice.values to it exactly (topology=(single, split); adding 'banana' fails), with set equality in both directions so the code carries no value set the line does not state. It also names the one property the table does not hold: ideas select requires at least one list, asserted as any_of == {pursue, research, defer, reject}.

problem: The evidence lookup orders records by their `at` stamp, which carries whole seconds. Two records of one gate written within the same second tie, and the tie falls to the file name, so 'the latest record by at' is not deterministic for fast rewrites of nearby commits (for example a red re-run and a base re-record inside one second).
proposed_resolution: Either stamp evidence records with millisecond precision like the event log, or settle ties by the file's mtime, and say which in topics/evidence-lookup.md when the wider build touches it. Not on the slice's critical path: one record per gate and commit means a tie needs two writes to one key, which replace each other anyway.

outcome.what_was_done: The evidence order is now total and independent of the clock's whole-second stamp. gate_evidence.evidence_write stamps `seq` on the record under flush.lock (EVIDENCE_LOCK_WAIT = 2.0 s; StoreBusy if not had): one more than the highest seq in the subject's directory (_next_seq), so a rewrite renumbers above everything there and two records of one second order by the write's order, never the file name. _evidence_records sorts by (seq, at, file name); every lookup that reads 'the latest record' inherits the order; `at` stays for people. evidence-record.schema.json gains a required integer `seq` (minimum 1) and the `at` description now says the lookup orders by seq; the three fixtures (valid_red, valid_green, invalid_missing-at) carry seq, so the invalid fixture still fails for exactly its stated reason. tools/build.py --check reports all generated copies current (evidence-record is a NON_PRELUDE schema; no generated literal carries it). rewrite/spec/records/evidence.md states the seq rule with the finding id. Test test_same_second_records_order_by_write writes two same-second red records whose file names sort against the write order and asserts the records come back in write order with ascending seqs, then asserts a rewrite moves its record last; reverting the sort to (at, name) in a scratch copy fails it.

problem: Flush validates the records this unit writes (cycle, closure, decision, notes) but a tracked file shape added later (a new record kind in the state tree) would be committed unchecked by flush unless its author extends _record_problem; the artifact-territory check does not cover records, and nothing reminds the next builder.
proposed_resolution: When the build widens past the seven record shapes, move the per-kind record check into a table (path prefix, schema, cap) that new record kinds must extend, next to the artifact registry, and have flush and the write hook read the same table.

outcome.what_was_done: The per-kind record check in flush is now a table, commits.record_kinds(): one row per tracked record kind — cycle-record (cycles/**/cycle.json, schema, no cap), closure-record (cycles/*/units/*.json, schema plus CLOSURE_CAP), decision-record (cycles/*/decisions/*.json, schema plus RECORD_CAP), decision-packet (cycles/*/decisions/*.md, PACKET_CAP), notes (notes.json, parse only) — each row carrying kind, claim(path), schema, cap and parse. _record_problem judges through the claiming row and returns None when no row claims the file; _flush_locked turns that into a `no_validator` refusal naming the file, for every changed file under the record folders (the cycles tree and notes.json), so a tracked record kind added later cannot be committed unchecked and nothing fails quietly when a kind is missing. rewrite/spec/topics/state-commits.md step 3 now says a new tracked record kind must register its validator in that table in the same step as it first lands in the state tree. Tests (test_state_commits.py): test_flush_refuses_an_unclaimed_record_file (a stray .factory/cycles/product-1/extra/stray.json is rejected, named with no_validator, and never committed, while a valid notes.json in the same flush commits; the flush is partial and not ok) and test_record_kinds_cover_the_shipped_tracked_records (every record schema the unit ships for a tracked record — cycle-record, closure-record, decision-record — has a row, each row claims its own path form, and every row names a shipped schema). Disabling the refusal in a scratch copy fails the first test.

problem: The S3R-state-core-C1-7 fix pasted its explanatory comment twice in compile_registry: the five-line block 'A ref: target with no pattern anywhere is a compile-time fault ... (plan 3.5: the RegistryError names the row).' appears at lines 172-176 and again, word for word, at lines 177-181, just before the loop that re-raises with '[<row>].<key>: ...'. Behaviour is correct; the text is noise a reader has to compare to see that the two copies say the same thing.
proposed_resolution: Delete one of the two identical comment blocks above the ref: compile loop in artifacts.py.

outcome.what_was_done: The orchestrating session deleted the second copy of the five-line comment in _compile_registry; no behaviour changed. tests/unit/test_artifacts.py passes.

problem: The S3R-2 fix treats any .factory/ whose only entry is named .git as an interrupted mount, and mount_state then runs shutil.rmtree on it. It never checks that .git is a pointer file into this repository's own .git/worktrees, which the finding's proposed fix required. Reproduced in a scratch copy: a .factory/ that is a separate repository with two commits and its one file deleted from the worktree (so only .git remains). vsdd init answered exit 0, state ready, created true, and that repository's history was gone. Before the fix, init refused this case with 'move it aside'.
proposed_resolution: Accept as an interrupted mount only a .factory/.git that is a regular file. Its 'gitdir:' must resolve inside this repository's common git directory under worktrees/, and that worktree's gitdir file must point back at <root>/.factory/.git. Refuse with 'move it aside' otherwise. Add a test: a .factory/ holding a nested repository's .git directory is refused and left untouched, and no state branch is created.

outcome.what_was_done: _is_interrupted_mount is strict now: besides .factory holding only the entry .git, the .git must be a regular file (a .git directory is a repository of its own and is never removed), its gitdir must be an existing worktree registration of this repository - commondir resolves to <root>/.git and the gitdir sits under its worktrees/ - and the registration's own gitdir file must point back at <root>/.factory/.git. Anything else returns False, so mount_state never rmtrees it and init answers the 'move it aside' refusal. Both halves verified: with the old lenient check the new tests fail (init answered ready and the nested history was gone); with the fix a nested repository is refused and left byte-for-byte whole. Interface note: mount_state and init behaviour on a foreign .factory changes from 'cleared' to 'refused'; that is the intended repair, not a plan-interface change.

problem: The S3R-18 family check takes the family as the module stem up to its first underscore. Plan 3.1 says <family> is the command's first word with '-' written '_', so a hyphenated first word can no longer register. Reproduced: a cmd_lock_release.py with words ('lock-release',) gives 'RegistrationError: the first word 'lock-release' does not match the module's family 'lock'' from both dispatch and commands(). No current spec command has a hyphenated first word, so the regression is latent.
proposed_resolution: Accept the entry when f"cmd_{words[0].replace('-', '_')}" equals the stem, or when the stem starts with it followed by '_'. Add a hyphenated-family case to test_registration_rejects_malformed_commands, both one that registers and one that is refused.

outcome.what_was_done: The registration check in _load_command no longer splits the module stem at its first underscore: the entry is accepted when the stem equals cmd_<words[0] with '-' written '_'> or starts with that followed by '_', so cmd_lock_release.py registers lock-release while cmd_survey_extra.py still refines survey. A hyphenated case (test_hyphenated_first_word_registers_by_its_module_stem) runs both commands() and a dispatched call, and fails against the old partition-based check.

problem: The new origin-mount test runs init in a fresh git clone that has no local user.email or user.name, and git() inherits os.environ. The test therefore passes only on a machine with a global git identity. Reproduced: with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, test_init_origin_mount failed (KeyError 'state': init refused for lack of an identity). The other 83 state-core unit tests passed in that run.
proposed_resolution: Set a local identity in the clone (git -C clone config user.email/user.name) before running init. Alternatively, have the suite's conftest set GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL to a file holding a test identity.

outcome.what_was_done: test_init_origin_mount sets repo-local user.email and user.name in the clone before init, so it no longer depends on a global git identity. Verified under GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null: failed without the lines ('KeyError: state'), passes with them.

problem: The S3R-4 up-front refusal checks only state_dir.is_dir(). A .factory that is a plain file, or a symlink to a non-directory, passes the check. init then creates the state branch, crashes in 'git worktree add' with 'internal error: GitError ... already exists', and leaves refs/heads/factory-artifacts behind. This is the failure S3R-4 described, reproduced in a scratch copy.
proposed_resolution: Before anything is created, refuse whenever .factory exists and is anything other than an empty directory or a verified interrupted mount (see C1-1). Extend test_init_refuses_a_non_empty_state_directory_without_leaving_a_branch with a .factory file case.

outcome.what_was_done: The up-front refusal in cmd_init._run now fires whenever .factory exists at all (plain file, symlink, non-empty directory) and is neither an empty directory nor a verified interrupted mount, before anything is created - the old order created the state branch first and died in worktree add with the branch left behind. test_init_refuses_a_plain_file_state_directory_without_leaving_a_branch added: exit 2 naming 'move it aside', no factory-artifacts ref created, the person's file untouched; it fails against the old code (verified).

problem: The S3R-6 fix changed a partial project's init from exit 2 to exit 1. The SL1-27 outcome still records 'detect reports partial and init exits 2 naming /vsdd-factory:status --fix', which is now false, and the ledger carries that text.
proposed_resolution: Re-record SL1-27's text: init exits 1 with state partial, mounted false, and next naming /vsdd-factory:status --fix (test_init_partial_refuses).

outcome.what_was_done: The SL1-27 outcome in step3-state-core.json is re-recorded: init exits 1 with state 'partial' and next naming /vsdd-factory:status --fix (the exit-2 wording predates the S3R-6 correction).

problem: The S3R-9 fix adds a reason code, 'unreadable', that is not in spec rules/artifacts.md. Plan 3.5 closes the code set: the spec's codes except artifact_frozen, plus criterion_contract. The departure is not recorded in the plan or the spec, so consumers of Problem.code (validate output, flush, the status report) meet a code the spec does not define.
proposed_resolution: Add 'unreadable' (file cannot be read or is not UTF-8) to the reason-code table in rules/artifacts.md and to plan 3.5's code list. Alternatively, report the condition under an existing code such as frontmatter_invalid.

outcome.what_was_done: The 'unreadable' reason code is added to the closed set: a row in the reason-code table of rewrite/spec/rules/artifacts.md for a file that cannot be read or decoded when the tree is checked as a whole (vsdd validate, flush), noting a write-time check always holds the text. plan 3.5 defines its code set as 'those of spec rules/artifacts.md except artifact_frozen, plus criterion_contract', so the spec row heals the departure without editing the plan (rewrite/plans/ is outside this task's writable set).
outcome.where: rewrite/spec/rules/artifacts.md (Checks and reason codes); next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/artifacts.py (check_paths, unchanged code)

problem: The S3R-19 compile-time ref: check reports '[<target>]: a ref: to a kind with no id row and no constant pattern'. It names the target kind, not the row and key that hold the bad cell. Plan 3.5 says a RegistryError names the row, and the fixer reports that both checks do. For a row 'things' with who = 'ref:nohope', the message names only [nohope].
proposed_resolution: In registry(), catch the RegistryError from _ref_pattern and re-raise it as '[<row>].<key>: ref:<target> names a kind with no id row and no constant pattern'. Assert '[things]' in test_registry_compiles_cells_loudly.

outcome.what_was_done: The compile-time ref check re-raises with the row and key holding the bad cell: the message reads '[<row>].<key>: ref:<target>: a kind with no id row and no constant pattern', where it named '[<target>]' alone. test_registry_compiles_cells_loudly now asserts '[things].who' in the message; it fails against the unwrapped raise (verified). _ref_pattern's own message was reworded to 'ref:<target>: ...' to fit - it is a private helper of the same module.

problem: render_config hand-types a second copy of every SPECS key and default (limits, spikes, holdout, delivery, branches, state, hooks, ...) and init writes all of them into factory.toml, including the literal delivery.protected_paths = [".github/**", ".env*", "CODEOWNERS", "CHANGELOG.md"]. Because the key is then present, config.loads never applies the computed default, so the AU-T2-15 fix is dead on every project init creates: changing release.changelog to RELEASES.md in an init'd file leaves protected_paths ending in CHANGELOG.md (reproduced). It also contradicts decision 5 and the AU-S2-03/AU-T2-13/AU-P2-03/AU-S2-09 outcomes ('config.SPECS is the one key list', 'limits and defaults exist once, in SPECS'): a key added to SPECS is silently not written, and a changed default drifts. No test compares the rendered file with SPECS.
proposed_resolution: Build the rendered sections from SPECS ({key: spec[0]}) with the detected values laid over them; leave delivery.protected_paths out of the rendered file (or write the computed list from the rendered [release]) so the loader computes it. Add a test that the keys init writes equal SPECS's fixed-section keys, that every undetected value equals its SPECS default, and that editing release.changelog in an init'd file moves protected_paths.

outcome.what_was_done: The code half is completed: render_config now walks SPECS['project'] instead of the hand-typed ('name', 'languages', 'ui', 'layout') tuple, so a key added to the SPECS project row is written without a second edit. Both tests the finding asked for are in and bite: test_init_writes_exactly_the_specs_keys asserts for every fixed section that the written keys equal SPECS[section] minus protected_paths and rules, and test_init_undetected_values_equal_specs_defaults now checks every written key - a key present in 'detected' must equal the detected value, every other key its SPECS default. Verified both directions: dropping limits.gate_minutes from the renderer fails the first test; writing limits.agents_per_run = 999 fails the second.

problem: init is not restartable at two kill points. (a) Killed after mount_state and before ensure_excludes: the next run detects 'ready' and returns at once, so .git/info/exclude never gets .factory/ and .worktrees/ and the person's git status shows '?? .factory/' for good (reproduced by raising in ensure_excludes, then re-running init: exit 0, ready, not excluded). (b) Killed inside 'git worktree add' (pointer written, checkout not done): the next run refuses with 'move it aside and run vsdd init again'; after the person does exactly that, init crashes with 'internal error: GitError ... is a missing but already registered worktree' (reproduced). The plan requires that an interrupted init resume.
proposed_resolution: Call ensure_excludes before mount_state and also on the ready path (it is idempotent). In mount_state run 'git worktree prune' before 'worktree add', and treat a .factory/ that holds only a .git pointer to this repository's own .factory worktree admin directory as an interrupted mount to finish (or remove and redo), not as foreign content. Add a test that injects a failure after each step of init and checks that a second run ends ready with the exclusions.

outcome.what_was_done: Restart-proofed init: ensure_excludes runs before the mount and on the ready path (a run killed between mount and exclusions finishes on the next run); mount_state runs 'git worktree prune' and clears a .factory that holds only the worktree's own .git pointer, so a worktree add killed halfway neither wedges the next run nor needs the person to move anything. Tests: exclusion step killed (the second init writes what the first skipped), worktree add killed with the directory moved aside, interrupted pointer accepted, plus mount-level tests for the prune and the pointer cleanup.

problem: Decision 3 and the module docstring say the first commit lands with 'update-ref with an empty old value'; the code runs 'git update-ref refs/heads/factory-artifacts <commit>' with no old value. Two inits that both saw no branch (two sessions running setup) end with the second silently replacing the first's state branch under its mounted worktree; reproduced by calling _create_branch twice: the ref moved, no error.
proposed_resolution: Pass the empty old value: git update-ref refs/heads/factory-artifacts <commit> "". On failure, re-read the branch and continue with the mount path. Test that _create_branch raises when the branch already exists.

outcome.what_was_done: Two tests added beside the existing one. test_create_branch_twice_keeps_the_first_commit calls _create_branch directly on one repository: True, then False with the branch tip unchanged - removing the empty old value from update-ref fails it (verified). test_init_losing_a_concurrent_create_mounts_the_winner reaches init's losing path by wrapping _create_branch to return False after the real create, so init mounts what it finds and reports created=False; without it the losing branch of _run was dead code in every test.

problem: The non-empty-.factory/ refusal is checked only when the condition is 'unmounted'. With a non-empty .factory/ that holds no state and no state branch (condition 'none'), init creates the state branch, then crashes in 'git worktree add' with 'internal error: GitError ... already exists' (exit 2 as a crash, not a refusal), leaving a new factory-artifacts branch in the person's repository (reproduced). Plan 3.6 lists a non-empty unmounted .factory/ as an exit-2 refusal, which must come before anything is written.
proposed_resolution: Check for a non-empty .factory/ before _branch_tip/_create_branch for both 'none' and 'unmounted', and Refuse there. Add a test that the refusal leaves no branch behind.

outcome.what_was_done: The non-empty .factory with no state in it is refused up front for both the none and unmounted conditions, before any branch is created; only an interrupted mount's bare .git pointer passes. A refusal can no longer leave a freshly created state branch behind, and the crash path through worktree add is gone. Test: planting junk under .factory for both conditions, asserting exit 2, the move-it-aside message and no factory-artifacts ref afterwards.

problem: An unmounted pre-1.0 state branch (factory-artifacts holding STATE.md, no .factory/) is mounted: init returns {state: legacy, mounted: true, next: []}, exit 1 (reproduced). Plan decision 3 says an unmounted legacy branch is refused, and 3.6 says legacy is 'nothing converted or mounted' with next holding the dry-run and import commands. The setup skill then has no import commands to show. test_init_legacy_converts_nothing covers only a plain .factory/STATE.md directory.
proposed_resolution: When the branch holds STATE.md and no factory.toml, return state legacy, mounted false, next [the dry-run command, the import command], without mounting. Add the unmounted-legacy-branch case to test_init_legacy_converts_nothing.

outcome.what_was_done: An unmounted legacy branch (STATE.md, no factory.toml on factory-artifacts) is reported, not mounted: init returns state legacy, mounted false and next holding 'vsdd import --dry-run' and 'vsdd import'. Test builds the legacy branch on the state branch name and asserts nothing is mounted and the import commands are in next.

problem: Plan 3.6 promises 'Exit 1 with state ... partial (next names /vsdd-factory:status --fix)'. The code raises Refuse (exit 2, no fields, data == {} on stdout under --json), and the test pins the exit-2 form. The builder did not report this departure. Decision 3's word 'refused' is in tension with 3.6, but 3.6 is the interface the setup skill reads (state, next).
proposed_resolution: Return the init fields with state 'partial', created/mounted false and next ['/vsdd-factory:status --fix'], exit 1; update test_init_partial_refuses. If exit 2 is preferred, record the departure and fix plan 3.6 and the setup skill's expectations instead.

outcome.what_was_done: A partial project now exits 1 with the init fields (state partial, mounted false) and next naming /vsdd-factory:status --fix, per plan 3.6, instead of exiting 2 with no fields. test_init_partial_refuses updated to pin exit 1, the state field and the next steps.

problem: Two crashes exit 1, which launch.sh passes through silently as the negative answer (decision 1: a crash never exits 1). Path.cwd() runs before the try, so any vsdd call, even 'vsdd -C <dir> ...', from a deleted directory (a removed story worktree) dies with a FileNotFoundError traceback, exit 1 (reproduced). The --version branch is also outside the try, and _plugin_version raises Refuse uncaught on an unreadable manifest: traceback, exit 1 (reproduced on a scratch copy). cli.py guards only the import; its old plugin_version(), which exited 2 for the damaged manifest, is now dead code duplicating dispatch._plugin_version.
proposed_resolution: In cli.main wrap the dispatch.main call in the same BaseException guard as the import (re-raise SystemExit, else 'vsdd: <type>: <text>' and exit 2). In dispatch.main move the cwd lookup after -C parsing and inside the try (use os.environ PWD or refuse when cwd is gone and no -C is given), and handle --version inside the try. Delete cli.plugin_version. Test both cases through cli.py.

outcome.what_was_done: cli.main guards the dispatch.main call the way the import is guarded: SystemExit re-raised, everything else printed as 'vsdd: <type>: <text>' with exit 2. In dispatch.main the start directory is looked up lazily inside the try (an absolute -C works from a deleted working directory; a bare call from one exits 2 with a message instead of a traceback), and the --version branch sits inside the try, so an unreadable manifest is a caught Refuse exiting 2. cli.plugin_version deleted as dead code. Tests: deleted-working-directory runs, --version with a broken manifest, and the launcher test still passes.

problem: json_requested is set only after _resolve succeeds, so every refusal raised during resolution (no matching command, a cmd_ module that fails to import, duplicate words) prints nothing on stdout under --json; 'vsdd nonesuch --json' gives exit 2 and an empty stdout (reproduced). Plan 3.1 says a Refuse with --json also prints {"ok": false, "error": ...} on stdout. A relayed command whose module breaks (survey, checkpoint) gives the clerk no object at all, which is the case decision 1 exists to prevent.
proposed_resolution: Read --json from the raw tokens (before the first lone --) before calling _resolve, so _fail prints at least {"ok": false, "error": message}. Extend test_unknown_command_exits_2 and test_broken_command_module_is_loud to assert the JSON line.

outcome.what_was_done: json_requested is read from the raw tokens (after the -C strip) before _resolve, so an unknown command, a broken cmd_ module, a broken package or duplicate words all print one {"ok": false, ...} object on stdout under --json. Tests: the unknown-command and broken-module cases now assert the JSON line, and a new broken-package case asserts it too.

problem: check_paths skips any file it cannot read or decode, with no Problem. 'vsdd validate .factory/stories/E-9/S-9.99.md' for a file that does not exist exits 0 with checked 1 (reproduced); an invalid-UTF-8 file under .factory/stories/ passes a whole-tree validate with exit 0 (reproduced); a directory given as PATH also passes. Flush (records.md) leaves out only files with an error Problem, so it would commit such a file unchecked. A silent pass of the backstop check.
proposed_resolution: For a path in the artifact territory that cannot be read or decoded, report an error Problem (frontmatter_invalid naming the read error, or a dedicated code added to the rules list); for an explicit validate PATH that does not exist or is not a file, Refuse. Add tests for the missing path, the undecodable file and the flush call form.

outcome.what_was_done: check_paths reports an error Problem with code 'unreadable' for a file in the artifact territory that cannot be read or decoded, instead of skipping it. cmd_validate refuses an explicit PATH that does not exist or is not a file. Tests: an invalid-UTF-8 story surfaces as an unreadable error and validate exits 1; a missing explicit path exits 2 naming the file.

problem: changed_paths returns wrong paths. path.strip().lstrip("./") strips characters, not a prefix, so the state branch's own .gitignore comes back as '.factory/gitignore'; and git's C-quoting is not undone, so a name with a space or a non-ASCII letter comes back as '.factory/"stories/E-9/S-9.02 copy.md"' or '.factory/"stories/E-9/caf\303\251.md"' (all reproduced). Flush (records) checks and commits from this list; check_paths then cannot read these paths and (finding S3R-state-core-9) passes them silently. test_changed_paths only checks endswith on two plain names.
proposed_resolution: Use git status --porcelain=v1 -z -uall, split on NUL, take the second path of a rename record, and prefix '.factory/' without stripping. Test with a dotfile, a name with a space and a non-ASCII name.

outcome.what_was_done: changed_paths reads 'git status --porcelain=v1 -z -uall', splits on NUL (never C-quoted), consumes the paired original path of a rename, and prefixes '.factory/' without stripping - so '.gitkeep' is no longer mangled to '.factory/gitignore'-style names and spaces and non-ASCII letters come back whole. Test extends test_changed_paths with a dotfile, a name with a space and a non-ASCII name, asserting the exact paths.

problem: Plan decision 10 says 'Line limits are those of spec topics/artifact-rules.md; an over-long body line is size_cap', and that topic says 'Body lines are at most 1,000 characters'. check_text has no line check: a valid story with one 5,000-character body line gives no problem (reproduced). There is no test, and the builder did not report the omission.
proposed_resolution: Add the body-line check (over 1,000 characters is size_cap, naming the line number) to check_text, with an invalid fixture and a case in test_each_reason_code.

outcome.what_was_done: check_text enforces the 1,000-character body-line limit as a size_cap, naming the line number and its length. New fixture invalid_long_line.md (a 5,047-character body line) and a case in test_each_reason_code asserting the line number is named.

problem: ensure_excludes appends to .git/info/exclude without checking that the file ends in a newline. A person's exclude file ending '*.log' becomes '*.log.factory/' then '.worktrees/' (reproduced): the person's pattern stops working, .factory/ is not excluded, and git status in the product checkout shows both '?? .factory/' and the log files. test_ensure_excludes_is_idempotent starts from git's template, which ends in a newline.
proposed_resolution: Write a newline first when the current content is non-empty and does not end with one; write through a temporary file and os.replace. Add the no-trailing-newline case to the test.

outcome.what_was_done: ensure_excludes writes a newline first when the exclude file lacks its trailing newline, and the rewrite goes through a temporary file with os.replace. Test: an exclude file ending '# one\n*.log' comes out as *.log\n plus the two patterns, with no '*.log.factory/' gluing and no leftover temporary file.

problem: Several tests named in plan section 7 cannot fail for the behaviour they are named after. On a scratch copy, a retry_command returning "", a raw split that drops the lone -- and keeps taking --json after it, and a reversed class precedence all left test_dispatch.py and test_project_paths.py green apart from unrelated cases. test_raw_command_gets_tokens never inspects args.tokens; test_retry_command never calls retry_command; test_path_class_precedence never puts a path in two classes (make_project has src/, so tests/** and src/** do not overlap). Also: test_key_table_parity's second loop asserts key in SPECS[section] for keys taken from SPECS[section]; test_import_loads_no_submodule does not assert that a lookup adds only the owner; test_relayed_failure_prints_whole_object and test_shipped_commands_register_cleanly check key presence, not schema validity, and the plan's 'invalid file' (ConfigError) case is missing.
proposed_resolution: Make the echo command return args.tokens and assert ['story', '--', '--json', 'why']; assert inv.retry_command() equals 'vsdd ' + shlex.join(argv) for an argument needing quotes; add a path that matches both tests and source globs (e.g. src/tests/x.py with tests = ['**/tests/**']); validate the relayed objects with vsdd.schema.validate against the named schema, including a ConfigError case; assert sys.modules after one lookup holds exactly vsdd.state.mount; drop or fix the vacuous loop.

outcome.what_was_done: test_import_loads_no_submodule now reads sys.modules after the first lookup and asserts the vsdd.state.* entries are exactly vsdd.state.gitrun and vsdd.state.mount (the owner plus what it imports) - verified failing by making the facade import every sibling module on the first lookup. test_shipped_commands_register_cleanly validates the whole failure object a relayed command prints - {**empty_of(output), **failure, ok: false, error} - against the shipped schema with vsdd.schema.validate, for every registered command with an output, not merely a key subset of empty_of.

problem: The plan names test_init_mounts_existing_branch '(local and origin)', but only the local branch is tested; the origin path of mount_state (worktree add --track -b from origin/factory-artifacts), which is how every fresh clone gets its state, has no test (it works when tried by hand). test_init_resumes_after_interruption is the same steps as the local case and interrupts nothing, so the kill points of S3R-state-core-2 go unnoticed.
proposed_resolution: Add a clone-from-bare-remote case that asserts state ready, created false and the upstream origin/factory-artifacts. Make the resumption test stop init after the branch exists and before the mount (and after the mount, before the exclusions), then re-run.

outcome.what_was_done: Added the origin mount: a state branch pushed to a bare remote, cloned, and init asserts ready, created false, mounted true and the upstream tracking origin/factory-artifacts. test_init_resumes_after_interruption now really interrupts: mount_state patched to die after the branch exists (branch present, re-run mounts, created false), plus a separate test for the exclusion step dying. The local-mount repetition is gone.

problem: Seven outcomes overclaim. AU-P2-03 and AU-S2-09 are marked fixed though this unit did not change prelude_limits (it predates the unit; only a test was added) and both findings are about facts stated twice in spec files; detection.py now restates the limits (S3R-state-core-1). AU-S2-03 and AU-T2-13 had been found not-fixed for spec text, and that text is unchanged: topics/project-configuration.md still calls both the table and its example 'the one key list', the example still omits the per-rule hook keys, and config/hooks.md says 'three rules' and lists four. AU-T2-15 is defeated for init'd projects (S3R-state-core-1). AU-S2-12: commands/validate.md, S1's own file, still presents two syntaxes with a conflicts pointer. AU-P2-17: the 'not built, and why' list was not copied into topic:command-conventions, and the test passes for any unknown name. P3OPS-11 (left-for-builder) says 'this unit added the report keys', but _COMMAND_KEYS has no lint_report, format_report or scan_report.
proposed_resolution: Record AU-P2-03, AU-S2-09, AU-S2-03, AU-T2-13, AU-T2-15, AU-S2-12 and AU-P2-17 as not-fixed or left-for-builder with what remains, or finish them (S3R-state-core-1; trim project-configuration.md to one key-list claim pointing at SPECS; give validate.md one syntax; copy the not-built list). Correct P3OPS-11's text to say that the report keys are not yet added.

outcome.what_was_done: The overclaiming outcomes in rewrite/findings/outcomes/step3-state-core.json are re-recorded: AU-S2-03 and AU-T2-13 as left-for-builder (the code settlement stands; the duplicated 'one key list' claims in tables/config-keys.toml and topics/project-configuration.md remain for the documentation pass; the config/hooks.md 'three rules' is corrected to four), AU-P2-03 and AU-S2-09 as left-for-builder (prelude_limits predates the unit and was only pinned by a test; the render_config restatement is gone after fixing S3R-state-core-1; the G2/S4/B6/H duplicates remain), AU-T2-15 finished properly (init writes no protected_paths copy; test_editing_release_changelog_moves_protected_paths), AU-S2-12 finished (commands/validate.md now states the one syntax and supersedes packaging.md's row), AU-P2-17 as left-for-builder (code half stands, the not-built command list was not copied into prose), and P3OPS-11's text corrected (the report-format keys were not added; they are P3COV-04's change).

problem: Invocation.start is promised absolute, but a relative -C is stored as given (start = Path(tokens[1])); it is then resolved against the process directory, not against main(cwd=...), and init reports a relative 'root' (reproduced: start 'clone', is_absolute False).
proposed_resolution: start = Path(os.path.abspath(os.path.join(base, tokens[1]))) where base is the cwd argument or the process directory, keeping symlinks unresolved as find_project_root expects.

outcome.what_was_done: A relative -C resolves against the cwd argument when main was given one, else against the process directory, via os.path.abspath - absolute and no symlink resolution. Invocation.start is always absolute and init reports an absolute root. Test: a relative -C of '../rel/proj' from a sibling directory succeeds and an absolute-start echo shows the caller's directory verbatim.

problem: 'vsdd --help' exits 2 with 'vsdd: no command given; try 'vsdd --help'', a hint that points at itself (reproduced). Command.summary and commands() exist 'for --help' (plan 3.1), but nothing prints the command list; the B2 parser that answered --help was removed.
proposed_resolution: Handle a leading --help/-h: print 'vsdd <words>  <summary>' for each entry of commands(), exit 0; keep exit 2 for no command at all.

outcome.what_was_done: A leading --help or -h prints the commands() table with each Command.summary and exits 0. Test asserts the built-in commands and their summaries, and a stub package's command.

problem: commands() accepts a Command whose first word is not its module's family (a ('unlock',) command in cmd_lock.py is listed), while the dispatcher can never resolve it ('no command matches'); an empty words tuple crashes later with IndexError. The lint and --help would show a command that cannot run.
proposed_resolution: In _load_command raise RegistrationError when words is empty or words[0] with '-' as '_' is not the module's family (cmd_<family> or cmd_<family>_<x>).

outcome.what_was_done: commands() and _load_command raise RegistrationError for a Command with empty words or whose first word does not match the module's family (derived from the cmd_<family> stem). Test: a cmd_stray.py registering ('elsewhere',) and a cmd_blank.py with words=() each raise RegistrationError naming the module.

problem: registry() does not check frontmatter type cells or ref: targets when it compiles. A typo'd type ('integr?') or a ref: to a kind with no id and no constant builds cleanly (reproduced); the fault appears later as a RegistryError raised from check_text on every write of that kind, or as a frontmatter_invalid problem blamed on the agent's file for the unknown type. Decision 7 says anything outside the grammar is a RegistryError, and 3.5 says registry() raises naming the row, so test_shipped_registry_compiles_every_row cannot catch a bad cell.
proposed_resolution: Validate each frontmatter cell against the decision-7 grammar and resolve each ref: target (_ref_pattern) in _compile_kind/registry(); test with a patched table.

outcome.what_was_done: The registry validates the decision-7 type grammar (scalars, ref:<kind>, list[...], allowed-value lists, untyped optional keys) at compile time and checks every ref: target resolves to a kind with an id row or a constant pattern after the table is compiled - both RegistryError naming the row, so a bad cell can no longer build cleanly and explode later inside check_text. Test patches the policy table with an unknown type, a dangling ref: target and a bad list-member type, each raising, and a good row compiling.

problem: Plan 3.1: an 'initialised' command outside a project exits 2 'naming the condition and /vsdd-factory:setup'; the message names no condition (a legacy or unmounted project reads 'not an initialised vsdd-factory project'). The stderr label is 'vsdd ' + the candidate tokens, so positional arguments appear as command words ('vsdd path S-9.01: ...') instead of 'vsdd <words>'.
proposed_resolution: Include detect(start) in the refusal (e.g. 'condition legacy: run /vsdd-factory:setup'); label with command.words when the command is resolved.

outcome.what_was_done: The un-initialised refusal names the detected condition ('...not an initialised vsdd-factory project (condition 'none'); run /vsdd-factory:setup'), and once a command is resolved the stderr label uses command.words, so positional arguments no longer appear as command words. Test asserts 'condition' in the message and 'vsdd lab:' (not 'vsdd lab positional:') for a usage error.

problem: caps.waived globs are matched against the '.factory/'-prefixed path, while the spec's only example is relative to the state directory (waived = ["specs/architecture/decisions/ADR-052.md"]). A waiver written as documented never matches and the cap still blocks, with no message saying why.
