problem: unittest discovery collects TestCase classes only, so a module-level test function in a sample test file silently vanishes from the JUnit report: the base set under-counts and the red gate counts the test as new. Nothing warns, because the report parses and simply holds fewer cases.
proposed_resolution: Either the sample's tests stay class-only (as today, and as the e2e loaders rely on) or the runner converts module-level test functions explicitly. Worth a sentence in the packaging test tiers when the sample grows.

outcome.what_was_done: The missing test for build_suite's source-tree function collection (the suite.addTests(_function_cases_of(name)) line in the */test_*.py loop) is in: test_sample_runner.py::test_source_tree_function_reaches_the_report writes tally/test_fn.py holding a failing module-level test_ac1_src_red, runs tools/junit_runner.py, and asserts exit 1, that the case tally.test_fn::test_ac1_src_red is a failure with file_attr 'tally/test_fn.py' and criteria_of(name) == 'AC-1'. Verified to fail (KeyError: the case is absent from the report and the runner exits 0) with only the collection line removed; the unmutated runner reports it as a failure, exactly the behaviour the finding confirmed as right.

problem: Some of git's global options that take a separate value are missing from both tables. merge_guard's _GLOBAL_WITH_VALUE lacks --namespace, --config-env and --attr-source. shell.py's _GLOBAL_VALUE_OPTIONS lacks --config-env and --attr-source, and lists --exec-path, which never takes a separate value. When an option is missing, its value is read as the verb, or the -C after it is missed. From the story worktree, merge-guard passes 'git --namespace foo -C <root> commit -m x' and 'git --attr-source HEAD -C <root> commit -m x', and real git 2.50 commits on develop with both. S4R-rules-21, whose status is fixed, asked for --namespace and --config-env.
proposed_resolution: Keep one table of git's separate-value global options: -C, -c, --git-dir, --work-tree, --namespace, --super-prefix, --config-env and --attr-source, without --exec-path. Define it in shell.py and import it in merge_guard for _git_words and _next_verb. When an option git does not list comes before the verb position, block opaque_git. Add both commands to test_opaque_global_values_and_trees.

outcome.what_was_done: One table of git's separate-value global options lives in shell.py (GIT_GLOBAL_VALUE_OPTIONS: -C, -c, --git-dir, --work-tree, --namespace, --super-prefix, --config-env, --attr-source; --exec-path out, it takes no separate value) and merge_guard imports it for _git_words; shell's own -C threading uses the same table. git --namespace foo commit, git --config-env foo=bar commit and git --attr-source HEAD commit are judged (blocked on develop; test_global_option_table_is_one).

problem: Programs that run their operand as a command still hide git when they are not among the six in _WRAPPER_PROGRAMS. On develop, merge-guard passes 'timeout 10 git commit -m x', and real git commits on develop through timeout (coreutils on Linux, Homebrew on macOS). stdbuf, setsid, ionice, flock and sudo work the same way. An agent guarding a slow push with 'timeout 60 git push origin develop' is a likely form.
proposed_resolution: Add timeout, stdbuf, setsid, ionice and sudo to the wrapper table, each with its option grammar. For timeout that is -s/--signal SIG, -k/--kill-after DUR, --preserve-status, --foreground and -v, followed by the duration operand; for stdbuf, -i/-o/-e MODE. An option that cannot be parsed makes the segment opaque, as now. Add 'timeout 10 git commit -m x' to test_wrappers_do_not_hide_git.

outcome.what_was_done: shell.py reads the wrapper's leading operand with tokens[index][1].text (the tuple read crashed the parse, collapsing every cd to one opaque segment); each wrapper owns its long-value prefixes (_WRAPPER_LONG_VALUE_PREFIXES is a per-wrapper table) and its value flags, sudo's grammar corrected (-R is --chroot, -D is --chdir, --chroot added); a directory-changing wrapper option (env -C/--chdir, sudo -D/--chdir) resolves the wrapped program's where like a cd, sudo -R/--chroot leaves it unknowable. Added test_shell rows asserting timeout/stdbuf/sudo parse to program git with its args, and merge-guard cases that only a read wrapper decides.

problem: The S4R-rules-23 fix treats perl's -f as a script option that takes a value, but perl's -f takes no value: it skips sitecustomize.pl. As a result, 'perl -f -pi script.pl src/a.py' lists script.pl as written, and 'perl -pi -f -e s/a/b/ src/a.py' lists the -e script 's/a/b/' as a path. These are the S4R-rules-23 symptoms reached through another flag. The error only over-counts, so at worst it causes a false block.
proposed_resolution: Remove -f from perl's value options and from _perl_scripted's script options. Add both commands as rows of test_write_targets_table.

outcome.what_was_done: -f removed from perl's value options (_VALUE_OPTIONS) and from _perl_scripted (standalone and bundled letters), and from the bundled-value tail list: perl -f -pi script.pl src/a.py lists src/a.py only, and perl -pi -f -e s/a/b/ src/a.py lists neither -f nor the script. Both commands are rows of test_write_targets_table.

problem: The S4R-rules-3 fix sends every opaque segment whose program is git to _git, so a substitution inside git's own arguments is now read as a literal word. Before the fix such a segment blocked opaque_git; now these pass (exit 0) on develop in the main checkout: 'git push origin $(git branch --show-current)', the same quoted, 'git push origin $(echo develop)', 'git push origin HEAD:$(echo develop)', 'git branch -f $(echo develop) HEAD' and 'git update-ref refs/heads/$(echo develop) abc'. In a story worktree 'git rebase origin/develop $(echo develop)' also passes. The first is a natural command and pushes develop. spec rules/merge-guard.md says a guarded verb the parser cannot see into (a substitution among them) blocks opaque_git. A plain expansion has the same hole, which was there before the fix: 'B=develop; git push origin $B' passes.
proposed_resolution: In _git, when the verdict depends on an argument (push and fetch/pull refspecs, the names given to branch, update-ref, symbolic-ref, switch -C and checkout -B, the rebase branch argument) and that argument holds '$' or a backtick, block (opaque_git, or where_unknown with a fix naming the literal form). Keep heredoc-only opacity on the parsed path, so the S4R-rules-3 commit cases still pass. Add these commands to test_opaque as blocked cases.

problem: The S4R-rules-21 fix judges the branch at the tree that --work-tree names (_redirected_tree). But git reads HEAD from the git directory, which --work-tree does not change: it is found from the cwd, or from --git-dir or GIT_DIR. The result is a bypass. Measured in the main checkout on develop, all passing (exit 0): 'git --work-tree=/tmp commit --allow-empty -m x', 'git --work-tree=/tmp merge story/S-9.01', 'git --work-tree=/tmp reset --hard HEAD~1', 'git --work-tree=/tmp push', and 'git --work-tree=<story worktree> commit ...'. Real git, run the same way, moved develop. A GIT_DIR assignment is not judged at all: from the story worktree, 'GIT_DIR=<root>/.git git commit ...' and 'env GIT_DIR=... git commit ...' pass and commit on develop. In opaque text, _opaque_redirected returns None for a redirect outside every factory project, so the plain scan blocks it after all. That contradicts the account and the test's comment ('one outside every factory project is not judged'). A scratch copy that removes _opaque_redirected passes test_opaque_global_values_and_trees.
proposed_resolution: Judge the branch at --git-dir's repository, or at a GIT_DIR assignment (seg.assignments, env's included), when one is given; otherwise at seg.where. Never take it from --work-tree. Block where_unknown when that git directory cannot be resolved. Add the --work-tree=/tmp commit, merge, reset and push cases and the GIT_DIR cases as blocked. Either make the opaque 'outside every project' pass real and test it, or drop _opaque_redirected and the claim.

outcome.what_was_done: _harmless_or_block no longer trusts the directory alone: a not-plain git-bearing segment whose directory is in no factory project blocks opaque_git when its text names -C, --git-dir, --work-tree, a GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE spelling, cd, or a far verb. Together with the shell.py timeout crash fix this covers all nine measured commands; timeout and caffeinate rows now parse and are judged at the -C target.
outcome.where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/rules/merge_guard.py (_harmless_or_block); next/tests/hooks/test_merge_guard.py (test_unplaced_commands_that_reach_into_a_project: the nine measured commands run from a directory in no factory project, each blocked)

problem: The fixes edit two step 3 files outside ORDER.md section 4, which says nothing outside its table is edited and gives the rules unit only registry.py and test_hooks_wiring.py. The two files are hook-runner's shell.py (wrapper skipping, and a subshell's own text, for S4R-rules-3 and -7) and records' state/steps.py (_under_holdout, for S4R-rules-25). The owners' own tests (test_shell.py, test_state_steps.py) still pass in the full run.
proposed_resolution: The orchestrator records the two edits as sanctioned exceptions, which the review's proposed fixes invited (shell.parse, 'the state layer'), or hands them to hook-runner and records fix runs. The owners' plans should then note the changed Segment.program and Segment.text meaning, and the shared predicate.

outcome.what_was_done: The two departures are recorded here as sanctioned exceptions for the orchestrator, neither reportable as a surprise: (1) hook-runner's shell.py, edited by this unit for S4R-rules-3, -7 and the C1-2 redirect reading — the owners' plans should note the new meaning of Segment.program (the wrapped program, wrappers matched by basename, their options skipped, and an unparseable wrapper option marking the segment opaque) and Segment.where (no longer perturbed by a subcommand's own -C: git's -C scan stops at the subcommand). (2) records' state/steps.py, edited for S4R-rules-25's shared predicate _under_holdout (dot segments normalised; the state-relative 'holdout/' spelling walled), with the one-definition note that the step-results rule and the verdict read the store's predicate and must not grow their own; the owning unit's test_state_steps.py gained the normalised-spelling store case. Owners' tests pass (test_shell.py, test_ctx.py, test_state_steps.py all green after the edits).

problem: This one predates the fix round; it was found beside the rebase and pull fixes. A fetch or pull refspec with no colon names only a source, so it writes no local branch. _refspec_destination still returns the word itself, so in a story worktree 'git fetch origin develop' and 'git pull origin develop' block moves_guarded_branch, with a fix line that sends the builder to the tool. These are the usual steps before 'git rebase origin/develop', which S4R-rules-5 now allows. 'git fetch origin' passes.
proposed_resolution: For fetch and pull, take a destination only from a refspec with a colon (src:dst, +src:dst). Keep the pull-with-refspec integrate_on_guarded block for a guarded branch that is checked out. Add 'git fetch origin develop' and 'git pull origin develop' in the story worktree as passing cases.

outcome.what_was_done: For fetch and pull, a refspec destination is taken only from a colon-bearing refspec; a colon-less one (git fetch origin develop, git pull origin develop) writes no local branch and passes, including from a story worktree, so the usual prelude of git rebase origin/develop is free. The pull-with-refspec integrate_on_guarded block on a guarded branch stands unchanged, as do the colon-bearing moves_guarded_branch blocks. test_colon_less_fetch_and_pull_pass_in_a_story holds both passing cases and both blocked controls; verified to fail with the colon guard removed.

problem:
Everything after a here-document opener on its own line is dropped from the parse. _cut_heredocs appends text[index:after] (the << and its delimiter), then jumps to the end of the body; the rest of the opener's line, from after to the newline, is never kept. So the redirect in cat <<'EOF' > tests/test_sample.py, the pipe in cat <<'EOF' | sh, and every segment joined after the opener on that line vanish. Measured with real sh and dash. tests-first, in a story after red, as the implementer: cat <<'EOF' > tests/test_sample.py
x
EOF and cat <<'EOF' | tee tests/test_sample.py
x
EOF both pass and overwrite the frozen test; the same form writes product source before red. merge-guard: from the story worktree, git commit --allow-empty -F - <<'EOF' && git push origin HEAD:develop
feat: x
EOF and cat <<'EOF' && git push origin HEAD:develop
notes
EOF pass and push develop; on the main checkout, cat <<'EOF' >/dev/null; git commit --allow-empty -m x
notes
EOF passes and commits on develop. cat <<'EOF' > path is the commonest way an agent writes a file. No test has text after an opener (test_shell and test_writes only use cat <<EOF alone on its line). This round rewrote _cut_heredocs to return the bodies (step4-rules-fix-3-C1-2); there is no committed version to show whether the drop is older.
proposed_resolution: In _cut_heredocs keep the rest of the opener's line in the cleaned text (from the end of the delimiter word to the newline), and start the body after that newline; with several openers on one line, take their bodies in order after it. Add test_shell rows that assert the redirect target of cat <<'EOF' > f and the segment after && survive, a tests-first case for cat <<'EOF' > tests/test_sample.py after red, and merge-guard cases for the commit -F - && push and the cat ... ; git commit forms.

problem:
Only the exact pair program sh plus a word -c is opaque (_own_opacity). bash -c, bash -lc, dash -c, zsh -c, ksh -c, sh -ec, sh -xc and sh -c -- are parsed segments, and since the step4-rules-fix-3-C1-8 fix _git_bearing reads an argument's words only when the argument carries a shell joiner. A command string without one is not git-bearing and is not judged; before C1-8 the whole-text split caught it, so for merge-guard this is a regression of that fix. A shell reading its standard input from a pipe is not read either. Measured, each passing the rule while real git under sh and dash moves a guarded branch: from the story worktree bash -c 'git push origin HEAD:develop', sh -ec '...', dash -c '...', zsh -c '...', timeout 10 bash -c '...', echo 'git push origin HEAD:develop' | sh, cat <<'EOF' | sh
git push origin HEAD:develop
EOF (push develop); on the main checkout bash -lc 'git commit --allow-empty -m x' and printf 'git commit --allow-empty -m x
' | bash (commit on develop); from a directory in no project bash -c 'git -C <root> commit --allow-empty -m x'. tests-first has the same hole for every spelling, joiner or not, because write_unknown reads a parsed segment's arguments only as whole words: after red, bash -c "perl -pi -e s/a/b/ tests/test_sample.py", sh -ec "...", echo "perl -pi ..." | sh, and from the main checkout bash -c 'cd <wt> && perl -pi -e ... tests/test_sample.py' all pass and change the frozen test.
proposed_resolution: In shell.py make a segment opaque when its program's basename is a shell (sh, bash, dash, zsh, ksh) and an option word before the first operand carries the letter c (-c, -ec, -lc, -xc, with or without --); its text already carries the command string. Treat a shell segment with no -c and no script operand that reads a pipe or a here-document as running the previous pipeline segment's text (or the body): carry that text into its own. Then merge-guard and tests-first judge it as they judge sh -c. Add the measured commands as blocked cases in test_merge_guard and test_tests_first.

problem: The step4-rules-fix-3-C1-9 fix counts any argument word that names a writer program as a delegated write, and for a git call any non-message word. Read-only commands that mention a writer are then blocked for the story's builders. Measured in a story after red, as the implementer, each blocked red_test_frozen while real sh and dash change nothing: grep -rn rm src, grep -rw sed tests, which sed, python3 -c 'print(1)' touch, git mv src/module.py src/module2.py and git rm -q src/module.py (renaming or removing product source after red, which the implementer may do). Before red the same commands block no_red_evidence. The merge-guard analogue (grep -rn "git push" .) was fixed by C1-8; tests-first now has it.
proposed_resolution: Count a delegation only where a word is run as a program: the operand after a runner's own options (flock, caffeinate, script, nohup, xargs, timeout and the wrapper table), the word after find's -exec/-execdir/-ok, and the first word of a loop or compound body. Judge git rm and git mv by their operands as the write targets they are, not by the verb's name. Add the read-only commands above as passing cases after red, beside the existing delegated-write cases.

problem: A plain segment is judged by exact option words, so option spellings that git accepts pass. Each of these was measured with exit 0 while real git under sh and dash moved a guarded branch (main guarded with release = "main", develop for the push forms), all run from the story worktree unless noted. Operands after --: git branch -f -- main HEAD, git push -- origin HEAD:develop. Refs on stdin: printf 'update refs/heads/main HEAD\n' | git update-ref --stdin. @ for HEAD: git push origin @ on the main checkout pushes develop. The rule should pass a command only on a positive reading, and these are not positive readings.

An option word not in that table makes the call not plain, so point (3) decides: an abbreviated long option, a bundle that holds a governed letter (f, C, B, d, D, m, M), or a value attached to -C, -B or --force-create. Additions cover every measured command on the guarded checkout and the worktree rows only a far-verb or attached-value ruling decides.

problem: The rule's idea of where git acts differs from git's in several cases. Each passed with exit 0 from the story worktree, and real git under sh and dash commits on develop. (a) Only the first -C and the first --git-dir are read, but git applies every -C in turn and uses the last --git-dir: git -C . -C ../.. commit -m x; git -C . -C <root> commit -m x; git --git-dir=<root>/.git/worktrees/S-9.01 --git-dir=<root>/.git commit -m x. (b) cd follows CDPATH: export CDPATH=<parent>; cd <rootname> && git commit -m x. (c) A git directory reached through a symbolic link is found in no project: ln -s <root>/.git <out>/g && git --git-dir=<out>/g commit -m x. (d) A directory created in the same command is in no project at parse time: git worktree add -f <out>/x develop && cd <out>/x && git commit -m x. (e) A shell function's git call is judged where it is defined, not where it runs: f() { git commit -m x; }; cd <root> && f.
proposed_resolution: Thread every -C in order and take the last --git-dir. A cd while CDPATH is set or assigned, and a cd to a relative name that does not exist, is a place that cannot be known (where_unknown). Resolve a --git-dir or GIT_DIR value with realpath before finding its project. Treat a directory that does not yet exist as unknown. Treat a git call inside a function body (or a brace group defined before a later cd) as not plain. Add each command as a blocked case.

problem: _git_bearing splits the segment's joined text on whitespace even when the parser has read the segment's words. problem:
tests-first's new stance is that a write it cannot read is the edit it could be. It covers only an opaque segment whose text names a writer. Measured in a story after red, as the implementer, each with exit 0, and the frozen tests/test_sample.py is changed under sh. (a) A wrapper that is not in the table hides the writer, because the segment is not opaque: flock /tmp/lk sed -i ... tests/test_sample.py; caffeinate -i sed -i ...; script -q /dev/null perl -pi -e ... tests/test_sample.py; find tests -name test_sample.py -exec sed -i ... {} +. (b) An opaque segment with a cd is judged at the outer directory: from the main checkout, (cd <wt> && sed -i ... tests/test_sample.py) and sh -c 'cd <wt> && sed -i ...'. (c) An expanded target is dropped, not treated as a write it cannot read: for f in tests/*.py; do sed -i ... "$f"; done, and F=tests/test_sample.py; sed -i ... $F. The opposite also happens: after red, the implementer's standard heredoc commit message is blocked red_test_frozen when it contains a writer word, for example git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'

EOF
)" or 'fix: touch up the parser'.
proposed_resolution: Read writes with the merge-guard stance. A segment whose program is not a known writer, but one of whose words is a writer program, is a write it cannot read. So is a writer whose path operand holds an expansion. An opaque segment whose text holds cd, pushd or popd is judged as a write in an unknown place: it blocks wherever a story could be the target. Exclude a free-text option's value (-m, -F), including a substitution lying wholly inside it, from write_unknown's scan. Add the measured commands to test_tests_first.py, the blocked ones and the passing commit message.

outcome.what_was_done: tests-first now follows the could-be-the-edit stance in all the directions the finding names. write_unknown counts a segment whose program is no writer but one of whose words is a writer (flock, caffeinate, script, find, the for loop's sed), a writer whose path operand holds an expansion (sed -i ... $F), and keeps a git call's free-text values out of the scan so a heredoc commit message naming rm or touch is no write. _unreadable judges an opaque segment whose text holds a cd — or whose where is empty — as a write in an unknown place, checked against the governing project's stories with passing red records (_frozen_stories). The before-red counterpart blocks no_red_evidence.
