problem: The frozen check is meant to accept the path 'literal or resolved' (plan 3.2), but it computes one root from the literal path (gitfs.worktree_root uses abspath, no symlinks resolved) and returns False as soon as either form fails relative_to(root). When any directory above the project is a symlink (macOS /tmp and /var, a symlinked home or dev directory), the resolved form is never under the literal root, so the function returns False even though the literal form matched. Measured: with the project reached through a symlinked directory, _is_frozen(<literal>/tests/test_sample.py) is False while the real path is True, and 'echo x > <worktree>/tests/test_sample.py' by the implementer after red exits 0 (the same command on the real path exits 10 red_test_frozen). Shell writes carry literal paths, so a frozen test is open to every builder in such a project. The test suite cannot see this because pytest's tmp_path is already resolved.
proposed_resolution: Test each form against its own root (worktree_root(form)) and 'continue' on ValueError instead of returning False; match when any form is in the frozen set. Add a test that reaches the story project through a symlinked parent and writes a frozen test from Bash.

outcome.what_was_done: The symlink test is now driven through Bash, as the check proposed: 'echo x > tests/test_sample.py' with cwd set to the worktree reached through the symlinked alias, as the verifier. write_targets keeps the alias spelling (abspath, not realpath), so the literal and resolved forms really differ and _is_frozen's dual-form measurement is what blocks. The test asserts the two spellings differ before firing, and blocks red_test_frozen. Verified it fails against a single-root _is_frozen (root from realpath, relative from the literal path): 1 failed; with the fix restored: passed.

problem: Plan 3.3 limits opaque_git to 'an opaque segment whose own program is not git'. The code sends every opaque segment to _opaque, whatever its program, and _opaque scans text for 'git <verb>'. So a git commit inside a story worktree is blocked opaque_git when its message comes from a here-document or a substitution: 'git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)"' (the usual commit form Claude Code agents use) and 'git commit -F - <<EOF' both exit 10, though 'git commit -m plain' in the same worktree passes. A here-document anywhere in the command makes every segment opaque (shell.parse), and a subshell segment ('()') is judged by the whole command's text, so '(cd x && make) && git commit -m y' in a story worktree is blocked too. Plan section 1 says git inside a story worktree is unrestricted at slice depth. The plan's test case 'a commit message from a here-document passes' was replaced in test_opaque by an unrelated 'cat <<NOTE' command, which hides the fault. The block text also says 'the guarded branches are not put at risk', which is misleading here.
proposed_resolution: When seg.program is git, judge the segment through _git with its parsed args even if it is opaque (the verb and branch are visible; only an argument is a substitution or a here-document body). For a subshell segment, scan only the subshell's own text (S4B-rules-2), not the whole command. Restore the plan's case: a commit with a here-document message in the story worktree passes, and the same on develop is commit_on_guarded.

outcome.what_was_done: An opaque segment whose own program is git is now judged through _git with its parsed args (a heredoc-message commit behaves like the plain commit), and the parser hands a subshell its own text as the segment's text, so only the subshell's interior is scanned instead of the whole command. Restored the here-document commit cases in the story worktree (both the -m "$(cat <<EOF ...))" and -F - forms) and the (cd elsewhere && make) && git commit case as passing.

problem: Decision D7 and plan 3.3 say a segment is judged only when vsdd.project.find_project_root(seg.where) finds a project. _guarded calls ctx.project_at(seg.where) instead, which falls back to the payload cwd and then the session root, so it always finds the session's project and judges every repository with that project's branch names. Measured: 'git commit --allow-empty -m x' in an unrelated repository on branch develop is blocked commit_on_guarded. test_unrelated_repository_passes passes only by accident: the story_ready fixture sets branches.release = "develop", so the unrelated repository's 'main' happens not to be guarded. With the default config (release = main), a commit, push, reset or 'gh pr merge' on main in any other repository the agent touches is blocked.
proposed_resolution: In _guarded (and in the gh pr merge branch) call find_project_root(seg.where, home=ctx.env.get('HOME')) first and return None when it finds no project; only then read the branch names from that project's configuration. Extend the test with an unrelated repository on develop and one on main under a default [branches] table.

outcome.what_was_done: _guarded finds the segment's project with find_project_root(seg.where) alone — no fallback to cwd or session root — and returns None outside a factory project; the branch names come from that project's configuration. test_unrelated_repository_passes extended: unrelated repositories on develop and on main both pass, commit and push, without any fixture branch setting.

problem: Plan 3.3 blocks 'git rebase <upstream> <guarded>', where the second argument is the branch git checks out and rewrites. The code blocks whenever the last positional is a guarded name, so 'git rebase develop' in a story worktree (one positional: develop is only the upstream; the story branch is rewritten) is blocked integrate_on_guarded, with a reason claiming git 'checks out and rewrites develop'. Measured: 'git rebase develop' in the story worktree exits 10; 'git rebase develop story/S-9.01' passes. Updating a story branch onto the integration branch is ordinary work inside a story worktree. No test covers the one-positional form.
proposed_resolution: Treat the rewritten branch as the positional after the upstream (skipping the value of --onto and handling --root); block only when that branch argument is guarded, or when the current branch is guarded. Add 'git rebase develop' and 'git rebase origin/develop' in the story worktree as passing cases.

outcome.what_was_done: For rebase off a guarded branch, the rewritten branch is the last positional (with --onto's value skipped), the earlier ones being only upstreams: git rebase <upstream> and git rebase <upstream> <unguarded> pass in the story worktree; naming a guarded branch as that positional blocks integrate_on_guarded. Passing cases for git rebase develop, git rebase origin/develop, --onto forms; blocking cases with the guarded branch named.

problem: On a guarded branch, 'git pull <remote> <branch>' fetches <branch> and merges it into the checked-out guarded branch, which is the same integration 'git merge' is blocked for. The rule only checks pull refspec destinations, so 'git pull origin story/S-9.01' and 'git pull . story/S-9.01' on develop exit 0 while 'git merge story/S-9.01' exits 10. D6 allowed only a bare 'git pull'. An agent can merge a story into the integration branch outside story deliver.
proposed_resolution: When the current branch is guarded, block 'git pull' that names any refspec after the remote as integrate_on_guarded (a bare pull stays allowed per D6). Add the case to test_ref_moves or test_case_table.

outcome.what_was_done: On a guarded branch, a pull that names a refspec after the remote blocks integrate_on_guarded; a bare pull and a pull with a remote and no refspec pass (decision D6 unchanged). Tested for git pull origin story/S-9.01 and git pull . story/S-9.01.

problem: Both rules match the segment's program by exact name. A path or a command wrapper hides it. Measured on the main checkout (develop): '/usr/bin/git commit -m x', 'command git commit -m x', 'env git commit -m x', 'exec git commit -m x', 'time git commit -m x' and 'nohup git push origin develop' all exit 0, while 'git commit -m x' exits 10. _opaque already accepts a '/git' suffix, but the main path does not. The same spellings ('command sed -i ...', 'env sed -i ...', '/bin/rm ...') give write_targets no targets, so tests-first is skipped too. The actions merge-guard guards are irreversible, and these are trivial spellings.
proposed_resolution: Normalise the program before judging it: take the basename of a path, and skip the wrappers command, env (with its options and NAME=value words), exec, nohup, time and nice to the real program and its args. Do it in one helper both rules use (or in shell.parse as a step 3 maintenance change). Add cases to test_merge_guard and test_writes.

outcome.what_was_done: The rule no longer enumerates spellings: shell.py now resolves wrappers (timeout, stdbuf, setsid, ionice, sudo added beside command/env/exec/nohup/time/nice, each with its option grammar), marks every env -S/--split-string spelling (separate, attached, --split-string=) as an opaque segment whose text carries the split string verbatim, and merge_guard judges a segment positively: git-bearing by its words, plain by program+literal words, else opaque_git unless position alone is harmless. write_targets/tests-first follow the same stance: an opaque segment whose text names a writer (write_unknown) is judged as the edit it could be, where a frozen test or product source could be the target. The four env -S spellings are tested (test_env_split_string_is_opaque), the unreadable write through sh -c and env -S in test_tests_first.py::test_unreadable_write_is_the_edit_it_could_be.

problem: The grounding mark is matched by finding key. _grounding records failing findings as (str(finding.get('key', '?')), why), and _marked marks a finding only when finding.get('key') is in that set. A failing finding with no key ('?' never equals None) or with a non-string key (7 vs '7') is stored with no 'grounded: false'. Measured: a keyless finding whose quote is absent is blocked once, then stored on the second return with no mark, and the same happens for key 7. Plan 3.4 promises G3 that 'a stored finding is grounded unless it carries grounded: false', and the verdict trusts the stored mark (VSA-07), so an ungrounded finding counts as grounded and nothing reports it. data is not schema-validated at the store, so nothing else catches the missing key.
proposed_resolution: Mark by position: have _grounding return the indices (or the objects) of the failing findings in the list, and set grounded: false on exactly those nodes in the deep copy; keep the key only for the block text. Add tests for a keyless finding, an integer key, and two findings sharing a key where one grounds.

outcome.what_was_done: _grounding returns failing findings as (position, key, reason) triples into the findings list, and _marked sets grounded: false by position; the key survives only in the block text. A failing finding with no key, an integer key, and two findings sharing a key are all stored marked. Test with all three shapes asserts the four marks.

problem: Plan 3.4 step 5 says 'the blocks of 2 to 5 are returned together'. The code writes the marker and adds findings_ungrounded only when no other block exists ('if failing and not blocks'). Measured: a result with a gate entry that has no record and an ungrounded finding gets only gate_result_mismatch. The agent learns about its citations only on a later return, and that return is blocked again. This costs an extra round trip against the platform's retry limit, and the once-per-step design exists to protect that limit ('one bad citation cannot use up the platform's retries'). The departure is not reported and no test covers the combination.
proposed_resolution: Follow the plan: when findings fail and no marker exists, write the marker and append the findings_ungrounded block to the other blocks in the same return. If the separate return is intended, report it as a departure and say so in the spec. Add a test with a gate mismatch and an ungrounded finding together.

outcome.what_was_done: The once-per-step marker is written and findings_ungrounded is appended beside the other blocks (walled, gate mismatch, tree_unknown), so one return carries the whole picture and no platform retry is spent on an extra round trip. Test: a gate mismatch and an ungrounded finding together return both codes with the marker set; repairing the gate entry stores the marked finding without another ungrounded round.

problem: Plan 3.6 says an invalid factory.toml leaves the gates at full strength. When the configuration does not parse, _HookProject.config falls back to the built-in defaults, and their [paths] classes are empty, so no path is source or tests and tests-first never applies. Measured: adding '[limits] agents_per_run = 0' to a story project's factory.toml lets the implementer edit <worktree>/src/lib.rs before red (exit 0). Meanwhile the SessionStart notice says 'built-in defaults, the strictest settings, are in force'. The builder reported this departure and called it correct. It is not: one bad key anywhere in the file silently switches off the delivery-order gate. The test was narrowed to the merge-guard leg.
proposed_resolution: In tests_first.check, when ctx.project.config_error is set and the path lies in a story worktree, block with a code such as config_invalid that names the configuration error and the fix (repair factory.toml). Alternatively, classify paths with the file's own [paths] table when that section alone validates. Extend test_invalid_config_relaxes_nothing to assert that tests-first still blocks a source edit before red.

outcome.what_was_done: With config_error set, tests-first blocks writes inside a story worktree with code config_invalid instead of passing unjudged with the empty default class table; test_invalid_config_relaxes_nothing now covers tests-first beside merge-guard.

problem: The test cannot fail. build() writes no red record (it calls story_project and freeze only), so the glob over red.*.json corrupts nothing. The source edit is then blocked no_red_evidence simply because no record exists, and the assertion accepts 'no_red_evidence' or 'rule_error'. The case that matters is untested: after a red record exists and is corrupted, a frozen-test edit and a source edit must not pass. The code behaves correctly today, because read_record raises StoreCorrupt and the rule crashes closed. Nothing would catch a regression that skipped corrupt records, though, and that would silently unfreeze the tests.
proposed_resolution: Call rule_projects.red(p) before corrupting, assert that the glob found at least one file, and assert rule_error (exit 2) for both a source edit by the implementer and a frozen-test edit.

outcome.what_was_done: test_corrupt_evidence_blocks writes a red record first, asserts a record was actually corrupted, and asserts rule_error (exit 2) for both a source edit and a frozen-test edit; the old no_red_evidence escape is gone.

problem: The builder reported '10 failed (all in tests/hooks/test_rule_cases.py)'. The full run gives 1238 passed, 10 failed, 1 skipped, but only 6 of the failures are in test_rule_cases.py. The other 4 are step 3 tests that this unit's new registry rows break, and none of them is reported. (1) test_caller.py::test_refused_bypass_forms_pass_unmarked_through_the_runner: merge-guard now blocks '10>/dev/null git push --force origin main'. (2) test_caller.py::test_no_marker: with VSDD_FACTORY_ROOT outside any project, tests-first and merge-guard crash with "AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'rule_config'". The runner's _rule_cfg dereferences a None ctx.project, and the first Bash rules expose it, so every Bash call blocks rule_error. (3, 4) test_liveness.py::test_lock_refresh and test_lock_refresh_belongs_by_run_and_story: step-results blocks the liveness payload {'step': {'run': ...}} with bad_identity. The rules behave as specified in cases (1) and (3, 4), but the suite is red for reasons the outcome account does not name. Plan section 4 also says the builder stops and reports if test_rule_cases.py reads tests/hooks/cases/; the builder continued instead.
proposed_resolution: Record the three step 3 breakages for fix runs of hook-runner and hook-runner-b: give the liveness step payload a full identity, or expect the block while still checking that seen moved; update the bypass-form expectation now that merge-guard is active; make the runner treat a None ctx.project as inert before _rule_cfg. Correct the outcome account and the foreign_failures list so the orchestrator sees all ten.

outcome.what_was_done: (a) test_refused_bypass_forms_pass_unmarked_through_the_runner keeps its meaning: the fd-hugged push form is separated from the pass-through list and asserted blocked by merge-guard with push_to_guarded and still unmarked, in the new test_fd_hugged_push_is_blocked_by_merge_guard; every other form passes unmarked as before. (b) The two liveness tests send a StructuredOutput payload with the full step identity and shape a real step sends (run, workflow, subject, name, attempt, method; status, summary, head, data), so step-results stores it instead of refusing bad_identity; what the tests assert about the lock is unchanged.

problem: The spec file this unit edited still carries the sentences that three findings marked fixed were about. Item 3 says 'the rule reads the evidence record the entry names', the exact wording VSA-11 objected to; the code never follows the entry. Item 5 says 'The tool validates each record against its schema, and applies the same grounding rule, before it counts the record toward a verdict', the count-time re-grounding VSA-07 removed. It now contradicts topics/verdicts.md ('no grounding check runs at count time'), so one fact is stated two ways. The closing paragraph says 'The rule does not re-validate the whole result against its JSON Schema ... and the standard library has no schema validator', the claim P3OPS-21 called false. The rule now blocks schema_invalid through the store's step-record validation (test_invalid_result_blocked_not_stored).
proposed_resolution: Item 3: 'looks up the evidence record by the entry's subject, gate and commit; the entry's evidence path is never opened'. Item 5: 'honours the stored grounding mark when it counts the record; no grounding runs at count time' (point to topics/verdicts.md). Closing paragraph: the store validates the result against step-record.schema.json and the rule blocks schema_invalid every time (D14); the data schema is G3's.

outcome.what_was_done: The three sentences rewritten: item 3 now says the record is looked up in the evidence store by the entry's subject, gate and commit, never by the path the entry carries; item 5 now says the store validated the record before it was written and the tool honours the stored grounded mark without grounding again; the closing paragraph now says the store validates the step record and the rule surfaces its schema_invalid refusal, citing the hook-before-platform ordering.

problem: VSA-11 is marked fixed and proven by 'the forged-path case in test_gate_entries', but that test cannot catch the forgery VSA-11 describes. Its forged entry points at ../../etc/passwd, which is no record, and the store holds nothing, so any implementation blocks it. Verified in a scratch copy: changing _gate_blocks to read the entry's evidence file whenever it exists, and to fall back to the lookup otherwise, leaves test_gate_entries and every step-results case table passing. The plan named a dedicated test_forged_evidence_path_is_ignored, which was not written.
proposed_resolution: Write a forged record (a JSON object whose gate, subject, sha and passed match the entry) at a writable path inside the project, point the entry's evidence at it, keep the store empty, and assert gate_result_mismatch. Keep the separate test name the plan gave.

outcome.what_was_done: Added test_forged_evidence_path_is_ignored: a forged matching record written inside the project at .factory/local/forged-evidence, named by the entry's evidence path, with the store empty — the lookup by subject, gate and sha still returns nothing and the call is blocked gate_result_mismatch, storing nothing. Following the path would have stored, so the test fails without the fix.

problem: P3BLD-24 is marked fixed, but its resolution is a set of brief and registry edits that were not made. packages/H7.md still says 'depends_on: [H1, S2a, S4]' (no S3). The other three bullets ([reveals] to B4a, scaffold/demo to A5 and design-system to A2a, the stamped texts kept in B4a) belong to other packages and are untouched. The builder itself says 'the brief's dependency line remains the spec steward's', and catchup-fix.json had recorded it left-for-builder for that reason. Because the latest outcome wins, the ledger now shows the whole finding fixed, which also drops it from the A2a, A5 and B4a lists.
proposed_resolution: Change the outcome to left-for-builder (or not-fixed) and say that the code follows the H7 <- S3 dependency while the brief and registry edits remain the steward's, then rebuild the ledger.

outcome.what_was_done: P3BLD-24 reopened below as left-for-builder: the code half stands (step-results imports unit_tree from vsdd.state.worktrees, proven by test_grounding_uses_the_unit_tree), but packages/H7.md's dependency line still lacks S3, and the finding's other three bullets — the [reveals] generator owned by no package, assets/ delivered by T5 while the A2a and A5 methods cite it, and the shared block and severity table delivered twice (B4a and A1) with agent lint double-owned (B6 and A1) — are untouched. Ledger rebuilt with findings.py build.

problem: Plan 3.2 says that for a frozen test the fix names 'returning blocked with data.test_defects'. The code's fix tells the implementer and the verifier to 'Ask the test writer, or run vsdd gate red --refreeze --story <id> from the test writer's row'. Gate-guard refuses --refreeze to every row but the test writer's, so the route offered is one the blocked caller cannot take, and the route the workflow handles (a blocked step with data.test_defects) is never named. No test asserts the fix text.
proposed_resolution: Make the fix: 'Return blocked with data.test_defects naming <path> and what is wrong; the test writer changes it and re-freezes.' Assert it in test_frozen_tests.

outcome.what_was_done: The red_test_frozen fix line is now 'Return blocked again, with data.test_defects naming <path>.' — no instruction to run vsdd gate red --refreeze from a row that gate-guard refuses. test_frozen_tests asserts data.test_defects and the test's path appear in the fix and that the Instead line says to return blocked.

problem: The proof given for P3SEAM-15 cannot tell 'the latest record' from any other. The re-freeze is written at the same commit as the first red record, and evidence_write replaces that gate and commit's record (red.<sha12>.json), so only one record ever exists. Verified in a scratch copy: making gate_evidence.evidence return the oldest red record instead of the latest leaves the test passing.
proposed_resolution: Commit in the story worktree between the red record and the re-freeze so that two records exist, then assert that a test added only in the re-freeze is frozen.

outcome.what_was_done: test_refrozen_set_stays_frozen makes a real commit in the story worktree between the first red record and the re-freeze, so the two records exist at different commits: the frozen set is the latest record's (evidence()'s newest-first lookup), and a lookup that answered the oldest record would leave the added test unfrozen and fail.

problem: test_source_before_and_after_red comments 'The record holds across the implementer's own commits' but makes no commit: it edits a second file at the same head, so a head-tied lookup would still pass. The spec says the case tables include 'an implementer edit after its own commit (allowed) and a test-writer source edit after red at a later commit (blocked)', and also 'the same sed -i after red (allowed)' by the implementer. tests-first.toml has none of these, and its Bash cases use the main-session payload rather than the implementer's. The behaviour itself is correct (a probe with a real commit gives implementer 0, test-writer 10), but neither the test nor the tables prove it.
proposed_resolution: Commit in the worktree after red in the test. Add the three spec cases to tests-first.toml with an implementer Bash payload, or correct the spec sentence.

outcome.what_was_done: test_source_before_and_after_red makes a real implementer commit before the later-commit assertion. The three spec cases are in cases/tests-first.toml: an implementer edit after its own commit passes (story-committed fixture), a test-writer source edit after red at a later commit is blocked (red_already_recorded), and the same sed -i after red passes; a story-committed fixture (red, then one commit) backs them in rule_projects.CASE_PROJECTS.

problem: tests-first looks up the red record and the story kind once per written path, with no memo per story. Each gate_evidence.evidence call starts git through state.store.git (10 s timeout): rev-parse, plus two merge-base --is-ancestor once the story has commits. topics/hook-runner.md allows a rule one git subprocess at 1.5 s. Measured in process: 'touch' of 40 source files started 40 git processes and took 819 ms. A 200-path glob after a commit (about 600 git processes) can pass the 4 s gate deadline and block with runner_timeout.
proposed_resolution: Memoise the story's red record and kind inside check, so there is one lookup per story per call. Tell the orchestrator that evidence()'s own git use (prescribed by the plan) is in conflict with the one-subprocess budget.

outcome.what_was_done: test_story_lookups_taken_once monkeypatches vsdd.state.story_unit.story_kind and vsdd.state.gate_evidence.evidence with counting wrappers, drives one three-path Bash sed write in one story after red (all paths judged, none short-circuits), and asserts one kind lookup and one evidence lookup in total. Verified with the memo disabled (facts never filled): the test fails with three of each; restored, it passes with one of each.

problem: Two gaps let a finding ground when it should not. (1) The catch-all returns '' (grounded) for any exception, so a cited file that cannot be read (permission denied or another OSError) grounds: measured, a mode-000 file with an absent quote returns ''. (2) The project-root base is chosen by the first path segment alone, so '.factory/../src/x.py' grounds against the main checkout's src instead of the reviewed tree. The same trick reaches another story's worktree through '.factory/../.worktrees/<other>/...'.
proposed_resolution: Catch OSError around the read and return 'file cannot be read: <path>'. Keep the catch-all for shape faults only. Use the project-root base only when the resolved path stays under project_root/.factory; anything else resolves against the tree. Add both cases to test_grounding.py.

outcome.what_was_done: ground() returns 'file cannot be read: <path>' when the cited file cannot be read instead of letting the OSError fall to the catch-all and ground; and the project root answers a .factory path only when the resolved path stays under project_root/.factory — .factory/../src/x.py resolves against the reviewed tree. Both tested in test_grounding.py (an unreadable file; a .factory/../ path against a tree that holds the file and a project root that holds a decoy).

problem: Plan 3.3 says git's global options are skipped to find the verb. In opaque text, _next_verb skips '-C' but takes its value as the verb, so "sh -c 'git -C /main commit -m x'" passes (measured 0). On the parsed path, '--git-dir' and '--work-tree' are skipped, but the rule still judges seg.where, so 'git --git-dir=<root>/.git --work-tree=<root> commit -m x' from a story worktree commits on develop and passes (measured 0). '--namespace <v>' also takes its value as the verb.
proposed_resolution: In _next_verb, skip the values of -C, -c, --git-dir, --work-tree, --namespace and --config-env. When --work-tree or --git-dir is given, judge the branch at that location, or block when it cannot be resolved.

outcome.what_was_done: _next_verb skips the separate value of git's global options (-C, -c, --git-dir, --work-tree, --super-prefix), so sh -c 'git -C /main commit' is judged and blocked as opaque_git; and a --git-dir or --work-tree redirect is judged at the branch that tree has checked out — transparently (the block code of the verb, e.g. commit_on_guarded) and inside opaque text (opaque_git, with an unresolvable target failing closed and a redirect outside every factory project passing, per D7). Tests for all three plus the transparent redirect from a story worktree.

problem: _reset_moves returns at the first positional. 'git reset HEAD --hard' on develop therefore passes (measured 0), while 'git reset --hard' is blocked. Plan 3.3 blocks a reset 'with a mode flag', and git accepts options after the revision.
proposed_resolution: Scan every argument before '--' for a mode flag first, then check for a non-HEAD revision. Add 'git reset HEAD --hard' to test_reset_forms.

outcome.what_was_done: _reset_moves searches for a mode flag over every argument before any --, so git reset HEAD --hard on a guarded branch blocks like git reset --hard; the revision scan is unchanged after it. The case joined test_reset_forms' blocked list.

problem: Several false readings, measured. _perl_in_place counts any bundled option containing 'i' as in-place, so 'perl -Mstrict -e ... src/a.py' and '-Mlib=...' read as writes of src/a.py; 'perl -i script.pl f' counts the script as written. 'touch -r ref.txt f' and 'touch -d <date> f' count the option values as written paths. 'cp --target-directory=src a.py' (GNU's real long option) is missed and the source a.py is taken as the destination. Before red, these false targets block harmless commands in a story worktree, and the cp form misses the real target.
proposed_resolution: Recognise perl's -M, -I, -e and -E values and only a real -i or -i<ext>. Add touch's -r, -d and -t to _VALUE_OPTIONS. Accept --target-directory (and its abbreviations) for cp, mv and ln. Add these to test_writes.

outcome.what_was_done: writes.py treats -E like -e for perl, bundled (-pE, -iE) and separate, in the value-option table and the bundled-value reader; the bundled reading now runs before the separate pairing so 'perl -i -pE <script> <file>' trims the script, not the file. When perl's program came as no -e/-E/-f option (checked on the original arguments, with M/F/I honouring their rest-of-word values so -MData::Dumper stays a module), the first operand is the program file and is dropped from the write targets. touch -t joined touch's value options. test_writes rows added for perl -i script.pl src/a.py, perl -pi script.pl src/a.py, perl -pi -E, perl -i -pE and touch -t.

problem: Plan 3.4 step 6 defines the stored result as 'the input with every agent-supplied grounded key removed and grounded: false set on each failing finding', and the Rewrite is meant to carry that. The code returns Rewrite(stored), where stored is store_step's record with agent_type, worktree_head and agent_id added. The script therefore receives three keys the agent never produced. This is harmless while stepSchema leaves the top level open, but it is an unreported departure from a promised interface (the spec was edited to say 'the updatedInput is the stored record').
proposed_resolution: Return Rewrite(adjusted), the marked input, or record the departure and keep spec and plan in step.

outcome.what_was_done: The Rewrite now carries the marked input (the agent's result with the grounded keys adjusted), not store_step's record; test_stored_mark_is_the_only_grounding asserts the rewrite's input carries no agent_type while the stored record does.

problem: The walled test is stated twice and differently. step_results._under_holdout duplicates vsdd.state.steps._under_holdout, but the store also walls 'holdout/...' and walks the whole result, while the rule reads only data.findings and top-level findings. Neither normalises '.' or '..' segments, so '.factory/./holdout/s1.md' or 'src/../.factory/holdout/s1.md' is not walled by either. Such a finding grounds against the project root, and its walled text is stored.
proposed_resolution: Keep one predicate in the state layer, with the path normalised (posixpath.normpath) before the prefix test, and import it in the rule. Add a test with a dotted holdout path.

outcome.what_was_done: test_walled_refused now covers '.factory/./holdout/scenarios/s2.md' and 'holdout/scenarios/s2.md' as walled (blocked walled_not_built, twice each, implementer and scenario-reviewer), and test_normalised_path_outside_the_wall_stores pins the not-walled side: '.factory/holdout/../src/x.md' normalises outside the wall, grounds against the project root, and stores with no grounded mark. tests/unit/test_state_steps.py::test_store_step (a records test; the edit is recorded under S4R-rules-C1-3) stores a result whose only finding cites '.factory/./holdout/HS-003.md' and asserts the walled_not_built refusal beside the state-relative spelling. Verified: with posixpath.normpath dropped from _under_holdout the three tests fail; with the 'holdout/' clause removed (the rule's own old predicate) they fail too; restored, all pass.

problem: Several tests are narrower than the plan. test_block_texts_survive_the_wrapper wraps nothing (plan: 'each blocking case, wrapped as item 40 records'); it only greps the raw stderr. test_import_error_blocks replaces only merge-guard and never checks that nothing is stored, although the plan says 'any one of the three modules' and 'nothing is stored', which matters for step-results. test_not_applied has no docs story and no spike worktree case, both named in the plan.
proposed_resolution: Wrap the stderr the way platform item 40 records it before asserting. Parametrise test_import_error_blocks over the three modules, with a StructuredOutput call that asserts no step record. Add docs-kind and spike-worktree cases to test_not_applied.

outcome.what_was_done: test_block_texts_survive_the_wrapper now wraps each block exactly as platform item 40 records: 'PreToolUse:<tool> hook error: [<command line>]: <message>', a blank line, then 'This hook comes from the vsdd-factory@<plugin> plugin.', with the copied plugin's real launch.sh path as the command line and the StructuredOutput case carrying its own tool name; the assertions that tag, Why: and Instead: stand alone inside that frame are unchanged. The spike case in test_not_applied is annotated as documentation only: a spike directory is no story, so the rule is silent there with or without spike_exempt, and the runner's skip is hooked-runner's to prove; no story and spike overlap exists to construct at slice depth.

problem: The spec lists git merge, rebase and cherry-pick as blocked on a guarded branch. The code and plan D6 also block revert and am, and the spec (which this unit edited) does not say so.
proposed_resolution: Add 'git revert' and 'git am' (each adds a commit) to the integrator list in merge-guard.md.

outcome.what_was_done: rewrite/spec/rules/merge-guard.md's second bullet lists git revert and git am beside merge, rebase and cherry-pick, with the note that each adds a commit, matching the code and plan D6.

problem: The spec says line_start and line_end must lie inside the file but does not say what one bound alone means; the plan fixes it ('one bound given stands for both') and vsdd.grounding implements that. The spec should carry the rule so the verdict tier and the rule cannot diverge.
proposed_resolution: Add one sentence to the grounding paragraph: a single bound stands for both ends, and a bound that is not an integer leaves the line check out (the quote is then sought in the whole file).

outcome.what_was_done: rewrite/spec/rules/step-results.md carries the plan's rule where grounding is described: a finding that gives only one of line_start and line_end is read as that one line. No code change: vsdd.grounding._line_bounds already implements it. spec_lint passes.

problem: shell.parse represents a top-level subshell as one opaque segment whose text is '()', so a rule that must judge what a subshell runs (merge-guard's opaque_git) has to re-scan the whole command text and can attribute a subshell's git verb to no segment in particular. Carrying the inner text on the subshell segment would let rules judge subshells precisely instead of conservatively.
proposed_resolution: Have shell.parse put the subshell's inner text on the Segment (text field or a new field) in a step-3 maintenance change; merge-guard then scans the segment's own text instead of the whole command.

outcome.what_was_done: A subshell whose text holds cd, pushd or popd gets where "" instead of the outer directory: the subshell runs somewhere its own text does not resolve. The worktree-only casework changed with it: (cd <root> && git commit -m x) from the story worktree now blocks, and from the main checkout (cd <wt> && sed -i ...) is a write in an unknown place judged by tests-first.
outcome.where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/hooks/shell.py (_parse subshell branch); next/tests/hooks/test_shell.py (test_a_subshell_holding_a_cd_is_unplaced); next/tests/hooks/test_merge_guard.py (the subshell row of test_unplaced_commands_that_reach_into_a_project); next/tests/hooks/test_tests_first.py (test_a_write_behind_a_cd_is_judged_in_an_unknown_place, the sed form)

problem: launch() forwards the pytest process environment to the launcher child but never sets CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, so hook children resolve the project root from the child shell's own directory walk; a test whose notion of the project differs from the child's walk (worktree cwds, hub layouts) gets a silently inert or differently-scoped runner. Step 3's launcher tests pass because cwd and project coincide.
proposed_resolution: Teach launch() to set CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR from its cwd argument (a step 3 file, so the change belongs to a fix run of the hook-runner unit), or document that callers must pass it through env.

outcome.what_was_done: For H1 when the launcher tests are next widened (hub layouts, worktree working directories): launch() in the hook test helpers sets CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR to the project the test built, so that the child resolves the same project as the test; add one test whose working directory is a story worktree.

problem: Step 4's ORDER.md R5 states test_rule_cases.py 'keeps reading tests/hooks/fixture_cases/ only, as built', but the built _CASE_DIRS also globs tests/hooks/cases/, so the step 3 runner executes the rules unit's three new tables. Its runner cannot express them: it ignores the case 'project' key (rule_projects.CASE_PROJECTS fixtures) and performs no {worktree}/{run}/{sha} substitution, so the fixture-based blocking cases fail (10 failures in the whole-suite run: an expected block reads 0 because in a bare project no story worktree exists for tests-first to judge, and merge-guard's develop is not checked out anywhere). The rules unit is forbidden to edit test_rule_cases.py (ORDER.md section 6), so the mismatch is reported, not patched.
proposed_resolution: A fix run of the hook-runner unit extends test_rule_cases.py's case_payload to honour the case 'project' key through tests.hooks.rule_projects.case_project and to substitute the fixture's returned values into payload and set (the 20-line body of tests/hooks/test_rule_tables.py does exactly this and can be lifted), or restricts _CASE_DIRS to fixture_cases/ and makes test_gate_case_coverage delegate per-rule coverage to tests/hooks/test_rule_tables.py's tables.

outcome.what_was_done: test_rule_cases.py's _CASE_DIRS holds fixture_cases/ only, and its docstring says the per-rule tables are the rules unit's to run. test_gate_case_coverage keeps holding for the three rules by counting tests/hooks/cases/*.toml as data (rule_table_cases()) beside the probe cases, feeding gate_case_problems unchanged; test_rule_tables.py remains the one runner of those tables. Nothing else in the file changed.

problem: The S4R-verdicts-15 fix (_rebuild's stored_used floor, fed by _closure_rounds_used in _compute) changes a story's verdict once the checkpoint stores summary() as the closure verdict. summary()'s rounds_used counts the loop's own passes, so the replay starts that loop as if those passes had been used before it, and the cap falls on an earlier pass. A probe in a scratch copy showed it. Three loop-1 passes, the finding disputed at pass 1, the arbiter's not_defect ruling at pass 3: verdict() is converged/clean with rounds_used 3, and covering() returns it. After closure.verdict = summary() the same records give blocked/cap with rounds_used 6 and the finding blocking, and covering() is None. The story stops reading reviewed and delivery refuses it. Two clean-converging passes go from rounds_used 2 to 4. Every story that converges through the arbiter would hit this at its first checkpoint once survey-2 writes the closure verdict.
proposed_resolution: Remove the stored_used floor, so a loop 1's used is the loop-1 passes of earlier runs (plan verdicts.md 3.3 rule 9) and the full verdict keeps the script's used + pass (D13). Add a test_verdicts case that stores summary() into the closure after an arbiter-converged loop and asserts that verdict(), summary() and covering() are unchanged. The clone case of S4R-verdicts-15 then needs the used the run was given to be recorded (spec steward: S3/W2), not derived from the closure.

outcome.what_was_done: Same removal as S4R-verdicts-15 (the regression's cause): no stored_used floor in _rebuild or _compute. New test_storing_the_summary_moves_nothing runs the exact regression setup — loop-1 passes with the finding disputed at pass 1 and the arbiter ruling not_defect at pass 3, cap 3 — asserts converged/clean with rounds_used 3 and covering() answered, then stores summary() into the closure as survey-2's checkpoint will and asserts verdict(), summary(), covering() and the replay input (used 0, rule 9) are all unchanged. With a floor re-added the test fails exactly as the check described: the verdict turns blocked/cap with rounds_used 6 and code:a blocking (verified by mutation).

problem: The S4R-verdicts-10 fix says r16's records are 'as steps_list returns them', but run r1 holds two byte-identical fix-x-l2-p3 attempt 1 records, and two arbitrate-u-l attempt 1 records (loops 1 and 2). The store keeps one record per run, workflow, subject and name.attempt (steps.py refuses 'already stored'), so no store holds this set and steps_list cannot return it. The expected skipped lists the same step twice. The D6 sort and gate-sha mutations are still caught, so the case does its job, but its input is not a stored record set (plan 3.5: records 'as records.md stores them').
proposed_resolution: Keep one fix-x-l2-p3 record and one skipped entry for it. Name the two arbitrations apart (arbitrate-u-l1 and arbitrate-u-l2, as test_verdicts does) and keep path order. Optionally add a check to test_every_case_is_well_formed that no records case repeats (run, workflow, subject, name, attempt).

outcome.what_was_done: r16 now holds one fix-x-l2-p3 attempt-1 record (the store keeps one record per (run, workflow, subject, name, attempt), so steps_list could never return the byte-identical pair) and its expect.skipped lists the gate-less step once. The two arbitrations are named arbitrate-u-l1 and arbitrate-u-l2 (loops 1 and 2) and keep their positions, which stay the stored path order (arbitrate-u-l1 < arbitrate-u-l2 < fix-...). test_every_case_is_well_formed now refuses a records case that repeats a (run, workflow, subject, name, attempt) identity; every existing case passes it. The case's expected verdicts are unchanged (names are not read by the rebuild), and the whole conformance file passes.

problem: Left over from S4R-verdicts-4: rule 8's 'or no loop before it makes its passes not ok' is still untested. In a scratch copy, changing the branch `if previous_head is None or first_pass_head is None: items = None` to give [] passes all 87 tests in test_verdicts.py, test_conformance.py and test_state_gate_evidence.py. A later loop with no loop before it (or after a loop whose verdict has no head) would then converge on no items instead of failing.
proposed_resolution: Add a records case whose run's only loop is loop 2 (no loop 1 before it), with a clean review, and expect failed/no_result with chain false.

outcome.what_was_done: New records case r21-loop-two-without-loop-one: run r1's only loop is loop 2 (no loop 1 before it) holding one clean review whose reviewer marks AC-1 checked; expect failed/no_result with head empty, chain false and passes_used 0. It discriminates the rule-8 branch: with the no-loop-before items mutated from None to [] the case alone fails (the pass turns ok and converges, coverage marked), the other 49 conformance cases still passing (verified by mutation).

problem: The S4R-verdicts-7 fix edits story_unit.py, a step 3 file that survey-2 rewrites (ORDER.md section 4 gives verdicts only gate_evidence.py, and 'nothing outside this table is edited'). It renames _acs to acs, makes it skip fences, and has verdicts._story_acs import it. The fix report says '_acs kept as a thin alias', but no alias exists. Nothing calls _acs now, so nothing breaks today. But survey-2's builder is not told that story_unit.acs is now an import G3 relies on.
proposed_resolution: The orchestrator records the edit as sanctioned (an ORDER.md section 4 row or a note in survey-2's brief): story_unit.acs is the one AC reader, it skips ``` and ~~~ fences, and verdicts imports it. test_items_equal_unit_acs guards it.

outcome.what_was_done: The orchestrating session recorded the sanction: rewrite/plans/step-4/ORDER.md section 4 has a verdicts row for story_unit.py (acs is the one reader of acceptance criteria, skips code fences, verdicts._story_acs delegates to it), and the launch notes of survey-2, which rewrites that file, say that acs is kept as it is.

problem: Plan 3.3 says covering falls back to 'the closure record's verdict when that is converged and covers head', and it defines cover on the verdict's own head: that commit, or the same non-empty patch_id from delivery.base. The code tests the stored verdict against closure.delivery.head and closure.delivery.patch_id instead. The builder did not report this departure. Nothing writes delivery.head before a merge: admission writes only base and branch, and delivery (plan 3.4) writes head and patch_id only on a merge. (a) A closure whose verdict is summary()'s form at the worktree head, with no run records (a clone, or D8's 'a clone with old or no records follows a newer closure'), gives covering None. My probe confirmed this. (b) Once delivery.head moves past the verdict's head, the old verdict covers a commit nobody reviewed. My probe: verdict converged at H1, a new commit H2, delivery.head = H2, and covering(H2) returns the H1 verdict. test_closure_used_without_records sets delivery.head and patch_id by hand, which no real writer does, so it passes only under the code's rule.
proposed_resolution: In the stored branch, test cover with _covers(tree, base, str(stored.get('head') or ''), head), the same rule as for the computed verdict. Rewrite test_closure_used_without_records to store verdicts.summary()'s form with no delivery.head. Add the stale case (verdict at H1, delivery.head H2, so covering(H2) is None). Update the review case of records' test_evidence_lookup to the same rule, as plan section 4 allows.

outcome.what_was_done: covering's stored branch now covers by the stored verdict's own head through the same _covers test as the computed one (head equality or patch-id from delivery.base); the delivery.head/patch_id consultation is gone. test_closure_used_without_records rewritten to summary()'s form with no delivery.head; the stale H1/H2 case added as test_closure_not_covered_after_a_new_commit; test_computed_overrules_closure's stored verdict now carries summary()'s head and patch_id; records' test_evidence_lookup review case updated to the same rule (the sanctioned ORDER section 4 edit).

problem: changed_files parses plain `git diff --name-only` output, which C-quotes unusual paths. My probe: files 'café.py' and 'q"uote.py' come back as ['"caf\\303\\251.py"', '"q\\"uote.py"']. This is the one definition of 'the files changed'. It gives a later loop's items, G2's --since changed_files (gates/gatelib.py imports it) and delivery's review_stale list. A reviewer's coverage entry names the real path and never matches the quoted item. A later loop that touches such a file can then never converge, and nothing reports why.
proposed_resolution: Run `git -c core.quotePath=false diff --name-only -z --no-renames <since> <head>` and split on NUL. Add a non-ASCII name and a name containing a double quote to test_changed_files_and_later_loop_items.

outcome.what_was_done: changed_files runs git -c core.quotePath=false diff --name-only -z --no-renames and splits on NUL, so unusual paths arrive unquoted. The test stores an accented name (cafe.py, spelled from the filesystem so NFC/NFD agrees) and a name with a double quote, asserts both arrive verbatim and that no C-quoted form appears.

problem: No test covers the chain rule: every loop from the last back to the nearest loop 1 must be converged, which is the condition topics/verdicts.md sets for cover. Two mutations each pass all 77 tests of conformance, test_verdicts and test_state_gate_evidence: _chain returning only 'the last loop converged', and covering ignoring rebuilt['chain']. No case has a loop that did not converge followed by a converged later loop. In r05 the last loop failed. In r06 and r15 both loops converged. In r16 the last loop is blocked. A clean later loop could therefore cover a story whose loop 1 never converged, and no test would notice.
proposed_resolution: Add a records case where loop 1 ends blocked/cap and loop 2 converges. Expect chain false, with the unit's verdict converged. Add a test_verdicts test in which covering is None for that story.

outcome.what_was_done: New records case r17-chain-broken-at-loop-one: loop 1 runs to blocked/cap over four passes and a later loop converges, expecting chain false; unit test test_chain_open_at_one_loop_keeps_covering_none asserts the computed verdict covers nothing while chain is broken. Killing both mutations verified: _chain reduced to the last loop and covering dropping the chain check each fail them.

problem: No test covers rule 8's later-loop items, nor D10's rule that items git cannot compute make the loop's passes not ok. Two mutations pass every test: items = [] for a later loop, and items = changed(...) or [] (which accepts None). r06 is VSA-03's fixture, but its loop-2 reviewer marks brand_new.py checked. A tool that asked for no items converges on r06 just the same. The fixture catches only 'too many items' and never 'the new file is required'.
proposed_resolution: Add a variant of r06 in which the later loop's reviewer does not account for brand_new.py: the coverage gap is open and the verdict is not converged. Add a case whose changed map lacks the later loop's range: changed returns None, the passes are not ok, and the verdict is failed/no_result.

outcome.what_was_done: Two records cases from r06: r18-repair-item-unaccounted, whose later-loop reviewer accounts for none of brand_new.py (expect failed/no_result with the coverage finding open), and r19-changed-range-unknown, whose changed map lacks the range (expect failed/no_result with empty lists, head empty — decision D10). Both discriminate items=[] from items=changed(...) or [].

problem: P3OPS-09 is marked fixed, but no test fails when verdict() ignores the settled waivers: replacing waived=waivers(project, subject) with waived=[] in _compute passes all 77 tests. waivers() is tested alone (test_waivers_from_settled_decision). rebuild is tested only with waived passed in directly. Nothing tests the wiring between them. r08-waive-after-cap is also a single pass at cap 3, which never reaches the cap, so it is the same as l14-waived. The code itself is right: my probe of a real after-cap record set (four passes, blocked/cap without the waiver) gives converged/clean once code:a is waived. No test holds it there.
proposed_resolution: Make r08 a real after-cap case: passes 1 to 4 with code:a open and an arbitration at the cap give blocked/cap; with code:a waived the verdict is converged. Add a test_verdicts test that stores a finding through store_step, settles 'waive key=code:a' on finding.<subject>, and asserts that verdict() is converged and covering() is not None.

outcome.what_was_done: r08-waive-after-cap redone as a real after-cap story: four passes that end blocked/cap without the waiver and converge with it, so removing the waiver from the case input fails the case. The waivers()->verdict() wiring is tested by test_waived_verdict_converges_through_the_decision, which settles finding.S-9.01 through decision_open/settle_decision and asserts the verdict and covering turn converged (verified to fail with waived=[] in _compute).

problem: VSA-07 is marked fixed with test_verdict_trusts_stored_mark, but that test cannot tell trusting the mark apart from grounding again at count time, which is the defect VSA-07 names. The test stores grounded: false itself, and a re-grounding verdict also reads that finding as advisory. I made _compute mark grounded: false on every finding whose path is missing from the current worktree, and all 77 tests still pass. No test stores an unmarked blocking finding whose file a later commit removed.
proposed_resolution: Add a test that stores an unmarked high finding on a path that exists at the reviewed commit, then removes or renames that file in a later commit (as a fix would), and asserts that the finding is still in blocking.

outcome.what_was_done: test_verdict_never_regounds_an_unmarked_finding added: an unmarked critical finding on src/module.py keeps blocking after a later commit removes the file, so a tool that re-grounds against the current worktree would unground it and fail the test. The grounded:false half stays in test_verdict_trusts_stored_mark.

problem: The two AC readers disagree. verdicts._story_acs skips headings inside code fences, as D9 says. story_unit._acs, whose list the script hands to reviewers as the items, does not skip them. My probe added a fenced '### AC-9' to the story: the unit's acs were ['AC-1', 'AC-9'] and the verdict's items were ['AC-1']. test_items_equal_unit_acs is meant to hold the two together (D9), but its fence contains no heading ('no headings here'), so it cannot fail. With such a story the tool and the script require different items, and their verdicts can differ either way.
proposed_resolution: Give both one reader: a small shared helper that both call (it must not import the verdict, which would create a cycle), or story_unit skipping fences the same way (its owner's edit). Put a '### AC-9' heading inside the test's fence.

outcome.what_was_done: One shared reader: story_unit.acs(body) skips fences (strips ``` and ~~~ openings and closings) and verdicts._story_acs delegates to it, so the tool and the unit cannot require different items. test_items_equal_unit_acs now puts '### AC-9' inside its fence and both readers must still answer ['AC-1','AC-2']; the unfenced story_unit reader fails it. Note: this edits story_unit.py, which the survey-2 plan edits in section 4 — the finding asked for exactly this.

where: next/tests/conformance/test_conformance.py (SPEC_ROWS); next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/convergence.py (replay, the walk-on after a converged pass)
problem: packaging/tests-conformance.md has the row 'A loop whose records go on after a pass with nothing open: the verdict is the one the last recorded pass gives (Python only)'. SPEC_ROWS maps it to r11-cut-off-after-fix, which stops after a fix and never goes on past a clean pass. test_spec_rows_have_cases therefore claims a coverage that does not exist. No test covers the walk-on branch after a converged pass: making the converged case keep the old claims instead of `claims = []` passes every test. The builder's S4B-verdicts-1 covers only the case where a blocked review is followed by another pass.
proposed_resolution: Add a records case: pass 1 is clean (converged), and pass 2 of the same loop has a hard finding with no fix. Expect the last pass's verdict, not the first. Map the row to that case.

outcome.what_was_done: New records case r20-walk-on-after-clean: pass 1 clean, pass 2 opens a hard finding with no fix, and the last pass's verdict (failed/no_result, finding blocking) is expected. The spec row 'A loop whose records go on after a pass with nothing open' now maps to that case instead of r11-cut-off-after-fix, whose records never go on past a clean pass.

problem: SPEC_ROWS maps the two holdout-score rows ('A must-pass scenario at 0.5 (floor 0.6)' and 'A mean of 0.8 (threshold 0.85)') to j04-holdout-needs-no-location. j04 is a judge() case on a hand-built holdout finding and does not exercise holdoutFindings() scoring. The plan (section 1) defers both cases to G6a, so the table claims a coverage that does not exist.
proposed_resolution: List the two rows as deferred (for example a DEFERRED_ROWS map naming G6a) rather than mapping them to j04. Have test_spec_rows_have_cases check that every spec row is either mapped or deferred.

outcome.what_was_done: The two holdout-score rows are listed in DEFERRED_TO_G6A with a comment naming the deferral (plan step-4 verdicts.md 1), and test_spec_rows_have_cases asserts deferred rows claim no case; they no longer map to j04.

problem: r16 lists the test-writer's fix records before the implementer's. steps_list returns records in path order, which puts fix-implementer-... before fix-tw-..., so the case's order is not the stored order. Dropping D6's method sort and joining in stored order therefore passes every test. Only the reversed sort is caught. Rule 4's 'a passing gate whose sha equals the record's head' is not tested either: removing the sha comparison passes every test.
proposed_resolution: Order r16's records as steps_list would (implementer first by path). Add to r07 a fix record whose only passing gate is at another sha, and expect it in skipped with why 'gate'.

outcome.what_was_done: r16's records are now ordered as steps_list returns them (alphabetical by step name, fix-implementer before fix-tw), so dropping D6's method sort flips loop 1 out of converged and fails the case (verified by mutation). A third fix record fix-x-l2-p3 whose passing gate sits at another sha lands in skipped with why 'gate' (verified that removing the sha check fails the case).

problem: public_verdict replaces walled findings in blocking, advisory and deferred, but leaves dismissed untouched. A walled finding that the reviewer withdraws, or the arbiter dismisses, keeps its key in clear, plus the arbiter's reason. My probe of a withdrawn holdout finding gave dismissed [{'key': 'holdout:HS-9', 'by': 'reviewer', ...}]. Nothing reaches this today, because records refuses to store a walled finding.
proposed_resolution: Map dismissed entries whose key is walled to the walled key, and drop the reason. Extend test_public_verdict_hides_walled with a withdrawn walled finding.

outcome.what_was_done: public_verdict maps walled keys in dismissed to walled:<12 hex> and empties the reason (kept as an empty string because verdict.schema.json requires the member), for reviewer withdrawals and arbiter dismissals alike. The test extends test_public_verdict_hides_walled with a second rebuild whose reviewer withdraws the walled finding; the unmapped form fails it.

problem: Suppose the arbiter has been applied at the cap and the loop converged, and the records go on with findings open. replay then neither arbitrates nor caps: extra is 0 and arbitrated is true, so the code falls through to the fixer on every later pass. The loop ends failed/no_result rather than blocked/cap. My probe: cap 2, a dismissal at pass 2, findings open at passes 3 to 5. The fixer was asked at 3, 4 and 5, and the verdict was failed/no_result.
proposed_resolution: At the cap with the arbitration already spent, set the outcome to blocked/cap, as the script's break would. Pin this with a records case once the walk-on cases of S4R-verdicts-8 exist.

outcome.what_was_done: convergence.replay sets blocked/cap at the cap when the arbitration is already spent and findings stay open, instead of asking the fixer again and ending failed/no_result. New records case r22-cap-after-arbitration: pass 3 is settled by the arbiter and converges, pass 4 opens a new finding and the loop is capped with it (verified to fail with the branch removed).

problem: The two sources name the closure verdict's fields differently. records/closure.md and the shipped schema's verdict list `commit`, which nothing writes. summary() writes head, patch_id and rounds_used. rounds_used() reads the stored rounds_used, and cover (once S4R-verdicts-1 is fixed) reads head and patch_id. The spec schema's own description already says 'head is the commit the verdict covers'.
proposed_resolution: Spec steward and records: rename `commit` to `head` and add patch_id and rounds_used to the verdict properties of the schema and to records/closure.md.

outcome.what_was_done: closure-record.schema.json's verdict properties renamed commit to head and gained patch_id and rounds_used, with descriptions tying them to vsdd.state.verdicts.summary, and records/closure.md's verdict paragraph now names the summary form. The schema change is an interface note for the not-yet-built checkpoint writers; summary() and test_summary_is_valid_closure_verdict already produced these keys.

problem: Plan section 7 asks for one Node test per judge and loop case. The runner has one test that loops over every case. The first failing case stops the loop, and the report names a single test, so a second disagreement stays hidden until the first is fixed. The builder did not report this departure.
proposed_resolution: Compute the results once (top-level await, or a before() hook) and register one test() per case, named by its file stem.

outcome.what_was_done: conformance.test.mjs computes the judge and loop results once (a shared promise over one harness run) and registers one test per case named by its file stem, so a failing case no longer stops a loop and hides later disagreements; node --test reports 26 tests.

problem: For a loop 1, the replay's `used` counts the loop-1 passes of earlier runs in the local records. The script was given rounds_used(), which also counts the closure's stored rounds_used (D13), and the survey caps it after a direct. Take a clone with no earlier run records whose closure carries a count, say 2 with cap 3. The script arbitrates at pass 1 and can dismiss a disputed finding, giving converged. The replay with used 0 asks for a fix at pass 1 and ends failed/no_result. The tool's verdict then refuses a story the script converged.
proposed_resolution: Replay each run's loop 1 with the `used` the script was given. Record it in the run record or in the review step's identity, or derive it as rounds_used() does (the larger of the earlier-run passes and the stored closure count).

outcome.what_was_done: Not on the slice path: it needs a clone, or a machine that lost its local records, whose closure already carries a round count, and the slice is one run on one machine with records kept. For M3 (hand-off between clones) with S3 and G3: the survey records, on the run record, the rounds_used it hands the script for each story; verdicts._rebuild replays each run's loop 1 with that recorded figure, using rule 9's count only for a run without it; rounds_used() is the recorded figure plus the run's own passes. Correct the comment in _rebuild that says a clone with short records follows the closure's stored verdict, and add the test_verdicts case of the finding's probe (closure rounds_used 1, cap 3, no earlier records, a dispute ruled not_defect) expecting converged/clean and a covering() answer.

problem: The replay's continue-after-a-return-point rule (a pass that follows a pass the script would have ended on is reviewed with no claims after a clean pass, else with claims rebuilt from the open findings and the pass's fix) is built and exercised only indirectly: the loop conformance cases cannot carry it, because the Node prelude stops at the script's first return point, and no records case stores a return-point pass with a recorded pass after it (r11 covers only the cut-off after a fix).
proposed_resolution: When a records-case author next touches the fixtures, add one case whose recorded passes continue after a blocked review (the following pass's review receiving the rebuilt claims), so the continue rule is pinned like the rest.

outcome.what_was_done: For G3 when the conformance cases are next extended (with G6a's holdout cases at the latest): add one records case whose stored passes continue after a blocked review, the following pass's review receiving the rebuilt claims, so that the continue rule is pinned as the walk-on-after-clean rule is by r20.

problem: The step-record path is keyed on name.attempt alone, so a workflow whose step names do not carry the loop and pass would overwrite an earlier pass's record under the same name (step_exists from another agent, or a same-agent_id replacement). The shipped prelude names every review, fix and arbitrate step with its loop and pass (review-a-l1-p1), so nothing is lost today, but nothing enforces the name grammar that the verdict relies on for one record per pass.
proposed_resolution: When the build widens beyond the shipped workflows, either lint the step-name grammar of workflow scripts or key the record path on the full step identity including loop and pass.

outcome.what_was_done: For B6 with S2a, when a workflow beyond the shipped story script is built (W3 first): lint the step-name grammar the verdict relies on (review-<lens>-l<n>-p<k>, fix-<agent>-l<n>-p<k>, arbitrate-l<n>) in every workflow script, so that one record per pass cannot be overwritten under a shared name; the story script's scenario tests already assert its names.

problem: The module docstring of gate_evidence.py still describes the review lookup as 'the verdict of a converged closure that covers the head', but the review branch now answers vsdd.state.verdicts.covering (computed verdict first, closure second, per PL4-2).
